     counterexamples are in `GLOBAL_PINNING.md`.

## 41. Why the canonical orthogonal-SCD construction cannot work

189. For two orthogonal endpoint-chain decompositions, ordering is not a free
     choice.  Form the right precedence digraph by putting an arc R(S)->R(T)
     whenever S subset T are consecutive in one left chain, and define the
     left precedence digraph dually, with the direction reversed.  The desired
     endpoint orders exist exactly when these digraphs are acyclic.  Empty
     placeholder chains only insert gaps and cannot remove a directed cycle.

     The standard Greene--Kleitman SCD and its complement fail this test for
     every k>=3.  In even dimension k=2m>=4 the failure is already central:
     the combined adjacent-rank precedence graph

        F_-^(rev) union F_+

     contains an explicit directed cycle of length 2m.  Here F_- records the
     rank-(m-1) intersection cells between middle chains and F_+ records the
     rank-(m+1) union cells.  Consequently the canonical orthogonal pair
     cannot be repaired by reordering or by adding empty slack slots; at least
     one nonempty split or reassignment is necessary in each endpoint family.

190. In fixed central delay d, a lower mask in left middle chain i and right
     middle chain j must occupy the band cell [i,j+d], so

        1 <= i-j <= d.

     The pure W-by-W chain band contains dW-binomial(d+1,2) lower cells, while
     the physical word contains dW+binomial(d+1,2) intervals of length at most
     d.  Thus the two boundary triangles have total size d(d+1).  With

        sigma=dW+binomial(d+1,2)-sum_(s<m) binomial(2m,s),

     at least max(0,d(d+1)-sigma) lower masks are forced into nonempty split
     boundary chains.  This identifies the actual job of the d extra slots:
     they are cycle-breaking chain pieces, not empty padding.  The complete
     proofs, including the symbolic 2m-cycle, are in `ORDERED_OSCD.md`.

## 42. Catalan compression is achievable globally

191. A theorem of Gregor--Micka--Mutze on saturating cycles in consecutive
     hypercube levels gives a useful construction for every even k=2m.  Put

        W=binomial(2m,m),
        K=Cat_m=W/(m+1),
        N=binomial(2m,m+1)=W-K.

     There is a Hamilton cycle P through all W middle m-sets such that, for
     every (m+1)-set U, all consecutive edges of P having union U form one
     nonempty contiguous block.  Compressing each block to its colour gives a
     Hamilton cycle through the complete (m+1)-layer of exact length N.

     The proof starts with a saturating alternating cycle between levels m and
     m+1.  Each of the K unused middle sets is inserted into any block indexed
     by a containing (m+1)-set.  All m-subsets of the same U form a clique in
     J(2m,m), so every insertion preserves the Hamilton cycle and its union
     colour.  This is a search-free all-dimension theorem.

192. The compressed cycle gives an exact width-preserving central parity
     braid.  Reverse the N old (m+1)-sets and concatenate the W middle sets of
     P after adjoining a new coordinate z.  The result is a Johnson Hamilton
     path through every rank-(m+1) set of the (2m+1)-cube, of length

        N+W=2W-Cat_m=W(2m+1).

     This settles the Catalan vertex accounting and one complete upper-colour
     layer.  It does not by itself supply all lower colours, long coordinate
     runs, deeper shadows, or a pin-surviving factor.

193. Independently, the Greene--Kleitman chain pairing supplies exactly
     W-Cat_m two-sided colour-perfect middle edges, hence a forest with
     Cat_m components.  It may branch: already in dimension six one middle
     vertex has degree three.  The remaining central theorem is therefore
     precise:

        choose, by alternating switches in the rank-(m-1) / rank-(m+1)
        incidence matching, a two-sided colour-perfect spanning linear
        forest with Cat_m components whose endpoints can be joined by
        Cat_m-1 Johnson bridges.

     Proving this Catalan linearization lemma would turn the exact binomial
     saving into a single global middle-layer skeleton.  Shadow inheritance
     and pinning would remain, but the previous vague search has now been
     reduced to a canonical matching problem.  Full details and all caveats
     are in `GLOBAL_RECURSION.md`.

## 43. Kneser normal form and exact Catalan balance laws

194. Complementation turns the adjacent-layer matching into a standard graph
     object.  Put A=binomial([2m],m-1).  A perfect matching between rank m-1
     sets S and containing rank m+1 sets U is equivalent to a permutation

        g:A->A,             S intersect g(S)=empty,

     by g(S)=[2m] minus U.  Thus it is a directed 1-factor of the Kneser graph
     KG(2m,m-1).  The matched pair produces the Johnson edge between the two
     middle sets lying strictly between S and U.  For a middle set P its
     induced degree is exactly

        d_g(P)=#{a in P : g(P minus {a}) subset P^c}.

     Hence the degree gate is: choose a disjointness permutation for which no
     middle cut (P,P^c) is crossed more than twice.  Ordinary Kneser
     Hamiltonicity does not by itself imply this extra load condition.

195. Every such matching has two exact, construction-independent balance
     laws.  If lambda(S,U)=U minus S is its two-coordinate transition label,
     then every coordinate occurs in exactly Cat_m labels.  If

        delta(P)=2-d_g(P),

     then

        sum_P delta(P)=2 Cat_m,
        sum_(P containing x) delta(P)=Cat_m  for every coordinate x.

     Therefore, once maximum degree two is achieved, the endpoint tokens of
     the resulting paths form a perfect coordinate 1-design.  Since the
     matching has W-Cat_m edges, any maximum-degree-two realization has
     exactly Cat_m path components; only cycle elimination and endpoint
     bridgeability remain.

196. Alternating 2-switches have a rigid geometry: every cross-switchable
     pair is a pivoted rook switch around one middle set.  Safe degree-transfer
     and cycle-opening switches exist under explicit local conditions, but
     the natural cyclic-parenthesis matching has a symbolic vertex of degree
     m, and switches at that pivot merely permute its spokes.  Thus a proof
     may require longer alternating cycles or a specially chosen Kneser
     permutation.  The exact switch formulas and open three-gate lemma are in
     `CATALAN_LINEARIZATION.md`.

## 44. A recursive pinning theorem compatible with Catalan blocks

197. For a bit b, take the union U_b of all selected intervals whose masks
     omit b.  If every connected component C of U_b is itself the interval of
     some b-negative selected mask R_C, then containment monotonicity forces
     every b-positive interval to meet the complement of U_b.  Therefore all
     bits can be pinned, and the coordinatewise maximal factor realizes every
     assigned mask.

     A recursive certificate is enough.  Arrange the negative intervals in a
     merge forest: linked child intervals must have a b-negative parent whose
     interval contains their hull, and final roots must be separated by a
     clean integer position.  Induction makes the roots exactly the components
     of U_b, so the preceding theorem applies.  In a Catalan construction,
     leaf path blocks carry negative roots and each component bridge carries
     the parent root.  This incurs no additional array positions.

198. Simple substitutes are provably insufficient.  Laminarity without gaps,
     bounded delay, and low local overlap can all leave a positive interval
     fully covered by negative barriers.  One global coatom root per bit is
     impossible for k>=3.  Moreover, if rho_b is the number of occurrence runs
     of bit b in an actual array, then

        sum_b rho_b >= sqrt(2^k-1)-1.

     Indeed the run endpoints divide the two-dimensional interval-endpoint
     plane into at most (1+sum rho_b)^2 constant-OR regions.  Thus a valid
     global proof needs exponentially many hierarchical components; the
     Catalan recursion has enough components, whereas a polynomial absorber
     scheme cannot.  Full proofs and the exact absorber min-max theorem are in
     `PINNING_THEOREM.md`.

## 45. Exact limits of repairing an orthogonal chain pair

199. Chain splitting is governed by a feedback problem, not merely by chain
     counts.  For an orthogonal pair, each directed precedence cycle has a set
     of left-chain generators and right-chain generators at which a nonempty
     split would destroy it.  The minimum number of cuts needed for both
     endpoint orders is exactly the two-coloured transversal number of this
     alternating-cycle support hypergraph.  Disjoint cycle supports therefore
     give immediate additive lower bounds on the required splits.

200. In the adjacent central layers this yields the necessary condition

        wfas(F_-^(rev) multiset-union F_+) <= 2d

     for a construction with only d extra endpoint slots on each side.  After
     cutting, triangular realizability is exactly a topological-order problem
     with release times and deadlines; acyclicity alone is insufficient.
     Abstract orthogonality admits families of disjoint four-cycle gadgets and
     hence arbitrarily large feedback cost.  Therefore no theorem about an
     arbitrary orthogonal SCD pair can prove nu(k)=B(k); the pair must have
     additional Boolean structure giving an O(d) cycle transversal together
     with the band deadlines and pin roots.  See `CHAIN_SPLITTING.md`.

## 46. Exact lower-shadow completion inside the saturating-cycle blocks

201. The upper-colour construction of paragraph 191 has one remaining local
     freedom: assign each of the Cat_m unused middle sets to a containing
     rank-(m+1) block U, and order the assigned middle sets between that
     block's two fixed terminal sets.  Label an m-subset of U by the unique
     coordinate it deletes from U.  A path through the block is then a path
     through deletion labels, and each consecutive label pair {a,b} realizes
     the lower colour U minus {a,b}.

     Lower-shadow completion is therefore equivalent to the following exact
     representative-path problem:

        assign every lower colour S to one containing upper block U;
        assign every unused middle set to one containing block;
        in each block, require that the assigned deletion-label edges form a
        terminal-compatible linear forest, extendable to one Hamilton path
        through all labels assigned to that block.

     The local extension criterion is exact: a prescribed edge set on a
     block's deletion labels extends to a Hamilton path with fixed terminals
     precisely when it is a linear forest, neither terminal is internal to a
     wrong component, and the component endpoints admit the required terminal
     ordering.  Satisfying these conditions in every block is necessary and
     sufficient for one Hamilton middle cycle with all upper and lower
     adjacent colours.

202. The total connector freedom is exactly Cat_m.  Private-colour absorbers
     and an adjacent two-block colour swap can repair certain local defects
     without losing the automatic upper colours.  However, a block may have
     an inaccessible lower colour, two demands may force the same terminal,
     or an assignment may force a duplicate deletion label.  Hence the
     saturating-cycle theorem alone cannot imply lower completion; a global
     representative assignment or absorber theorem is still required.  The
     full iff theorem and local obstructions are in `BLOCK_SHADOWS.md`.

## 47. Unconditional near-width completion of both adjacent shadows

203. There is now an unconditional asymptotic theorem for the first two-sided
     shadow gate.  For k=2m, let W=binomial(2m,m).  Construct a 4-uniform
     hypergraph with vertex classes

        rank-(m-1) colours,
        rank-(m+1) colours,
        two labelled copies of every middle m-set.

     For each S subset U with ranks m-1 and m+1, let X,Y be the two middle
     sets strictly between them and add the four lifted edges

        {S,U,X^a,Y^b},        a,b in {0,1}.

     A hypergraph matching projects to a Johnson graph of maximum degree two
     with no repeated lower or upper colour.  Its exact degrees are

        d_colour=2m(m+1),
        d_clone=2m^2,
        maximum codegree=2m=o(m^2).

     Hence the Pippenger--Frankl--Rodl nibble already selects W-o(W)
     simultaneous lower/upper colours.

204. To control cycles, declare a conflict whenever selected lifted edges
     project to a simple Johnson cycle of length at most a fixed L.  The
     conflict degrees satisfy

        Delta_i=O_L(D^(i-2)),
        Delta_(i,j)=O_L(D^(i-j-1)),       D=Theta(m^2).

     The Delcourt--Postle conflict-free matching theorem applies and produces
     a W-o_L(W) matching with projected girth greater than L.  Delete one edge
     from every remaining cycle, costing at most W/(L+1).  A diagonal choice
     L->infinity gives a spanning linear forest with W-o(W) two-sided rainbow
     edges and o(W) components.

     Concatenating the component paths gives a permutation of all middle sets
     missing only o(W) adjacent colours.  Appending the two intermediate
     middle sets of one Boolean diamond for each missing colour costs o(W).
     Therefore:

        For every even k=2m there is a sequence T of middle m-sets of length
        W+o(W) whose adjacent intersections cover every rank-(m-1) set and
        whose adjacent unions cover every rank-(m+1) set.

205. This is the first unconditional leading-constant-one theorem for a
     nontrivial two-sided portion of the problem.  It does not yet imply a
     universal OR array: depth-two and deeper shadows, coordinate-run
     factorability, the lower-band growth diagram, and pin survival remain.
     The ambient-size hypothesis in the Glock--Joos--Kim--Kuhn--Lichev black
     box fails here; the proof specifically uses the Delcourt--Postle theorem,
     whose stronger conflict-codegree hypotheses are checked directly.  The
     complete audit is in `ASYMPTOTIC_MATCHING.md`.

## 48. What Kneser Hamiltonicity does and does not provide

206. In the Kneser normal form, a perfect adjacent-layer matching is an
     arbitrary directed cycle cover g of KG(2m,m-1), not necessarily one
     Hamilton cycle.  For each middle P, its m facets and the m facets of P^c
     induce a canonical K_(m,m).  The projected degree of P is exactly the
     number of selected arcs crossing this biclique from the P side to the
     P^c side.  Thus maximum projected degree two is equivalent to every
     canonical biclique having at most four selected unoriented arcs, split at
     most two in each direction.  The total four-crossing defect is exactly
     4 Cat_m, so this is an almost-everywhere equality constraint.

207. The standard inductive Hamilton construction for KG(2m,m-1) cannot be
     used unchanged.  For every even m>=4 it preserves a spanning alternating
     path through one canonical K_(m,m), which forces projected degree at
     least m.  The modern all-Kneser Hamiltonicity proof sends this boundary
     family n=2r+2 through that induction, so ordinary Kneser Hamiltonicity
     supplies no dispersed-cycle guarantee.  A successful cycle must break
     every canonical biclique into linearly many separated visits.

208. There is nevertheless no fractional obstruction.  Give every incidence
     interval (S,U), S subset U, weight

        1/binomial(m+1,2).

     Then every lower and upper colour has weight one, every middle vertex has
     weighted degree 2m/(m+1)<2, and every family X of middle vertices obeys
     the graphic-forest inequality

        x(E(X)) <= |X|-1.

     Hence the uniform point lies simultaneously in the perfect-matching,
     degree-two, and Johnson graphic-forest polytopes.  The exact Catalan
     lemma is an integrality/rounding problem for this symmetric intersection,
     not a density impossibility.  The canonical-cut formula, projected-cycle
     certificate, and construction audit are in `KNESER_PROJECTION.md`.

## 49. The all-upper-ranks problem is a nested block tower

209. The upper half does not require an unrelated search at every rank.  A
     sufficient global object is a nested union-block tower.  For each
     r=m,m+1,...,k let P_r be a sequence containing every r-set.  Require that
     P_r is partitioned into consecutive blocks B_U, in the order in which U
     occurs in P_(r+1), and

        union_(X in B_U) X = U.

     Expanding one block recursively shows that every entry of every P_r is
     the union of one contiguous segment of the bottom row P_m.  Consequently
     P_m alone has interval unions covering every rank at least m.

210. A one-level refinement has an exact Johnson formulation.  Given a cyclic
     Hamilton order U_0,...,U_(N-1) of the (r+1)-sets whose consecutive
     intersections C_i=U_(i-1) intersect U_i are distinct r-sets, the sequence

        C_i, [all still-unused r-subsets assigned inside U_i], C_(i+1)

     is a U_i-coloured block: all its consecutive vertices lie in U_i, and
     its union is U_i.  Since the r-subsets of one U_i form a clique in the
     Johnson graph, arbitrary assigned vertices can be threaded between the
     terminals.  This is exactly the saturating-cycle expansion.

211. Iterating requires more than ordinary Hamiltonicity.  The expanded P_r
     must again have distinct consecutive intersections so it can serve as
     the prescribed upper order for the next refinement.  In deletion-label
     coordinates this is precisely the representative-path problem of
     Section 46.  Thus the full upper theorem is:

        construct a nested family of terminal-compatible block paths whose
        lower edge colours are globally collision-free at every level, with
        only o(W) total repetitions at the bottom level.

     Such a tower would solve every upper shadow simultaneously.  It would
     then remain to impose the delay/run condition on P_m and use the
     negative-root growth diagram for all lower masks.  This replaces the
     vague demand for "all longer shadows" by one recursive compatibility
     theorem.

## 50. Exact middle-level quotient and why symmetry alone is insufficient

212. Take any Hamilton cycle in the middle-level graph on ranks m and m+1 of
     [2m+1], and distinguish a coordinate z.  Split the old m-sets into the
     no-z and with-z copies and suppress the two outer kinds of vertices.  The
     result is exactly two Johnson path factors on the W old middle sets:

        an upper factor with N=W-Cat_m edges using every rank-(m+1) union
        colour once;
        a lower factor with N edges using every rank-(m-1) intersection
        colour once.

     Each factor has exactly Cat_m nontrivial paths, and their endpoint sets
     are the same 2 Cat_m vertical labels.  Conversely, lifting two such
     factors gives one middle-level Hamilton cycle exactly when their two
     endpoint-pairing involutions alternate in one cycle.

213. This quotient explains the Catalan count but does not identify the two
     factors.  Complement symmetry only gives F_-=complement(F_+), not both
     colour systems in one factor.  The diagonal choice F_-=F_+ produces
     Cat_m disjoint cycles after lifting rather than one Hamilton cycle.  To
     fold the two copies into the desired single factor one still needs
     Cat_m-1 colour-preserving incidence-four-cycle switches, with no degree
     or cycle defect.  Thus the middle-level theorem and Catalan linearization
     share the same switch obstruction; the quotient does not bypass it.
     Exact statements and the converse construction are in
     `MIDDLE_LEVEL_QUOTIENT.md`.

## 51. The fixed-parameter near-Ucycle construction fails centrally

214. A simple-string near-Ucycle would be a powerful factorization device,
     but the known Curtis--Hines--Hurlbert--Moyer construction cannot be
     specialized to the central regime.  For a rooted m-subset of a cyclic
     2m-set, the cyclic gap vector is exactly a uniformly random composition
     of 2m into m positive parts, equivalently independent Geometric(1/2)
     variables conditioned to have sum 2m.  Part sizes around log_2(m) then
     have constant-order occupancy.

     A local central-limit and occupancy argument shows that a positive
     proportion of these compositions have no part size of multiplicity one.
     Such subsets are not ``good'', hence not ``awesome'', in the terminology
     of that construction.  Consequently its central Euler tour omits

        Omega(binomial(2m,m))

     middle sets.  This is a real density obstruction to that family, not
     merely a nonuniform error term.  Independently, the published proof uses
     fixed-dimensional Schur asymptotics and a residual parameter n-2k-1,
     so its formal estimates also leave their domain at n=2k.

215. The queue implication itself remains exact.  If a cyclic word has L
     distinct length-m windows which are m-subsets of [2m], those windows form
     a simple Johnson cycle.  Every coordinate occurs in incidence runs of
     exactly length m, and the singleton word is an automatic delay-(m-1)
     factor.  Adjacent intersections and unions are the length-(m-1) and
     length-(m+1) symbol windows.  Thus a genuinely new central near-Ucycle
     would solve the run/factorization gate, but it would still need a theorem
     making all shorter and longer symbol windows cover their ranks.  The
     complete audit and positive-density proof are in
     `CENTRAL_NEAR_UCYCLE.md`.

## 52. Exact limit of the equitable-factorization shortcut

216. The common edge set in the Catalan matching problem has two graph
     structures.  In the inclusion graph H_m it must receive a proper
     D-edge-colouring, D=binomial(m+1,2); in the Johnson graph each colour must
     have degree at most two.  Koenig/de Werra solves the first marginal, and
     Hilton--de Werra solves the second marginal independently, but neither
     theorem couples them.

     A generic frequency-two coupling theorem is false.  On a six-cycle with
     alternating edges e_1,f_1,e_2,f_2,e_3,f_3, take

        Q_0={e_1,e_2,e_3},
        Q_1={e_1,f_1,f_2},
        Q_2={e_2,f_1,f_3},
        Q_3={e_3,f_2,f_3}.

     Every edge lies in exactly two Q's, every Q has average colour load 3/2,
     and the Q's are pairwise linear; nevertheless every proper two-colouring
     alternates and makes Q_0 monochromatic.  Hence frequency, average load,
     and linear overlap cannot prove the Boolean result.

217. For the actual Boolean graph the exact surviving target is the polytope

        P_m={x>=0: x(delta_H(v))=1 for all v,
                    x(Q(P))<=2 for all middle P}.

     Proposition 4B is precisely the integer decomposition

        1=x^(1)+...+x^(D),  x^(c) integral in P_m.

     The combined incidence matrix is not totally unimodular or balanced: a
     Johnson triangle gives a 3-by-3 minor of determinant two.  Thus one needs
     Boolean-specific normality/IDP or a special alternating-cycle theorem for
     the overlapping canonical K_(m,m)'s.  The exact Kempe-exchange formula,
     obstruction, and remaining polyhedral statement are in
     `EQUITABLE_FACTORIZATION.md`.

## 53. Unconditional completion of every fixed central band

218. The adjacent-shadow theorem extends to every fixed depth.  Fix J and a
     larger block parameter ell.  A cyclic Johnson block is obtained by
     choosing ell disjoint exchange pairs and flipping them in order, first
     forward and then backward.  It has 2ell distinct middle states; every
     q-window, q<=J, is geodesic, and its rank-(m-q) intersection and
     rank-(m+q) union colours are distinct within the block.

     Package one whole block as a hyperedge whose vertex classes are the
     middle layer and all 2J shadow layers.  The block hypergraph has fixed
     uniformity 2ell(1+2J), asymptotically equal vertex degrees

        Theta_(ell,J)(m^(2ell)),

     and maximum pair codegree only O(D/m).  The Pippenger--Frankl--Rodl
     almost-perfect matching theorem therefore packs blocks covering all but
     o(W) vertices in every class.  Linearizing the cycles, explicitly
     repairing the o(W) omissions, and padding their ends costs o(W) after a
     slow choice ell=ell(m)->infinity.

219. Consequently, for every fixed J there is a middle-row sequence of length

        W+o_J(W)

     whose consecutive q-window intersections and unions cover every set of
     ranks m-q and m+q for all q<=J.  Every internal coordinate one-run can
     simultaneously be made at least J+1.  Its maximal delay-J factor is
     therefore an OR sequence of length W+o_J(W) covering the entire fixed
     band m-J,...,m+J.  A second diagonal yields some unspecified
     J(m)->infinity with the same conclusion.  This removes every fixed-depth
     obstruction at once; it is a genuine all-k construction theorem, not a
     finite search result.

220. Two limitations are exact.  First, the tempting directed-edge conflict
     formulation fails the Delcourt--Postle hypothesis: fixing one geodesic
     q-path leaves Theta(D^q) disjoint q-paths with the same deep colour, so
     Delta_(2q,q) has no required power saving.  Treating a whole long block
     as one matching edge is what avoids this collision.

     Second, equal block occupancy in every rank is intrinsically nonuniform
     when q grows.  At q on the order of sqrt(m log m),

        binomial(2m,m-q)/W=exp(-Theta(q^2/m))

     is polynomially small, so the rank classes no longer have comparable
     degrees.  The correct growing-depth object must use rank-dependent
     occupancies.  A precise candidate uses 2m-swap cycles but retains only

        c_q approximately (2m) binomial(2m,m-q)/W

     designated q-window colours in each block.  About W/(2m) blocks then
     have exactly the right total capacity at every depth.  What remains is a
     growing-uniformity multiscale matching/resolvable-design theorem, not
     merely a sharper estimate for the equal-occupancy nibble.  Full proofs
     and the direct-conflict obstruction are in `FIXED_DEPTH_SHADOWS.md`.

## 54. Rhombic strips are host geometry, not yet a width construction

221. A facet-Hamiltonian cycle of the permutahedron is a cylindrical rhombic
     strip through the Boolean lattice: it is a sequence of permutation flags
     related by adjacent transpositions, and every nontrivial subset is a
     prefix during one contiguous activity interval.  Thus it organizes
     compatible Gray cycles in every rank simultaneously.  This is closely
     aligned with the desired all-rank flag geometry, but adjacent
     transposition is not the last-occurrence dynamics of an OR array.  A
     singleton update is move-to-front; among adjacent swaps, only the swap in
     positions one and two has that form.

222. The canonical recursion in the facet-Hamiltonicity proof does not hide a
     near-width compression.  Group each recursive connector which moves the
     new element from back to front into one directed fan.  The number g_k of
     fans obeys

        g_1=0,  g_k=2g_(k-1)+1,

     so it yields exactly 2^(k-1) chain pieces.  Relative to Boolean width the
     ratio is asymptotic to sqrt(pi k/8), and the reversed recursive copies
     also orient inherited fans backwards.  This rules out the canonical
     grouping, not every possible global regrouping of the strip.

223. The strip's native facet-activity intervals also fail exact pinning.  For
     a coordinate b, the legal times against all active masks omitting b are
     exactly the permutation states beginning with b.  Hence pin survival
     would require every activity interval of S to contain a state beginning
     with every b in S.  In the published k=4 cycle, {1,3} is active only at
     3124 and 3142, so it has no legal pin for bit 1.

224. The precise positive bridge is a directed flag-compression lemma.  If a
     sequence of N permutation flags covers every subset as a prefix and every
     consecutive flag is obtained by one singleton move-to-front update, then

        nu(k)<=N+k-1.

     Initialize the first permutation in reverse order and use the requested
     singleton for each later update; the suffix-OR chain at each selected
     time is exactly that flag.  Therefore the sharp rhombic target is to
     select W+o(W) flags which hit all but o(W) facet intervals and whose
     successive pairs bound directed front fans.  This would be a genuine
     Theta(sqrt(k)) compression of the existing facet cycle.  The full audit,
     exact k=4 pin obstruction, and flag-compression proof are in
     `RHOMBIC_MTF.md`.

## 55. Exact local theorem for move-to-front chain transitions

225. The local state-fiber problem is now completely characterized.  Write a
     saturated chain C with minimum B, singleton increments e_1,...,e_h, and
     top complement Z.  An ordered partition exposes C exactly when it is

        [an ordered partition of B], e_1,...,e_h,
        [an ordered partition of Z].

     Thus a symmetric chain of minimum rank r has a(r)^2 exposing states,
     where a(r) is the ordered Bell number; treating B as one block discards
     most of the actual freedom.

226. Let D be a target chain with nonempty minimum A.  There is some exposing
     state of C and one move-to-front update leading to an exposing state of D
     if and only if the two quotient chains

        C-A  and  D-A

     are cross-nested, i.e. their union after duplicate suppression is one
     chain.  For an empty target minimum, anchor at its first singleton
     increment and use the analogous quotient.  Equivalently, the filtered
     source chain must pass through the target increment prefixes in order or
     already dominate the entire target increment set.  This quotient-chain
     theorem is an exact existential one-edge test.

227. Existential edges do not compose automatically.  A multi-element update
     coalesces its elements into one first block.  If the current first block
     is exactly the source minimum B and the next nontrivial target has minimum
     A, any valid next step obeys

        |B-A|<=1.

     In particular, a central m-set first block can only transition to the
     special symmetric chain with minimum B-{a} and first increment a.  This
     proves that a dense quotient graph, by itself, cannot yield an MTF tour:
     it has forgotten the refinement state needed by the next edge.

228. A correct weaker global target is a state-transversal path cover.  Any
     prescribed ordered-partition state with s blocks can be reset from an
     arbitrary state in exactly at most s updates, by requesting its blocks in
     reverse order.  Hence N chains divided into p genuine MTF state paths,
     with first-state block counts s_j and q uncovered masks, give

        nu(k)<=N-p+sum_j s_j+q.

     It is enough asymptotically to have pH+q=o(W), not one Hamilton path.
     The standard Greene--Kleitman last-pair transitions cannot do this: they
     leave W(k-1) path starts, and W(k-1) target templates also have no
     incoming dominance arc because their first star is coordinate 1 while no
     Greene--Kleitman minimum contains coordinate 1.  A successful recursion
     must therefore retain actual ordered-partition interface states or use a
     different chain cover.  Full proofs and the prefix-fence formula are in
     `MTF_TRANSVERSAL.md`.

## 56. Auxiliary rank-balanced decorated formulation

229. Use the full pair-flip cycle with all m exchange pairs, so each block has
     R=2m middle states.  Put

        W=binomial(2m,m),
        N_q=binomial(2m,m-q),
        rho_q=N_q/W.

     If one additionally insists that retained depth-q windows cover the
     rank-(m-q) layer essentially once, the average number of retained
     q-windows per block is forced to be

        c_q=R rho_q.

     This is the unique profile for that auxiliary exact-once decorated
     formulation.  It is not a physical quota in the OR problem: keeping a
     window costs no extra array position, and repeated colours are harmless
     provided every target occurs somewhere.

230. The exact total size of a fully balanced decorated block is

        r_bal=R(1+2 sum_(q=1)^m rho_q)
             =R 2^(2m)/W
             =(2 sqrt(pi)+o(1)) m^(3/2).

     There is an exact common fractional solution.  In the symmetric family
     of all parameterized blocks, retain each individual lower and upper
     q-slot independently with probability rho_q.  A middle vertex has degree
     d, a full q-colour has degree d/rho_q, and decoration multiplies the
     latter by rho_q.  Thus every vertex in every rank class has weighted
     degree exactly d.  The growing-depth obstruction is integral, not a
     density inconsistency.

231. A cyclic cut also has enough capacity without copying a long prefix.  For
     every 1<=q<m,

        R rho_q <= R-q.

     Indeed rho_q<=(m/(m+1))^q and
     1-rho_q>=q/(m+1+q)>=q/(2m).  Hence all designated q-windows can avoid the
     q starts destroyed by one cut.  For h=o(m), endpoint run padding over
     W/R blocks costs only O(hW/m)=o(W); h on the order of sqrt(m log m) also
     makes the literal outer tails o(W).

232. The auxiliary decorated theorem would separate into two integral stages:

        A. pack W/(2m)+o(W/m) full pair-flip blocks whose middle states are
           disjoint and cover all but o(W) middle sets;

        B. for every q<=h, solve simultaneous capacitated matchings from the
           rank-(m-q) and rank-(m+q) targets to the surviving (block,start)
           windows, with average capacity R rho_q per block.

     This is sufficient but stronger than necessary: without prescribed
     per-block quotas, Stage B reduces simply to union coverage of every
     shadow layer.  Also the unquotiented full-block hypergraph has codegree
     `D` on complementary middle pairs; after quotienting antipodal pairs its
     maximum relative codegree is `2/m^2`.  Standard fixed-uniformity
     Pippenger--Frankl--Rodl still cannot simply be quoted.  Section 57
     replaces the full blocks by sublinear partial blocks and records the
     weaker physical target.  The exact fractional capacity calculation,
     which remains useful as a collision ledger, is in
     `RANK_BALANCED_BLOCKS.md`; the correction is in
     `SHADOW_SLOT_HALL.md`.

## 57. Partial blocks remove the artificial tight-Hamilton obstruction

233. The full `2m` pair-flip block is stronger than the OR construction
     needs.  For any `ell<=m`, start from a middle set, choose ordered
     distinct departures `a_1,...,a_ell` and arrivals `b_1,...,b_ell`, flip
     `a_i` to `b_i` in order, and then flip `b_i` back to `a_i` in the same
     order.  The resulting cyclic block has `2ell` distinct middle states.
     Every transition window of depth `q<ell` is geodesic, its lower and
     upper colours have ranks `m-q` and `m+q`, and every nonconstant
     coordinate run has length exactly `ell`.

234. The parameterized partial-block hypergraph has exact degree

        D=2ell (m)_ell^2.

     If two middle sets have Johnson distance `q<ell`, their exact codegree
     ratio is

        lambda_q/D=2/binomial(m,q)^2;

     at `q=ell` the factor two disappears, and at greater distance the
     codegree is zero.  Hence, for `1<ell<m`,

        Delta_2/D=2/m^2.

     This is substantially sharper than the earlier coarse `O(1/m)` bound.
     At `ell=m`, complementary middle sets are forced twins and have
     codegree `D`; quotienting antipodal pairs removes that defect, but there
     is no reason to incur it in the first place.

235. Choose a desired shadow depth `h` and block length with

        h << ell << m.

     A near-factor into partial blocks uses `W/(2ell)+o(W/ell)` blocks, so
     copying or padding `O(h)` states at every seam costs only

        O(hW/ell)=o(W).

     For example `h=(1+epsilon)sqrt(m log m)` and `ell=m^(3/4)` work in the
     length ledger.  The block rank is `r=2ell`, while

        r Delta_2/D=o(1),  r^2 Delta_2/D=o(1).

     Fixed-rank Pippenger--Frankl--Rodl plus a rigorous diagonal argument
     already proves a rate-free version: there exist functions

        h->infinity,  h/ell->0,  ell/m->0

     and a partial-block matching leaving `u` middle masks with

        h u=o(W).

     Hence Stage A and all seam/run costs are unconditionally solved at some
     unspecified growing depth.  What remains open is the prescribed-scale
     version, in particular `h=Theta(sqrt(m log m))`.  Standard
     Pippenger--Spencer formulations fix `r`, but the exact local statistics
     are now on the natural random-greedy scale.  The detailed diagonal proof
     is in `MIDDLE_BLOCK_FACTOR.md`.

236. Terminology must be kept straight.  A full block is a tight Hamilton
     cycle of `K_(2m)^(m)`, since its states are the `2m` cyclic intervals of
     length `m` in an ordering of `[2m]`.  In the non-coprime case
     `gcd(2m,m)=m` it is not a Katona wreath under the standard wreath
     definition; the two notions coincide only in the coprime case.  Known
     approximate tight-Hamilton decomposition theorems fix uniformity before
     sending the vertex number to infinity and do not cover the diagonal
     regime `m=(2m)/2`.  Partial blocks bypass that unnecessarily strong open
     decomposition problem.

237. Stage B also simplifies conceptually.  The physical OR problem imposes
     no per-block quota: windows of different depths do not consume one
     another, and every window may be used.  For a selected block family the
     exact condition is simply that the total number of missing lower and
     upper colours, summed over all required depths, is `o(W)`; those masks
     can then be repaired literally.  An arbitrary random middle factor is
     insufficient--for `q=o(sqrt(m))` it misses a constant fraction of the
     q-th shadow layer--so the block selection must be a two-sided,
     multiscale shadow design.  Complete shallow shadows and progressively
     increasing collision slack as

        rho_q=binomial(2m,m-q)/W

     decays are the remaining global selection problem.  Exact proofs and
     the revised theorem ledger are in `PARTIAL_BLOCK_PACKING.md` and
     `SHADOW_SLOT_HALL.md`.

## 58. Explicit prescribed-depth factor via a linear code

238. Stage A is now completely explicit at the depth needed for literal-tail
     repair.  Let `ell=2^t`, put

        p_i=e_1+...+e_i  (0<=i<=ell),

     and let

        P_ell={p_i, 1+p_i:0<=i<ell}

     be the standard `2ell` pair-flip cycle in `F_2^ell`.  Enumerate the
     codimension-one subspace `U=F_2^t x {0}` as
     `u_0=0,...,u_(ell-1)`, take `v notin U`, and define a linear syndrome map

        phi(e_i)=u_i+u_(i-1) (i<ell),
        phi(e_ell)=v+u_(ell-1).

     Telescoping gives `phi(p_i)=u_i`, `phi(1+p_i)=v+u_i`; hence `phi` maps
     `P_ell` bijectively onto `F_2^(t+1)`.  Therefore `P_ell` is a complete
     transversal for `ker(phi)`, and its kernel translates partition
     `Q_ell`.  Cartesian fibers partition every `Q_s`, `s>=ell`, into the
     same isometric cycles.

239. Fixing a perfect matching of the original `2m` coordinates partitions
     the middle layer into orientation cubes `Q_s`, indexed by their full,
     empty, and split coordinate pairs.  Tile every stratum with `s>=ell` by
     paragraph 238.  The omitted low-split strata contain at most

        2^m sum_(s<ell) binomial(m,s).

     Choose a power of two with `m^(3/4)<=ell<2m^(3/4)` and take

        H=(1+epsilon)sqrt(m log m).

     The omission is `2^(-m+o(m))W=o(W/H)`, while prefix and seam padding
     costs `O(HW/ell)=o(W)`.  Thus there is an explicit middle row of length
     `W+o(W)` at the full prescribed depth `H`, containing every middle set,
     preserving every selected block shadow through `H`, and satisfying the
     delay-`H` run condition.  This removes the growing-rank nibble and the
     nonconstructive Gruslys threshold from Stage A.  The proof and remaining
     syndrome freedom are in `LINEAR_CYCLE_TILING.md`.

240. Relative to the fixed coordinate pairing, a rank `m-q` target is an
     intersection shadow of some `ell`-block if and only if it has at least
     `ell-q` split coordinate pairs; the union statement is dual.  This is
     only an individual representability test.  It does **not** imply that
     one fixed-pair factor has enough physical starts of every pair type to
     realize all targets simultaneously.  The exact type-capacity ledger in
     paragraph 249 below shows a sharp global obstruction at depths larger
     than `sqrt(m)`.  Thus the explicit factor solves Stage A, but Stage B
     must mix different coordinate pairings.

## 59. The multiscale law is the symmetric-chain radius law

241. Put `rho_q=binomial(2m,m-q)/W`.  Pure random-like shadow coverage is
     sufficient beyond

        q_*=(1+o(1))sqrt(m log log m):

     if a selected factor misses a fixed depth-q target with probability at
     most `exp(-c/rho_q)`, then the summed expected omissions from `q_*`
     through `H` are `o(W)`.  The inner band must still be deliberately
     resolved; a random factor misses a constant fraction when
     `q=o(sqrt(m))`.

242. There is an exact fractional solution for the inner band which uses
     whole certification depths rather than independent slots.  Define

        p_0=1-rho_1,
        p_d=rho_d-rho_(d+1) (1<=d<q_*),
        p_(q_*)=rho_(q_*).

     Give a block of type d all its middle states and both shadow rows through
     depth d, and weight type d by `p_d/D_M`.  Every middle and every
     certified shadow target then has weighted degree exactly one, because

        sum_d p_d=1,
        sum_(d>=q) p_d=rho_q.

     Rounding this typed fractional matching with total defect `o(W)`, while
     retaining Poisson-scale statistics in its uncertified deeper windows,
     would prove `nu(2m)=W+o(W)`.

243. The probabilities in paragraph 242 are canonical integers:

        W p_d=binomial(2m,m-d)-binomial(2m,m-d-1),

     exactly the number of radius-d chains in every symmetric chain
     decomposition.  A type-d block is the disjoint union, over its cyclic
     starts, of radius-d chain segments

        L_d<...<L_1<X<U_1<...<U_d.

     Thus integral rounding is equivalent to a wreath-resolved SCD: decompose
     the central band into symmetric chains with the forced radius counts and
     bundle equal-radius chains into partial pair-flip cycles.

244. This has an exact shift normal form.  For the chain centred at X, write
     its downward labels `r_0,r_1,...` and upward labels `u_0,u_1,...`, and
     define

        f(X)=X-{r_0(X)}+{u_0(X)}.

     Wreath resolution is equivalent to f being a radius-preserving
     permutation (outside the repair set) and satisfying

        r_i(fX)=r_(i+1)(X),
        u_i(fX)=u_(i+1)(X).

     Then `f^jX=X-{r_0,...,r_(j-1)}+{u_0,...,u_(j-1)}`, so all consecutive
     intersections and unions are automatically the SCD members.  The
     remaining all-rank theorem is therefore a de-Bruijn-type shift system on
     SCD flags, not an amorphous SAT or shadow-assignment problem.  Full
     proofs are in `PARTIAL_BLOCK_MULTISCALE.md`.

## 60. Two canonical shift candidates are now ruled out

245. The Greene--Kleitman SCD does not become shift-compatible after deleting
     a small exceptional family.  Project every middle word to the next
     middle word obtained by its canonical first lower/upper label swap.  If
     `W=binomial(2m,m)`, the exact indegree distribution is

        #{X:deg^-(X)=j}=binomial(2m-j-1,m-j),

     and hence

        #{X:deg^-(X)>=t}=binomial(2m-t,m-t).

     In particular exactly `W/2` vertices have positive indegree and
     asymptotically `W/4` branch.  A linear subforest contains at most `W/2`
     of the projection edges, so linearization requires replacing

        W/2-Catalan(m)=(1/2-o(1))W

     transitions.  Moreover every canonical projection edge lowers the SCD
     radius by one, whereas the required shift must preserve radius.  The
     Gregor--Micka--Mutze Hamilton cycle connects whole Greene--Kleitman
     chains at their extrema and does not alter either obstruction.  The full
     Dyck-factor proof is in `GK_PROJECTION_COUNTS.md`.

246. The explicit syndrome tiling from Section 58 also has an intrinsic
     higher-shadow ceiling.  Its syndrome map has redundancy

        r=log_2(2ell).

     For a fixed cyclic `q`-window of active coordinates, two kernel
     translates give the same lower flag whenever their difference lies in
     the kernel supported on that window.  For `q>r` every flag therefore has
     multiplicity at least `2^(q-r)`.  At `q=2r`, at most `2^(-r)W=o(W)`
     centres can carry distinct depth-q flags, whereas an SCD requires
     `(1-o(1))W`.  A finite-field ordering makes the factor face-simple
     through the sharp logarithmic range `q<=log_2 ell`, but no choice of the
     low-redundancy syndrome can turn it into the required deep SCD shift.
     This is proved in `CUBE_SHADOW_TILING.md` and
     `SHIFT_SCD_PRODUCT_AUDIT.md`.

## 61. What survives from the fixed-pair architecture

247. Fix an oriented split core `(S,eta)` for a perfect matching of the
     `2m` coordinates, and let `T` be the remaining pair indices.  One SCD of
     `B_T` simultaneously pairs every lower target indexed by

        F in binomial(T,(|T|-q)/2)

     with its unique same-chain upper target

        F^+ in binomial(T,(|T|+q)/2).

     The ordered difference `F^+-F` is exactly the required q-flip flag.
     Every prescribed perfect matching between the two middle levels of an
     odd residual cube extends to a full SCD.  Thus central edges may be
     designed globally first and completed vertically afterward.

248. At depth one this freedom is sufficient asymptotically.  A cloned
     four-uniform matching formulation has colour degrees

        2(m-s+2),

     middle-clone degrees `2s`, and pair codegree at most four on the typical
     split strata.  Almost-perfect conflict-free matching yields a
     two-sided-rainbow fixed-pair linear forest with `W-o(W)` edges and
     `o(W)` components.  Cutting it into the exact SCD radius-class sizes
     costs only `o(W)` further defects.  This is a genuine general theorem,
     not a finite-k search result; see `FIXED_PAIR_RESIDUAL_SCD.md`.

249. One fixed coordinate pairing nevertheless cannot reach the tail depth.
     Let `V_(f,q)` be the number of physical middle starts with `f` full,
     `f` empty, and `m-2f` split pairs, and let `T_(f,q)` be the number of
     rank-`m-q` targets forced to use source type f.  Then

        T_(f,q)/V_(f,q)
          =(m-2f)_(q)/(2^q (f+1)^(overline q)).

     At the saddle `f_*=(m-q)^2/(4m)`, the reciprocal capacity is

        V_(f_*,q)/T_(f_*,q)
          =exp(-(1+o(1))q^2/m).

     Consequently every factor confined to one coordinate matching misses
     `1-o(1)` of rank `m-q` once `q/sqrt(m)->infinity`.  This is deterministic:
     no retuning, coupling, or absorption inside that factor can repair it.

250. The obstruction belongs to the pairing, not to the target.  For every
     central-band target there is a polynomial-size reservoir of perfect
     coordinate matchings in which at least one matching gives it favourable
     type capacity.  The next viable theorem is therefore:

     > choose disjoint algebraic blocks from a polynomial reservoir of
     > fixed-pair factors, cover all but `o(W)` middle masks, and route every
     > shadow target through a factor in which its type is favourable.

     Sparse prescribed-face absorbers already exist inside each factor.  The
     unresolved step is the mixed-factor rounding, not further optimization
     of a single cube tiling.  Exact formulae and the reservoir proof are in
     `CUBE_SHADOW_TILING.md`.

## 62. A cleaner global object: cyclic-interval SCD resolution

251. There is a second, more conceptual formulation in odd dimension which
     avoids committing to coordinate pairs.  Put `n=2m+1` and

        W=binomial(n,m),  B=W/n=Catalan(m).

     For a cyclic order `pi=(x_0,...,x_(n-1))`, write

        I_pi(j,r)={x_j,x_(j+1),...,x_(j+r-1)}

     with cyclic indices.  A **cyclic-interval SCD resolution** is a family
     of B cyclic orders together with thresholds `a_(pi,j)<=m` such that the
     `W` chains

        C_(pi,j)=(I_pi(j,r): a_(pi,j)<=r<=n-a_(pi,j))

     partition the Boolean lattice.  Each is a saturated symmetric chain.
     At rank m the construction is necessarily a decomposition of all
     m-sets into tight cyclic wreaths, so this object is a strengthened,
     vertically resolved form of the Baranyai--Katona wreath conjecture.

252. Such a resolution would immediately give the conjecturally correct
     asymptotic constant one.  Choose

        H>(1/2+epsilon)sqrt(n log n),  H=o(n),

     and for every cyclic order output the erosion word

        E_(pi,j)=I_pi(j,m-H),  0<=j<n,

     followed by its first `2H+1` entries.  Consecutive unions satisfy

        E_(pi,j) union ... union E_(pi,j+r)=I_pi(j,m-H+r)

     for `0<=r<=2H+1`.  Every mask in ranks

        m-H,...,m,m+1,...,m+1+H

     lies in one of the resolved chains and is therefore represented.  Append
     the masks outside this band literally.  The exact nonzero length is at
     most

        W +(2H+1)W/n
          +2 sum_(r=0)^(m-H-1) binomial(n,r)-1
        =W+o(W).

     The odd-to-even lift doubles both this length and the next even width,
     so the same conclusion holds in even dimensions.  Therefore a
     cyclic-interval SCD resolution proves

        nu(k)=(1+o(1))binomial(k,floor(k/2)).

253. The formulation also explains why local central paths felt productive
     but never closed the problem.  They build isolated fragments of the
     cyclic interval resolution.  The missing theorem is global: bundle an
     SCD's forced radius distribution into cyclic move-to-front blocks.  An
     approximate version--discarding and repairing `o(W)` chains--already
     suffices asymptotically and may be substantially easier than the exact
     wreath conjecture.

## 63. Revised research priority

254. Finite `k=11,13,14` defect chasing is frozen.  It can certify isolated
     values but cannot explain the sequence.  The priority order is now:

     1. construct an MTF--SCD state-path cover with reset cost `o(W)`; the
        mixed-coordinate theorem of paragraph 250 and the approximate
        cyclic-interval resolution of paragraph 251 are two structured
        sufficient subproblems;
     2. obtain `nu(k)=W(k)+o(W(k))` and only then optimize the seam/repair
        ledger toward the rank-slack value `B(k)`;
     3. specialize the general mechanism to `k<20`, using computation only
        to certify the finitely many boundary cases.

     This is the correct big-picture bottleneck.  More local repair of one
     fourteen-bit path is no longer part of the active programme.

## 64. Outer tails have a width-order construction

255. Literal tail repair was unnecessarily expensive.  Split `2m` bits into
     two m-bit halves, take SCDs of both half-cubes, and schedule a
     suffix--prefix gadget for every pair of chains whose minimum ranks a,b
     satisfy

        a+b<=r.

     The gadget `reverse(increments(C)) || increments(D)` covers `C x D`.
     Symmetry of the chain endpoints implies that the resulting word covers
     both

        |S|<=r  and  |S|>=2m-r.

     Its exact length is

        2 sum_a N_m(a) w_m(a) C_m(r-a),

     where `N_m(a)=binomial(m,a)-binomial(m,a-1)`,
     `w_m(0)=m`, `w_m(a)=m-2a+1` for `a>0`, and `C_m(t)` is the number of
     half-cube chains with minimum at most t.  The Euler/complement-dual
     version in `TRUNCATED_TAIL_CONSTRUCTION.md` is a slightly longer
     alternative.

256. Take `r=m-h`, `h=c sqrt(m)`, with `c->infinity` arbitrarily slowly and
     `c=o(m^(1/6))`.  Vandermonde's identity and a hypergeometric variance
     calculation give

        L(m,m-h)
          =O((1+c^2)binomial(2m,m-h)
             +c exp(-2c^2)binomial(2m,m))
          =o(W).

     Thus the central construction no longer needs to reach literal-tail
     depth `Theta(sqrt(m log m))`; it only needs

        H=sqrt(m) omega(1).

     This is still beyond every single fixed-pair factor by paragraph 249,
     so mixed coordinate pairings remain essential, but the demanded depth
     is now substantially smaller.  The full construction and estimate are
     in `TRUNCATED_IDEAL_PRODUCT.md`.

## 65. Representation theory explains the radius law but not the shift

257. RSK gives an exact explanation of the radius law.  Balanced binary
     words decompose as

        binomial([2m],m)
          = disjoint_union_(d=0)^m SYT(m+d,m-d),

     and the size of the d-th shape is exactly

        binomial(2m,m-d)-binomial(2m,m-d-1).

     Thus a middle mask together with its SCD radius is equivalently a
     two-row standard Young tableau.

258. Standard global tableau operators do not supply the desired shift.
     The canonical crystal/Greene--Kleitman swap always changes radius
     `d->d-1`; evacuation is reverse-complement and has Hamming distance
     divisible by four; promotion can change `2m-2` coordinates; and an
     involution cannot satisfy a depth-two shift recurrence.  These are
     structural obstructions, not failed examples.

259. Elementary Bender--Knuth moves leave a more limited residue.  Pair the
     labels `(1,2),(3,4),...` and use the commuting odd generators.  For a
     tableau Q, let `s(Q)` be the number of label pairs occupying
     incomparable boxes.  Its orbit is an exact `s(Q)`-cube, lies entirely
     in one RSK radius class, and every nontrivial cube edge maps the middle
     word to some Johnson neighbour.  The low-dimensional orbits satisfy

        #{Q:s(Q)<ell}
          <=sum_(s<ell) binomial(m,s)2^s3^(m-s)
          =exp((log 3+o(1))m)=o(W)

     for every `ell=o(m)`.  However, inverse RSK does **not** make
     `tau_i` swap the word coordinates `i,i+1`; inverse bumping can move a
     nonlocal pair.  Hence these are abstract tableau cubes, not the
     coordinate-pair cubes required by `LINEAR_CYCLE_TILING.md`, and no
     locally geodesic middle skeleton follows.  The surviving result is the
     exact radius-pure host decomposition and its counting bound.  Complete
     corrected proofs are in `TABLEAU_CRYSTAL_AUDIT.md`.

260. The exact MTF audit closes this particular bridge negatively.  If
     `Q' = tau_i Q` is a nontrivial Bender--Knuth edge, the two canonical
     crystal chains have one of only two flag relations: either their
     minima and top complements swap one coordinate while the increment
     words agree, or one coordinate rotates through

        minimum -> one increment position -> top complement.

     For every positive radius `d`, the chain length is `2d>=2`.  In both
     flag relations, the quotient chains from the exact one-step MTF
     criterion contain crossing singleton or two-element prefixes.  Hence
     there is no MTF transition in either direction between the two chains,
     even after allowing every exposing ordered-partition state in both
     fibers.  Thus every positive-radius Bender--Knuth cube cycle splits into
     singleton MTF components; only the `Cat_m=o(W)` radius-zero chains can
     be threaded freely.

     Replacing the canonical chains by the natural chains of a locally
     geodesic middle cycle does not help.  If

        X_(t+1)=X_t-a_t+b_t,

     the radius-d window chain at t has increment word

        a_(t+d-1),...,a_t,b_t,...,b_(t+d-1).

     After anchoring at the next minimum, the two quotient chains agree
     through the departures `a_(t+d),...,a_(t+1)` and then cross: the old
     chain adds the obsolete departure `a_t`, while the new chain adds
     `b_(t+1)`.  The reverse direction crosses at its first singleton.
     Therefore this second natural assignment also has component length one,
     not `>>sqrt(m)`.  Resetting the positive-radius chains separately costs
     `Theta(W sqrt(m))`, because the mean SCD radius is `Theta(sqrt(m))`.
     Full proofs are in `BK_MTF_AUDIT.md`.

## 66. The weakest sufficient global theorem is an MTF--SCD path cover

261. The central-row shift condition is sufficient but not necessary.  The
     intrinsic state of an OR prefix is an ordered partition Pi of the
     coordinates by last-occurrence time.  Its suffix ORs are the prefix
     unions of Pi, and appending a mask X performs exactly

        Pi -> M_X(Pi)=(X,B_1-X,B_2-X,...),

     after empty blocks are deleted.

262. If the chains of an SCD can be assigned to genuine MTF state paths, one
     state per chain, then no separate shadow theorem is needed: each state
     exposes its whole assigned chain.  If there are p path components,
     their prescribed initial states have at most H blocks, and q Boolean
     masks are left uncovered, the exact reset lemma gives

        nu(k)<=W+(H-1)p+q.

     Therefore `(H-1)p+q=o(W)` already proves constant one.  A Hamilton tour
     would give the stronger bound `nu(k)<=W+k-1`, but is unnecessary.

263. This places the current constructions in the correct hierarchy.

     * A cyclic-interval SCD resolution is an especially rigid MTF--SCD
       cover using singleton rotations; it inherits the wreath conjecture.
     * A fixed central derivative row is another rigid realization, forcing
       consecutive flag shifts.
     * The general MTF--SCD path cover permits arbitrary tied update blocks
       and is strictly weaker than both.

     A radius-pure host cycle of length `ell>>sqrt(m)` would make the typical
     reset ledger `O(W sqrt(m)/ell)=o(W)`, but paragraphs 259--260 show that
     neither abstract Bender--Knuth cycles nor their two natural chain flags
     supply even a two-chain MTF component at positive radius.  The sharp
     local-to-global question is therefore to construct long radius-pure
     paths directly in the exact MTF state-fiber graph, rather than infer
     them from tableau adjacency.
     The exact state-fiber and one-step quotient criteria are in
     `GLOBAL_MTF_SCD_HANDOFF.md` and `MTF_TRANSVERSAL.md`.

## 67. Mixed pairings have the correct fractional geometry

264. For a fixed coordinate matching and source pair type f, the normalized
     number of depth-q occurrences of a target is exactly

        lambda_(f,q)
          =2^q (f+q)_(q)/(m-2f)_(q).

     If `pi_q(f)` is the type distribution in rank `m-q`, then the exact
     size-bias identity is

        pi_q(f) lambda_(f,q)=rho_q^(-1) pi_0(f).

     Thus averaging over coordinate matchings cancels the type bias exactly.
     After truncating to `f=m/4+O(sqrt(m log m))`, a polynomial family of
     random coordinate matchings simultaneously supports an
     `m^(-a)`-approximate typed fractional perfect matching in every fixed
     central band.  The weighted pair codegree is at most
     `2/(m-H)+o(1)`.

265. This is a genuine advance over the favourable-type reservoir: the
     fractional all-rank solution now exists globally.  It does not yet
     round integrally.  The average typed block contains
     `Theta(ell sqrt(m))` certified chain atoms, so fixed-uniformity matching
     theorems give no diagonal estimate.  Degree and pair-codegree alone
     cannot suffice for growing edges (finite projective planes are the
     standard warning), and the quantitative conflict-free error becomes
     `1-o(1)` at this rank.  The correct next step is to atomize an SCD first
     and bundle its chain atoms afterward.  Proofs are in
     `MIXED_PAIR_ROUNDING.md`.

266. Section 64 removes the former outer-shadow bookkeeping entirely.  Take

        H=sqrt(m omega(m)),  omega(m)->infinity slowly,

     certify every rank in the central band by the exact SCD-radius law, and
     append the truncated chain-product word for both outer tails.  No Poisson-like
     tracking beyond H is now required.  The only remaining asymptotic
     theorem is integral rounding of the central-band chain atoms with total
     defect `o(W)`.

## 68. Odd graphs, Dyck heights, and the cyclic route

267. The middle-only cyclic problem is already solved exactly.  Mütze,
     Standke and Wiechert proved that, for every `m`, the odd graph

        O_(2m+1)=KG(2m+1,m)

     has a spanning `C_(2m+1)`-factor consisting of exactly `Catalan(m)`
     cycles.  Every such minimum odd cycle is a wreath.  Indeed, label each
     edge `A_i A_(i+1)` by the unique omitted coordinate

        z_i=[2m+1]-(A_i union A_(i+1)).

     For a fixed coordinate z, membership toggles on every edge not labelled
     z.  If `t_z` edges have label z, closure around the odd cycle gives
     `2m+1-t_z` even, so every `t_z` is odd.  Since the `t_z` sum to `2m+1`,
     each equals one.  The omitted labels are therefore a permutation and

        A_i={z_(i+1),z_(i+3),...,z_(i+2m-1)}.

     Multiplication by two modulo `2m+1` turns these into all length-m cyclic
     intervals of one coordinate order.  Thus the former proposed task of
     packing `W-o(W)` minimum odd cycles is obsolete: the literature gives a
     partition of all W middle masks.

268. The vertical radius counts have an exact Dyck-path model.  If
     `D_m` is the family of Dyck paths of semilength m and `h_P(j)` is the
     height at a pointed vertex, then

        #{(P,j):h_P(j)=d}
          =binomial(2m+1,m-d)-binomial(2m+1,m-d-1).

     A bijective proof cuts the pointed Dyck path, inserts one up-step, and
     reverses/complements the suffix to obtain a ballot path of length
     `2m+1` ending at height `2d+1`.  The right side is exactly the number of
     radius-d chains in an SCD.  Therefore the Petr--Turek idea of attaching
     one cyclic permutation to each Dyck path automatically has the correct
     radius multiset when the radius at a cut is its height.  What remains is
     the vertical statement that these selected fixed-start intervals cover
     every noncentral rank.  Full calculations are in
     `CYCLIC_INTERVAL_SCD_HYPERGRAPH.md`.

269. The explicit MSW factor does not supply that vertical statement.  Let
     `pi(x)` be its length-`2m` flip-position permutation for a Dyck path x
     and put

        q(x)=(pi(x),infinity).

     The rank-`m-1` interval at cut i is exactly

        L_i(x)={q_(i+1),q_(i+3),...,q_(i+2m-3)},

     with cyclic indices; the corresponding rank-`m+2` interval is its
     complement.  For `m=4`, the fourteen MSW cycles miss the four rank-three
     sets

        {1,4,7}, {2,5,8}, {2,5,9}, {4,7,9},

     and hence also their four rank-six complements.  Their complete
     multiplicity distribution is

        #{S: multiplicity(S)=0,1,2,3}=(4,35,44,1).

     Therefore the MSW factor is an exact middle skeleton, not an automatic
     cyclic-interval SCD.  The formula above is an exact collision test, and
     deeper shadows are obtained by shortening the same alternating subword.

270. Choosing one distinguished coordinate gives a useful normal form for
     every wreath factor.  Each wreath becomes a Johnson path

        X_0,X_1,...,X_m  in binomial([2m],m),
        X_m=[2m]-X_0,

     with edge-unions `Y_i=X_i union X_(i+1)`.  Across all Catalan(m) paths,
     the X-vertices partition rank m and the Y-values partition rank `m+1`
     of `B_(2m)`.  Conversely any such complementary path factor reconstructs
     the wreath factor.  Its first lower-shadow colors are precisely

        X_i intersection X_(i+1),
        [2m]-Y_0, [2m]-Y_(m-1),
        {infinity} union ([2m]-(Y_(i-1) union Y_i)).

     The next cyclic-route problem is consequently a two-sided rainbow
     complementary Johnson path factor, followed by its deeper-shadow
     analogue.  This is much sharper than cycle packing and keeps the exact
     middle solution.  Complete proofs, the `m=4` certificate, the general
     collision formula, and a remote-audited constructor are in
     `ODD_GRAPH_EXACT_WREATH_FACTOR.md` and `msw_shadow_audit.cpp`.

## 69. Random vertical shadows and the exact conditioning barrier

271. There is now an exact probabilistic benchmark for the outer part of the
     central band.  Put `n=2m+1`, `W=binomial(n,m)`,
     `N_q=binomial(n,m-q)`, and `mu_q=W/N_q`.  For `W/n` independent uniform
     wreaths, a fixed depth-q target is missed with probability

        exp(-mu_q+o(1)).

     More strongly, if `M_q` is the number missed, then uniformly while
     `mu_q=o(m^2)`,

        Var(M_q)/E(M_q)^2 <= 1/E(M_q)+O(mu_q/m^2).

     The proof is exact: conditioned on one rank-`m-q` set S being a cyclic
     interval, a distinct T with `c=|S intersection T|` is also an interval
     with probability

        (2q+2)/binomial(m+q+1,m-q),                c=0,
        2/[binomial(m-q,c) binomial(m+q+1,m-q-c)], 0<c<m-q.

     The maximum is `(2+o(1))/m^2`, which gives the second moment.

272. The ideal model has two different thresholds.  Literal coverage of
     every target in one rank occurs only at

        q^2/m=log m+log log 4+o(1).

     But the total number of omissions over all depths q at least q_* is
     `o(W)` already at

        q_*^2/m=log log m-log 2+o(1).

     In the finer occurrence-mean scale, the one-sided transition is

        mu_c=.5 log m-2 log log m-.5 log log log m+log 2+o(1);

     for both complementary sides the last constant is `2 log 2`.  Hence a
     Poisson-like outer stage would substantially reduce the range requiring
     structured resolution, but it cannot give literal complete coverage.

273. Conditioning on an exact middle factor is the genuine missing theorem.
     For the uniform exact wreath-factor distribution,

        Pr(target S is missed)
          =PM(H_m-H_m(S,q))/PM(H_m).

     The desired estimate is that this ratio is at most
     `exp(-(1-o(1))mu_q)`.  Exactness, coordinate symmetry, and the correct
     mean multiplicity do not imply it.  A uniformly relabelled exact
     fixed-coordinate-pair partition has mean `(1-o(1))mu_q` but, for
     `q/sqrt(m)->infinity`, misses a fixed target with probability `1-o(1)`.
     Its multiplicity is carried by a rare favourable-type tail.

274. A precise switching target is available.  Let `F_j(S,q)` be the exact
     factors in which S occurs j times.  If forward/reverse factor trades
     satisfy

        A_j/B_(j+1) >= (1-o(1)) mu_q/(j+1)

     through `j=(1+o(1))mu_q`, then double counting gives the required
     exponential miss bound.  Constant-size trades are not automatic.  The
     wreath-interaction multigraph is exactly `(2m+1)(m-1)`-regular, and the
     support of every nontrivial wreath replacement must contain a cycle.
     Mesoscopic trades, or trades after cutting wreaths into long geodesic
     paths, may be necessary.

275. Quadratic collision energy must not be used across the whole central
     band.  If W slots are placed in N targets, write `W=aN+b`; the least
     possible pair-collision count is

        N binomial(a,2)+ab.

     Its excess over `W-N` is

        N(a-1)(a-2)/2+b(a-1),

     which is asymptotic to `W(W/N)/2` when `W/N` diverges.  Thus the former
     proposed all-depth condition `sum(C_q-(W-N_q))=o(W)` is impossible.
     The correct exact energy is

        D_q=sum_S (multiplicity(S)-1)_+,
        D_q-(W-N_q)=M_q.

     Consequently q=1 and all shallow depths must be deliberately
     near-rainbow, while an exact-factor switching theorem is useful only in
     the outer range `q>=q_*`.  Complete proofs are in
     `RANDOM_VERTICAL_FACTOR.md`; `MSW_ATOM_FLOW.md` has been corrected to use
     the linear rather than quadratic all-depth objective.

## 70. Fixed-depth shadows do not bootstrap by ordinary products

276. There is an endpoint-capacity obstruction to concatenating independently
     certified depth-J stages.  If witnesses are internal to modules and a
     module is responsible for at most `2J+1` ranks, one endpoint supplies at
     most one mask in each of those ranks.  Covering the ranks

        m-c sqrt(m),...,m+c sqrt(m)

     therefore forces total module length

        Omega_c(W sqrt(m)/(J+1)).

     Thus `J=o(sqrt(m))` stages cannot be appended at near-width cost.  The
     same endpoints must be reused across a growing number of depths.

277. Literal coordinate-block tensors have an independent entropy barrier.
     Partition `2st` coordinates into `t` blocks of size `2s`, and suppose a
     local gadget handles only restrictions of ranks `s-J,...,s+J`.  If

        p_(s,J)=2^(-2s) sum_(|u|<=J) binomial(2s,s+u),

     then the fraction of global middle sets eligible in every block is at
     most

        O(sqrt(st)) p_(s,J)^t.

     Uniformly for `t>=2`, eligibility in even the first block has fraction
     `O((J+1)/sqrt(s))`.  Hence a fixed local band cannot be tensor-powered
     until its formal additive depth exceeds the global square-root scale:
     almost every global target has an off-band local restriction.

278. The full-SCD Cartesian product has an exact, stronger obstruction.  Let
     factor chains C,D have radii a,b and write

        C_(-a)<...<C_a,  D_(-b)<...<D_b.

     Their global middle members form the diagonal Johnson path

        T_i=C_i union D_(-i),  |i|<=r=min(a,b).

     All internal consecutive intersections and unions of this path are
     exactly the central square

        {C_u union D_v: |u|,|v|<=r}.

     Thus its chain rectangle has exactly

        2(2 min(a,b)+1)|a-b|

     unresolved cells.  Since factor SCD rectangles partition the Boolean
     lattice, no internal window from a different rectangle can supply those
     cells.

279. If

        v_a=binomial(2s,s-a)-binomial(2s,s-a-1)

     is the forced number of radius-a chains in `B_(2s)`, the exact total
     Cartesian deficit in `B_(4s)` is

        E_s=2 sum_(a,b) v_a v_b (2 min(a,b)+1)|a-b|.

     The chain radius containing a uniform factor subset, divided by
     `sqrt(s)`, converges to density

        4x^2 exp(-x^2)/sqrt(pi).

     Consequently `E_s=Theta(2^(4s))=Theta(W_(4s)sqrt(s))`, and a constant
     fraction of this deficit already lies in a `C sqrt(s)` central band.
     Even granting every rectangle a free `J=o(sqrt(s))` halo leaves the
     same order of deficit.

     There are `binomial(2s,s)^2=(sqrt(2/pi)+o(1))W_(4s)/sqrt(s)` diagonal
     rectangles.  Padding each by depth `d=sqrt(s omega(s))` would itself
     cost `Theta(sqrt(omega)W)`.  Hence the rectangles must also be spliced
     into components whose average length is `omega(d)`.

280. The surviving product target is therefore not another tensor estimate.
     It is a **non-Cartesian radius-transfer braid** which must simultaneously:

     * route the Clebsch--Gordan residual radius `|a-b|` across different
       chain rectangles;
     * make the cross-rectangle windows partition the residual rectangle
       tails;
     * reuse essentially the same W endpoints through
       `sqrt(m) omega(1)` depths; and
     * have only `o(W/d)` physical components, so reset cost is `o(W)`.

     Proving such a braid would be a genuinely new growing-depth theorem.
     It does not follow formally from the current fixed-J block matching.
     Complete statements and proofs are in
     `FIXED_DEPTH_BOOTSTRAP_OBSTRUCTIONS.md`.

## 71. Cyclic-quotient SCDs lift, but their rotation bundles do not MTF-thread

281. The Hersh--Schilling SCD of the necklace quotient `B_n/C_n` does give a
     near-complete ordinary chain cover after lifting.  There are at most

        n 2^(n/2)=o(W(n))

     periodic binary words.  Delete every quotient chain meeting one of
     them.  In each remaining quotient chain choose nested representatives;
     its `n` simultaneous coordinate rotations are then pairwise-disjoint
     saturated symmetric chains.  Altogether this gives `W-o(W)` ordinary
     chains and misses only `o(W)` masks.  Thus stabilizers and periodic
     necklaces are not the obstruction.

282. Exact MTF composition imposes a new three-minimum condition.  Let three
     nontrivial saturated chains of the same minimum rank have distinct
     minima `B_0,B_1,B_2`, and suppose exposing states for them occur in this
     order under two genuine one-step MTF updates.  If the first update set
     is `X`, comparison of the source and target minima in the residual
     prefix chain forces

        B_1-B_0 subseteq X.

     The block `X` is tied at the front of the middle state.  On the next
     update, all but at most one element of `X` must lie in `B_2`; otherwise
     the tied residue either contaminates the new minimum or cannot be its
     first singleton increment.  Hence necessarily

        |B_1-(B_0 union B_2)| <= 1.                 (71.1)

     This is state-independent: it allows every exposing state and arbitrary
     nonempty update masks, not only singleton or full-minimum updates.

283. Literal rotation orbits fail (71.1) exponentially often.  For distinct
     nonzero shifts `a,b`, the number of sets satisfying

        |B-(sigma^a B union sigma^b B)| <= 1

     is at most

        2^n(1+n/7)(7/8)^(n/27).

     Indeed, from the triples `{i,i-a,i-b}` one greedily selects at least
     `n/27` disjoint triples.  On each, the uncovered pattern `100` is one of
     eight assignments, and globally it may occur at most once.  Summing over
     fewer than `n^2` ordered shift pairs still gives `o(W)` exceptional
     sets.

284. Consequently, in any state-path cover which stays inside each lifted
     quotient chain's rotation bundle, every nonexceptional rotated chain can
     only be a path endpoint.  Such a cover has at least

        (1/2-o(1))W

     components.  Since every nontrivial component start needs at least two
     ordered-partition blocks, the reset excess is `Omega(W)`.  Thus the
     literal plan

        quotient chain -> lift all coordinate rotations -> MTF-thread them

     cannot prove constant one.  The six-coordinate Hersh--Schilling chain

        [100100] < [110100] < [110110]

     is a small explicit witness: its three rotated minima are `{1,4}`,
     `{2,5}`, `{3,6}`, so no ordering of all three can be one MTF state path.

285. This does **not** rule out cross-bundle transitions.  One may still use
     necklace chains merely as an index set and connect a state over one
     quotient chain to a state over a different quotient chain, choosing new
     ground-set orders rather than literal coordinate rotations.  That
     possibility is untested, not disproved, and it is no longer supplied by
     the cyclic-quotient theorem itself.  Any such construction must arrange
     almost all successive minima to satisfy (71.1).  Full proofs are in
     `CYCLIC_QUOTIENT_MTF_AUDIT.md`.

## 72. The wreath-matrix kernel has exact rank selectors, but only signed ones

286. Petr--Turek's wreath matrix admits a useful vertical reinterpretation.
     Let `Omega` be the unoriented cyclic orders of `[n]`, `n=2m+1`, and for
     every rank r let

        (B_r x)_S=sum_C x_C 1{S is a cyclic r-interval of C}.

     Since a middle wreath determines its cyclic order, their matrix is

        M=B_m^T B_m.

     If x is an exact middle factor, then `B_m x=1` and
     `x^T M x=W` is constant.  Hence the positive spectrum computed in *The
     wreath matrix* cannot distinguish vertically good and bad factors: the
     difference of every two exact factors lies in `ker M`.  The exact
     rank-r duplicate energy is instead

        E_r(x)=||B_r x-mu_r 1||_2^2,
        mu_r=W/binomial(n,r),

     and is encoded by the extended Gram operator `K_r=B_r^T B_r`.

287. Their four-wreath kernel vector is an exact **rank selector**.  In the
     cyclic order `C=(1,2,...,n)`, fix `2<=a<=m`, put

        tau=(1 2),  sigma=(a+1 a+2),
        z_a=e_C-e_(tau C)-e_(sigma C)+e_(tau sigma C).

     Then

        B_r z_a=0                         for 1<=r<=m, r!=a,

     while, with `K={3,...,a}`,

        B_a z_a=
          e_(K union {2,a+1})-e_(K union {1,a+1})
         -e_(K union {2,a+2})+e_(K union {1,a+2}).       (72.1)

     The proof is the two-boundary geometry of a cyclic interval.  Unless a
     target contains exactly one element of each swapped adjacent pair, the
     four signs cancel.  If it does, its two boundary cuts are those pairs,
     so its length is a or n-a.  Formula (72.1) follows by listing the four
     endpoint choices.  Thus `z_a in ker B_m` for `a<m`, and it changes only
     the complementary rank pair `a,n-a`.

288. Relabelings of (72.1) span every real rank-a discrepancy with zero point
     marginals.  More precisely, if `A_a` is the point-versus-a-set incidence
     matrix, then `ker A_a` is spanned by the elementary squares

        e_(Kxy)-e_(Kx'y)-e_(Kxy')+e_(Kx'y').            (72.2)

     One proof takes an f orthogonal to all squares.  The difference
     `f(R union {x})-f(R union {y})` is unchanged when the `(a-1)`-set R
     moves along its Johnson graph, hence equals `c_x-c_y`; therefore
     `f(S)=constant+sum_(i in S)c_i`, the row space of `A_a`.

     Every weighted collection of b cyclic orders has point marginal `ab`
     at rank a.  For an exact factor `b=W/n`, and the constant vector
     `mu_a 1` has the same marginal.  Therefore

        B_a x-mu_a 1 in ker A_a.                         (72.3)

289. Combining (72.1)--(72.3) gives an exact simultaneous real-balancing
     theorem:

     > For every exact middle wreath factor x there is a real signed vector
     > `z in ker B_m`, which is a linear combination of relabeled
     > `z_2,...,z_(m-1)`, such that
     >
     >    `B_a(x+z)=mu_a 1` for every `1<=a<m`,
     >
     > while `B_m(x+z)=1`; complementary upper ranks are balanced too.

     Equivalently, the map

        ker B_m -> direct_sum_(a=2)^(m-1) ker A_a,
        z |-> (B_2z,...,B_(m-1)z)

     is surjective and has an explicit rank-by-rank right inverse.  Thus
     there is no real-linear or representation-theoretic obstruction to
     simultaneous perfect vertical marginals.  This is nevertheless only a
     signed/fractional theorem: the coefficients of `x+z` need not lie in
     `[0,1]`, the means mu_a are usually nonintegral, and the unpointed
     matrices forget nested start choices.

290. The smallest selectors are not even individual moves of the exact-cover
     polytope.  An adjacent swap changes exactly two middle intervals.  Each
     diagonal pair

        {C,tau sigma C},  {tau C,sigma C}

     in `z_a` therefore shares at least `n-4>0` middle sets.  Neither pair can
     coexist in an exact factor, so a single four-wreath relation is **never**
     a legal two-for-two switch.  The precise integral successor is:

     > Combine many relabeled rank-a selectors into a circuit z whose
     > positive and negative wreath supports are separately disjoint, with
     > the negative support inside the current factor and `x+z` again 0/1;
     > require its rank-a action to reduce the number of missing targets by
     > a definite fraction.  Do this for `a=m-q` through the required band.

     Rank marginals would not regress because the signed generators are
     rank-local.  What remains wholly unproved is the cancellation into such
     disjoint-support circuits, followed by the nested-start matching.  This
     is the exact point where the spectral relaxation meets integrality.

291. The stronger Petr--Turek Dyck labeling conjectures do not supply that
     nesting automatically.  Already for `m=2`, the two pointed Dyck height
     profiles demand `3+2` active starts at depth one.  Any decomposition of
     `binomial([5],2)` into wreaths is a pair of complementary Hamilton
     5-cycles.  Their current-to-predecessor permutation matchings form one
     alternating 10-cycle, whose only perfect matchings use `5+0` or `0+5`
