     starts.  Hence no assignment of the two height multisets works, for any
     compatible middle factor.  The Dyck identity solves the global radius
     ledger, not its placement among wreaths.  Complete proofs and the
     representation-theoretic audit are in
     `WREATH_MATRIX_VERTICAL_AUDIT.md`.

## 73. Cool-lex does not MTF-thread Greene--Kleitman fibers

292. A second natural constant-one route is now ruled out sharply.  Identify
     the middle layer of `B_(2m)` with balanced binary words, give each word
     its Greene--Kleitman/BTK chain, and order the words cyclically by
     cool-lex.  For a chain with bottom `B`, ordered singleton increments

        e_1,...,e_(2d),

     and top complement `Z`, every maximal singleton flag exposing it is

        (a permutation of B), e_1,...,e_(2d),
        (a permutation of Z).

     Hence arbitrary permutations of the bottom and top blocks do not change
     the central queue discipline: if `d>0`, a singleton move-to-front step
     can drop from the middle set only `e_d`.  More precisely, two maximal
     flags are adjacent exactly when deleting the moved symbol from their
     permutation words gives the same ordered word.

293. Allowing ties and arbitrary-mask moves does not remove the obstruction.
     The full exposing fiber consists of arbitrary ordered partitions of the
     bottom and top blocks, with the `e_i` still appearing as singleton
     blocks in their fixed order.  The exact quotient-chain criterion says
     that a transition into a target chain

        A < A+f_1 < ... < A+f_1+...+f_t

     exists from some source exposing state iff, after quotienting by `A`,
     every source-chain member is either a prefix

        F_j={f_1,...,f_j}

     or contains the full star set `F_t`.  This is the strongest existential
     test over **all** tied bottom/top fibers, not merely the canonical BTK
     flags.

294. For `m>=2`, a directed cool-lex successor edge passes that strongest
     test iff its **target** Greene--Kleitman chain has radius zero.  The proof
     is local.  Away from two boundary words a cool-lex move has the form

        1^a 0^b 1 epsilon v  ->  epsilon 1^a 0^b 1 v.

     If the target radius is positive, the source middle set contains a
     paired target coordinate while either omitting a preceding target star
     or omitting the full upper-star tail.  It therefore violates the prefix
     fence already as one source-chain member.  The two boundary rotations
     fail by the same paired-coordinate test.  A radius-zero target is a
     singleton quotient chain and is automatically compatible.

295. Consequently the cyclic cool-lex order has exactly

        Cat_m = binomial(2m,m)/(m+1)

     usable directed edges among

        W=binomial(2m,m)

     chain centers.  Any path cover constrained to this order has at least

        W-Cat_m = (1-1/(m+1))W

     components.  Reset/init cost is therefore `Omega(W)`, so this family
     cannot produce a `W+o(W)` universal OR sequence.  This remains true
     after arbitrary bottom/top permutations, arbitrary ties, and arbitrary
     nonempty move masks.

296. The strategic lesson is not that all prefix-shift codes or all SCDs
     fail.  It is that any proposed SCD/Gray-code pairing should first be
     screened by the exact quotient-prefix fence.  A viable constant-one
     order needs `W-o(W)` compatible directed adjacencies; cool-lex with the
     Greene--Kleitman SCD has only `Cat_m=o(W)`, essentially the opposite
     extreme.  Full proof and the independent small-case C++ checker are in
     `COOLLEX_GK_MTF_AUDIT.md` and `gk_extension_mtf_test.cpp`.

## 74. The Catalan-compressed even-to-odd central lift is unconditional

297. The central compression conjectured in `DIMENSION_MAPS_HANDOFF.md` can
     be proved exactly from the saturating-cycle theorem.  Put

        M=binomial(2m,m),  N=binomial(2m,m+1),
        M-N=Cat_m.

     A saturating cycle between ranks m and m+1 of `B_(2m)` has the form

        U_0,Q_0,U_1,Q_1,...,U_(N-1),Q_(N-1),U_0,

     where the U's are all rank-(m+1) sets and the Q's are distinct rank-m
     sets.  Hence the U's form a Hamilton cycle in `J(2m,m+1)` with distinct
     adjacent-intersection colors `Q_i=U_i intersection U_(i+1)`.

298. Cut this cycle at one Q-edge and call the resulting upper Hamilton path
     R.  There are exactly `Cat_m+1` rank-m sets not used as the remaining
     boundary colors: the `Cat_m` sets outside the saturating cycle and the
     one Q at the cut.  Assign each such leftover set to any containing U.
     Choose the cut next to a U containing an outside set, assign that set to
     one endpoint U, and assign the removed Q to the other endpoint U.

     For each U, list its incoming boundary facet, all leftover facets
     assigned to U, and its outgoing boundary facet.  Concatenate these
     lists, identifying shared boundary facets.  Any two successive facets
     inside one block have union U.  The resulting path P visits every
     rank-m set exactly once, and its adjacent-union word consists of one
     nonempty contiguous run for every U, in the order R.  Therefore

        compress_equal_runs(Delta P)=R

     with the exact Catalan saving `M-N=Cat_m`.  No Hall theorem is hidden
     here: every assigned set is literally an unused facet of its chosen U,
     so capacity is automatic.

299. If z is a new coordinate and the paths are oriented with
     `P_0 subset R_0`, then

        reverse(R) || ({z} union P_0,...,{z} union P_(M-1))

     is a Hamilton path through the full rank-(m+1) layer of `B_(2m+1)`.
     The seam is a Johnson edge because its intersection is P_0.  Thus the
     width-exact central enumeration and seam conditions of the proposed
     even-to-odd inverse lift are now theorems in every dimension, rather
     than search assumptions.

300. This does not yet solve the OR recursion.  The constructed P need not
     have complete lower intersection shadows, and neither P nor R is yet
     guaranteed to have the long runs and pin-compatible lower factors.  A
     successful recursive theorem must make the compression **two-sided**:
     the union colors should have the contiguous-run structure above while
     the intersection colors simultaneously carry the dual lower structure.
     Full proof and the exact endpoint construction are in
     `CATALAN_COMPRESSED_LIFT.md`.

## 75. Auxiliary SCD adjacency and the Greene--Kleitman cycle order fail the exact MTF screen

301. Let `D,E` be two SCDs and project an edge

        u subset v=u+{x}

     of `E` to the two `D`-chains containing its endpoints.  Edge-disjointness
     only guarantees that those chains are distinct, and orthogonality only
     makes the chain labels along one `E`-chain distinct.  Neither condition
     implies a move-to-front transition.  The exact cross-edge obstruction is:

        C_D(u) -> C_D(v)  implies  x in minimum(C_D(v));
        C_D(v) -> C_D(u)  implies  u=maximum(C_D(u)),

     apart from the unique target chain with empty minimum.  For the first
     implication, quotient by the target minimum.  If x were a target
     increment, comparability with every target prefix would force it to be
     the immediately preceding increment, placing u in the target chain--a
     contradiction.  The reverse implication is the dual prefix-fence
     argument: the extra x can dominate the complete target star set only
     when u is its top.

302. These conditions are still not sufficient.  In `B_4`, the complementary
     edge-disjoint Greene--Kleitman SCD contains

        {3} subset {2,3}.

     Its endpoints lie in the standard chains `*01*` and `01**`.  The added
     bit 2 is in the target minimum, but after quotienting by `{2}` the source
     contains `{1,3}` while the target contains `{3,4}`.  These sets cross,
     so no transition exists in that direction; the reverse direction fails
     the top-end condition.  Thus even a canonical auxiliary SCD edge can
     give no directed edge in the full tied-state MTF graph.

303. The Gregor--Micka--Mutze Hamilton cycle containing the entire
     Greene--Kleitman SCD also fails after chain compression.  If `f(C)` and
     `ell(C)` close the first and last two stars, respectively, then

        C -> ell(C)

     is a genuine one-step transition, but `C -> f(C)` fails whenever C has
     at least three stars: after quotienting by the target minimum, the source
     first exposes the old first star e_1 while the target requires e_3.
     The reverse first/last-pair directions fail by the same prefix fence,
     except for the unique longest-chain and shortest-chain boundary cases.

304. Their dimension recursion replaces almost every parent chain by four
     descendants.  In each ordinary descendant block, in either its forward
     or reversed order, at most one of the three internal directed
     adjacencies is an MTF transition.  Even granting every inter-block
     connector, the cycle ordering therefore has at most

        (1/2+o(1)) W(n+2)

     usable directed adjacencies and any path cover constrained to that order
     has `(1/2-o(1))W(n+2)` components.  The whole-cube Hamilton cycle is a
     valid endpoint gluing of monotone cube paths, not a compressed recency
     braid of their chain fibers.

305. The GMM ordering also does not repair the central-diamond projection.
     It orders the same Greene--Kleitman chains, so the projection remains the
     branching forest from `GK_PROJECTION_COUNTS.md`, with exact indegree law

        #{X: indegree(X)=j}=binomial(2m-j-1,m-j).

     Asymptotically one quarter of its vertices branch, and every linear
     subforest has at most W/2 edges.  Hence it is not a `Cat_m`-component
     path factor and cannot become one by reading it in the GMM chain order.

306. Multiple lexical or orthogonal SCDs remain potentially useful only
     after a genuinely state-aware selection.  The auxiliary graph must be
     decorated by the target anchor, the complete quotient-prefix order, and
     the residual block refinement inherited by the next step.  Expansion of
     the bare chain quotient is irrelevant if its edges fail this local
     screen.  Full proofs and the published-recursion audit are in
     `ORTHOGONAL_SCD_MTF_AUDIT.md`.

## 76. Direct flagged Johnson codes have a monotone depth invariant

307. The fixed-SCD obstruction does not apply if the flag is allowed to
     evolve freely with the middle set.  There is nevertheless an exact
     invariant.  Let an ordered partition Pi expose a middle set S as the
     union of its first j blocks, apply one arbitrary-mask MTF update, and let
     the new state expose a distinct middle set T of the same rank.  Then the
     number of blocks in the T-prefix is at most j.

     Indeed, if the target prefix ends at the residual of old block q, then

        T = X union B_1 union ... union B_q.

     If q>=j this contains S, contradicting `|S|=|T|` and `S!=T`.  Hence
     q<j and the new prefix has at most q+1<=j blocks.  This holds for
     arbitrary ties, masks, and multi-exchange steps.

308. Every Johnson edge still lifts in one step.  If

        S=B_1 union ... union B_j,
        T=S-{a}+{b},  a in B_r,

     update by

        X={b} union (B_r-{a}) union B_(r+1) union ... union B_j.

     The new prefix `X,B_1,...,B_(r-1)` has union T.  Optional elements from
     earlier blocks may also be moved into X.  However, preserving depth j
     forces a to lie in the last block B_j and forces every earlier block to
     retain at least one element.  Thus a deep flagged Johnson walk is a
     rotating queue of nonempty blocks.

309. This gives a sharp residence-time obstruction.  Every arriving element
     enters the first block.  After ell subsequent depth-preserving steps its
     block can have moved right by at most ell positions; optional refreshes
     only move it back to the front.  If it leaves after ell steps while the
     depth is greater than ell, the departure forces the new depth to be at
     most ell.  In particular, an element which enters and leaves at the next
     transition collapses the flag permanently to one block.

310. Every transposition Gray path through all six 2-subsets of a 4-set has
     such an immediate re-exit.  Otherwise, viewing the 2-subsets as the six
     edges of K_4, consecutive shared endpoints would orient the list as an
     Euler trail of K_4.  This is impossible because K_4 has four odd-degree
     vertices.

311. This local fact yields an asymptotic no-go theorem for every cyclic
     **genlex transposition** order, including the reflected/revolving-door
     and Chase families.  Fix a suffix of c coordinates.  Every genlex block
     whose suffix weight lies in `[2,c-2]` contains a contiguous six-state
     `J(4,2)` subblock and hence a depth-one collapse.  The fraction of middle
     sets in the four bad suffix weights `0,1,c-1,c` is

        O(c 2^(-c) exp(O(c^2/m))).

     Taking c a suitable logarithm of m makes the largest cyclic gap between
     collapses o(W).  After any cut, the lift therefore reaches depth one
     within o(W) states and never recovers.  Only those o(W) states can expose
     rank-(m-1) sets, but that rank contains `(m/(m+1))W=(1-o(1))W` masks.

312. Cool-lex is genlex but sometimes changes two pairs.  Its four-free,
     weight-two local order is, up to reversal,

        0011,1001,1100,0110,1010,0101.

     It has an element of residence time at most two in every cyclic cut.
     The same block argument forces depth at most two after o(W) states.  A
     depth-two state exposes at most one proper lower prefix, so all states
     together cannot cover even the two ranks m-1 and m-2, whose total size
     is `(2-o(1))W`.

313. Hence the direct flagged route remains viable only for a new
     **long-residence** Johnson code designed together with its queue flags.
     For W-o(W) steps it needs omega(1), realistically Theta(sqrt(m)), useful
     blocks; every departure must occur in the last block; and the resulting
     prefix unions must cover the central band.  Singleton blocks specialize
     to a subset universal cycle/sliding-window word.  The fixed-uniformity
     tight-Euler-tour theorem of Glock--Joos--Kuhn--Osthus does not cover the
     central regime `uniformity=n/2`.  Full proofs are in
     `FLAGGED_JOHNSON_MTF.md`.

314. The required depth scale is itself forced.  If j_t is the number of
     blocks in the middle prefix at state t, that state exposes at most
     j_t-1 nonempty masks below the middle.  Consequently universality needs

        sum_t (j_t-1) >= (2^(2m)-W)/2 - 1,

     and Stirling gives

        average_t j_t >= (sqrt(pi)/2+o(1)) sqrt(m).

     Thus a successful long-residence code must maintain Theta(sqrt(m))
     useful flag depth on average; this scale is information-theoretic, not
     an artifact of the symmetric-chain approach.

## 77. Integral wreath corrections are necessarily mesoscopic

314. The real rank selectors from Section 72 cannot be rounded by any
     bounded local cancellation.  For two unoriented cyclic orders C,D on
     `n=2m+1` coordinates, let `d_circ(C,D)` be their adjacent-swap distance,
     allowing a final rotation or reversal.  One adjacent swap changes only
     two cyclic middle intervals, and therefore

        |W_m(C) intersection W_m(D)| >= n-2 d_circ(C,D).

     In particular, two wreaths that can occur on the same side of an exact
     factor trade must be disjoint and hence have distance at least `m+1`.
     This is the missing integral geometry behind the signed matrix kernel.

315. A connected union of s relabelled Petr--Turek four-wreath selector
     squares has cyclic-order support diameter at most `2s`.  If its reduced
     sum is a nonzero support-feasible trade, the preceding distance bound
     forces

        s >= ceil((m+1)/2).

     Thus every fixed six- or eight-wreath cancellation fails for large m;
     in fact every nondegenerate commuting adjacent-swap `2^d` cube fails
     already for `m>=2`, because one sign class contains two orders at
     distance two.  Rank-local integrality must propagate through
     `Omega(m)` selector cells before it can even respect middle-set packing.

316. There is nevertheless a canonical legal move at factor scale.  If F is
     any exact wreath factor and pi is a coordinate transposition, then for
     `m>=2` the order families F and `pi F` are disjoint, and

        1_(pi F)-1_F

     is a support-feasible `Cat_m`-for-`Cat_m` trade.  Form the bipartite
     interaction multigraph whose sides are F and `pi F`, with one edge for
     every middle set joining the two wreaths that contain it.  Each connected
     component covers the same middle masks on its two sides and therefore
     switches independently.  If there are c components, these switches give
     an exact c-dimensional cube **inside** the integral factor fibre.

317. This component cube is the correct replacement for the forbidden
     order-level Boolean cubes.  For a component K and rank a, record the
     exact effect vector

        delta_(K,a)=B_a(1_(K intersection pi F)-1_(K intersection F)).

     Integral vertical correction is now an honest vector-balancing problem
     for the component effects `delta_(K,a)`, with no post-rounding step and
     no risk of breaking middle coverage.  The next positive theorem must
     show that suitable relabelings give many independently switchable,
     sufficiently spread component effects, or else prove that a giant
     component obstruction persists.  Full proofs are in
     `INTEGRAL_WREATH_CIRCUIT_OBSTRUCTION.md`.

## 78. The MSW factor has a positive-density integral selector cube

318. The giant-component obstruction does **not** persist for every
     relabeling.  Let `F_m` be the explicit Mutze--Standke--Wiechert wreath
     factor on `2m+1` coordinates and take the adjacent transposition
     `tau=(2 3)`.  For every Dyck word `R` of semilength `m-2`, the two MSW
     blocks indexed by

        x_R=1100R,              y_R=1010R

     have omitted-label words

        C_R=(4,2,3,1,T_R),      D_R=(2,1,4,3,T_R).

     Their transposed words are

        C'_R=(4,3,2,1,T_R),     D'_R=(3,1,4,2,T_R),

     and a direct cut-by-cut calculation proves the disjoint equality

        W_m(C_R) disjoint_union W_m(D_R)
          = W_m(C'_R) disjoint_union W_m(D'_R).

     Therefore each `R` gives one independently switchable legal two-for-two
     factor trade.  Different `R` give different interaction components.
     The resulting integral cube has dimension

        Cat_(m-2) = (1/16+O(1/m)) Cat_m.

     This is the first positive-density family of bounded-size integral
     moves inside an exact middle-layer factor.

319. The action of one such trade on rank `m-1` is exactly an elementary
     Petr--Turek square.  With

        K_R=4+([2m-4] minus (R union {2m-4})),

     its signed support is

        + K_R union {2,2m}       - K_R union {3,2m}
        - K_R union {2,2m+1}     + K_R union {3,2m+1}.

     These four-target supports are disjoint as `R` varies.  Thus the real
     rank selectors from Section 72 have now been lifted integrally on a
     linear fraction of the MSW factor, without breaking any middle mask.
     At lower ranks the same switch has correlated side effects; controlling
     those effects is now the substantive remaining issue.

     The selector is also stable under every complete Dyck prefix.  If `P`
     and `R` have semilengths `s` and `m-s-2`, respectively, then

        P1100R,                 P1010R

     give the same sealed two-for-two component for the shifted transposition
     `(2s+2,2s+3)`.  For each fixed `s` this supplies

        Cat_s Cat_(m-s-2)

     independent size-two components.  The proof is the exact concatenation
     law `rho(PQ)=(rho(P),2s+rho(Q))`: cyclically rotating the common prefix
     behind the four-letter gadget reduces the identity to the original cut
     table.  Summing the number of contextual occurrences over all boundaries
     gives `Cat_(m-1)`.  Different depths may overlap, but this establishes a
     recursive Catalan hierarchy of legal local charts and suggests a
     prefix-free, suffix-recursive absorption scheme.

320. The complete Catalan component hierarchy for `(2 3)` is now proved in
     every dimension:

        number of components of size Cat_j+Cat_(j+1)
          = Cat_(m-j-2),                 0<=j<=m-2.

     The component consists of all Dyck
     words `AR`, where `R` has semilength `m-j-2` and `A` is either one
     primitive Dyck word of semilength `j+2`, or `10` followed by a primitive
     Dyck word of semilength `j+1`.  Boundary connectivity of the top class,
     together with suffix-local induction, proves that MSW transposition
     edges preserve and connect exactly these classes.

321. The contextual size-two components are genuine legal selectors, but a
     later all-rank audit shows that they cannot themselves be the bulk
     frame.  Their complete action and the resulting obstruction are stated
     in Section 83 below.  Their viable role is a sparse final absorber; bulk
     correction must use the larger components in the proved hierarchy,
     commutators between successive factor fibres, or another nonlocal legal
     circuit.  Complete proofs of the component identities are in
     `MSW_TRANSPOSITION_COMPONENTS.md` and
     `MSW_MULTIRANK_LOCAL_TRADES.md`.

## 79. The published four-level lexical factor needs Catalan-scale rewiring

322. Contracting the lower outer paths in the Gregor--Jager--Mutze--Sawada--
     Wille middle-four-level factor gives a spanning linear forest on the
     rank-`r` sets of `[2r+1]`.  It has every rank-`r-1` intersection colour
     exactly once and

        D_r = binomial(2r+1,r)-binomial(2r+1,r-1)

     components.  This is a useful one-sided atom, but its ordinary upper
     union colours are not distinct.

323. There is an explicit symbolic collision family of size `Cat_(r-1)`.
     For Dyck words `w,v` whose semilengths sum to `r-2`, the two lower words

        w 00010 v,              w 00001 v

     induce distinct contracted edges with the same upper union colour

        w 00111 v.

     The pairs are edge-disjoint and their common colours are distinct.
     Hence the union-colour duplicate excess satisfies

        delta_r >= Cat_(r-1)
                = (1/4+O(1/r)) Cat_r
                = (1/(8r)+O(1/r^2)) binomial(2r+1,r).

     In particular, merely joining the `D_r` path components can never make
     the forest two-sided; at least `Cat_(r-1)` forest edges must first be
     rainbow-pruned.  The loss is Catalan-scale and therefore still
     `o(width)`, so it refutes the shortcut but not the asymptotic programme.

324. After any pruning, the exact residual problem is a coloured endpoint
     cycle: if `delta` edges are deleted, there are `D_r+delta` path
     fragments and exactly that many connector slots.  The connectors must
     form one cycle through the oriented fragments, use every missing upper
     colour, and cover every deleted lower colour.  If one retains the upper
     flags instead of ordinary union colours, aligning the lower and upper
     lexical forests is exactly a path-fragment Hall problem under
     coordinatewise containment.  The canonical reverse-complement
     isomorphism is containment-valid on only `2^r` of the
     `binomial(2r+1,r)` vertices.  Thus a Catalan-scale global rewiring is
     unavoidable in either formulation.  Full statements are in
     `GJM_FOUR_LEVEL_AUDIT.md` and `CONTRACTED_FLAG_CRITERION.md`.

## 80. Honest atomic compression of the mixed-pair necklace reservoir

325. A typed pair-flip block of length `R=2 ell` is internally the disjoint
     union of `R` nested chain segments, but those segments cannot be treated
     as global atom vertices.  Already at radius one, segments with the same
     middle member intersect; segments centred at Johnson-neighbouring middle
     sets can be chosen to share their lower member.  Since the Johnson graph
     is connected, the overlap graph of all native positive-radius segments
     is connected.  Any equality quotient identifying intersecting segments
     therefore collapses every useful atom to one vertex.

326. A preassigned SCD is not a free repair.  A prescribed radius-`d` flag
     requires `d` specified coordinate pairs in the block's perfect matching,
     an event of probability

        (2m-2d-1)!!/(2m-1)!!.

     For `d=Theta(sqrt(m))` this is superpolynomially small, whereas a
     constant fraction of the SCD chains have such radii.  Thus a polynomial
     mixed-pair reservoir is generically incompatible with any fixed SCD;
     constructing an adapted one is the original wreath-resolved-SCD problem.

327. There is nevertheless an exact lower-uniformity reduction.  Project a
     typed block to its `R` middle masks, and for every nonmiddle target `S`
     declare a conflict clique consisting of all projected blocks whose
     native chain segments contain `S`.  A selected family is mask-disjoint
     exactly when its projected `R`-edges form a matching and it takes at
     most one member of every conflict clique.  If `n_(>=q)` selected blocks
     carry radius at least `q`, its complete certified-band defect is exactly

        D(M)=W-R|M|+2 sum_(q=1)^h (N_q-R n_(>=q)(M)).

     Therefore the required conclusion is `D(M)=o(W)`, not merely an
     `o(W)` middle-vertex defect.

328. After polynomial thinning, the projected base hypergraph has rank
     `R=o(m)` and relative pair-codegree `O(m^-2)`, so the earlier
     projective-plane obstruction disappears at the base level.  The price is
     a growing structured conflict system: target-clique intersections have
     relative size `O(m^-1)`, a typical edge meets `Theta(R sqrt(m))`
     cliques, and the radius tails in the displayed defect must remain
     balanced.  The precise missing theorem is an atomic conflict-rounding
     or alternating-necklace absorption theorem satisfying that weighted
     defect bound.  Ordinary Pippenger matching after atom compression is
     invalid.  Full proofs and parameters are in
     `NECKLACE_ATOMIC_COMPRESSION.md`.

329. Exact conflict-freeness is stronger than the OR problem needs.  For an
     arbitrary multiset of typed blocks, let `c_S` be the number of emitted
     occurrences of a central-band mask and put

        E(M)=sum_S (c_S-1)_+.

     If `T(M)` is the total number of emitted certified slots, the number of
     uncovered masks is the exact identity

        U(M)=|central band|-T(M)+E(M).

     Consequently it is enough to select physical block length `W+o(W)`,
     balance the single total slot ledger to `o(W)`, and make the **total**
     collision excess `E(M)=o(W)`.  Projected middle blocks may overlap and
     individual conflict cliques may be hit repeatedly.  This low-excess
     necklace-rounding theorem is strictly weaker than a conflict-free
     matching and is the weakest clean statement currently known to imply
     `nu(2m)=W+o(W)` after the outer-tail repair.  The most plausible proof is
     a colour-balanced nibble followed by exact necklace switchings that
     descend the total-excess potential.

## 81. The unchanged MSW factor has macroscopic shallow defects

330. The new integral switches cannot be avoided by repairing a small
     exceptional family around the original MSW factor.  Exact remote
     enumeration of its first lower cyclic-interval shadow gives the missing
     counts

        m=4,5,6,7,8,9,10,11:
        4,32,176,837,3709,15811,65860,270337.

     Dividing by `binomial(2m+1,m-1)`, the missing fractions are

        .0476,.0970,.1368,.1672,.1908,.2092,.2241,.2363.

     At `m=11` the factor misses `270337/1144066` targets already at depth
     one.  Its full multiplicity histogram there is

        multiplicity 0,1,2,3,4,5,6:
        270337,462000,352978,51434,6779,524,14.

     The defect is therefore macroscopic, not `O(Cat_m)`.  No asymptotic
     limit is inferred from the finite table, but it decisively rules out the
     proposed Catalan-size literal repair of the unchanged factor.  A
     positive-density switch family or a globally different factor is
     necessary.  The independent constructor and all-depth audit are in
     `msw_shadow_audit.cpp`; the remote-only run and conclusions are recorded
     in `MSW_SHALLOW_DEFECT_AUDIT.md`.

## 82. Exact heat-bath law for interaction-component switches

331. Interaction components admit an exact probabilistic interpretation.
     Let `F` be any exact wreath factor, let `tau` be a coordinate
     transposition, and independently choose the `F`-side or `tau F`-side of
     every interaction component.  The result `G` is always another exact
     middle factor.  At every rank `r`, with

        Delta_(K,r)=B_r(1_(K intersection tau F)-1_(K intersection F)),

     one has

        E[c_r(G) | F,tau] = (c_r(F)+tau c_r(F))/2,

        Cov(c_r(G) | F,tau)
          = (1/4) sum_K Delta_(K,r) Delta_(K,r)^T.

     Cross-rank covariances have the identical formula with
     `Delta_(K,r) Delta_(K,s)^T`.  Thus the mean performs one exact
     random-transposition/Johnson diffusion step, while the component effects
     are precisely its integral rounding noise.

332. For `f_r=c_r(F)-mu_r 1`, the quadratic ledger is

        E||c_r(G)-mu_r 1||^2
          =||f_r||^2-(1/4)||f_r-tau f_r||^2
             +(1/4)sum_K||Delta_(K,r)||^2.

     A giant component makes the last two terms cancel; useful fragmentation
     is exactly what can turn continuous smoothing into an integral descent.
     Weighted sums give the same identity simultaneously across ranks.

333. There is also an exact zero-event formula.  If a target occurs on both
     sides of some component it survives every cube choice.  Otherwise, let
     `d_S` be the number of components on exactly one side of which it occurs.
     Fair independent switching gives

        Pr(S is missing)=2^(-d_S).

     Hence the expected total missing potential is the sum of these powers,
     and some deterministic cube vertex attains at most that sum.  One fixed
     transposition cannot suffice: every target invariant under it and absent
     from `F` is absent from `tau F` as well, and asymptotically half of a
     central layer is invariant under a random coordinate pair.  The
     contextual Catalan charts must therefore be combined across several
     prefix-free boundaries.  Complete proofs are in `FACTOR_HEAT_BATH.md`.

## 83. Exact multirank profile and the local-Haar obstruction

334. Every contextual two-for-two selector has a closed all-rank formula.
     Rotate its omitted-label words so their exceptional four-letter block
     comes first, and split the common tail into its even and odd position
     lists `E,O`.  If

        partial(K)=e_(K union {gamma})-e_(K union {beta}),

     then for `2<=r<=m-1`, with `l=r-1`,

        B_r z = partial(suf_l O)+partial(suf_l E)
                -partial(pre_l E)-partial(pre_l O).

     It is zero at ranks `1,m`; complementary ranks carry the complementary
     vector.  For `2<=r<=m-2` the support has eight entries with coefficients
     `+-1`.  At rank `m-1` the two `O` terms cancel and the result is one
     elementary square of support four.  Thus the correlated side effects
     are exactly four nested Boolean flags, not arbitrary noise.

335. The hoped-for Catalan/Haar recursion using only these local trades is
     impossible.  Across **all** Dyck boundaries there are `Cat_(m-1)` local
     columns, and their rank-`m-1` projections are linearly independent over
     every field.  A triangular pivot is given by the first position at which
     the target's Dyck height becomes negative: it recovers the boundary
     `p`, then the prefix `P`, and finally the suffix `R` by restoring its
     unique deleted first-return step.  Consequently

        B_(m-1) sum c_(p,P,R) z_(p,P,R)=0
          implies every c_(p,P,R)=0.

     Hence no nontrivial combination of the local charts can repair a deeper
     rank while preserving a completed first shadow.  Their total first-
     shadow support is only `O(Cat_m)=O(W/m)`, so they also cannot form a bulk
     frame on that layer.

336. The correct division of labour is now rigorous.  Larger/nonlocal
     interaction components must perform bulk alignment and satisfy a
     weighted heat-bath inequality of the form

        sum_q w_q sum_K ||Delta_(K,m-q)||^2
          <= (1-epsilon_m)
             sum_q w_q ||sum_K Delta_(K,m-q)||^2.

     Conditional expectation then yields an integral energy descent.
     A reserved disjoint subfamily of the size-two charts may absorb the final
     `O(Cat_m)` specially located residue, but all ranks must be solved
     simultaneously because of the independence theorem.  The exact
     all-rank formulas, triangular proof, and heat-bath variance gate are in
     `MSW_MULTIRANK_LOCAL_TRADES.md`.

337. The continuous part of this bulk inequality is already sharp.  Every
     rank discrepancy of an exact factor has zero point marginals, so it lies
     in Johnson harmonics `j>=2`.  For a uniform coordinate transposition,

        E_tau ||(f+tau f)/2||^2 <= (1-2/n)||f||^2.

     Combining this character-ratio estimate with the heat-bath variance
     identity gives an exact sufficient theorem.  A weighted multirank energy
     contracts by `epsilon_m` if

        E_tau sum_(q,K) w_q ||Delta_(K,m-q)||^2
          <= (8/n-4 epsilon_m)
                sum_q w_q ||f_(m-q)||^2.

     Thus no further spectral or fractional theorem is missing.  The whole
     bulk gate is the displayed component-variance estimate for the larger
     legal components.  Fixed-boundary size-two squares give equality at the
     first shadow—their variance cancels their mean smoothing exactly—so they
     cannot prove strict descent.

## 84. Full-component heat ledger and the one-layer obstruction

338. The complete MSW interaction hierarchy, rather than only its sealed
     size-two charts, has now been audited exactly for the transposition
     `tau=(2 3)` through `m=10`.  At rank `r` put

        A_r=||sum_K Delta_(K,r)||_2^2,
        V_r=sum_K ||Delta_(K,r)||_2^2.

     The heat-bath energy change is `(V_r-A_r)/4`, so `A_r-V_r>0` is strict
     contraction.  For every audited `m>=5` and every `2<=r<=m-2`, the gap
     is positive.  At the first lower shadow `r=m-1` it is negative for every
     `m=3,...,10`; the exact sequence is

        -4,-8,-20,-48,-124,-340,-984,-2972.

     At `m=10`, the complete lower-rank gap vector for `r=2,...,9` is

        37131936,13725044,3946552,1197228,
        358564,97096,14156,-2972.

339. These computations are evidence, not an all-dimensional proof, but the
     stable sign pattern makes the next theorem substantially sharper:

        prove that full-component resampling contracts every rank below
        `m-1`, while its only unstable mode is the adjacent shadow;
        then construct a top-shadow-invisible circuit or absorber whose gain
        dominates that one negative term.

     This is a one-layer obstruction rather than an undifferentiated
     multirank failure.  It also explains why the local two-for-two squares
     could not be the bulk engine: they give `A=V` at the adjacent shadow,
     whereas the strict deeper contraction is created by alignment among
     effects belonging to the larger nonlocal components.  The executable
     ledger and exact data are recorded in `MSW_HEAT_LEDGER_AUDIT.md`.

## 85. Exact orbit potential and the failure of one-cube randomization

340. Identify the right side of the interaction graph with the original
     factor by applying `tau^-1`.  Every component is then a subset `K` of
     the original factor and its two selectable sides are exactly `K` and
     `tau K`.  If `a_K(S)` is the number of occurrences of a target `S` in
     `K`, the opposite-side count is the exact identity

        b_K(S)=a_K(tau S).

     Hence fixed targets `tau S=S` are frozen component by component.  On a
     moved orbit `{S,tau S}`, if one component contains both targets then
     neither can ever disappear.  Otherwise, if their occurrence families
     meet `d` components, independent fair switching gives

        E[number missing in {S,tau S}]=2^(1-d).

341. Component dimension alone cannot make this expectation small near the
     middle.  Let `H` be the number of targets already robust on both sides
     of one component and let `U=N_r-H`.  Since the two sides have only
     `2W` total rank-`r` occurrences,

        2H + sum_(nonrobust S) d_S <= 2W.

     Convexity of `2^(-x)` yields

        E M_r >= U 2^(-2(W-H)/U).

     At every fixed depth `r=m-q`, `W/N_r=1+O_q(1/m)`.  Therefore an
     `o(N_r)` expected miss count requires all but `o(N_r)` targets to be
     robust inside a component before randomization.  A single
     transposition also freezes asymptotically half of a central layer.
     Repeated fair switching of one cube is consequently not an asymptotic
     construction.

342. There is an exact adaptive-routing statistic.  Let `Z` be the missing
     targets and `D` the targets of multiplicity at least two.  If
     `Psi_tau(c)` is the unavoidable missing mass after redistributing only
     inside `tau`-orbits, then

        E_tau Psi_tau(c)
          = |Z| - e_(J(n,r))(Z,D)/binomial(n,2).

     Thus an adaptive multi-transposition theorem must prove both that holes
     have many Johnson edges to duplicates and that the duplicate
     occurrences on many such edges lie in at least two interaction
     components.  This is the exact replacement for the false claim that a
     high-dimensional component cube is automatically a useful random
     rounding device.  The proofs, the missing/excess identity, and the
     full orbit ledger are in `COMPONENT_CUBE_POTENTIAL.md`.

## 86. The first genuine nonlocal Haar circuit

343. Adaptive use of several factor fibres is not merely a formal hope.  At
     `m=4` (`n=9`) there are two actual exact wreath factors `F,G` with

        B_4 F = B_4 G = 1,
        B_3 F = B_3 G,
        B_2 F != B_2 G.

     They have ten common wreaths and differ by a support-feasible
     four-for-four trade `w=G-F`.  Its complete deeper effect is

        B_2 w = -e_13+e_23+e_14-e_24
                 +e_15-e_25-e_19+e_29.

     Thus `B_4w=B_3w=0` but `B_2w` is nonzero.  This is the first legal Haar
     direction in the exact-factor fibre: it changes the second lower shadow
     while preserving both the middle layer and the first lower shadow.

344. The circuit is genuinely nonlocal.  Starting from the MSW factor, three
     preparatory component switches for transpositions

        (1 3), (2 4), (1 5)

     create a factor in which the final four-for-four side is one interaction
     component for `(1 2)`.  This explains why no such circuit occurs in the
     original one-transposition cube.  It also validates the algebraic
     three-cube/commutator direction suggested by the orbit obstruction.

345. Two obvious suspensions fail from `m=4` to `m=5`: inserting one common
     adjacent pair at a common gap of all eight orders, and inserting two new
     labels antipodally while retaining each old cyclic order.  Replaying the
     same four transpositions without a contextual modification also fails.
     Hence the exact all-dimensional target is a **factor-level commutator
     suspension**: lift the preparatory switches and the final component
     through a Dyck prefix/suffix recursion, rather than padding the finished
     eight-order identity.  The eight orders, both exact completions, switch
     provenance, and standalone verifier are in `NONLOCAL_HAAR_M4.md` and
     `verify_nonlocal_haar_m4.cpp`.

## 87. Exact Catalan hierarchy and boundary connectivity

346. For every `m`, the complete `(2 3)` MSW component law is

        number of components of size Cat_j+Cat_(j+1)
          = Cat_(m-j-2).

     The component indexed by `R in D_(m-j-2)` is exactly

        { A R : A is primitive of semilength j+2,
                or A=10 followed by a primitive of semilength j+1 }.

     Suffix locality proves that every proper class is closed and connected;
     boundary connectivity proves the top class is connected.  The explicit
     distinct leading pivots in `MSW_COLEX_PIVOT.md` therefore prove
     unconditionally that the entire fixed `(2 3)` hierarchy is linearly
     independent at the first shadow over every field.

347. Let `Gamma_m^partial` be the MSW path-owner graph for swapping the first
     two coordinates.  Its connectivity is now proved for all `m`.  The MNW
     flippability hypergraph supplies a spanning tree of base-pattern
     supports.  Every capped support remains connected under three exact
     context operations:

        x -> Ux,             x -> xV,             x -> 1x0,

     for Dyck `U,V`.  Suffixes follow from literal concatenation locality.
     Prefixes use the exact owner functor

        H_U(1bR)=11 theta_b(U) R,

     where `theta_b(U)` replaces the opening `1` of the last primitive
     component of `U` by `b`.  The outer-primitive operation follows from
     literal reversal of MSW paths.  An arbitrary MNW context cut decomposes
     uniquely into these three operations.

348. This decomposition removes the earlier mirror-wrap gap rather than
     proving the false wrap-fibre claim.  Mirrors are needed only at the
     finite base patterns.  Both orientations of `alpha(w)`, `beta`, `gamma`,
     and `delta` have explicit common-hub certificates; the parameterized alpha
     certificate is symbolic, and the other base tables are finite.  Gluing
     the capped supports along the MNW spanning tree connects every root
     beginning in `10`; the final middle-piece vertex of any other root
     attaches it to that component.

     Hence `Gamma_m^partial` is connected for every `m`, and the Catalan
     component hierarchy is unconditional.  Its total number of components
     is

        K_m=sum_(r=0)^(m-2) Cat_r ~ Cat_m/12.

     For fixed `j`, the fraction of components of size
     `Cat_j+Cat_(j+1)` tends to `3/4^(j+1)`.  Thus three quarters of all
     components are size two, while exponentially rarer components provide
     corrections at every Catalan scale.  The audited proofs are in
     `MSW_PREFIX_CONTEXT_FUNCTOR.md`, `MSW_CAP_CONTEXT_DECOMPOSITION.md`,
     `MSW_BOUNDARY_CONNECTIVITY.md`, and
     `MSW_COMPONENT_HIERARCHY_REDUCTION.md`.

## 88. Antipodal shadow suspension and the voltage gate

349. The linear part of the state-level Haar suspension problem has an exact
     all-dimensional solution.  Work in the ordinary cyclic-interval order
     (equivalent to the every-other-position order because the cycle length
     is odd).  For a cycle `C` on `n=2m+1` old coordinates, insert new
     coordinates `x,y` in gaps `i,i+m`, and sum over all `i`; call the
     resulting operator `P_m`.  A direct gap count proves that, whenever

        B_m w = B_(m-1) w = 0,

     one has in dimension `2m+3`

        B_(m+1) P_m w = B_m P_m w = 0,

     while on either sector containing exactly one new coordinate,

        (B_(m-1) P_m w)_(U union {x})
          = (m-1)(B_(m-2)w)_U.

     All other sectors at that rank vanish.  Thus the next-shadow map is an
     explicit scaled injection, and `P_m` commutes with every permutation of
     the old coordinates.

350. This does not yet give a factor move.  For one old cycle and one old
     middle interval `S`, the full translate family contains each of
     `S union {x}` and `S union {y}` exactly `m+1` times at the new middle
     rank.  Hence the cyclically equivariant lift is never a wreath packing.
     A legal suspension has to choose one pointing per changed wreath.

351. A rigid translation-stable sufficient pointing condition is
     voltage-flatness. Pair equal rank-`m` occurrences across the two sides
     of the old trade, and choose occurrence bijections for equal
     rank-`m-1` targets. Label an occurrence edge `CD` by the difference of
     its cyclic start positions in `D` and `C`, as an element of
     `Z_(2m+1)`. Bi-flat pointings satisfy

        a_D-a_C = start_D-start_C

     on every occurrence edge. Equivalently, every cycle voltage is zero.
     Under this bi-flat condition, antipodally extending each old cycle at
     its chosen point gives two genuine middle-wreath packings with equal
     middle and first-lower shadows.  Translating all pointings and summing
     recovers `P_m`; therefore, if the old second-lower effect is nonzero,
     at least one translated pointed trade retains a nonzero new
     second-lower effect. Bi-flatness is sufficient, not necessary.

352. The exact general pointed criterion is coarser. For a middle target,
     the relative offset is seen only through five classes

        X0=[0,m-2], X1={m-1}, Y1={m},
        Y0=[m+1,2m-1], B={2m};

     these encode the two one-new middle targets, the no-new complement,
     and the no-new first-lower target. For a rank-`m-1` occurrence, only
     three classes are visible:

        X=[0,m-2] union {2m}, 0={m-1}, Y=[m,2m-1].

     Pointed antipodal extensions have equal new middle and first-lower
     rows iff (i) the five-class labels agree for the unique two occurrences
     of every middle target, and (ii) the three-class occurrence multisets
     agree for every rank-`m-1` target. This is necessary and sufficient,
     and every such pointed side is automatically a middle-wreath packing.
     A coarse solution need not survive common translation, so the averaging
     argument proving a nonzero deeper effect is then unavailable.

353. Nonzero voltage holonomy is an exact obstruction only to the rigid
     exact-offset derived-cover lift. A closed walk of nonzero voltage puts
     two pointings of one old wreath in a lifted component, and those two
     wreaths overlap. It is not an obstruction to an arbitrary coarse
     pointed thinning. The certified m=4 Haar edge illustrates the
     distinction. In
     ordinary interval order let

        C     = (1,6,4,3,2,8,7,5,9),
        tau C = (2,6,4,3,1,8,7,5,9),  tau=(1 2).

     The target {1,3,4,6} starts at positions 0,1, giving voltage +1;
     {2,3,4,6} starts at 1,0, giving voltage -1. Flatness would require the
     same exact potential difference to equal both values modulo 9; the
     parallel-edge cycle has holonomy 2. Hence the known edge is not
     transposition-equivariantly bi-flat. But choosing both pointings equal
     to 1 puts the four local offsets in the same coarse class X0, so this
     two-edge witness does not rule out the exact coarse criterion.

354. Adding the common old factor completion does not remove the strict
     voltage cycle: its middle occurrence graph is disjoint from that of the
     changed trade. This rules out only the bi-flat route, not a coarse
     pointwise extension. The honest remaining alternatives are therefore:
     (a) cancel holonomy and use the translation-stable theorem, or (b) solve
     the exact five-state/three-state constraints and separately certify a
     nonzero deeper effect. Either route still requires completion of the
     resulting partial packing to a reachable exact factor. Full formulas
     and proofs are in `HAAR_ANTIPODAL_SUSPENSION.md`.

355. The exact coarse criterion has been exhausted on the certified m=4
     four-for-four trade. For fixed antipodal direction d=4, the 9^4=6561
     pointings on each side yield 6561 distinct combined B5,B4 signatures,
     with zero overlap between the two sides. Allowing directions d=4 or
     d=5 independently gives 18^4=104976 distinct signatures per side,
     again with zero overlap. Thus this particular edge has no direct
     one-extension-per-changed-wreath antipodal suspension to m=5. This is
     a finite certified no-go, not an all-m theorem and not a consequence
     of the voltage witness. The checker is
     `search_haar_pointed_thinning.cpp`.

356. The rigid bi-flat extension problem itself now has an exact
     classification.  First solve the forced rank-m voltage graph.  If its
     voltage is exact, choose a base potential `a_v^0`; every solution is

        a_v=a_v^0+z_K

     with one cyclic phase `z_K` per connected middle component.  A flat
     rank-(m-1) occurrence bijection then exists if and only if, for every
     lower target and every residue, the negative and positive occurrence
     counts having phase `a_v-start_v` are equal.  The allowable matching
     graph is a disjoint union of complete bipartite phase buckets, so this
     is the complete Hall criterion.  In group-ring form it is

        sum_K X^(z_K) f_(T,K)(X)=0
        in Z[X]/(X^(2m+1)-1)

     for every lower target `T`.  Lower-occurrence bijections therefore
     never cancel pre-existing middle holonomy; they only extend an already
     flat middle cochain.

357. For a single transposition component, contract the voltage-zero edge
     from each old wreath to its translated copy.  Every moved orbit
     `{S,tau S}` becomes an owner-transfer edge

        owner(S) -> owner(tau S)

     of gain `start(tau S)-start(S)`.  Bi-flatness is exactly balance of
     this gain graph.  If the two transposed labels are at cyclic distance
     `m` in any changed wreath, the graph has a gain-`+/-1` loop and is
     immediately unbalanced.  This gives a structural all-m obstruction,
     not merely a failed matching choice.

358. The finite m=4 no-go in paragraph 355 has a three-target mathematical
     certificate.  One negative/positive order pair contains the common
     targets `{1,2,3,4}`, `{1,2,3,5}`, `{3,4,6,8}` at start pairs
     `(8,6),(7,7),(1,4)`.  If `x=a-8,d=b-a`, coarse middle equality requires

        kappa(x)=kappa(x+d+2),
        kappa(x+1)=kappa(x+d+1),
        kappa(x+7)=kappa(x+d+4).

     The five kappa fibres at m=4 are
     `{0,1,2},{3},{4},{5,6,7},{8}`; direct fibre intersection is empty for
     every `x`.  Hence the fixed-direction direct lift fails already on
     three middle targets, without considering the lower row.  Proof,
     nine-row certificate, and the general phase theorem are in
     `HAAR_HOLONOMY_CLASSIFICATION.md`.

## 90. Strategic reset: exact obstruction to pointwise Catalan absorption

359. The finite-case repair programme is frozen.  From this point onward a
     finite construction is relevant only if it proves, tests, or refutes an
     all-dimensional lemma.  The primary target is first

        nu(k)=(1+o(1)) binom(k,floor(k/2)),

     and only afterward the additive conjecture `nu(k)=B(k)`.  The two
     equivalent global languages are a vertically resolved wreath factor in
     odd dimension and a near-width move-to-front path cover of symmetric
     chains.

360. Universal phase erasure for the antipodal suspension is incompatible
     with a partial factor.  For one old wreath and pointing multiset `D`,
     the five-state middle signature at phase `s` is independent of `s` if
     and only if `D` is a constant multiple of the full cyclic group
     `Z_(2m+1)`.  This follows already from the singleton boundary state,
     whose multiplicity at phase `s` is `mult_D(s-1)`.  Any two distinct
     pointings of the same old wreath overlap in the new middle layer.
     Hence no nonempty phase-oblivious, orderwise lift can be a packing.

361. A literal common Dyck context cannot suspend a fixed trade forever.
     If `d_circ` is cyclic adjacent-swap distance, two same-sign orders in a
     partial `(2m+1,m)` wreath factor must have distance at least `m+1`.
     Common prefix/suffix insertion preserves their old distance.  More
     generally, an order-dependent lift from dimension `m0` to `m0+t` must
     create at least

        m0+t+1-d_circ(C,D)

     new units of separation for every eventually tight pair.  The certified
     `m=4` Haar side has minimum distance seven, so any literal common-context
     lift already fails by `m=7`.

362. The complete fixed `(2 3)` Catalan hierarchy is not an absorber or a
     flow network.  Its rank-`m-1` component effects have distinct colex
     pivots and are linearly independent over every field; therefore no
     nonempty selection from that fixed cube preserves the first lower row.
     At the outer boundary the quotient is connected, so the only switch is
     the global transposition of the whole factor.  Combining this with
     paragraphs 360--361 leaves one honest successor theorem: a
     noncommutative component-splitting construction which performs
     preparatory switches under several transpositions, recomputes components
     after each switch, reroutes middle owners across Dyck contexts, and only
     then completes the partial factor.  Full statements and proofs are in
     `CATALAN_SEAM_ABSORPTION_OBSTRUCTION.md`.

## 91. Contractive repair lifts and the exact Catalan braid gate

363. Exact vertical preservation is stronger than necessary.  Put

        W_m=binom(2m+1,m),   C_m=Cat_m=W_m/(2m+1),

     and let `R_(m,H)(F)` be the shortest auxiliary OR word covering all
     central-band masks, through depth `H`, missing from a wreath factor
     `F`.  If an all-dimensional lift satisfies

        R_(m+1,H)(L_m F)
           <= a R_(m,H)(F)+O(H C_m)

     for one constant `a<4`, then

        nu(k)=(1+o(1)) binom(k,floor(k/2)).

     The proof divides by the exact width ratio

        W_(m+1)/W_m=4-2/(m+2),

     starts the iteration halfway to the target dimension, and uses
     geometric contraction.  Taking
     `H=ceil(sqrt(m omega(m)))`, with `omega -> infinity` and `omega=o(m)`,
     makes both the seam overhead and the binomial tails `o(W_m)`.  This is
     Theorem 2 of `CONTRACTIVE_DEFECT_LIFT.md`.

364. A coordinate-cut double sector transports every inherited flag to at
     most two tagged descendants.  All windows changed at a bounded number
     of cuts are covered by radius-`O(H)` halo words, costing only
     `O(H C_m)` rather than the raw `O(H^2 C_m)` number of crossing windows.
     Thus its inherited coefficient is `a=2`.  The only remaining issue is
     positive/integral completion to a new exact factor.

365. The first proposed completion by two independent Cartesian endpoint
     sectors is count-impossible.  Two such sectors use more one-tag middle
     states than exist.  Even transferring one cap state per endpoint path
     is insufficient, because every internal Catalan path needs a one-tag
     connector.  Hence the completion must be one global rank-transfer
     braid; independent local caps cannot work.

366. `PRISM_SEGMENT_COMPLETION.md` gives the exact global ledger.  For every
     old complementary path

        P=(x_0,y_0,x_1,...,y_(m-1),x_m),  x_m=X\x_0,

     and new coordinates `p,q`, the lower-vertex words

        O_0(P)=(x_0p,y_0,...,y_(m-1),x_mq),

        O_2(P)=(x_0q,(X\y_(m-1))pq,...,(X\y_0)pq,x_mp)

     are complementary Johnson paths.  Across the old factor they cover
     every zero-tag and two-tag lower-middle vertex and the four tagged old
     endpoints.  The uncovered lower support is exactly

        (x_1p,...,x_(m-1)p),  (x_1q,...,x_(m-1)q)

     for every old path.  Its mass identity is

        2(m-1)C_m
          =(m+2)(C_(m+1)-2C_m).

367. The preceding statement is only a lower-support decomposition, not an
     exact middle-level factor.  At the upper-edge level let

        D_m=C_(m+1)-2C_m=2(m-1)C_m/(m+2).

     In the minimum-rung scaffold (one tag change per residual path), the
     provisional zero-tag, one-tag, and two-tag edge occurrence counts minus
     their available target counts are exactly

        (+D_m,-2D_m,+D_m).

     In particular the outer two-tag paths already use every two-tag upper
     colour, whereas each antipodal path in the leftover one-tag prism must
     use at least one two-tag rung.  In the minimum-rung scaffold exact
     completion therefore requires precisely `D_m` net rank transfers

        one zero-tag edge + one two-tag edge
               -> two one-tag edges.

     A residual path may use any odd number of rungs; every extra rung pair
     creates further two-tag excess.  Moreover, define

        g(x_i)=y_(i-1) union y_i

     on the old internal middle vertices.  The zero-tag scaffold contains
     every target exactly when `g` is onto after repetitions are removed.
     In that case retain one representative of each fibre.  The remaining
     `D_m` vertices canonically index both the removable zero-tag edges and
     the matching rungs `x_ip-x_iq`; there is no separate Hall problem at
     this stage.  This correction supersedes any claim that a bare path
     factor of the leftover lower vertices is sufficient.

368. The sharp remaining positive theorem is the **punctured-prism braid
     lemma**: make `g` surjective, choose a fibre transversal, factor the
     residual prism into one-rung antipodal paths with the prescribed
     complementary rung set, make the resulting one-tag colours bijective,
     and preserve the complement endpoint pairing, while cutting the two
     tagged old internal segments only `O(C_m)` times in total.  The atomic
     square

        (U_0-U_1)+(x_ip-x_iq)
          -> (U_0-x_ip)+(U_1-x_iq),
        x_i=U_0 intersect U_1,

     realizes the local sector transfer.  A single such switch between two
     components generally cross-pairs their endpoints, so the unresolved
     issue is global strand topology, not local adjacency.  Such a braid gives

        R_(m+1,H)<=2R_(m,H)+O(HC_m)

     and therefore proves asymptotic optimality.  A cut obstruction forcing
     four inherited repair sections would refute this route.  This is the
     sharp exact-recursive target; the fractional MTF route in the next
     section is the primary asymptotic target.  Isolated finite-`k` score
     improvements are not relevant to either.

## 92. Long-run MTF atoms and a symmetric fractional SCD

369. There is an exact converse to the move-to-front residence obstruction.
     Write a Johnson path as

        S_(t+1)=S_t-{p_t}+{q_t}.

     If the next `d+1` departures are distinct members of `S_t` and the
     preceding `d` departures are distinct nonmembers of `S_t`, put

        L_t=S_t-{p_t,...,p_(t+d-1)}.

     Then one can choose an ordered-partition state beginning

        L_t,
        p_(t+d-1),...,p_t,
        p_(t-1),...,p_(t-d), ...

     and the exact update from time `t` to `t+1` is the single mask
     `L_(t+1)`.  Its prefix chain contains the saturated symmetric chain

        L_t < ... < S_t < ... < S_t+{p_(t-1),...,p_(t-d)}

     of radius `d`.  Thus two-sided long residence is explicitly sufficient,
     not merely necessary, for a deep MTF flag.

370. Map a binary Gray cycle in an orientation cube of a fixed coordinate
     pairing to the corresponding Johnson cycle of middle sets.  If its
     transition sequence has run length `rho`, then every block of `H`
     consecutive starts, at any fixed radius `d` with `H+d<=rho`, gives
     `H` pairwise disjoint symmetric chains and one genuine MTF state path.
     Distinctness has a short coordinate proof: for starts `t<u`, transition
     direction `c_t` is empty in the lower target at `t` but split at `u`,
     while `c_(u-1)` is full in the upper target at `u` but split at `t`.

371. Goddyn--Gvozdjak long-run Gray codes satisfy

        rho(s)>=s-3 log_2 s.

     Hence in the all-split `m`-cube, for every
     `h=O(sqrt(m log m))`, there are atoms of common length

        H=m-3 log_2 m-h=Theta(m)

     for every radius `0<=d<=h`.  Initializing one atom costs at most
     `2d+2` entries and every later chain costs one.  A packing of `p`
     such atoms with `N` chains and `q` uncovered masks gives

        nu(2m)<=N+sum_atoms(2d+1)+q.

     Thus `p=O(W/H)`, `q=o(W)` makes all reset cost `O(Wh/H)=o(W)`.

372. These atoms satisfy the entire SCD ledger fractionally.  Put

        N_q=binom(2m,m-q),
        c_d=N_d-N_(d+1) for d<h,  c_h=N_h.

     Fix one length-`H` atom of each radius and take its full orbit under
     coordinate permutations.  Give the radius-`d` orbit total mass
     `c_d/H`.  A fixed vertex at depth `q` receives mass

        sum_(d>=q) (c_d/H)(H/N_q)=1.

     Therefore the central-band atom hypergraph has an exact fractional
     perfect matching.  The MTF dynamics, rank counts, and interface cost
     are all solved simultaneously at the fractional level.

373. The remaining global theorem is now static: round this symmetric
     fractional matching to pairwise disjoint atoms leaving only `o(W)`
     central-band vertices uncovered.  With
     `h=ceil(sqrt(m log m))`, the masks outside the band are already `o(W)`;
     such a rounding proves `nu(k)=(1+o(1))W(k)`.  Treating an atom as an
     unstructured growing hyperedge is insufficient because adjacent
     chain members retain codegree `Theta(1/m)`.  A proof must expose the
     internal chain/path bundle during absorption.  One fixed coordinate
     pairing is also insufficient at this depth, so the full permutation
     orbit (equivalently a reservoir of pairings) is essential.  Complete
     statements and proofs are in `GLOBAL_LONG_RUN_MTF_ATOMS.md`.

## 93. OR-level atom integrality and the quantitative nibble audit

374. Full atom disjointness is stronger than the OR problem requires.  If
     genuine MTF atoms expose `V_r` distinct masks at rank `r`, then after
     traversing the atoms one may append every missing mask literally.  No
     disjointness between different atoms is needed.  For radius-`d_j`
     atoms with a total of `N` states this gives the exact bound

        nu(2m)<=N+sum_j(2d_j+1)
                    +sum_r(binom(2m,r)-|V_r|).

     Thus it is enough to have `N=W+o(W)`, total reset cost `o(W)`, and
     total rank defect `o(W)`.

375. A long-run atom is an exact Pascal strip.  Writing `A_t^u` for its
     rank-`m+u` member at start `t`, one has

        A_t^u subset A_s^v  iff  0<=s-t<=v-u.

     In the full coordinate-permutation orbit, two same-rank vertices at
     Johnson distance `a` have normalized codegree

        2(H-a)/(H binom(m+u,a)binom(m-u,a)),

     whose maximum is `(2+o(1))/m^2`.  Comparable vertices at depths
     `u<v`, `ell=v-u`, have normalized codegree

        [H(ell+1)-binom(ell+1,2)]
             /[H binom(m-u,ell)].

     Adjacent chain ranks therefore have intrinsic normalized codegree
     `(2+o(1))/m`.

376. No currently cited generic matching theorem closes this gap.  The
     earlier claim that Grable's theorem rounded one growing row was wrong:
     its leftover factor is roughly

        ((H Delta_2 log|V|)/D)^(1/(2H-1+o(H))),

     which tends to one for every useful `H->infinity`.  The 2025
     Gould--Kelly theorem assumes a fixed-uniformity hierarchy and gives an
     error `B^(-1+gamma)log^A D`.  In fact the complete atom has a stronger
     high-order obstruction than the adjacent-rank pair bound: it exposes
     `H(2h+1)` masks while using only `O(H+h)` active coordinates, so its
     full-edge codegree forces

        B <= exp(O(log(m)/h+log(m)/H))=1+o(1)

     in the intended range.  Hence a custom sparse-certificate or
     overlapping chain-exposed construction is genuinely necessary; this
     is not an omitted black-box citation.

377. Deep central ranks can nevertheless be removed unconditionally.  Take

        h=ceil(sqrt(m log m)), H=m/log m, delta=1/log m

     and `delta W/H` independent random radius-`h` atoms.  Their total MTF
     cost is `o(W)`.  A depth-`q` target is missed with probability at most

        exp(-delta W/binom(2m,m-q)).

     Therefore all ranks with

        |q|>=q_0=ceil(sqrt(8m log log m))

     have only `o(W)` misses in total for some deterministic choice of the
     reservoir.  The primary integrality problem is reduced to the shallow
     strip `|q|<=q_0`.

378. Oriented radius-`d` chains have a state-free rotor.  If a chain is

        (L;z_1,...,z_(2d);R),

     then for any `x in L,y in R` its canonical successor is

        (L-x+y; x,z_1,...,z_(2d-1); R-y+z_(2d)).

     This directed graph is `(m-d)^2`-regular in both directions, and every
     arc is one exact MTF update.  The sharpened remaining theorem is to
     choose `W+o(W)` chain centres covering the shallow strip with total
     defect `o(W)` and with a rotor path cover having `o(W)` initialization
     cost.  Full proofs and the corrected theorem ledger are in
     `GLOBAL_MTF_ATOM_INTEGRALITY.md`.

## 94. Sparse-checkpoint and SCD-Hamilton no-go theorems

379. Selecting only `s` rank rows from each `H`-state Pascal strip produces
     a certificate edge of size `sH` with only `O(H+h)` active coordinates.
     Its full-codegree parameter satisfies

        B_s <= exp(O((H+h)log(m)/(sH)))=m^(O(1/s))

     when `H>>h`.  Thus a fixed number of checkpoints retains a polynomial
     parameter.  If every unchecked rank is within distance `g` of a
     checkpoint, however, then `s>=(2h+1)/(g+1)` and

        log B_s=O((g+1)log(m)/h).

     For `h>>log m` and bounded `g`, this is again `B_s=1+o(1)`.  This is an
     exact density tradeoff, not a weakness of a particular nibble theorem.

380. Checkpoint injectivity does not force an omitted row.  For any `r`-set
     `S` and any `t<=min(r,2m-r)`, choose distinct `x_i in S` and distinct
     `y_i notin S`.  The `t` saturated chains

        S-x_i subset S subset S+y_i

     have pairwise distinct lower checkpoint endpoints and pairwise distinct
     upper checkpoint endpoints, but all funnel through the same middle
     mask.  Any sparse-certificate theorem must therefore add genuine
     pseudorandomness, expansion, or absorption; intermediate coverage is
     not a deterministic shadow consequence.

381. There is also a precise obstruction to importing the known Hamilton
     cycle containing the Greene--Kleitman SCD.  If a saturated chain is

        C=(L;z_1,z_2,...,z_d),

     then the Greene--Kleitman first-star operation is

        f(C)=(L+z_2;z_3,...,z_d).

     No single move-to-front update can take a state exposing `C` to one
     exposing `f(C)`, or conversely.  In the forward direction, `z_2` must
     be moved ahead of the unselected `z_1`, after which `z_1` necessarily
     contaminates the next prefix before `z_3`.  In the reverse direction,
     MTF preserves the old order `z_2` before `z_1`.  By contrast, deleting
     the last two stars is one-update compatible: MTF is intrinsically a
     suffix-queue operation, not a prefix-deletion operation.

382. The Gregor--Micka--Mutze recursive chain ordering replaces essentially
     every parent chain by

        A=*C*, f(A), f(ell(A)), ell(A)

     up to reversal.  It therefore has two forbidden first-star boundaries
     per positive-length parent.  Since

        binom(2m-2,m-1)/binom(2m,m)=1/4+o(1),

     this gives `(1/2-o(1))W` one-update barriers.  Consequently the known
     SCD-compatible Hamilton cycle cannot be read as a `W+o(W)` rotor path;
     repairing its barriers separately costs `Omega(W)`.  A useful SCD must
     instead admit an ordering with only `o(W)` prefix-deletion barriers.
     Full proofs are in `SPARSE_CHECKPOINT_SCD_AUDIT.md`.

## 95. Exact ECO locality and the fixed-coordinate obstruction

383. The MSW flip permutation is natural under insertion of a Dyck peak in
     any gap.  If `I_g(w)` is obtained from a Dyck word `w` by inserting
     `10`, then the two new coordinate labels occur consecutively in
     `rho(I_g(w))`; deleting them recovers `rho(w)` in exactly the old
     order.  Their order is `(p,q)` when the height of the insertion gap is
     odd and `(q,p)` when it is even.  Thus every ECO child is literally a
     parent MSW path with one adjacent two-letter seam in flip order.

384. This locality is path-dependent and cannot be read as a lift by one
     common new coordinate pair.  The insertion gap, hence the two deleted
     physical labels, varies with the Dyck word and ECO site.  Relabelling
     every child separately destroys targetwise shadow provenance.  More
     sharply, if every child inserted the same fixed pair, then each path
     would have all but at most one lower-middle vertex in the one-tag
     sector and no lower-middle vertex in the two-tag sector.  The nonempty
     two-tag rectangle would therefore be uncovered.  A raw ECO inheritance
     has Catalan growth coefficient `4`, not the strict coefficient `<4`
     required by the contractive-defect theorem.

385. There is no Catalan-mass obstruction to repairing this failure.  If
     `ell(w)` is the final-descent length, then

        sum_(w in D_m) ell(w)^2 <= 52 Cat_m.

     Hence even `O(ell(w)^2)` local work per parent costs only `O(Cat_m)` in
     total.  The exact missing all-dimensional lemma is an endpoint-safe
     paired antipodal braid which globalizes the varying inserted coordinate
     roles while preserving complementary endpoints and upper colours.  A
     proof of that lemma with old-defect multiplicity below four would feed
     directly into the contractive-defect theorem and imply
     `nu(k)=(1+o(1))W(k)`.  Full proofs and the corrected scope are in
     `MSW_ECO_INSERTION_AUDIT.md`.

## 96. Critical Catalan contraction and the reduced Mütze--Weber gate

386. A constant inherited coefficient below four is sufficient but not
     necessary.  Put `C_m=Cat_m` and

        W_m=binom(2m+1,m)=(2m+1)C_m.

     If an exact-factor lift satisfies

        E_(m+1,H) <= (C_(m+1)/C_m) E_(m,H) + B_(m,H),

     then the normalized inherited coefficient is exactly

        [(C_(m+1)/C_m)W_m]/W_(m+1)=(2m+1)/(2m+3).

     These factors telescope rather than contract geometrically.  Starting
     at `j_0`, the exact bound is

        E_(M,H)/W_M
        <= [(2j_0+1)/(2M+1)] E_(j_0,H)/W_(j_0)
           +[1/(2M+1)] sum_(m=j_0)^(M-1) B_(m,H)/C_(m+1).

     Since the initial normalized defect is at most `O(sqrt(j_0))`, one may
     take `H=sqrt(M log M)` and `j_0=M^(3/5)`.  Therefore the critical
     Catalan rate still proves `nu(k)=(1+o(1))W(k)` provided

        (1/M)sum B_(m,H)/C_m=o(1).

     This is a genuinely different sufficient route: the inherited
     multiplier may be `4-O(1/m)`, but the uncharged distinct seam defect
     must be sub-Catalan on average.  The proof and the exact ECO charging
     target are in `CRITICAL_CATALAN_LIFT.md`.

387. The literal two-outer-family MSW lift nevertheless fails already at
     depth one.  Its terminal and primitive Catalan families use different
     old-coordinate embeddings.  Under a fixed prism split, residual edges
     have at least one new tag and cannot repair the explicit zero-tag hole
     `T_m` in the unchanged MSW second-upper map.  Thus neither the strict
     coefficient-two recurrence nor the critical charging recurrence has
     been proved by raw ECO locality.  The all-dimensional obstruction and
     exact flag tables are in `MSW_OUTER_DEPTH_ONE_DICHOTOMY.md`.

388. The Mütze--Weber dangling-path recursion remains the clean positive
     completion because it owns every lower vertex and upper colour before
     joining its exposed ports.  Its formerly stated refinement target had
     two requirements: complementary endpoints and equal path lengths.  The
     second is automatic.  A Johnson path between complementary
     `(m+1)`-sets of a `(2m+2)`-set has at least `m+1` edges, hence at least
     `m+2` lower vertices.  There are `C_(m+1)` paths and exactly

        binom(2m+2,m+1)=(m+2)C_(m+1)

     lower vertices in total, so equality holds on every path.  Therefore
     the sole structural gate is now an `O(C_m)`-switch antipodalization of
     the published dangling system; geodesicity and exact wreath length
     then follow for free.  The updated theorem is in
     `MUTZE_WEBER_PRISM_TRANSLATION.md`.

## 97. Endpoint-sector obstruction and the exact signed T-join gate

389. The endpoint multiset of the published Mütze--Weber central recursion
     is not complement-stable.  Write `C=C_m` and
     `D=C_(m+1)-2C_m`.  Its three disjoint terms contribute endpoints as
     follows:

        U_m o 00:       2D endpoints in sector 00,
        P_m o 10:       2C endpoints in sector 10,
        mixed P':       C endpoints in 00 and C endpoints in 01.

     Hence the exact sector vector is

        (n_00,n_10,n_01,n_11)=(2D+C,2C,C,0).

     Complementation exchanges `00<->11` and `10<->01`, so no internal
     tail permutation preserving the endpoint set can produce complementary
     paths.  At least `D+C` endpoint replacements are necessary: the initial
     signed imbalances are `2D+C` and `C`, and one replacement can reduce
     their total absolute value by at most two.  Thus `Theta(C_m)` is both
     necessary and the desired sufficient scale.

390. Endpoint movement has an exact capacitated signed-T-join formulation.
     Let `H_0` be the published edge set, `T_0` its lower endpoint set, and
     choose a complement-invariant target set `T` of the same cardinality.
     For an old edge take `x_e in {-1,0}` and for a nonold edge take
     `x_e in {0,1}`.  Put

        b(v)=+1  for v in T_0 minus T,
        b(v)=-1  for v in T minus T_0,
        b(v)=0   otherwise, including every upper vertex.

     Then `H=H_0+x` has degree two at every upper vertex, degree one exactly
     on `T`, and degree two at every other lower vertex if and only if

        sum_(e incident v) x_e=b(v)

     at every vertex.  The bipartite incidence matrix is totally unimodular.
     Every integral solution decomposes into alternating trails whose ends
     are endpoint-status changes, plus alternating cycles.  An old endpoint
     being internalized has a blue inserted terminal edge; an old internal
     vertex becoming an endpoint has a red deleted terminal edge.  Trails
     may join equal or opposite endpoint types.  Therefore fractional
     integrality is not the remaining issue; the support of this T-join
     must be `O(C_m)` for the OR seam budget.

391. Degree balance does not by itself force the correct path components.
     For complement-invariant `T`, add the artificial matching

        M_T={{v,bar(v)}:v in T}.

     The graph `(H_0+x) union M_T` is 2-regular.  The switched system is a
     family of complementary paths if and only if every cycle of this
     augmented 2-factor contains exactly one edge of `M_T`.  A cycle with
     zero matching edges is an unwanted closed component of `H`; a cycle
     with several matching edges joins several non-antipodal path
     components.  Exactly one closes one path at its complementary endpoints.

392. The surviving all-dimensional theorem is therefore exact: construct
     a complement-invariant `T` and a signed T-join `x` of support
     `O(C_m)` such that every augmented cycle contains exactly one antipodal
     edge, and retain two-copy bulk shadow provenance away from those cuts.
     Lemma 4.1 of `MUTZE_WEBER_ENDPOINT_TJOIN.md` then forces every path to
     have the exact wreath length automatically.  Halo compression charges
     the `O(C_m)` changed boundaries by `O(HC_m)`.  This is an endpoint-moving
     alternating-trail/cycle-control problem; fixed-endpoint flippable tail
     swaps are formally ruled out.

## 98. Endpoint monodromy rules out the natural paired-alpha schedule

393. Endpoint-safe segment surgery has a nonabelian invariant which is not
     visible in the signed T-join degree equations.  If successive
     transversal boundaries reconnect `r` oriented path strands by
     permutations `pi_1,...,pi_h`, then the path beginning on strand `i`
     ends on terminal strand

        Pi(i),             Pi=pi_h ... pi_1.

     For distinct complementary endpoint pairs, the surgery preserves every
     pair if and only if `Pi=id`.  Thus the degree boundary is abelian, while
     endpoint ownership retains the full permutation product.

394. An MNW `alpha` 6-cycle acts on its three path tails by a 3-cycle `pi`.
     Its natural antipodal translate preserves the orientation of the three
     strands and acts by the same `pi`, not by `pi^(-1)`.  The proposed
     two-boundary braid therefore has monodromy

        pi^2=pi^(-1) != id.

     Reverse-complement is the natural source of the inverse local picture,
     but it acts on another root triple.  The original support

        {1w11000,1w10100,1w10010}

     has final-descent multiset `{3,2,1}`, whereas its mirrored support

        {10110 mu(w) 0,11010 mu(w) 0,11100 mu(w) 0}

     has the constant final-descent value `ell(mu(w))+1`.  Hence the two
     supports are never equal; an inverse boundary is not available on the
     same three unchanged strands.

395. This gives a general leaf obstruction.  A nonempty loose hypertree of
     static `alpha` boundaries has a path strand occurring in exactly one
     boundary, so that strand has nontrivial endpoint monodromy.  Adding one
     natural antipodal copy of every tree hyperedge still acts twice by the
     same 3-cycle at a leaf, and `pi^2` remains nontrivial.  Consequently the
     loose spanning trees used to merge middle-level or odd-graph factor
     cycles cannot serve as endpoint-safe factor refinements.

396. The signed T-join in Section 97 must therefore be supported on an
     endpoint-balanced hypergraph circulation, not on a tree of static
     flipping charts.  Every moved strand must lie on a dependency whose
     ordered permutation product is the identity.  The remaining options
     are a genuine inverse boundary created after preparatory switches,
     three compatibly phased copies of a 3-cycle, or a cyclic noncommutative
     chart schedule.  Full proofs are in
     `PAIRED_ALPHA_BRAID_OBSTRUCTION.md`.

## 99. Contracting the all-zero MW lexical matching gives almost no MTF edges

397. Mütze--Weber prove that the all-zero middle-level 2-factor contains
     every edge of `rev(LM)`, the central matching of the reversed
     Greene--Kleitman SCD.  More generally, every dangling path in
     `P_(2m)(m,m+1)` contains all of the corresponding reversed-lexical
     matching edges.  On each dangling path

        x_0,y_0,x_1,y_1,...,y_(s-1),x_s,

     the matching pairs `y_i` with `x_(i+1)`; `x_0=F(P)` is the unique
     unmatched lower vertex and is a radius-zero SCD chain.  Contracting
     therefore gives `Cat_m` paths through all

        W_m=binomial(2m,m)

     reversed-GK chains exactly once.  This support statement is exact but
     does not survive the MTF state test.

398. Write a reversed-GK template as

        u_0 * u_1 * ... * u_(2d),

     with each `u_i` Dyck.  A direct induction through the actual MW
     recursion, combined with the exact quotient-chain/fence criterion,
     gives the complete transition classification.  A forward contracted
     edge is one-update compatible exactly when its target has radius one
     and terminal block `u_2` is nonempty.  The reverse edge is compatible
     exactly for the first edge of a dangling path, equivalently when the
     forward target has radius one and `u_2` is empty.  Radius at least two
     fails in both directions, and no edge passes both directions for
     `m>=2`.

399. With `C(z)=1+zC(z)^2`, the compatible forward edges number

        A_m=[z^(m-2)] C(z)^4
           =binomial(2m-2,m-2)-binomial(2m-2,m-4)
           =W_m*2(m-1)/((m+1)(m+2)).

     The compatible reverse edges are the `Cat_m=W_m/(m+1)` first edges.
     Hence even after orienting every boundary independently in its favorable
     direction, the number of usable underlying adjacencies is only

        U_m=A_m+Cat_m
           =W_m*3m/((m+1)(m+2))=O(W_m/m).

     Any MTF path cover constrained to the contracted MW paths has at least

        W_m-U_m=(1-o(1))W_m

     components.  Thus the hoped-for `Cat_m` reset count is false: almost
     every obstruction is internal to a dangling path.  Arbitrary bottom/top
