     ordered partitions and path reversals are already included in this
     negative result.  Full definitions, the recursion/fence audit, and the
     Catalan enumeration are in `MW_CONTRACTED_SCD_MTF_AUDIT.md`.

400. A literal two-step repair cannot improve the known general constant.
     The `Cat_m` support paths contain `W_m-Cat_m` adjacencies, only
     `U_m=O(W_m/m)` of which have distance one.  Any traversal retaining
     this chain order and inserting auxiliary states at bad boundaries has
     length at least

        W_m+(W_m-Cat_m-U_m)=(2-o(1))W_m.

     Thus even proving distance two for every remaining boundary would be
     weaker than the existing `(sqrt(2)+o(1))W_m` construction.  The
     canonical nested-prefix repair peels target stars one update at a time;
     the exact radius count is

        N_(m,d)=[z^(m-d)] C(z)^(2d+1),

     and the typical radius grows on the `sqrt(m)` scale.  An absorber can
     evade this lower accounting only if its intermediate states expose
     other, not-yet-visited SCD chains and thereby change the MW order
     globally.

## 100. The canonical MSW antipodal factor is super-Catalan-far from MW

401. Let `n=m+1`, let `H_0=P_(2n)(n,n+1)` be the all-zero Mütze--Weber
     dangling-path factor, and let `H_CF` be the canonical
     Mütze--Standke--Wiechert Chung--Feller factor whose paths run from
     every Dyck root `w` to `bar(w)`.  Although `H_CF` has exactly the
     desired antipodal endpoints, it is not a sparse refinement of `H_0`:

        |H_0 triangle H_CF| >= 2(n-1) Cat_n
                             = (8+o(1)) m Cat_m.

     Thus the literal difference is an `Omega(m Cat_m)`-support signed
     T-join, not the required `O(Cat_m)` one.  Bounded-size local switches
     need `Omega(m Cat_m)` applications.  Catalan-many switches of length
     `Theta(m)` are not excluded, but still have the wrong edge-support and
     seam-halo cost.

402. The proof uses one published matching and one new exact crossing
     lemma.  Put

        R_n=rev(LM_(2n)(n,n+1)).

     Mütze--Weber prove `R_n subset H_0`, and `|R_n|=n Cat_n`.  If a Dyck
     word has first-return decomposition `w=1u0v`, number the edges of its
     MSW path from zero and define

        a(10v)=1,
        a(1u0v)=1+a(mu(u))  for u nonempty,
        mu(u)=overline(rev(u)).

     Direct substitution of the MSW flip recursion

        rho(1u0v)=(d, d-rho(mu(u)), 1, d+rho(v)), d=|u|+2,

     into the reversed-parenthesis matching test proves that the unique
     `R_n` edge of the root path `P(w)` is edge `a(w)`.  Hence

        |R_n intersect H_CF|=Cat_n.

     Since both factors have `2n Cat_n` edges and
     `|H_0 minus R_n|=n Cat_n`, their intersection has size at most
     `(n+1)Cat_n`, giving the displayed symmetric-difference bound.

403. The exact complementary-matching recurrence now proves the sharper
     identity

        |H_0 intersect H_CF|=3 Cat_n,
        |H_0 triangle H_CF|=2(2n-3) Cat_n,

     with exactly three common edges on every individual MSW root path.
     The complete recurrences and the resulting Catalan long-braid theorem
     are in `MW_MSW_CATALAN_BRAID.md`; the independent remote audit is
     `mw_msw_difference_probe.cpp`.

## 101. The MW-to-MSW difference has only Catalan-many alternating pieces

404. Write the first-return decomposition of a Dyck root as `w=1u0v` and
     number its canonical MSW path edges from zero.  The three common MW
     edges have indices

        0, a(w), b(w),

     where

        a(10v)=1,
        a(1u0v)=1+a(mu(u))                    (u nonempty),

     and, for semilength at least two,

        b(10v)=2+a(v)                         (v nonempty),
        b(1100v)=3,
        b(1u0v)=1+b(mu(u))                    (|u|>=4).

     The first nonzero index is the unique crossing with
     `R_n=rev(LM)`.  The other is the unique noninitial crossing with the
     complementary MW matching `K_n=H_0 minus R_n`.  Simultaneous
     substitution of the MSW flip recursion and the actual all-zero MW
     three-sector recursion proves

        E(P(w)) intersect R_n={e_(a(w))},
        E(P(w)) intersect K_n={e_0,e_(b(w))},
        0<a(w)<b(w)<2n.

405. Colour `H_0 minus H_CF` red and `H_CF minus H_0` blue.  Removing the
     three common edges, including edge zero, leaves at most three blue
     path segments per MSW root.  Every red edge meets a blue edge at its
     upper endpoint, because both factors have degree two there and hence
     red and blue degrees agree.  Therefore

        #components(H_0 triangle H_CF)<=3 Cat_n.

     Orient red edges lower-to-upper and blue edges upper-to-lower.  This is
     a directed balanced graph except at the endpoint symmetric difference,
     which has at most `2 Cat_n` vertices.  Directed Euler decomposition in
     every weak component gives at most

        Cat_n open alternating trails + 3 Cat_n alternating circuits.

     Thus `H_0 triangle H_CF` is an exact signed T-join with at most
     `4 Cat_n` long alternating pieces.  The edge support is
     `Theta(n Cat_n)`, but the piece/seam count is Catalan.  Consequently
     Section 100 rules out only a sparse-edge refinement; it does **not**
     rule out a Catalan long-segment braid.

406. Toggling all pieces gives the canonical complementary factor, so the
     endpoint and one-antipodal-edge conditions hold at the end.  What is
     not yet proved is that the Euler pieces admit a dynamically legal
     schedule and fixed-coordinate target provenance.  Cutting all MW paths
     at the `3 Cat_n` common edges gives at most `4 Cat_n` maximal red path
     sections; the two noninitial cuts on every MSW path give at most
     `3 Cat_n` blue sections.  Thus the simultaneous replacement has at
     most `7 Cat_n` factor-contiguous sections globally.  The unresolved
     provenance issue is narrower: each blue section inherits its parent
     after deleting a path-dependent ECO coordinate pair, not one common
     fixed pair.  Euler pairing controls endpoint trails, whereas this
     section ledger controls topological cuts.  Full proofs are in
     `MW_MSW_CATALAN_BRAID.md`.

## 102. Alpha switches generate all even monodromy but cannot move endpoints

407. For a connected 3-uniform alpha-support hypergraph, the oriented
     3-cycles on its hyperedges generate the full alternating group on its
     vertices.  This follows by adjoining hyperedges along a connected
     order and conjugating each new 3-cycle by the already generated
     alternating group.  Hence every connected alpha-support component has
     formal monodromy group `A(U)`.  MNW's spanning-tree theorem for the
     complete family `Psi_m` must not be used to claim global `A_(Cat_m)`
     without another check: `Psi_m` also contains constant base patterns of
     different support sizes, whose strand permutations may be odd.  This
     is only a formal group statement in any case; overlapping geometric
     charts need not remain dynamically flippable after earlier switches.

408. Every alpha switch is an alternating circuit.  Its signed boundary is
     zero and it preserves the degree, hence endpoint status, of every
     physical vertex.  The published MW endpoint sectors are

        (2D+C,2C,C,0),

     which are not complement-invariant.  Therefore no word in alpha
     switches, of any length, can perform the endpoint-moving part of
     antipodalization.  Alpha cycles can only be used after a nonzero-boundary
     signed T-join, such as the long pieces in Section 101.

409. After endpoint repair, orient paths `s_i -> t_i` and let `kappa` satisfy
     `t_(kappa(i))=bar(s_i)`.  If a switch word has terminal monodromy `pi`,
     the augmented path-plus-antipodal cycles are the cycles of
     `kappa^(-1)pi`.  Hence every augmented cycle has exactly one antipodal
     edge if and only if

        pi=kappa.

     On each connected alpha component, the formal alpha group can achieve
     this precisely when `kappa` preserves the component and restricts to
     an even permutation.  Dynamic validity and an `O(Cat_m)` word remain
     separate gates; a verified odd non-alpha generator could remove only
     the parity gate, not the endpoint-boundary obstruction.

410. The finite endpoint matching at Johnson distance three cannot persist
     asymptotically.  Every old last endpoint has form `A 01 B` with `A,B`
     Dyck.  For

        L_n=1^(n-1) 0^(n-1) 01,

     any complement-Dyck word has at most `floor((n-1)/2)` ones in its first
     `n-1` positions.  Thus

        d_J(L_n,overline(D_n))>=ceil((n-1)/2).

     The distance-three matching observed through fourteen bits is a finite
     coincidence and must fail starting at sixteen bits.  An explicit
     all-dimensional endpoint bijection is

        A 01 B -> overline(1 A 0 B),

     but its trails are necessarily long in the worst case.  The group,
     boundary, parity, and distance proofs are in
     `ALPHA_ENDPOINT_MONODROMY.md`.

## 103. Fixed top-level sector provenance needs no special Euler pairing

411. In the induction from `2n-2` to `2n` coordinates, fix the final two
     coordinates as tags.  The all-zero MW central factor has exactly the
     following possible tag edges: `C_(n-1)` edges of `M^S` flipping the
     final coordinate and `2C_(n-1)` edges of `M^{FL}` flipping the first
     new coordinate.  Thus it has at most `3C_(n-1)` tag edges.  Every
     canonical MSW root path flips every coordinate exactly once, so the
     canonical factor has exactly `2C_n` edges flipping the fixed tag pair.

412. Start from any at-most-`4C_n` directed Euler decomposition in Section
     101.  Cut each alternating trail immediately before and after every
     tag-flipping edge.  Every surviving piece either lies wholly in one of
     the four fixed two-bit sectors or is one tag edge.  The total number of
     pieces is at most

        4C_n+2(2C_n+3C_(n-1)) <= 11C_n.

     Hence an `O(C_n)` fixed-top-level-sector decomposition exists for
     **every** Euler transition pairing; recursively choosing the degree-four
     transitions is not needed for this cut count.  The remaining provenance
     gate is more specific: a constant-fixed-tag MSW piece need not project
     to a segment of one old MSW path after deleting the fixed pair, because
     its ECO-inserted coordinate pair is path-dependent.  The next theorem
     must solve this coordinate-consistent projection problem inside the
     blue pieces.  Proofs are in `MW_MSW_CATALAN_BRAID.md`, Section 9.

413. The sector-local split is not ordinary seam-halo inheritance.  A
     literal cut-and-reconnect operation at `s` old edges preserves every
     other old internal edge.  Since

        |H_0 minus H_CF|=(2n-3)C_n,

     any pure old-segment reconnection producing the canonical factor needs
     at least `(2n-3)C_n` cuts.  The `O(C_n)` alternating pieces replace
     bulk transitions rather than retain them.  They help provenance only
     if each long blue section has a certified window-carrying coordinate
     map to an old section.  Path-local ECO deletion supplies such a map for
     a varying coordinate pair; globalizing those maps in fixed coordinates
     is the precise surviving gate.  This no-go is Proposition 6 of
     `MW_MSW_CATALAN_BRAID.md`.

## 101. Exact multi-step MTF distance and the contracted-MW two-step no-go

404. There is an exact extension of the one-update quotient-chain
     criterion.  Let

        D=(A,A+f_1,...,A+f_1+...+f_g)

     be a target chain.  If `A` is nonempty, put

        K_t=A union {f_1,...,f_(t-1)}  (1<=t<=g+1),

     while for `A=empty` put

        K_t={f_1,...,f_t}  (1<=t<=g).

     The minimum number `delta(C,D)` of arbitrary-mask MTF updates between
     the full exposing fibers of two chains satisfies

        delta(C,D)<=t
        iff
        C-K_t and D-K_t are cross-nested.

     Necessity follows by writing the surviving blocks of `t` MTF updates
     in reverse chronological order.  They form an initial segment of the
     target fiber and are all deleted by `K_t`; the residual source state
     consequently exposes both quotient chains.  For sufficiency, extend
     the two cross-nested quotients to one singleton permutation, then move
     `f_(t-1),...,f_1,A` to the front (or `f_t,...,f_1` when `A` is empty).
     Thus exact MTF distance is the first target prefix whose deletion
     removes the quotient crossing.  The full proof is Theorem 2 of
     `MW_CONTRACTED_DISTANCE_AUDIT.md`.

405. Applying the `t=2` test to the actual all-zero MW recursion gives a
     sharper candidate no-go than Section 99.  Remote exact reconstruction
     through `m=7` gives, among the `W_m-Cat_m` forward contracted
     boundaries,

        distance 1: A_m=W_m*2(m-1)/((m+1)(m+2)),
        distance 2: Cat_m,
        distance >=3: W_m*m(m-1)/((m+1)(m+2)).

     Hence a `1-O(1/m)` fraction already fails the strongest existential
     two-update fiber test, and the raw transition mass is at least

        W_m*(3m^2+m+2)/((m+1)(m+2))=(3-o(1))W_m.

     `MW_CONTRACTED_DISTANCE_AUDIT.md` states the strengthened two-prefix
     splice invariant which proves this distribution by induction.  The
     general prefix-erasure theorem above is fully proved; before treating
     the all-`m` numerical distribution as an independent theorem, audit
     that splice invariant against the published MW recursion.  Even if it
     passes, intermediate states could help only through a separate global
     theorem charging them injectively to other unvisited SCD chains.

## 102. ECO seam targets do not become sub-Catalan by deduplication

406. The terminal ECO family alone has Catalan-many distinct seam values.
     If `rho(w)=(r_1,...,r_(2m))`, its parent and terminal-child wreath
     orders are

        C(w)=(z,r_2,r_4,...,r_(2m),r_1,r_3,...,r_(2m-1)),

        C(w10)=(z,r_2,...,r_(2m),p,
                   r_1,r_3,...,r_(2m-1),q).

     Removing the inserted coordinates `p,q` leaves old arcs of lengths
     `m` and `m+1`.  A child lower depth-one value is a length-`m` cyclic
     interval, so exactly

        1+2=3

     such values avoid both inserted coordinates.  They are three parent
     middle intervals.  Because the parent MSW wreaths partition the middle
     layer, over all `w in D_m` these are `3 Cat_m` pairwise distinct masks.
     Their complements give `3 Cat_m` distinct upper seam masks containing
     both new coordinates.  At lower depth `j`, the corresponding raw count
     per terminal child is exactly `2j+1`.

407. Therefore the critical Catalan lift cannot put every unresolved ECO
     seam into its exceptional term and hope that duplicate target values
     reduce `Theta(Cat_m)` occurrences to `o(Cat_m)`: distinctness already
     costs `3 Cat_m` at depth one.  This does not refute the critical lift,
     because the displayed masks are actual windows and hence are covered.
     It forces a targetwise ledger: certify covered seams for free, charge a
     genuinely missing seam to a specified old missing target, and budget
     only the remaining genuinely missing masks.  The theorem and its exact
     scope are in `CRITICAL_ECO_SEAM_DISTINCTNESS_NO_GO.md`.

## 103. Cyclic-interval lifting is the hard bridge; initialization is not

408. An exact cyclic-interval SCD resolution has no hidden asymptotic seam
     cost, even when its radii are placed adversarially among the wreaths.
     Put `n=2m+1`, `W=binom(n,m)`, `B=W/n`, and let `H_pi` be the maximum
     chain radius in order `pi`.  Since exactly

        N_q=binom(n,m-q)

     SCD chains have radius at least `q`,

        sum_pi H_pi
          <= sum_(q=1)^m min{B,N_q}
          = O(W sqrt(log(n)/n)).

     The last estimate follows from

        N_q/W
          = product_(i=0)^(q-1) (m-i)/(m+2+i)
          <= exp(-q(q+1)/n).

409. One order with maximum radius `H<m` is linearized by writing the
     cyclic intervals

        E_j=I_pi(j,m-H),  j=0,...,n-1,

     and repeating `E_0,...,E_(2H)`.  Consecutive ORs satisfy

        union_(s=0)^r E_(j+s)=I_pi(j,m-H+r),

     so this one word covers every assigned chain in the order, regardless
     of the individual radii.  The `H=m` order is handled by the singleton
     cyclic word.  Concatenating all orders therefore gives

        nu(n) <= W+O(W sqrt(log(n)/n)).

     The same proof allows `o(W)` uncovered masks, appended literally.  Thus
     any exact or approximate cyclic-interval resolution immediately has
     the desired constant-one OR cost; resets are not a separate theorem.

410. The known necklace-poset SCD cannot provide those wreath bundles by
     literal coordinate-rotation lifting.  If the lower-middle members of
     one aperiodic lifted quotient chain are

        {sigma^t X:t in Z_n}

     and can be reordered into one tight wreath, then two rotations must be
     Johnson adjacent, so

        |X triangle sigma^a X|=2

     for some `a ne 0`.  If `g=gcd(n,a)` and `L=n/g`, the number of binary
     words satisfying this for fixed `a` is at most

        g binom(L,2) 2^g.

     Summing over `a` gives `O(n^4 2^(n/2))=o(W)`.  Periodic words are also
     `o(W)`.  Hence only `o(W)` chains from a literal necklace lift can lie
     in cyclic-interval bundles.  This obstruction occurs before the MTF
     threading obstruction: almost every rotation orbit is not even an
     unordered wreath.

411. Conversely, the exact MSW odd-graph factor supplies the horizontal
     wreaths but not the vertical chains.  For pointed starts `v`, define

        L_q(v)=I_pi(j,m-q),
        U_q(v)=I_pi(j,m+1+q).

     A factor extends to a cyclic-interval SCD exactly when there are nested
     start sets

        Omega=A_0 superset A_1 superset ... superset A_m

     such that the labelled edges `L_q(v)U_q(v)`, `v in A_q`, form a
     perfect matching at every depth.  Taking an arbitrary ordinary SCD
     first creates no matching freedom: its lower-middle member uniquely
     determines its pointed wreath start, and even its central upper member
     must already agree.  The unchanged MSW factor fails this vertical gate
     at depth one in the explicit nine-coordinate example.  Thus necklace
     SCDs and MSW solve orthogonal halves; the exact missing theorem is a
     global re-bundling/nested-rainbow compatibility theorem.  Full proofs
     and the initialization audit are in
     `CYCLIC_INTERVAL_LIFT_INITIALIZATION_AUDIT.md`.

## 104. The canonical MSW defect fails the critical ECO cardinality gate

412. Let `L_m` be the number of missing rank-`m-1` targets in the
     unchanged MSW wreath factor on `2m+1` coordinates.  Complementation
     gives the same number of missing rank-`m+2` targets, so the two-sided
     depth-one defect is `E_m=2L_m`.  Any proposed critical recurrence

        E_(m+1) <= (C_(m+1)/C_m) E_m + B_m

     has the unavoidable cardinality residual

        B_m >= 2 max(0,L_(m+1)-(C_(m+1)/C_m)L_m).

     From the exact data through `m=12`, this lower bound divided by `C_m`
     is

        2.857, 3.592, 4.015, 4.284,
        4.476, 4.624, 4.742, 4.840

     for `m=4,...,11`.  It is already a growing Catalan multiple before
     any Hall obstruction is examined.

413. This has an exact asymptotic interpretation.  Put

        N_m=binom(2m+1,m-1),  p_m=L_m/N_m,  e_m=E_m/C_m.

     Then

        e_m=2p_m*m(2m+1)/(m+2)=(4+o(1))m p_m.

     Dividing the critical recurrence by `C_(m+1)` makes it telescope:

        e_(m+1) <= e_m + B_m/C_(m+1).

     Therefore a Cesaro-sub-Catalan error,

        (1/M) sum_(m<M) B_m/C_m -> 0,

     would force `p_m->0`.  The computed miss fractions instead increase
     monotonically from `0.0476` at `m=4` to `0.2465` at `m=12`.  This is
     not an all-dimensional disproof because positive limiting density has
     not been proved, but it makes the targetwise Hall programme for the
     **unchanged** canonical factor cardinally implausible.  The exact
     formulas and proof are in `MSW_CRITICAL_CARDINALITY_AUDIT.md`.

414. The big-picture target should consequently move one level earlier.
     Prove positive limiting miss density to close the canonical branch, or
     globally re-bundle/switch a positive-density family of wreaths so that
     the new first-shadow defect is `o(N_m)` *before* applying ECO.  Having
     linearly many deletion parents per individual hole cannot repair an
     excess in the total number of child holes.

## 105. Blue-section coordinate provenance has an exact Catalan atlas

415. The path-dependent ECO coordinate pair does not create a super-Catalan
     number of coordinate sections.  For a parent word of length `2n-2`,
     insertion at gap `g` uses the fixed physical pair

        P_g={g+1,g+2}

     and the fixed increasing injection which skips that pair.  Thus there
     are only `2n-1` deletion-chart types.  Cutting each canonical MSW path
     at its three common MW edges leaves at most three ordinary path
     intervals.  The tight-wreath order is the `+2` order on the odd
     omitted-label cycle; an ordinary cyclic interval becomes at most two
     intervals in that order.  Hence all blue pieces form at most

        6 Cat_n

     charted tight-row intervals.  Windows of length at most `H+1` which
     meet a charted-section boundary have at most `12H Cat_n` start
     positions.  Consequently occurrence-level fixed-coordinate provenance
     is globally chargeable at `O(H Cat_(n-1))` cost.  No special recursive
     Euler transition pairing and no section holonomy theorem is needed for
     this count.  More strongly, the deletion atlas is flat: iterated
     order-preserving peak deletions compose to deletion of the union of
     their physical coordinate pairs, so a closed labelled-coordinate chart
     loop is the identity.  Different parent presentations retain different
     coordinate subsets; they are distinct arrows, not nontrivial
     permutation monodromy.

416. Cross-chart target collisions have an exact word law.  If `delta_i`
     deletes adjacent positions `i,i+1` from a binary target word `u`, then,
     for `i<j`,

        delta_i(u)=delta_j(u)
        iff u_i...u_(j+1) has period two.

     This follows by comparing the only possibly different middle factors:

        u_(i+2)...u_(j+1)=u_i...u_(j-1).

     In particular, one-tag presentations (`u_i != u_(i+1)`) collapse
     exactly within one maximal alternating block.  Therefore the number of
     **distinct** one-tag parent targets is the number of runs of ones in
     the transition word `d_i=u_i xor u_(i+1)`, not the raw number of
     transitions.  Zero-tag collisions are exactly zero-runs and two-tag
     collisions are exactly one-runs.

417. This correction does not create a typical-degree obstruction.  The
     number of length-`2m+O(1)` words having at most `eta m` distinct
     one-tag parents is at most

        2 sum_(s<=eta m) binom(2m+O(1),2s)
        =2^((2m+O(1))H_2(eta)+o(m))=o(Cat_m)

     for every fixed `eta<1/2`.  So all but a sub-Catalan family still have
     linearly many distinct deletion neighbours.  The surviving targetwise
     gate is bounded-load Hall expansion in the *actual root-owned chart
     subgraph*, plus the cardinality obstruction in Section 104.  Section
     geometry is solved; target surjectivity is not.  Full proofs are in
     `MSW_BLUE_SECTION_PROVENANCE.md`.

## 106. Triangular endpoint ordering is a one-sided bandwidth gate

418. Let `L` and `R` be two width-sized orthogonal chain partitions and
     let `G` be their bipartite incidence graph: one edge joins two chains
     when they share a mask.  For bijective orders `pi,sigma` of the two
     chain families define

        b^+(G)=min_(pi,sigma) max_(LR in E(G)) (pi(L)-sigma(R)).

     The minimum number `d` of empty endpoint slots required merely to
     label every occupied cell by an interval with left endpoint at most
     its right endpoint is exactly

        max(0,b^+(G)).

     Indeed, any realization in `W+d` positions compresses to orders with
     `pi(L)<=sigma(R)+d`.  Conversely, given such orders, put all empty
     left slots after the occupied left slots and all empty right slots
     before the occupied right slots.  This realizes every edge in the
     physical upper triangle.  Thus even triangular endpoint support is not
     bookkeeping which can be postponed after constructing an abstract
     orthogonal pair.  The forced within-chain precedence orders and pinning
     remain additional gates.

419. The bandwidth condition forces a complete nested sequence of almost
     Hall-tight cuts.  If `b^+(G)<=d`, then for every `s` there is a nested
     suffix `X_s` of exactly `s` left chains satisfying

        |N_G(X_s)|<=s+d.

     Consequently, if every `alpha W` left chains expand by a factor
     `1+epsilon`, then every triangular realization needs at least

        (epsilon*alpha+o(1))W

     extra endpoint slots.  An expander-like or independently randomized
     orthogonal-SCD incidence graph is therefore categorically incompatible
     with a `W+o(W)` construction, even before precedence and coordinate
     pinning are tested.

420. For the conjectural exact value `nu(k)=B(k)`, the permitted one-sided
     bandwidth is only `B(k)-W(k)=Theta(sqrt(k))`.  Hence an orthogonal-SCD
     proof would need to construct, together with the chains themselves, a
     recursively nested incidence flag whose neighborhood excess is never
     more than `Theta(sqrt(k))`.  This is a concrete all-dimensional audit
     invariant.  It closes the shortcut "choose any known orthogonal SCD
     pair and order it afterward" but does not obstruct the MTF path-cover
     or Catalan-braid routes, which build order and chain flags jointly.
     The exact theorem and flag characterization are in
     `TRIANGULAR_BANDWIDTH_OBSTRUCTION.md`.

421. There is also a useful positive converse at the component scale.  If
     every connected component of the incidence graph has at most `s`
     chains on either side, then `b^+_0(G)<=2s-1`; if every component is
     balanced, then `b^+_0(G)<=s-1`.  Order component imbalances with
     bounded partial sums and list both colour classes component by
     component.  Thus `poly(k)`-sized incidence components would make the
     triangular-support overhead `poly(k)=o(W)` automatically.  The
     obstruction is global expansion, not local density.  The precedence
     digraphs and pin survival would still have to be handled afterward.
     For two SCDs every incidence component is automatically balanced:
     count the masks of one fixed middle rank in the component, one per
     left chain and one per right chain.  Hence orthogonal SCD components
     of size at most `s` per side actually give `b^+_0(G)<=s-1`.

## 107. Constant one reduces to a three-chain box theorem

422. Split the coordinates into a fixed number `t` of balanced blocks and
     choose an SCD in every block cube.  A tuple of component chains is a
     symmetric product box with heights `ell_1,...,ell_t`, and these boxes
     partition the Boolean lattice.  If

        w(ell_1,...,ell_t)
          =[z^floor((sum ell_i)/2)] product_i(1+z+...+z^(ell_i)),

     then the exact middle-rank partition gives

        sum_over_chain_tuples w(ell_1,...,ell_t)=W(k).

     This identity is independent of the chosen SCDs.

423. Suppose every fixed `t`-dimensional chain box has a contiguous-union
     word of length at most

        w(ell_1,...,ell_t)+O_t((1+sum ell_i)^(t-2)).

     Concatenating the local words covers the whole Boolean cube.  The exact
     SCD height distribution has fixed moments

        average_C (1+ell(C))^r=O_r(k^(r/2)),

     while a balanced block split satisfies

        product_i W(k_i)/W(k)=Theta_t(k^(-(t-1)/2)).

     Therefore the total local boundary error is `O_t(W(k)/sqrt(k))`, and

        nu(k)<=W(k)+O_t(W(k)/sqrt(k)).

424. In particular, it is enough to prove one polynomial-size local lemma:
     every three-chain box of heights `p,q,r` has a word of length

        width([0,p]x[0,q]x[0,r])+O(p+q+r).

     Two dimensions are provably insufficient.  A rectangle needs exactly
     `p+q` entries merely to represent its two pure coordinate axes, whereas
     its balanced width is only `p+1`; equivalently, its longest symmetric
     chain has `p+q+1` cells, forcing that many chains in any orthogonal
     partner.  Thus three dimensions are the first product geometry where a
     surface-order local error has the right global scale.  This is a new
     all-dimensional route, not a claim that the local three-box conjecture
     is solved.  Full proof of the aggregation and the exact local target are
     in `FIXED_DIMENSION_GRID_REDUCTION.md`.

425. The three-chain local problem has an exact normalization.  Close every
     emitted mask to the least triple of chain prefixes containing it.  If a
     witnessing interval originally joins to a box point `T`, every entry in
     it is contained in `T`, so closing the entries leaves the join equal to
     `T`.  Hence `g_3(p,q,r)` is exactly the least length of a sequence of
     grid triples whose contiguous componentwise maxima cover the box.

426. The rank-slack theorem applies verbatim to a chain box.  For the cube
     `[0,d]^3` it gives

        g_3(d,d,d)>=width([0,d]^3)+(2/3)d+O(1).

     A separate shell projection gives `g_3(p,q,r)>=p+q+2r` for
     `p>=q>=r`, in particular `g_3(d,d,d)>=4d`.  Thus a linear local boundary
     term is necessary, but all audited elementary lower bounds remain on
     the scale allowed by the three-box conjecture.  See
     `THREE_BOX_LOWER_BOUND_AUDIT.md`.

427. The first nontrivial local cube is exact:

        g_3(2,2,2)=10.

     The word

        4 12 20 48 1 16 3 5 13 21

     covers all 26 nonzero ideals of three two-step chains.  Length nine has
     a checked DRAT refutation (786 variables, 6524 clauses; `drat-trim`
     reports `s VERIFIED`).  The artifacts are under
     `three_box_certificates/cube_2/`.  Its box rank-slack bound is only nine,
     so local equality with the rank-slack expression already fails by one.

428. A fixed middle derivative row is impossible for every cubic side.
     In `[0,2a]^3`, each of the three top increments occurs in only `a+1`
     middle points, and these three supports are pairwise disjoint.  Every
     rank-slack-feasible fixed delay is at least `a+1`; the run criterion
     would force all three short supports to touch one of only two row
     boundaries.  Any width-plus-boundary construction must therefore use
     genuinely variable central witnesses.

429. There is an explicit all-depth shadow walk on the translated middle
     hexagon `H_a`.  Traverse each radius-`s` hexagon as a closed cycle and
     concatenate the cycles radially.  Its length is

        M_a+a,  M_a=3a^2+3a+1.

     Every nonpositive-sum cube point is the componentwise minimum of a
     contiguous walk interval, and every nonnegative-sum point is the
     componentwise maximum of one.  Ordinary ring edges biject with both
     adjacent middle layers.  The six-side proof and independent audit are
     in `THREE_BOX_HEX_SPIRAL.md` and `THREE_BOX_HEX_SPIRAL_AUDIT.md`.

430. Perfect shadows do not make the ring order realizable.  For any
     monotone `O(a)`-offset central witness band whose order consists of
     contiguous complete radius rings, factorability of the two internal
     extreme-side runs on every ring forces

        sum_i (r_i-l_i)<=3a^3+O(a^2).

     The exact avoidance ledger then leaves at most `3a^3+O(a^2)` physical
     intervals containing no complete middle witness, but the lower half has
     `4a^3+O(a^2)` targets.  This rules out outward/inward ring order,
     arbitrary ring-block permutations, cuts, orientations, and `O(a)`
     repetitions.  It does not rule out genuine cross-radius interleaving.
     See `THREE_BOX_SPIRAL_BAND_OBSTRUCTION.md` and its audit.

431. Raw orthogonal-chain count is not an obstruction.  In `[0,m]^3`, the
     hook SCDs `(xy)z` and `(xz)y` have double intersections exactly at

        (j,i,i), (m-i,m-j,m-j),  i+j<m.

     Cutting the right chains at the first point and pairing prefix `(i,j)`
     with suffix `(i+1,j)` produces orthogonal partitions of sizes

        W_m and W_m+m

     exactly.  This rechain is not yet an interval construction: its two
     endpoint-precedence DAGs contain cycles.  The remaining ordered-chain
     problem is to alter the rechain with only `O(m)` additional splits (or
     prove that impossible), then establish coordinate pinning.  Proof and
     audit are in `THREE_BOX_NEAR_ORTHOGONAL_CHAINS.md` and its audit.

432. The current three-chain frontier is summarized in
     `THREE_BOX_PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS.md`.  A proof of constant one now requires
     either (i) an interleaved-radius middle order with `O(m)` factor band,
     enough lower-interval avoidance capacity, complete upper shadows, Hall,
     and pins; or (ii) two ordered orthogonal chain partitions with
     `W_m+O(m)` chains and an exact interval-labeling rule.  The canonical
     fixed-row, contiguous-ring, and first hook-rechain realizations are
     rigorously closed.

433. The apparent interleaving escape is itself sharply constrained.  Let
     `H_s` be the translated middle hexagon of `[-s,s]^3`,

        M_s=3s^2+3s+1,

     choose one witness for every middle target in a word of length `M_s+D`,
     and let `H` be the largest mesh distance to an internal run of one of
     the three positive extreme-coordinate increments.  Exact pin survival
     and the middle-avoiding interval ledger give

        4s^3+(9/2)s^2+(3/2)s-1
          <= sM_s+2(H+1)D+3(s+1)D+3D^2+2D.

     Hence `D=O(s)` forces

        HD >= (1/2-o(1))s^3,

     and therefore `H=Omega(s^2)`.  Uniform, random, periodic, and every
     certified low-discrepancy cross-radius weave are impossible; a surviving
     near-width order must have a macroscopic phase desert.  The same theorem
     applies to every induced near-outer subcube, but it does not prove that
     the deserts for different radii align in one physical interval.  See
     `THREE_BOX_INTERLEAVING_OBSTRUCTION.md` and its audit.

434. The exact two-sided adjacent-shadow skeleton is frozen.  Join a lower
     color `w` of sum `-1` to an upper color `u` of sum `+1` when

        u-w=e_i+e_j,  i!=j.

     This color graph has a unique perfect matching.  Degree-one peeling on
     the six outer walls forces the outer hexagon, then induction forces all
     concentric ring edge sets `R_1 union ... union R_s`.  Thus an exact
     common lower/upper rainbow has no hidden Hamilton-path freedom.  If the
     radius-`r` forced edges occur in `b_r` normalized maximal trail blocks,
     any linear middle row costs at least

        M_s + sum_(r=1)^s b_r.

     With `D=O(s)`, the near-rainbow edge-cover defect is confined to only
     `O(s)` alternating corridors relative to this unique matching.  Combining
     the trail ledger with the anti-mixing theorem proves, conditionally on
     using an exact common rainbow, that `sum_r(b_r-1)=Omega(s)`.  It does not
     imply linearly many distinct split radii or a bounded number of phases.
     Full statements and scope are in
     `THREE_BOX_ADJACENT_SHADOW_MATCHING.md` and its audit.

435. The hook precedence obstruction has now been independently audited.
     For every `a+j<m`, four explicit incidences force opposite orders on a
     diagonal prefix chain and a suffix-containing chain.  Their support gaps
     have congestion at most two, so every cut-based repair needs at least

        ceil(m(m+1)/4)

     cuts.  This remains true for every one-prefix/one-suffix rematching of the
     same whole pieces.  The consequent

        n >= W_m+(m^2+5m)/8=(7/6-o(1))W_m

     bound is proved only for pure refinements with no compensating cross-chain
     remerge.  The cap no-rechain lemma is valid with the unchanged left hook
     partition, but simultaneous surgery on both endpoint families remains
     outside its scope.  These qualifications are essential; the theorem
     kills this architecture, not every ordered-chain construction.  See
     `THREE_BOX_NEAR_ORTHOGONAL_PRECEDENCE_OBSTRUCTION_AUDIT.md`.

## 108. The long-run MTF route reduces to shallow growing-row integrality

436. Full disjoint packing of MTF atoms is unnecessary.  If atom `j` has
     `H_j` states, initialization size `s_j`, and the union of all exposed
     prefix-chain rows misses `Q` Boolean masks in total, then direct MTF
     traversal followed by literal insertion of the missing masks gives

        nu(k) <= sum_j(H_j-1+s_j)+Q.

     Thus overlaps between atoms are harmless; the correct target is

        total states = W+o(W),  total initialization = o(W),  Q=o(W).

     For the full coordinate orbit of a length-`H` Pascal-strip atom, exact
     orbit counting gives same-rank normalized codegree `Theta(m^-2)` and
     adjacent nested-rank codegree `Theta(m^-1)`.  Higher rectangular subsets
     have genuine high-order clustering, so fixed-uniformity matching/nibble
     theorems cannot simply be invoked while `H` grows.  In particular the
     prior black-box Grable/Pippenger-style rounding claim is retracted.

437. There is nevertheless an unconditional reservoir reduction.  For

        h=ceil(sqrt(m log m)),  H=m/log m,
        q_0=ceil(sqrt(8m log log m)),

     `o(W)` random radius-`h` atoms can be chosen so that the total uncovered
     masks at depths `q_0<=|r-m|<=h` is `o(W)`, while their traversal length is
     also `o(W)`.  The outer tails cost `o(W)` literally.  Hence only the
     shallow band

        |r-m| <= Theta(sqrt(m log log m))

     remains for a constant-one proof.  Oriented chains form an explicit
     `(m-d)^2`-regular rotor graph; a wreath is exactly one rigid cyclic rotor
     orbit.  The remaining theorem is therefore: choose `W+o(W)` centers in
     long rotor paths whose exposed rows have total shallow-band defect
     `o(W)`.  This is the current precise integrality problem, not another
     finite-`k` search.  Exact formulas and proofs are in
     `GLOBAL_MTF_ATOM_INTEGRALITY.md`.

438. A later audit makes the atom-packing formulation in 436--437 optional,
     not the smallest frontier.  In odd dimension `n=2m+1`, the
     Muetze--Standke--Wiechert theorem already gives an exact factor of the
     middle layer into `B=W/n=Cat_m` cyclic-interval wreaths.  For a wreath
     `pi`, let `C_q(pi)` be its `n` cyclic intervals of length `m-q`, and let
     `M_q(F)` be the number of depth-`q` colors missed by an exact middle
     factor `F`.  If the wreaths are ordered and `o_(i,q)` counts colors of
     `C_q(pi_i)` already seen earlier, then the exact collision ledger is

        M_q(F)=sum_i o_(i,q)-(W-N_q),
        N_q=binom(2m+1,m-q).

     Consequently the following single lemma is sufficient for constant one:
     choose an exact middle wreath factor and

        H=sqrt(m omega(m)),  omega(m)->infinity,
        H=o(m^(2/3)),

     such that

        sum_(q=1)^H M_q(F)=o(W).

     Linearizing each wreath costs `W+O(HW/m)=W+o(W)`, the missing central
     colors cost `o(W)` literally, and the truncated two-tail word costs
     `o(W)`.  At depth one the entire unavoidable overlap allowance is only

        (W-N_1)/(W/n)=4-6/(m+2)

     repeated colors per wreath on average.  Thus a useful factor must be
     nearly lossless; generic random/Poisson selection is pointed in the
     wrong direction.  Full atoms have fatal high-order clustering, partial
     nibbles solve only the already-solved middle layer, the antipodal
     quotient needs relative leftover `o(n^(-1/2))` beyond current black-box
     theorems, and standard SCD projections have `Omega(W)` MTF boundaries.
     The exact audited frontier is
     `GLOBAL_MTF_ATOM_ROUNDING_FINAL_AUDIT.md`.

## 109. Four-chain boxes clear only the first-shadow gate

439. Pair the coordinates of `[0,m]^4`, apply the square hook SCD in each
     pair, and in every product rectangle traverse its central diagonal.
     Concatenating the `(m+1)^2` paths gives an explicit permutation of the
     entire four-box middle layer.  Its block-internal adjacent meets and
     joins each miss exactly

        m(m+1)=O(m^2)

     targets; seam edges can only improve this.  Thus four dimensions really
     evade the frozen three-dimensional adjacent-shadow obstruction at the
     correct surface scale.  The tempting all-depth extrapolation is false:
     an imbalanced local rectangle of half-heights `H,K` has one-sided tail
     defect

        |H-K|(2 min(H,K)+1),

     and summing over all chain pairs gives exactly

        m(m+1)^2(m+2)/6=Theta(m^4)

     missing targets on each side.  Therefore this is not yet a proof of
     `g_4<=width+O(m^2)`; a new cross-rectangle interleaving/factor theorem is
     required.  See `FOUR_BOX_CENTRAL_DIAGONALS.md`.

## 110. Phase separation in three boxes is now quantitatively obstructed

440. The anti-mixing theorem admits a heterogeneous strengthening.  For a
     monotone witness band of length `M_a+D`, let `[u_i,v_i]` be any internal
     coordinate-threshold run avoiding middle index `i`, put
     `lambda_i=v_i-u_i`, and let `C_alpha,C_beta` be the maximum
     multiplicities with which the resulting forward and backward charge
     intervals cover an endpoint-offset increment.  Then

        sum_i(r_i-l_i)
          <= sum_(i in J) lambda_i
             +(C_alpha+C_beta)D+(M_a-|J|)D.

     Together with the exact middle-avoiding interval ledger this gives

        V_a <= sum_(i in J)lambda_i +(C_alpha+C_beta)D
               +(M_a-|J|)D+3D^2+2D.

     The threshold and run may vary with `i`; this is precisely what prevents
     an apparent desert for three extreme coordinates from hiding cheap runs
     of other thresholds.

441. Apply that lemma to the perfectly nested six-side order `O_a`.  Every
     noncentral index has an avoiding run with total

        sum_i lambda_i=a^3-a,

     and the exact charge bounds are `C_alpha<=2a`, `C_beta<=a`.  Hence

        Q <= a^3-a+(3a+3)D+3D^2.

     Since the lower half has

        V_a=4a^3+(9/2)a^2+(3/2)a-1

     targets, this architecture requires

        D >= (1-o(1))a^(3/2),

     not surface slack `O(a)`.  Perfectly aligning the nested extreme-run
     deserts therefore makes the full multiscale pin obstruction worse, not
     better.

442. At the opposite extreme, suppose the `6a` intact side blocks are
     arranged in `B` maximal side-homogeneous batches, with arbitrary radius
     permutations and independent reversals.  A nine-block-window argument
     supplies a heterogeneous run cover with leading run budget `3a^3` and
     span `O(a)`.  Universality with `D=O(a)` forces

        BD=Omega(a^2),

     and hence `B=Omega(a)`.  Thus boundedly many macroscopic side phases and
     the perfectly nested phase order are both ruled out.  The survivors are
     genuinely irregular `Theta(a)`-switch schedules and long alternating
     near-rainbow defect corridors.  The complete proof, source repairs, and
     independent audit are in `THREE_BOX_PHASE_SEPARATION_RESEARCH.md` and
     `THREE_BOX_PHASE_SEPARATION_AUDIT.md`.

## 111. Four-box tails admit endpoint compression, but still no OR factor

443. For the central-diagonal four-box construction, the exact one-sided
     number of internally missed targets at depth `d` is

        D_(m,d)=sum_(a=1)^A n_a(n_a+1),
        A=min(d,m,2m-d),
        n_a=m+1-ceil((d+a)/2).

     Consequently `D_(m,d)=d m^2+O_d(m)` for fixed `d`, and

        sum_(d=1)^D D_(m,d)=D(D+1)m^2/2+O_D(m)

     through every fixed depth `D`.  Every off-middle point is respectively
     the join or meet of two middle points, so appending dedicated pairs gives
     a two-sided depth-`D` shadow sequence of length

        M_m+2D(D+1)m^2+O_D(m).

444. More globally, a `4r-1`-occurrence two-arm fan covers the `r^2` upper
     and `r^2` lower tails associated with one radius-`r` anchor.  Appending
     all fans gives an explicit all-depth two-sided shadow sequence of exact
     length

        2m^3+5m^2+4m+1=3M_m+O(m^2).

     This is a real compression of the raw `Theta(m^4)` tail ledger to
     `Theta(m^3)` occurrences.  It also shows that two independently movable
     interval endpoints encode a quadratic tail fibre.

445. The fan is not a `g_4` word.  Lower targets in the shadow calculation
     are coordinatewise meets of middle points, whereas an OR factor must
     realize them as joins of factor labels with surviving pins.  Moreover,
     any near-width repair of all old upper tails needs a positive fraction
     of physical witnesses of length `Omega(m)`; literal bounded-window
     stitching is impossible, though long windows using the transfer
     identities remain viable.  The two missing theorems are therefore
     (i) packing the fan arms into `M_m+O(m^2)` middle occurrences and
     (ii) a compatible variable-band factor/pinning theorem.  See
     `FOUR_BOX_INTERLEAVING_RESEARCH.md` and its independent audit.

## 112. The first wreath shadow is feasible but not yet multiscale

446. For an exact wreath factor in odd dimension `n=2m+1`, let `mu(S)` count
     occurrences of an `(m-1)`-set as a cyclic interval of length `m-1`.
     For `m>=2`, exactly

        sum_S mu(S)=W,
        sum_(S contains x)mu(S)=(m-1)Cat_m,
        mu(S)<=floor((m+2)/2).

     A new explicit factor of the `126` four-sets of `[9]` into fourteen
     wreaths has perfect first shadow: its `84` triples occur with histogram
     `42` once and `42` twice.  Thus the four holes in the canonical MSW
     factor are not forced by parity, margins, or color matching.  This
     particular perfect-shadow factor has no rainbow coordinate cut, so the
     two properties are genuinely different.

447. A clean sufficient first-shadow condition is available.  If `t`
     coordinates are rainbow cuts--meaning all internal intersections in the
     complementary Johnson path factors are distinct--then

        M_1 <= binom(2m+1-t,m-1-t),
        M_1/W <= 2^(-t) exp(O(t^2/m)).

     Hence any exact factor with `t=o(sqrt(m))` and `t->infinity` rainbow
     cuts has `M_1=o(W)`.  No such all-`m` factor is currently constructed.

448. There is also a conditional four-level bridge.  A Hamilton cycle in
     ranks `m-2,m-1,m,m+1` of `B_(2m-1)` suppresses to a middle Johnson
     cycle.  If its lower and upper square-completion maps are injective and
     its residual central edges contain the required perfect matching, then
     deleting the other `Cat_m` central edges yields exactly `Cat_m` paths
     whose rank-`m-1` meet colors and rank-`m+1` join colors are both perfect.
     The published GJM lexical Hamilton cycle cannot instantiate this bridge:
     `Cat_(m-2)` explicit, edge-disjoint lower square-completion collision
     pairs survive all its upper-level joining switches.

449. The bridge still gives neither equal complementary length-`m` paths,
     nor the remaining odd first-shadow sector, nor any depth `q>=2`.
     Therefore none of 446--448 proves the weak multiscale wreath lemma

        sum_(q=1)^H M_q=o(W).

     The honest next theorem is either a multidepth analogue of the
     rainbow-cut lemma or a nonlexical square-resolved cycle together with
     complementary path control and deeper consecutive-shadow estimates.
     Proofs, the finite certificate, and the audit are in
     `WREATH_FIRST_SHADOW_RESEARCH.md` and
     `WREATH_FIRST_SHADOW_AUDIT.md`.

## 113. Central SCD projection edges are almost orthogonal to MTF transitions

450. Let a saturated chain `C` own a central diamond

        S < T=S+a < U=S+a+b,

     and let the alternate middle set `T'=S+b` lie in chain `D`.  The exact
     quotient-chain criterion for one move-to-front update gives a
     state-fiber obstruction, independent of how either chain is exposed:

     * `D -> C` is impossible whenever `min(C)` is nonempty, because after
       quotienting by `min(C)`, the equal-rank sets `T` and `T'` remain
       incomparable;
     * `C -> D` is impossible whenever `min(D)` is nonempty and `D` continues
       above `T'`.  Cross-nesting forces `b in min(D)` and then forces the
       successor of `T'` in `D` to equal `U`, contradicting disjointness.

     This theorem quantifies over all ordered-partition states exposing the
     chains, not only canonical recency states.

451. In any SCD of `B_(2m)`, put

        W=binom(2m,m),  K=Cat_m=W/(m+1).

     The only exceptional transition heads are the `K` singleton middle
     chains and the unique chain with empty minimum.  Hence any
     vertex-disjoint directed path system using the SCD's central projection
     edges has at most `K+1` edges that are also one-step MTF transitions.
     Even if an ideal two-sided rainbow linear forest with `K` components
     exists, at least

        W-2K-1=(1-o(1))W

     of its `W-K` internal adjacencies are MTF-incompatible.  A prescribed
     chain-by-chain traversal therefore costs at least

        2W-2K-2=2W-o(W)

     updates before initialization.  This is a lower bound only for that
     realization framework, not for `nu(2m)`.

452. Conversely, any exact two-sided rainbow linear forest extends, by
     normalized inclusion matchings above and below the three central ranks,
     to a saturated partition of the Boolean lattice into exactly `W`
     chains.  The extension need not be symmetric.  Thus the pure linear-
     forest problem remains a legitimate derivative/chain-partition design
     problem, but it does not solve the MTF state-transversal problem.  The
     two routes must no longer be conflated.  Full proofs and the independent
     audit are in `SCD_MTF_ESCAPE_RESEARCH.md` and
     `SCD_MTF_ESCAPE_AUDIT.md`.

## 114. Multidepth wreath cuts reduce the weak lemma to logarithmically many local sectors

453. Let `F` be an exact middle wreath factor on `n=2m+1` coordinates,
     containing `B=Cat_m` wreaths, and fix depth `q`, so the target rank is
     `m-q`.  Cutting one wreath at a coordinate `z` exposes exactly

        m+q+1

     cyclic `(m-q)`-interval slots avoiding `z`.  Thus the aggregate slot
     count and target count in the `z`-free sector are

        K_q=(m+q+1)Cat_m,
        A_q=binom(2m,m-q)
           =Cat_m (m+1)(m)_q/(m+1)^(overline q).

     If `h_(z,q)` is the number of missing colours and `e_(z,q)` is the
     duplicate excess, exact occurrence counting gives

        h_(z,q)=e_(z,q)-(K_q-A_q).

     Hence a coordinate covers its whole depth-`q` free sector exactly when
     its duplicate excess is the unavoidable arithmetic excess.  For fixed
     `q`, the full-cut and nested-core forced excesses are respectively
     `(q(q+1)+o(1))Cat_m` and `(q(q-1)+o(1))Cat_m`.

454. If `t_q` coordinates cover their `z`-free sectors at depth `q`, every
     globally missing `(m-q)`-set must contain all of those coordinates.
     Consequently

        M_q/W <= (m)_(q+t_q)/
                 ((m+2)^(overline q)(2m+1)_(t_q))
              <= 2^(-t_q)
                 exp(-q(q+t_q+1)/(m+q+1)).

     Therefore the weak multiscale wreath condition follows from

        sum_(q<=H) 2^(-t_q) exp(-q^2/(2m))=o(1).

     In particular, `t_q >= (1/2)log_2 m+omega(1)` uniformly is sufficient;
     the covering coordinates may vary with `q`.  To pass from this estimate
     to `nu(k)=(1+o(1))W(k)`, retain the inherited tail-compatible scale

        H=sqrt(m omega(m)),  omega(m)->infinity,  H=o(m^(2/3)).

     This is a sharply local sufficient reduction, not an existence theorem
     for the required factors.

455. First-shadow perfection does not propagate.  An exact factor of the
     `126` four-sets of `[9]` into fourteen wreaths has coordinate `9` as a
     rainbow depth-one cut: its `56` core triples enumerate all triples of
     `[8]`.  Nevertheless the depth-two pairs `{1,3}` and `{4,6}` occur in
     no wreath at all.  This certificate was independently recompiled and
     checked remotely.  Thus any all-depth proof must use genuinely
     multiscale interaction; one perfect cut contains insufficient
     information.  The theorem, strengthened verifier, finite rows, and
     independent audit are in `MULTIDEPTH_WREATH_CUT_RESEARCH.md`,
     `scratch/verify_m4_rainbow_not_depth2.cpp`, and
     `MULTIDEPTH_WREATH_CUT_AUDIT.md`.

## 115. Depth-truncated four-box fans admit an actual OR factor

456. Put `P_m=[0,m]^4` and let

        M_m=[z^(2m)](1+z+...+z^m)^4
           =(2m^3+6m^2+7m+3)/3.

     For every `1<=D<=2m`, there is an explicit word of points of `P_m`, of
     length at most

        M_m+D(11m^2+13m+3),

     whose contiguous coordinatewise maxima contain every point of ranks
     `2m-D,...,2m+D`.  Under the prefix-atom encoding this is one genuine
     bitwise-OR word, not merely a two-sided shadow row.  Taking `D=2m-1`
     and appending the full point also gives the non-sharp but unconditional
     all-point bound

        g_4(m,m,m,m)
        <=M_m+22m^3+15m^2-7m-2.

457. The key local identity is that a canonical radius-fan target at rank
     depth `d` has a middle-row witness of exactly `d+1` terms, independently
     of the fan radius.  Keep only fan arms needed through depth `D`, repeat
     every block endpoint and every upper peak to a plateau of length `D+1`,
     and concatenate the blocks.  Every internal atom run then has length at
     least `D+1`.  If

        A_j=intersection_(i=max(1,j-D))^(min(L,j)) T_i,

     the exact erosion identities turn every retained lower meet and upper
     join into a contiguous maximum of `A`.  Counting raw fan terms, block
     endpoints, upper peaks, and the final factor extension gives the stated
     bound.  Two independent line-by-line audits found only local wording
     corrections; neither changes the theorem.

458. This theorem is deliberately scoped.  For `D=o(m)` it gives a
     near-width word, but only for a sublinear central band.  The complement
     of that band still has `Theta(m^4)` points, so literal tails destroy the
     estimate.  At full depth, the `Theta(m^2)` canonical upper fan blocks
     each contain a peak-only atom; a common delay `D>=2` forces
     `Omega(Dm^2)` peak mass.  Thus literal full fan blocks cost
     `Omega(m^3)`.  Nothing here proves the complete unequal-box surface
     theorem needed by the fixed-dimensional chain-box reduction, and hence
     nothing here yet proves `nu(k)=(1+o(1))W(k)`.

459. The peak-sharing gate now has an exact triangular form.  Write
     `c=H-r` and define

        P_(c,u)=(c+u,m-c,0,m-u),
        E_(c,r,x)=(c+r,m-c-x,x,m-r).

     Then for `0<=u<r<=m-c` and `0<=x<r`,

        E_(c,r,x) join P_(c,u)
          =(c+r,m-c,x,m-u),

     exactly the required upper tail.  All radii with fixed `c` share one
     peak chain and the same critical atom level; intervening peaks are
     harmless precisely for `u<=s<=r`.  The live local problem is to order
     this triangular arm family so one physical peak chain serves many
     radii, then couple the lower reflection and preserve factorability.
     This is a reduction, not yet a packing theorem.  Full proofs and audits
     are in `FOUR_BOX_FACTOR_ESCAPE_RESEARCH.md` and
     `FOUR_BOX_FACTOR_ESCAPE_AUDIT.md`.

## 116. Variable witness bands do not rescue the literal full-fan row

460. For a prescribed row `T_1,...,T_L`, let its selected central witnesses
     be arbitrary monotone intervals

        I_i=[i+alpha_i,i+beta_i],
        0<=alpha_1<=...<=alpha_L<=d,
        0<=beta_1<=...<=beta_L<=d,
        alpha_i<=beta_i.

     For each atom `b`, put

        Z_b=[L+d] minus union_(i:b notin T_i) I_i.

     Exact factorization is coordinatewise: it exists iff
     `I_i cap Z_b` is nonempty for every `b in T_i`.  For an internal
     support run `[u,v]`, this is equivalently

        beta_(u-1)-alpha_(v+1)<=v-u.

     Thus the nonuniform problem has an exact run criterion, not merely a
     SAT encoding.

461. A lower meet `S_(u,v)=intersection_(i=u)^v T_i` has the natural
     physical core

        J_(u,v)=intersection_(i=u)^v I_i
               =[v+alpha_v,u+beta_u].

     The maximal factor realizes this meet exactly iff `J_(u,v)` is
     nonempty and intersects `Z_b` for every common atom `b`.  More generally,
     arbitrary assigned lower windows are governed by the same surviving-pin
     theorem after deleting all central and lower intervals whose labels omit
     `b`.  Linked central intervals, `alpha_(i+1)<=beta_i`, automatically
     translate every upper consecutive join.

462. Apply this to pairwise position-disjoint contiguous copies of every
     literal combined full fan, with no insertions or shared occurrences
     inside the copies.  A peak-only atom forces the band to close across the
     peak, while the canonical deepest lower core in the same radius-`r`
     block forces it to reopen by at least `2r-1`.  These beta-increases lie
     in disjoint physical blocks.  Summing every radius and both orientations
     gives the exact architectural obstruction

        d >= 2 sum_(H=1)^m sum_(r=2)^H (2r-1)
          = m(2m^2+3m-5)/3
          = Omega(m^3).

     Hence changing one fixed delay into arbitrary monotone witness intervals
     does not produce surface slack for the literal full-fan concatenation.
     The theorem does not cover an interleaving which breaks the fan blocks,
     shares physical occurrences, replaces the canonical upper witnesses,
     or assigns non-core lower windows.

463. Grouping peaks by a common threshold also fails canonically.  For the
     depth-one target of radius `r`, only peaks `r` and `r-1` from that
     threshold family lie below the target.  Consequently one maximal
     atom-positive run can service only `O(1)` canonical depth-one witnesses,
     forcing `Omega(m^2)` atom-run incidences over all threshold levels.
     Different atom runs may overlap physically, so this is not by itself a
     cubic length bound.  The exact general criteria, scoped obstruction,
     and independent audit are in `VARIABLE_BAND_FOUR_BOX_FACTOR.md` and
     `VARIABLE_BAND_FOUR_BOX_FACTOR_AUDIT.md`.

## 117. The triangular arm--peak problem is quadratic and canonical sharing cannot be sparse

464. Fix one threshold diagonal `c` and put `R=m-c`.  Suppress the affine
     coordinates and identify the canonical middle points with the triangle

        T_R={(0,0)} union {(s,y):1<=s<=R, 0<=y<s}.

     The target indexed by `0<=u<r<=R`, `0<=x<r` is the bounding rectangle
     `[u,r] x [0,x]`: an interval of triangular points has the required
     coordinatewise maximum exactly when its cells have

        min s=u, max s=r, min y=0, max y=x.

     An explicit block for radius `r` is

        E_(r,r-1),...,E_(r,0),P_(r-1),...,P_0.

     Concatenating these blocks for `r=1,...,R` covers every upper target in
     exact length `R(R+1)`.  Every nonpeak arm occurs once; the peak mass is
     quadratic.

465. This scale is unavoidable even for arbitrary entries and witnesses.
     The targets at rank depth `R` form an antichain of exact size

        floor((R+1)^2/4),

     so the endpoint-chain lower bound gives `Omega(R^2)` length.  Moreover,
     no exact-once permutation of the triangular cells works for `R>=3`.
     The `x=0` targets force all peaks into one pure contiguous block and
     force that block to be monotone; every nonpeak then lies outside it, so
     the interior target `(u,r,x)=(1,2,1)` cannot reach a peak without also
     forcing `u=0` or `r=R`.  This proves repetition is necessary, but not
     yet that unrestricted repetition is quadratic.

466. Under the canonical two-provider requirement--the witness for
     `(u,r,x)` contains both arm `E_(r,x)` and peak `P_u`--there is an exact
     chain-cover obstruction.  On one oriented side of one physical `P_u`
     occurrence, nested witness intervals force their arm types to form a
     chain in the coordinatewise poset

        A_u={(r,x):u<r<=R, 0<=x<r}.

     Its exact width is

        width(A_u)=min(R-u,ceil(R/2)).

     Therefore, if `k_u` is the number of physical `P_u` occurrences,

        2k_u>=width(A_u),

     and summing gives at least `(3/16+o(1))R^2` peak occurrences.  Summing
     over `c` forces `Omega(m^3)` canonical peak mass.  Duplicating arms,
     reordering blocks, or interleaving them cannot repair this while the
     same two providers are required.

467. Reverse-complement supplies the lower reflected family, but the upper
     and lower canonical alphabets share only one boundary point.  Hence the
     remaining escape is genuinely noncanonical: a three-provider interval,
     cross-`c` sharing, a below-middle factor, or a four-dimensional growth
     diagram.  The exact construction and obstruction are in
     `TRIANGULAR_PEAK_SHARING.md`; every count and the arbitrary-entry scope
     of the canonical chain argument were independently checked in
     `TRIANGULAR_PEAK_SHARING_AUDIT.md`.

## 118. Logarithmic wreath cuts: strong certificates are bounded, hole kernels remain viable

468. In an exact middle wreath factor on `n=2m+1` coordinates, distinguish
     two cut notions.  A full depth-`q` covering cut at coordinate `z`
     means that every `(m-q)`-set avoiding `z` occurs as a cyclic interval.
     At depth one, a core-rainbow cut is the stronger assertion that the
     internal cut slots enumerate those `(m-1)`-sets exactly once.  These
     notions cannot be interchanged.

469. For every first-shadow colour `S`, attach to each occurrence of `S`
     the unordered pair of symbols immediately outside that occurrence.
     These boundary pairs form a simple matching on `[n]\S`.  The resulting
     exact degree equations imply

        at most five coordinates can be simultaneous depth-one
        core-rainbow cuts.

     The bound is sharp at `m=2`, where two complementary Hamilton cycles
     of `K_5` realize all five cuts.  Thus logarithmically many
     core-rainbow certificates are impossible, but this theorem says nothing
     comparable about the weaker full-covering cuts.

470. Let `H_q` be the family of missing depth-`q` masks.  The full-covering
     coordinates have the exact description

        C_q = intersection(H_q)                 if H_q is nonempty,
        C_q = [n]                               if H_q is empty.

     Therefore the surviving logarithmic-cut problem is a kernel problem:
     arrange that every hole at depth `q` contains a prescribed marked set
     `Z_q`.  A coordinate-transitive exact factor has a sharp dichotomy at
     every depth: either the shadow is complete and every coordinate covers,
     or no coordinate is full covering.  An intermediate logarithmic kernel
     must deliberately break coordinate transitivity.

471. If `Z` has size `t` and its unmarked cyclic gap lengths in one wreath
     are `g_1,...,g_t`, shortening middle windows from `m` to `m-q`
     creates exactly

        sum_i min(q,(g_i-m+q+1)_+)

     additional `Z`-free slots.  Under the fixed gap sum
     `N=2m+1-t`, the exact maximum is

        P_q(m,t)
          = max_{0<=ell<=min(t,floor(N/(m-q)))}
              min(ell*q, N-ell*(m-q-1)).

     This yields the necessary gap-surplus inequalities for any full kernel.
     They have ample arithmetic slack for `t` logarithmic in `m`.
     Likewise, uniform fractional wreath weights give every depth-`q`
     colour load

        lambda_q=(m+2)^(overline q)/(m)_q >= 1.

     This proves fractional and aggregate-count feasibility only; it does
     not rule out an integral divisibility or trade-lattice obstruction.

472. Combined with the multidepth amplification theorem, the corrected
     all-dimensional target is now precise: construct an exact middle wreath
     factor with exact shallow shadows or with common hole kernels
     `|Z_q|=(1/2)log_2 m+omega(1)` throughout the controlled band, using
     integral kernel-preserving absorption or trades.  No such factor is
     constructed yet.  The proved obstruction, exact kernel identity,
     gap law, and independent audit are in
     `LOGARITHMIC_WREATH_CUTS.md` and
     `LOGARITHMIC_WREATH_CUTS_AUDIT.md`.

## 119. Noncanonical triangular words require portals and linear repetition

473. For the fixed-`c` triangle `T_R`, restrict first to spanning words over
     the triangular alphabet: every cell occurs at least once, but witnesses
     may be completely noncanonical.  If `q` is the number of occurrences
     beyond

        |T_R|=1+R(R+1)/2,

     then

        q >= ceil((floor(R/2)-2)/2) = R/4-O(1).

     The proof is an incidence ledger.  The zero-height adjacent targets
     force at least `R` physical peak--peak edges.  The positive adjacent
     targets force at least `ceil((R-1)/2)` peak--nonpeak edges.  Since
     one peak occurrence has only two physical sides, the latter portals
     require linearly many excess peak occurrences.  This is unrestricted
     with respect to two- versus three-provider witnesses, though it does
     assume the word spans and stays inside `T_R`.

474. Every positive-height witness crosses a physical peak--nonpeak portal.
     At one fixed portal, boxes obtained by extending left form one nested
     chain and boxes obtained by extending right form another; every interval
     crossing the portal has box equal to the join of one state from each
     chain.  Thus a hypothetical near-once construction is exactly a
     superposition of `O(R)` two-chain grids.  This is the mechanism that
     escapes the canonical theorem: one portal supplies a grid, not merely
     one chain on one side of `P_u`.

475. There is a rigorous three-provider grid for each fixed lower endpoint
     `u`, showing that `R` abstract grids suffice to cover all targets.
     Its literal concatenation has length `(3R^2+R)/2` for `R>=2`, but
     it omits some triangular cells (for example `E_(4,2)`) and is therefore
     a structural coverage certificate, not a spanning repetition upper
     bound.  The missing theorem is physical superposition: insert every
     omitted cell and share the repeated column-one and diagonal chains
     without destroying the portal grids.

476. Remote exhaustive verification gives spanning universal words with
     excesses `1,2,4` for `R=3,4,5`.  The exact value is proved only for
     `R=3`; failed searches at smaller excess for `R=4,5` are not lower
     bounds.  The observed numbers equal

        floor((R-1)^2/4),

     the size of a strict-interior equal-depth antichain, but no injection
     from those targets to repeated positions is known.  The rigorous
     portal theorem, linear lower bound, corrected gadget scope, and audit
     are in `NONCANONICAL_TRIANGULAR_BRAID.md` and
     `NONCANONICAL_TRIANGULAR_BRAID_AUDIT.md`.

## 120. The triangular target family has an exact one-level fold quotient

477. Remove the boundary cell `P_0=(0,0)` and define

        phi_R(s,y)=(s-1,max(y-1,0)).

     This maps `T_R\{P_0}` onto `T_(R-1)`.  Its only two-element
     fibres are over nonzero lower peaks:

        phi^(-1)(P_0)={P_1},
        phi^(-1)(P_a)={P_(a+1),E_(a+1,1)}  (a>=1),
        phi^(-1)(E_(a,b))={E_(a+1,b+1)}    (b>=1).

     The parameter map

        (u,r,x) -> (u-1,r-1,x-1)

     is a bijection from upper targets with `u,x>=1` to the entire lower
     target family.  Folding any such witness is exact.  Conversely, deleting
     `P_0` from any universal upper word and folding every remaining
     entry produces a universal lower word; spanning is also preserved.

478. There is an explicit section of this quotient.  Replace each lower
     nonzero peak `P_a` by the complete two-letter block
     `[P_(a+1),E_(a+1,1)]`, replace `P_0` by `P_1`, and raise both
     coordinates of every lower nonpeak by one.  Complete replacement blocks
     lift every lower witness, including the delicate lower-height-zero case,
     to the corresponding upper target with `u,x>=1`.  If the lower word
     has length `n` and `p_+` occurrences of nonzero peaks, the block
     lift has exact length `n+p_+` and spans every upper cell except
     `P_0`.

479. The complementary boundary family has one common length-`2R`
     scaffold:

        P_R,P_(R-1),...,P_0,E_(2,1),E_(3,2),...,E_(R,R-1).

     Peak subintervals cover every `x=0` target.  For `u=0,x>0`, the
     interval from `P_r` through `P_0` and then through `E_(x+1,x)`
     has exactly the required bounding rectangle.  Concatenating this
     scaffold with the full block lift is therefore a rigorous universal
     spanning recursion.  If the lower excess is `q`, its upper excess is
     exactly

        q+R+p_+.

480. The literal recursion is numerically wasteful because it recopies the
     `2R-1` scaffold cell types already present in the lift.  Superposing
     a boundary realization with a sparsified/rearranged lift at
     `o(R)` repair per level would yield `o(R^2)` triangular
     repetitions and reopen the four-box constant-one route.  This is a
     sufficient architecture, not a necessary normal form: an obstruction
     to this particular scaffold embedding would not by itself prove an
     unrestricted quadratic lower bound.  The exact fold, reverse quotient,
     corrected scope, and independent audit are in
     `TRIANGULAR_FOLD_RECURSION.md` and
     `TRIANGULAR_FOLD_RECURSION_AUDIT.md`.

## 121. Complete-graph reformulation, long witnesses, and the first six-radius braid

481. The triangular alphabet has an exact graph interpretation:
     `E_(s,y)` is the edge `{y,s}` of `K_(R+1)`, and `P_0` is
     one extra loop at zero.  A target is a Ferrers rectangle in the ordered
     edge matrix; an interval must touch all four sides.  This makes
     rotation systems, edge sequencings, and Euler/Hierholzer splicing
     natural candidates, but ordinary local edge adjacency is insufficient.

482. There are exactly

        T_R=sum_(r=1)^R r^2

     target rectangles.  If a universal word has length `n` and every
     target has a witness of length at most `Lambda`, distinct targets
     need distinct physical intervals, so

        T_R <= Lambda*n-Lambda*(Lambda-1)/2.

     Consequently any near-once word
     `n=|T_R|+O(R)=(1/2+o(1))R^2` has at least one target whose shortest
     witness has length `(2/3+o(1))R`.  A successful braid must therefore
     create long nested clean intervals; arranging constant-size provider
     triples locally cannot suffice.

483. A new spanning universal certificate at `R=6` has length `27`,
     while `|T_6|=22`.  Remote exhaustive verification checks all
     `91` targets, all `22` alphabet cells, and zero misses.  Therefore

        1 <= rho(6) <= 5.

     The word is stored in `scratch/triangular_r6_plus5.txt`.  Since
     `floor((R-1)^2/4)=6` at `R=6`, the earlier quadratic
     small-case pattern is false both as an all-`R` formula and as a
     universal repetition lower bound.  This is the first finite evidence
     that genuinely favors the linear-overhead portal braid.

484. The current exact ledger for the spanning triangular subproblem is

        rho(1)=0, rho(2)=0, rho(3)=1,
        1<=rho(4)<=2, 1<=rho(5)<=4, 1<=rho(6)<=5.

     Only the first three values are exact.  The graph reformulation,
     long-witness theorem, linear lower bound, finite certificates, and
     independent audit are in `TRIANGULAR_MIN_REPEATS.md` and
     `TRIANGULAR_MIN_REPEATS_AUDIT.md`.

## 122. Fan-capped avoidance removes the quadratic endpoint loophole

485. Let `I_i=[ell_i,r_i]`, `1<=i<=M`, be selected witnesses for an
     antichain, ordered so that both endpoint sequences increase, and let
     `D=N-M`, `w_i=r_i-ell_i`.  If `F` is a distinct target family of chain
     height `h>=1` whose chosen witnesses avoid containing every complete
     `I_i`, define

        A_t=#{x:[x,t] contains no complete I_i}.

     Then the exact fan-capped theorem is

        |F| <= sum_t min(A_t,h)
            <= sum_i min(w_i,h)+hD.

     At a selected endpoint one has the exact identity
     `A_(r_i)=r_i-ell_i=w_i`; the other `D` endpoints each contribute at
     most `h`.  At fixed `t`, the suffix ORs form a chain, so at most `h`
     distinct members of `F` can occur.  The coefficient one in `hD` is
     sharp.

486. Combining the fan theorem with the audited heterogeneous run cover
     gives

        |F| <= sum_(i in J) min(lambda_i,h)
               +(C_alpha+C_beta)D+(M-|J|)h+hD.

     This is the correct capped replacement for the old avoidance ledger's
     `O(D^2)` endpoint term.  It is unrestricted with respect to fixed rows:
     it uses only the monotone endpoint band of the chosen antichain
     witnesses.

487. In the three-box lattice `[0,2a]^3`, applying the theorem to bounded-
     height lower rank slabs proves several new consequences:

        nested phase order:
        D >= 17/30 a^2 + 4/5 a + 1/30;

        contiguous complete-ring orders:
        D=Omega(a^2);

        side-batched orders:
        13D+24aB >= a^2-O(a);

        general anti-mixing:
        V_a <= aM_a+(2H+6a+2)D.

     Thus the old `D^2` escape is gone for bounded-height slabs.  This rules
     out the nested and complete-ring local architectures throughout the
     full subquadratic-error regime.  It does not prove that every irregular
     middle order has a cheap capped run cover, so it is not a complete
     three-box impossibility theorem.  The proof and independent line-by-
     line audit are `FAN_CAPPED_AVOIDANCE.md` and
     `FAN_CAPPED_AVOIDANCE_AUDIT.md`.

## 123. Exact triangular NFA/SAT and the fourth radius

488. A compact proof-producing SAT encoding now solves the triangular word
     problem at fixed radius and length.  For each Ferrers target it runs a
     17-state nondeterministic suffix automaton: state zero means no retained
     suffix, states `1,...,15` record which of the four boundary providers
     have appeared, and the final state records that a witness has completed.
     The automaton may abandon or restart a candidate suffix, but it can
     reach state 15 only through one contiguous allowed segment touching all
     four sides.  Exactly-one state clauses therefore give a sound and
     complete `O(n R^5)`-size CNF without one selector per physical interval.

489. For `R=4`, length 12 is UNSAT and length 13 is SAT.  Kissat emitted a
     DRAT refutation for length 12; `drat-trim` independently returned
     `s VERIFIED`.  The length-13 model decodes to a word covering all 30
     targets and all 11 cells.  Consequently

        rho(4)=2.

     The generator, proof, exact CNF, model, manifest, and mathematical
     correctness proof are preserved under `scratch/certificates/` and in
     `TRIANGULAR_NFA_SAT.md`.

490. A separately verified `R=7` word has length 38, hence

        1 <= rho(7) <= 9.

     It is stored in `scratch/triangular_r7_plus9.txt`.  Its structure is not
     accidental: it contains a length-24 completion core equal, as a
     multiset, to the exact order-free low-fold lift of the certified `V_5`
     core plus three extra star portals `P_1,P_4,P_5`.  Removing one extra
     `E_(3,2)`, one `P_4`, and one `P_5` leaves the exact 21-letter
     edge-balanced ledger with `kappa=6`; every order-preserving deletion
     fails, so reaching the conjectural `rho(7)<=6` requires a genuine
     rebraid.  The exhaustive small-word ledger is in
     `R7_CERTIFICATE_STRUCTURE.md`.

## 124. Exact edge-balanced portal obstructions

491. The low fold on the complete-graph edge alphabet is injective and
     misses exactly the new first-column edges.  Consequently it gives an
     exact no-waste **multiset** lift of an edge-balanced completion core.
     It is not by itself a recurrence of ordered cores.  The raw lifted
     multiset has unique `P_1` and unique `E_(2,1)`, and a proved low-portal
     theorem shows that no ordering of such a multiset can be a valid core
     once the parameter is at least four.

492. If `P_1` is unique in an edge-balanced core of parameter `S`, then
     every diagonal

        D_y=E_(y+1,y),  1<=y<=S-3,

     must be repeated.  Independently, the occurring star labels form a
     vertex cover of `1-2-...-S` containing vertex one, so at least
     `ceil(S/2)` distinct star labels occur.  Comparing these two disjoint
     demands with the exact `S`-portal budget proves that every edge-balanced
     core with `S>=7` has at least two copies of `P_1`.

493. The earlier lean reset

        extra E_(3,2) -> extra E_(2,1)

     is an exact algebraic multiset identity, but its output has unique
     `P_1` and repeats only `D_1`.  The nested-barrier theorem therefore
     proves that no ordering of this reset profile is a core from output
     parameter five onward.  A viable recurrence must instead carry a
     second `P_1` or pay for a growing ladder of repeated diagonals.  The
     21-letter `R=7` candidate isolated in item 490 performs precisely the
     second-`P_1` trade and passes all known multiplicity obstructions.

494. There is a second independent gap in a naive fold induction.  A lower
     completion core covers strict targets only for `u>=1`; after folding,
     those witnesses cover upper targets with `u>=2,x>=2`.  The entire upper
     family `u=1,x>=2` must be constructed separately, in addition to the
     height-one corridor and terminal suffix fan.  The corrected recurrence
     target is therefore: choose a portal multiset satisfying the duplication
     and star-cover necessities, preserve transported strict witnesses,
     cover the missing `u=1` family, braid a clean height-one corridor, and
     preserve the fan.  This remains conjectural.  The complete proof ledger
     and independent correction audit are in
     `EDGE_BALANCED_CORE_RECURSION.md` and
     `EDGE_BALANCED_CORE_RECURSION_AUDIT.md`.

## 125. Subcritical fixed-dimensional aggregation

495. The fixed-dimensional product reduction needs substantially less local
     accuracy than the earlier linear-error target suggested.  Fix `t>=2`.
     For a `t`-chain box of edge-height vector `ell`, let `g_t(ell)` be its
     shortest nonzero range-maximum word and `w(ell)` its width.  If,
     uniformly for **every** height vector including unbalanced and zero
     sides,

        g_t(ell) <= w(ell)+K(1+sum_i ell_i)^c,

     then

        nu(k) <= W(k)
          +O_(t,c,K)(W(k)(1+k)^((c-t+1)/2)).

     Therefore every exponent `c<t-1` implies

        nu(k)=(1+o(1))W(k).

496. The proof takes a balanced `t`-block split of the Boolean coordinates
     and an SCD in each block.  Product-chain boxes partition the cube and
     their central coefficients sum exactly to `W(k)`.  If `L` is the
     height of a uniformly selected SCD chain in an `s`-cube, then

        Pr(L>=2d)=binom(s,floor(s/2)-d)/W(s)
                 <= exp(-d^2/s),

     hence every real moment satisfies `E(1+L)^c=O((1+s)^(c/2))`.
     The number of product boxes relative to `W(k)` is
     `Theta(k^(-(t-1)/2))`; multiplying these two factors gives the stated
     exponent.  A local zero whose translated box minimum is nonempty costs
     at most one additional entry per box and is absorbed by the `1` in the
     error term.

497. In particular, the three-box route needs only a **uniform** local error
     `O((1+p+q+r)^(2-epsilon))`, not linear error.  The four-box route needs
     a uniform exponent below three.  A bound only for diagonal cubes such
     as `g_4(m,m,m,m)` is insufficient, because the SCD product contains
     highly unbalanced and degenerate height vectors even after the Boolean
     coordinate blocks themselves are balanced.  The theorem and its
     independent audit are `SUBQUADRATIC_PRODUCT_AGGREGATION.md` and
     `SUBQUADRATIC_PRODUCT_AGGREGATION_AUDIT.md`.

## 126. Proof-certified obstruction for the first edge-balanced `R=7` core

498. The 21-token multiset `M_6^*` isolated from the verified `R=7` word has
     now been tested by an exact fixed-multiset SAT encoding.  Position/token
