     variables choose a permutation with exact multiplicities; strict-target
     selector variables require one clean provider interval for every target;
     additional clauses impose the nested suffix fan and terminal `P_0`.
     The encoding is sound and complete for this precise completion-core
     question.

499. The resulting formula has exactly `23691` variables and `188975`
     clauses.  It is UNSAT.  A DRAT proof was independently rechecked on a
     second RunPod using a freshly compiled `drat-trim`, which returned
     `s VERIFIED` after `585688` resolution steps.  Regenerating the CNF gives
     a byte-identical file.  Therefore:

        no permutation of this specific multiset M_6^*
        is an R=7 completion core.

     This does **not** rule out another 21-token multiset, prove
     `rho(7)>6`, or rule out unrestricted triangular excess six.  The exact
     theorem scope, hashes, regenerated formula, proof, and independent log
     are in `TRIANGULAR_CORE_SAT_AUDIT.md` and `scratch/certificates/`.

## 127. Universal capped-run cover and the remaining constant-four barrier

500. For the middle hexagon `H_a`, every block of `4a+2` consecutive distinct
     points in an arbitrary **linear** ordering contains an internal
     constant-coordinate threshold peak run.  Assigning such a run to each
     eligible index gives an unconditional run cover with

        |J| = M_a-(4a+2),
        C_alpha <= 4a+3,
        C_beta = 0,

     and capped intrinsic cost

        sum_(i in J) min(lambda_i,3a-1)
          <= 2a(M_a-4a-2) = (6+o(1))a^3.

     The proof reduces a peak-free scalar word to a valley.  Three valley
     pivots split the middle into two monotone point paths, each of length at
     most `2a+1`, contradicting a longer peak-free block.

501. A sharper theorem holds for every arbitrary permutation and reversal of
     the intact half-open side blocks, even with `Theta(a)` side switches.
     Every coordinate plateau has at most `a+2` vertices, and for `a>=3` the
     same assignment has exact cost at most

        (a+1)(M_a-4a-2)
          = 3a^3+2a^2-2a-1.

     Thus the fan-capped theorem forces `D=Omega(a^2)` for the entire intact-
     side-block regime.  Ordinary batching, reversal, and frequent side
     switching cannot realize a subquadratic three-box error.

502. Across all three coordinates, the internal index-edge sets of distinct
     peak plateaux are disjoint, so their total intrinsic length is at most
     `M_a-1`.  Any arbitrary order escaping the preceding cheap-cover
     mechanisms must consequently contain `Theta_delta(a)` almost-disjoint
     directed central coordinate-line subsequences longer than
     `(4/3-delta)a`.  The remaining geometry is a rotating triangular
     long-line braid, not a random or phase-separated order.

503. The lower target family has size `V_a=4a^3+O(a^2)`.  Therefore a
     universal capped-run cover of cost `<(4-epsilon)a^3`, with the already
     proved `O(a)` congestion and omitted indices, would force
     `D=Omega(a^2)`.  Combined with item 495, this would contradict every
     uniform three-box local error exponent `c<2` and close that subcritical
     aggregation route.  The current universal constant six is not enough;
     the constant three theorem applies only to intact side blocks.

504. The tempting binary short-peak-density strengthening is false.  There is
     an explicit search-free ordering in which at most

        (3/8+O(1/a))

     of the length-`(4a+2)` windows contain any internal threshold run with
     `lambda<=a`.  Put arbitrary leftovers first, then concatenate the full
     high positive lines `X_t,Y_t,Z_t` for
     `t=a-floor((a-1)/2),...,a-1`, with the cross coordinate monotone on each
     line.  These lines are pairwise disjoint.  Every join creates a plateau
     at the global minimum `-a`, hence a valley, while every suffix peak is a
     full line of at least `a+2` points.  The suffix has
     `(15/8+o(1))a^2` points and only the `(9/8+o(1))a^2`-point prefix can
     contaminate short-peak windows.  This refutes short/not-short density,
     not the weighted capped-run program; the latter must exploit the exact
     long-run cost distribution, non-peak components, or heterogeneous
     assignments.  The construction and proof are in
     `SHORT_PEAK_DENSITY.md`.  The universal cover theorem and audit remain in
     `UNIVERSAL_CAPPED_RUN_COVER.md` and
     `UNIVERSAL_CAPPED_RUN_COVER_AUDIT.md`.

## 129. The rotating-braid interior crosses below the critical constant

509. A clean direct braid is a concatenation of disjoint directed peak
     plateaux whose fixed coordinates rotate `x,y,z,x,...`.  Classify an
     internal block as type A when the preceding fixed coordinate decreases
     and the following one increases along it, and as type B for the reverse.
     Two consecutive B blocks create a singleton or two-position peak at
     their join.  For an A block of fixed level `t_j`, immediate peak
     maximality gives the exact transition inequality

        lambda_j <= t_(j-1)+t_j+t_(j+1)-2.

510. Pooling the three copies of each coordinate level, using line capacity,
     and optimizing the resulting weighted level ledger first gives the valid
     bound `287a^2/96+O(a)`.  Feeding the assumed lower mass
     `lambda_j>(4/3)a` back into the same envelope sharpens this to

        sum_j lambda_j
          <= (4+2sqrt(6))/3 a^2+O(a)
          < (3-1/30)a^2+O(a).

     Thus a critical direct braid leaves at least
     `(5-2sqrt(6))a^2/3-O(a)>a^2/30-O(a)` ordering edges outside its displayed
     plateaux, and its displayed vertex density is below `89/90+o(1)`.

511. More importantly, assign every admissible start physically lying in
     block `P_j` to the next block `P_(j+1)`.  Since a forward window has
     length `4a+2`, it contains that next block.  A secant inequality for
     adjacent lengths, combined with the mass-feasible level envelope, gives

        sum_(braid starts) q_i
          <= (16+8sqrt(6))/9 a^3+O(a^2)
          = 3.9551019935... a^3+O(a^2).

     This is the first proved strict saving below the decisive constant four
     inside the only surviving long-line geometry.

512. The remaining starts lie in gaps between maximal direct-braid
     components.  At the extremal feasible point, the margin in item 511 is
     exactly `(4/3)a` times the forced gap mass.  Therefore it suffices to
     service gap starts at average cost **strictly below** `(4/3)a`, with
     compatible `O(a)` congestion.  Equivalently, with
     `sigma=a^(-2)sum lambda_j` and `s=m/a`, the exact residual budget is

        Q_gap <=
          (4-epsilon-(10/3)sigma+(8/3)s)a^3+o(a^3).

     Edge defect alone cannot prove this because one long peak can service
     `Theta(a)` overlapping starts.  The next theorem must exploit component
     maximality, boundary valleys, non-peak threshold components, or a
     heterogeneous left/right assignment.  Proof and independent audit are
     `ROTATING_BRAID_ANALYSIS.md` and
     `ROTATING_BRAID_ANALYSIS_AUDIT.md`.

## 130. Explicit four-box construction outside the jointly thick sector

513. For a product of four chains with sorted edge heights

        h <= a <= b <= c,

     there is a deterministic range-maximum word of length

        g_4(h,a,b,c)
          <= (h+1)(a+1)(b+c+1)-1.

     The construction is completely elementary.  Decompose the rectangle
     `[0,a]x[0,b]` into `a+1` saturated hook chains.  Pair each hook with
     the chain `[0,c]`; the descending-then-ascending chain-rectangle word
     covers their Cartesian product in the sum of their chain lengths.
     This gives a three-box word of length `(a+1)(b+c+1)-1`.  Repeat it in
     the `h+1` fourth-coordinate slices, restoring each omitted nonzero
     slice origin by one literal point.  The displayed bound follows.

514. Put `S=h+a+b+c`.  For every fixed `delta>0`, the construction is
     subcritical whenever

        (h+1)(a+1) <= (S+1)^(2-delta),

     because then `g_4=O((S+1)^(3-delta))`.  By the subcritical aggregation
     theorem, a uniform extension to the complementary sector would prove

        nu(k)=(1+o(1))W(k).

     Hence the four-box route no longer has to handle arbitrary unbalanced
     or degenerate vectors: only boxes whose **two shortest directions are
     jointly thick** remain.  The sorted choice is optimal within this
     slice-and-hook scheme; the two alternative coordinate choices lose
     exactly `c(b-a)` or `b(c-a)` before multiplying by `h+1`.

515. This result is constructive and independently audited, but it is not
     yet the missing uniform four-box theorem.  For typical balanced SCD
     height tuples all four sides have order `sqrt(k)`, so the jointly thick
     sector carries non-negligible width mass.  The current mathematical
     target is therefore a two-slice fusion or mixed-entry construction
     which makes adjacent fourth-coordinate slices share connector mass.
     The proof and audit are `CONSTRUCTIVE_CONSTANT_ONE_NEXT.md` and
     `CONSTRUCTIVE_CONSTANT_ONE_NEXT_AUDIT.md`.

## 131. Audited run spectrum: a valid average law, not a forced staircase

516. Fix selected middle witnesses and an admissible internal-run assignment
     of one-sided span at most `sigma`.  With

        Def_R(h)=sum_i (h-lambda_i)_+,
        B_a(h)=hM_a-|S_h|,

     the exact simultaneous capped-spectrum inequality is

        Def_R(h)
          <= B_a(h)+(C_alpha+C_beta+h)D
          <= B_a(h)+(2sigma+h)D.

     For the universal forward-window assignment the exact span convention
     gives `sigma=4a+3`.  At the full nonzero lower-half cap `h=3a-1`, this
     is equivalent, when `D=o(a^2)`, to

        sum_i min(lambda_i,3a-1) >= (4-o(1))a^3,

     or average capped cost at least `(4/3-o(1))a`.  This strengthens and
     systematizes the fan ledger and is fully proved.

517. The spectrum theorem does **not** imply that almost every individual
     run has length at least `(4/3-o(1))a`.  The exact direct exceptional-set
     consequence is only

        #{i: lambda^*_sigma(i)<=t}
          <= [B_a(h)+(2sigma+h)D]/(h-t),

     optimized over `h>t`.  At proportional thresholds this permits
     `Theta(a^2)` exceptions.  Indeed the complete leading cap spectrum is
     compatible with an abstract distribution having `3/5` of the indices
     at cost `a` and `2/5` at cost `2a`.  Thus capped average cannot be
     upgraded to pointwise concentration without new geometry.

518. Consequently Fable's claimed forced partition into approximately
     `9a/4` rides, three-phase handoff, trapezoid trajectory, and exact
     transportation equations are retracted as theorems.  The correct
     geometric consequence is the already proved long-corridor theorem:
     for every fixed `0<delta<4/3`, a near-width word forces
     `Theta_delta(a)` directed central-line peak plateaux longer than
     `(4/3-delta)a`, occupying `Omega_delta(a^2)` total mass.  They need not
     partition the order and their transitions remain unclassified.

519. Literal middle witnesses admit a sharper valid consequence: if `K`
     selected middle witnesses are singleton intervals, then `K<=D+1`.
     More generally, if `K` witness widths are at most `r<h`, then

        K(h-r) <= B_a(h)+hD.

     The prior claim that almost every witness width is at least `8a/9`
     was another invalid average-to-concentration step.  The corrected proof
     and full claim-by-claim audit are in `FABLE_RUN_SPECTRUM_AUDIT.md`.

## 132. Three-short-side fusion and the exact limit of independent chains

520. For sorted four-box heights `h<=a<=b<=c`, put

        d=(h+a-b)_+,
        Psi(d)=ceil(d/2)(floor(d/2)+1).

     Nested hook decompositions give an explicit SCD of
     `[0,h]x[0,a]x[0,b]` with exactly

        r=(h+1)(a+1)-Psi(d)

     symmetric chains.  Pairing each of these chains with `[0,c]` and using
     the shortest descending/ascending chain-rectangle connector proves

        g_4(h,a,b,c)
          <=(h+1)(a+1)(b+c+1)-1-c Psi(d).

     Thus fusion across the first three directions gives a genuine saving
     whenever `b<h+a`.  In the equal box it improves the leading word
     coefficient from `2` to `7/4`.

521. This architecture can be evaluated exactly.  If `L_j` are the edge
     heights of the three-short-side SCD chains, its word length and the
     actual four-box width are

        |P|+cr-1,
        sum_j(min(c,L_j)+1),

     respectively.  Its exact excess over width is therefore

        sum_j max(c,L_j)-1.

     For the equal box the width coefficient is `2/3`, so the excess is
     `(13/12)m^3+O(m^2)`.  More generally the architectural error is
     `Theta(S(h+1)(a+1))`.  Hence this fusion changes the constant but not
     the critical cubic exponent in the jointly thick sector.

522. The necessary next object is now exact: a connector which shares
     entries across **different** neighbouring SCD chains.  Independent
     chain rectangles are already locally shortest when entries and
     witnesses are confined to their own rectangle; that conditional
     optimality is not a lower bound against mixed cross-chain words.
     The construction, exact accounting, and independent audit are
     `THICK_FOUR_BOX_SLICE_FUSION.md` and
     `THICK_FOUR_BOX_SLICE_FUSION_AUDIT.md`.

## 133. Labeled ride capacity: the exact surviving global gate

523. A single entry achieving one prescribed coordinate can participate in
     `Theta(ah)` targets in an `h`-rank slab.  For `1<=h<=a`, the exact
     uniform maximum is

        h(2a+1)-floor(h^2/4).

     The explicit `4a+1`-position two-arm portal realizes

        h(2a+1)-h(h+1)/2

     such targets through one portal entry.  It is order-sharp but not
     constant-sharp when `h=Theta(a)`.  Therefore per-entry caps and local
     coordinate-achievement counting cannot by themselves sum to a
     quadratic word defect.

524. Fresh achievements do yield a rigorous global compatibility graph.
     If `M` selected middle targets are partitioned into `R` directed rides,
     there are `Q=M-R` internal transitions.  Make a bipartite graph between
     the `Q` fresh head demands and `Q` fresh tail demands, joining a pair
     exactly when their physical difference regions overlap at a cap-
     compatible position.  Every realization satisfies

        N>=2Q-nu(Gamma),
        D>=M-2R-nu(Gamma)=Delta(Gamma)-R.

     Thus a quadratic Hall deficiency would close the ride architecture.

525. An explicit delay-`a`, factorable two-ride A turn matches `a-1` tail
     demands from the first ride with `a-1` head demands of the second.  The
     shared maximal-factor entry is exactly `(a-j-1,j+1,a)`.  Hence the
     fresh middle-label defect is not additive ride by ride.  This example
     does not construct all below-middle targets, and continuation around a
     full three-direction windmill remains conjectural.  The corrected scope
     and exact capacity audit are in `LABELED_RIDE_CAPACITY.md` and
     `LABELED_RIDE_CAPACITY_AUDIT.md`.

## 134. Gap service closes the few-component braid endpoint

526. Fix `1<c<2` and call a directed peak plateau dangerous when
     `lambda>ca`.  Resolve the dangerous plateaux into `r` maximal direct
     rotating components, with total edge mass `E=sigma*a^2` and count
     `m=sa`.  Defining gaps as components of the complement of the complete
     dangerous **vertex union**, there is an internal-run assignment with
     congestion at most `4a+3` and leading cost

        Q <=(3c+2sigma-2cs)a^3+O(a^2r+a^2).

     The exact construction services deep gap starts at cost at most `ca`,
     uses the secant next-block assignment inside each direct component,
     and pays universal cost `2a` only on a bounded interface zone and each
     terminal component block.

527. Hence, if `r=o(a)` and the normalized excess dangerous length

        e_c=sigma-cs

     satisfies `e_c<(4-3c)/2-eta`, then

        Q<=(4-2eta)a^3+o(a^3).

     At an additional mass-feasibility endpoint `e_c=o(1)`, choosing
     `c=4/3-1/1000` gives the explicit strict coefficient
     `4-3/1000`.  Few components alone do not imply this conclusion; the
     excess-mass condition is essential.

528. Pointwise seam cheapness is false.  An explicit `a=12m` family of
     high full lines separated by `Theta(a)` one-point valley separators
     has the property that every local one-sided avoiding run near an
     interior separator costs more than `4a/3`.  Thus the remaining
     `r=Theta(a)` case requires global resource amortization, not one cheap
     run per seam.  The theorem, exact finite accounting, counterexample,
     and independent audit are `BRAID_GAP_SERVICE.md` and
     `BRAID_GAP_SERVICE_AUDIT.md`.

## 135. First-dangerous service removes component count at zero excess

529. A stronger assignment ignores direct-component boundaries.  For each
     eligible start, inspect its forward window of length `L=4a+2`.  If it
     contains a complete dangerous directed plateau, assign the **first**
     such plateau; otherwise the dangerous-free-window lemma supplies a run
     of cost at most `ca`.  If `P_j` has predecessor `P_(j-1)`, excess
     `delta_j=lambda_j-ca`, and preceding gap size `g_(j-1)`, the number of
     starts assigned to it is at most

        min(L-lambda_j,lambda_(j-1)+1+g_(j-1)).

     This localization is valid even when consecutive dangerous plateaux
     belong to different rotating components.

530. A cyclic secant sum then gives the audited global bound

        Q <= ca M_a
             +2a sum_j delta_j
             +sum_(j>=2) delta_j min(g_(j-1),L-lambda_j)
             +O(a^2).

     In normalized form, with `e_c=a^(-2)sum delta_j` and seam term `H_c`,

        Q <=(3c+2e_c+H_c)a^3+O(a^2),

     where

        H_c <=(4-c+o(1))e_c,
        H_c <=(2-c)(3-sigma)+o(1).

     Thus for any fixed `c<4/3`, the endpoint condition `e_c=o(1)` implies

        Q<=3ca^3+o(a^3)<4a^3

     with no restriction on the number of braid components.  This removes
     the transparent-separator obstruction at the exact endpoint.  Proof
     and independent audit are `FIRST_DANGEROUS_GLOBAL_SERVICE.md` and
     `FIRST_DANGEROUS_GLOBAL_SERVICE_AUDIT.md`.

531. Scalar length, gap, edge-mass, and line-capacity constraints alone do
     not force a useful threshold.  An explicit feasible abstract profile
     has `a` plateaux of normalized length `3/2`, each on an available
     parallel line and separated by one point.  For every `1<c<4/3`,

        e_c=3/2-c,
        H_c=o(1),
        3c+2e_c+H_c=3+c+o(1)>4.

     A saturated two-atom version still defeats the scalar inequalities.
     These profiles are not asserted to extend to full valid hexagon orders;
     they prove that the next theorem must use transition signs, cross-line
     intersections, the run spectrum, or boundary geometry—not merely the
     one-dimensional dangerous-length distribution.  The exact no-go is
     `MULTISCALE_DANGEROUS_PROFILE.md`.

## 136. Exact cross-chain fusion in the first nontrivial packet

532. The smallest mixed packet is now solved exactly.  For

        R_c=[0,1]x[0,1]x[0,c]

     with coordinatewise maximum,

        g(R_c)=ceil(3c/2)+2

     for every `c>=0`.  The explicit word uses the `c` forced pure-height
     markers, alternating positive `X/Y` pivots, and two level-zero pivots.
     Every pure `X`, pure `Y`, mixed `XY`, and vertical target has an explicit
     interval witness.

533. The lower bound is entirely combinatorial.  The `c` pure vertical
     targets and the two level-zero atoms force `c+2` literal entries.  If
     `e` further entries are present, exceptional heights inject into those
     extras; every other height forces its unique vertical marker into a
     distinct gap whose two pure-colour neighbours are opposite.  A witness
     for the level-zero mixed target consumes one additional coloured gap.
     Hence `c<=2e`, giving the matching length lower bound.

534. Independent chain-rectangle connectors use `2c+3`, so this packet saves

        floor(c/2)+1=Theta(c).

     This is the first proved cross-chain fusion with a leading-order saving,
     and it positively supports the thick four-box program.  A naive
     two-port extension is nevertheless blocked: a black-box core exposing
     every height as both a prefix and a suffix maximum needs at least
     `2c-1` positions.  That port theorem applies only under its stated
     height-zero external and one-port witness hypotheses, not to arbitrary
     mixed tails.  The exact proof, independent audit, and verifier are
     `CROSS_CHAIN_PACKET_CONNECTOR.md`,
     `CROSS_CHAIN_PACKET_CONNECTOR_AUDIT.md`, and
     `scratch/diamond_packet_verify.cpp`.  The next constructor target is
     the uniform strip `[0,1]x[0,s]x[0,c]`.

## 137. Assignment-free interval-supply law

535. For each forward window, let `q_i` be the minimum effective cost of a
     complete internal peak plateau: its own cost when directed, and zero
     (via an interior cross-coordinate singleton peak) when nondirected.
     Choosing a minimum plateau gives a span-`4a+3` assignment.  The audited
     capped-spectrum theorem therefore implies, in every hypothetical
     `D=o(a^2)` word,

        sum_i min(q_i,3a-1) >=4a^3-o(a^3).

536. Define

        supply(t)=sum_(directed P: lambda(P)>t)(L-lambda(P)),
        L=4a+2.

     A plateau of cost `lambda` can be complete in at most `L-lambda`
     forward windows.  Clipping boundary service and using layer cake gives
     the assignment-free MASTER inequality

        integral_0^(2a) min(M_a,supply(t)) dt
          >=4a^3-o(a^3).

     Since normalized supply is nonincreasing, for every fixed
     `0<c<4/3`,

        supply(ca)/a^2
          >=(4-3c)/(2-c)-o(1).

537. Consequently the number of directed peak plateaux longer than `ca` is
     at least

        [(4-3c)/((2-c)(4-c))]a-o(a).

     At `c=1`, at least `a/3-o(a)` distinct coordinate lines carry a
     directed plateau longer than `a`; line uniqueness is valid at this
     threshold.  This is a genuine distributional requirement, not
     pointwise concentration or spatial clustering.  Static edge and line
     spectra still satisfy it, so the remaining information must come from
     how those plateau service intervals and transitions are coupled.
     The corrected theorem audit is `FABLE_INTERVAL_SUPPLY_AUDIT.md`; several
     side claims in Fable's draft (a reversed service inequality, subunit
     line uniqueness, and automatic spatial clustering) are explicitly not
     retained.

        Q <= ca M_a+2a sum_j delta_j
             +sum_(j>=2) delta_j min(g_(j-1),L-lambda_j)+O_c(a^2).

     `c>1`; the predecessor term is bounded directly by

        sum_j delta_j lambda_(j-1) <=2a sum_j delta_j.

     Hence, under `D=o(a^2)`, the mass law

        2e(c)+H(c) >=4-3c-o(1)

     is certified for every fixed `0<c<4/3`.  The theorem is not uniform for
     a threshold `c=c(a)->0`, because the plateau count and omitted-boundary
     constants are only `O_c(a)` and `O_c(a^2)`.  Two independent line-by-line
     checks are `FABLE_THEOREM_O_AUDIT.md` and
     `FABLE_PROVENANCE_AUDIT.md`.

545. Fable Section 10.4 contains a decisive scalar error and is not part of
     the theorem ledger.  For the normalized plateau counting measure `mu`,
     the count tail and weighted service supply are

        F(c)/a = mu((c,2]),
        supply(ca)/a^2 = integral_(x>c) (4-x) dmu(x),

     respectively.  They are not equal.  The valid count consequence of the
     supply theorem is only

        F(c)/a >=(4-3c)/((2-c)(4-c))-o(1),

     tending to `1/2`, not `2`, as `c->0+`.  The old atom
     `mu=delta_(3/2),H=0` is excluded by the extended **mass** law, not by
     supply.

546. More importantly, the corrected scalar system does not force edge
     saturation or a dense adjacent chain.  The whole continuum

        mu=2 delta_x, H=0,  4/3<=x<=3/2,

     satisfies every corrected mass, weighted-supply, edge, line, and seam
     inequality.  At `x=4/3`, one has `sigma=8/3<3`.  Therefore the claims
     `sigma->3`, a unique `2 delta_(3/2)` corner, and reduction of the entire
     problem to a dense-chain general-pattern/2-cycle ledger are false.
     Boundary-reservoir, unsaturated, and gap-carrying profiles remain.

547. The historical Fable notebook deliberately retains obsolete exploratory
     sections.  The following must not be cited as theorems: pointwise
     `8/9` or `4/3` run concentration; a forced ride/staircase partition;
     `9a/4` rides and three-phase handoff; unique windmill geometry; automatic
     spatial clustering; the unweighted Section-10.4 supply system; or forced
     dense saturation.  The late same-coordinate literal-adjacency
     proposition is correct, but its two-letter Lemma R mishandles equality
     seams (they create a cost-one two-position peak), and Theorem P silently
     uses a `ca+1` minimum plateau length absent from its statement.  Those
     two claims remain uncertified and outside this handoff.  The authoritative
     remaining general gate is still a non-scalar transition,
     boundary-reservoir, cross-line-intersection, or pinning theorem, not an
     exclusively dense 2-cycle problem.

     A narrower repaired two-cycle statement is proved.  Fix `c>0`.  A
     hypothetical `D=o(a^2)` order cannot have one contiguous interval,
     covering all but `o(a^2)` positions, tiled by literally adjacent directed
     peak plateaux alternating between two fixed coordinates, when every
     plateau has cost greater than `ca`.  Rise-to-fall equality seams cost one
     rather than zero, still only `O(a^2)` total; between such seams the third
     coordinate has at most `4a+2` plateau edges.  The service contradiction
     then follows from the capped run spectrum.  This theorem does not cover
     shared endpoints, `Theta(a)` interspersed reset gaps, or arbitrary scalar
     profiles.  The exact taxonomy and proof are `FABLE_TWO_CYCLE_AUDIT.md`.

## 142. Position-sensitive closure of the atomic scalar frontier

560. The corrected scalar laws missed a strong small-cap spatial constraint.
     Let `R_c` be any set of middle-order indices for which at least one valid
     forward or backward window of length `L=4a+2` contains no complete
     directed peak plateau longer than `ca`.  The dangerous-free-window lemma
     assigns every such index a run of integer cost at most `floor(ca)`.
     Applying the subset run-spectrum inequality at an integer cap
     `floor(ca)<h<=a` gives the exact finite bound

        |R_c| (h-floor(ca))
          <= h(h+1)(2h+1)/6 + (2L+2+h)D.

     If `D=o(a^2)` and fixed `0<c<2/3`, optimizing at
     `h=floor(3ca/2)` yields

        |R_c|/a^2 <= (9/4)c^2+o(1).

     Thus a region locally free of `c`-dangerous plateaux has quadratic, not
     merely linear, density in the small threshold.  The complete proof and
     independent line-by-line audit are `BOUNDARY_RESERVOIR_PROFILE.md` and
     `BOUNDARY_RESERVOIR_PROFILE_AUDIT.md`.

561. This quadratic law removes all unsaturated members of the atomic family

        mu_a -> 2 delta_x,  4/3<=x<3/2,

     provided the first-dangerous seam functional satisfies `H_a(c)->0` for
     every sufficiently small fixed `c` along the same subsequence.  For fixed
     `c<x`, weak convergence gives dangerous plateau vertex mass
     `(2x+o(1))a^2`.  Vanishing seam mass makes the total `2L`-clipped internal
     gap mass `o(a^2)`, while a macroscopic prefix or suffix gap loses only
     `O(a)` positions.  Hence

        |R_c| >= (3-2x+o(1))a^2.

     Combining with item 560 gives `3-2x<=(9/4)c^2` for every small fixed
     `c`; taking `a->infinity` first and then `c->0` forces `x>=3/2`.

562. The remaining saturated endpoint `2 delta_(3/2)` is itself geometrically
     impossible, by a separate cross-line packing theorem requiring neither
     run spectrum nor seam assumptions.  Keep the `(2+o(1))a` directed peak
     plateaux of length `(3/2+o(1))a`, and let `n_x,n_y,n_z` count their three
     coordinate directions.  Their coordinate levels are distinct within a
     direction.  If `I` is the number of genuinely intersecting selected-line
     pairs and `R` the total unused points on those selected lines, then

        R >= (2/3) I-o(a^2).

     Indeed, at a point incident with two or three selected lines, all but at
     most one plateau must omit it; only `O(a)` word-seam endpoints can be used
     twice.  Conversely, exact line sizes, the minimum absolute-level sum, and
     the at-most-`24 epsilon^2 a^2` nonintersecting fringe give

        R <= (1/2) I+12 epsilon^2 a^2+o(a^2),
        I >= (1-28 epsilon^2-o(1))a^2.

     Fixed `epsilon<1/10` makes these inequalities incompatible.  The theorem
     and its independent proof are `SATURATED_ATOM_CROSSLINE.md` and
     `SATURATED_ATOM_CROSSLINE_AUDIT.md`.

563. Consequently **no** atom profile `2 delta_x`, `4/3<=x<=3/2`, remains as
     a geometric survivor under the hypotheses above.  This is a genuine
     advance beyond the scalar ledger in item 546, not a contradiction to it:
     item 546 correctly says the scalar variables alone admit the continuum;
     items 560--562 add clipped physical position and cross-line incidence.
     Non-atomic mixtures, near-threshold mass, and profiles with positive seam
     functional remain open, so the three-box obstruction and
     `nu(k)=(1+o(1))W(k)` are not yet proved.

564. The live Fable transcript has also been re-audited through record 720.
     Its Section 12 correctly accepts the weighted-supply correction and the
     unsaturated scalar counterprofile, but remains internally inconsistent:
     it calls independently proved Theorem O conjectural; its window-cost tail
     inequality does not by itself imply plateau-edge saturation; its revised
     two-letter `P'/P''` claims still lack uniform span, congestion, maxima,
     and gap-hosting arguments; and “windmill v3” is conditional heuristic
     arithmetic, not a uniqueness theorem.  None of those unsupported claims
     enters this ledger.  Exact record counts, hashes, and corrections are in
     Section 12 of `FABLE_PROVENANCE_AUDIT.md`.

## 143. General boundary--seam inequality beyond atomic profiles

565. The boundary-reservoir argument extends quantitatively to an arbitrary
     limiting directed-plateau measure.  In an internal complement gap of `g`
     positions, the exact number having neither a forward nor a backward
     gap-contained length-`L` window is

        I_L(g)=g                 for 0<=g<=L,
               =2L-g            for L<g<2L,
               =0               for g>=2L.

     Hence `I_L(g)<=min(g,L)`.  Splitting dangerous successors into the short
     band `ca<lambda<=(c+eta)a` and those with excess greater than `eta*a`
     gives the finite inequality

        M_a-sum_j lambda_j
          <= |R_a(c)|
             + [L/(eta*a*(L-2a))] a^3 H_a(c)
             + L n_a(c,eta)+2L+m.

     The two word-boundary gaps cost only `2L`; shared plateau endpoints give
     the final `+m`.  This statement is exact and non-atomic.

566. Let `mu_a` converge weakly to `mu`, put

        sigma_c=integral_(c,2] x dmu(x),
        nu(c,eta)=mu((c,c+eta]),

     and take continuity endpoints.  Dividing item 565 by `a^2` and combining
     with the quadratic reservoir law gives, for fixed `0<c<2/3`,

        3-sigma_c
          <= r(c)+(2/eta)H(c)+4nu(c,eta)
          <= (9/4)c^2+(2/eta)H(c)+4nu(c,eta).

     In particular, if `H(c)->0` as `c->0` through continuity points, choose
     `eta=c+sqrt(H(c))` after taking the profile limit.  The seam and short-band
     terms vanish, forcing total directed-plateau edge mass `sigma=3`.  No
     threshold is allowed to depend on `a`.

567. Eliminating `r(c)` yields the explicit necessary seam lower bound

        H(c) >= (1/2) sup_eta eta
          [3-sigma_c-(9/4)c^2-4mu((c,c+eta])]_+.

     This still does not close the general problem.  The abstract pair
     `mu=2delta_(4/3)` with a specified positive seam function satisfies the
     corrected mass, weighted-supply, line-capacity, seam-upper, and new
     boundary-lower inequalities.  It is not asserted geometrically
     realizable.  Thus the remaining general gate is now precisely the
     positive-seam region, requiring a transition/level or stronger seam
     coupling theorem.  Proof and independent audit are
     `GENERAL_BOUNDARY_RESERVOIR.md` and
     `GENERAL_BOUNDARY_RESERVOIR_AUDIT.md`.

## 144. Compact exact pair-shadow encoding for `k=11`

568. A rank-eight target `U` has 28 possible rank-six centers.  At a center
     `T`, the twelve induced Johnson edges split into two groups of six,
     according to which of the two elements of `U-T` the neighbour adds.
     Three consecutive vertices have union `U` exactly when the two selected
     incident edges use opposite groups.  Dually, a rank-four target has 21
     centers and two groups of five, according to which excess center element
     is removed.  This is an exact local characterization, not a relaxation.

569. For each target-center, introduce two group-OR variables and their AND.
     For target 958 this replaces 1,008 explicit pair variables and 3,025
     clauses by 84 variables and 477 clauses.  Across every rank-four and
     rank-eight target it replaces 200,970 variables/603,405 clauses by
     34,650/182,985, saving 166,320 variables and 420,420 clauses.  The same
     gate works both up front and in the exact lazy target loop, including
     sparse candidate graphs.  `K11_COMPACT_PAIR_SHADOWS.md`, its independent
     audit, and `scratch/verify_k11_compact_pair.cpp` prove equivalence and
     enumerate every old witness.

570. Summing degrees on all 28 rank-six subsets of a rank-eight `U` does give

        2 i_U+c_U+e_U=56,

     with 168 internal, 504 cut, and 28 dummy edges.  It was deliberately not
     encoded: the current unary equality would cost 95,676 variables and
     285,321 clauses for one target, is already the sum of 28 degree equations,
     and contains no triple-witness information.  The compact group gate is
     both exact and vastly cheaper; the no-go audit is
     `K11_R8_INDUCED_FLAG_MOMENT_AUDIT.md`.

## 145. Mixed-profile cross-line obstruction

571. For every fixed threshold `1<b<2`, select all directed internal
     coordinate-peak plateaux of length greater than `ba`.  Write `m` for
     their count, `E` for their total edge length, `n_x,n_y,n_z` for their
     direction counts, `T` for the sum of their absolute coordinate levels,
     `N` for the number of cross-direction selected-line pairs which do not
     meet in the hexagon, and `J` for the number of points incident with
     selected lines in all three directions.  The exact local omission charge
     gives

        E <= 2am-T-(m^2-n_x^2-n_y^2-n_z^2)/2+N+J+O_b(a).

     The key point is the sharpened pointwise charge `R>=I-J-O(a)`: a genuine
     pair intersection costs one omission except that a triple-line point
     services its three pairs with only two omissions.  The `O(a)` term is
     only the shared-endpoint loss.  No atomicity, length concentration,
     direction balance, or seam hypothesis is used in this finite theorem.

572. Keeping the additive-triple term, rather than replacing `J` by the
     universal `I/3` bound, produces an exact limiting variational gate over
     the three direction-level measures.  The one-dimensional discrete Riesz
     rearrangement inequality bounds the normalized triple count by

        Theta(alpha,beta,gamma)
          = beta*gamma-(beta+gamma-alpha)_+^2/4

     after ordering `alpha>=beta>=gamma`.  End-fringe placement is retained
     jointly through `T-N`; separating those two ledgers loses the decisive
     information.

573. Consequently, no weak limiting directed-plateau measure supported on
     `[4/3,3/2]` can arise along a sequence satisfying both `D=o(a^2)` and
     `H_a(c)->0` for every sufficiently small fixed `c`.  Boundary-reservoir
     saturation first forces total plateau edge mass `3`.  The remaining
     direction-count optimization has maximum upper bound

        3271/1152 < 3,

     a contradiction.  This excludes every atomic, non-atomic, and mixed
     profile in that exact support interval, including the abstract
     `(9/4) delta_(4/3)` profile which survives all corrected scalar and
     triple-blind inequalities.

574. The scope is important.  The theorem does not yet treat positive-seam
     profiles, measures only approximately supported on `[4/3,3/2]`, or
     arbitrary tails outside that interval.  Those require a stability
     theorem or a solution of the enriched length/direction/level/additive-
     triple variational gate.  The complete proof and independent line-by-line
     audit are `MIXED_PROFILE_CROSSLINE.md` and
     `MIXED_PROFILE_CROSSLINE_AUDIT.md`; the audit verifies the finite
     endpoint accounting, discrete Riesz passage, piecewise optimization, and
     the constant `3271/1152`.

## 146. Compact exact four-shadow encoding for `k=11`

575. Fix a rank-three target `S` and a candidate middle Johnson edge `B--C`
     of a four-vertex witness.  The common core is

        B intersection C = S union {x,y}.

     The induced graph on rank-six supersets of `S` is `J(8,3)`, with 420
     middle edges.  At each endpoint there are five support edges removing
     `x` and five removing `y`; the two outer edges must remove opposite
     coordinates.  Dually, a rank-nine target induces `J(9,6)`, with 756
     middle edges, and the two outer edges must add opposite members of the
     two-element complement of `B union C`.

576. For each eligible middle edge and each of the two assignments of `x,y`
     to its endpoints, one existential flag `z` needs only three clauses:

        z -> selected middle edge,
        z -> OR(left support group),
        z -> OR(right support group).

     OR all orientation flags for the target.  Existential projection is
     exactly the old disjunction over explicit three-edge paths; reverse
     Tseitin implications are unnecessary.  Opposite coordinate assignments
     force distinct outer endpoints, so the gate is exact even in a
     disconnected cycle-cover relaxation and in sparse candidate graphs.

577. The per-target reductions are

        rank 3: 21000 variables / 84001 clauses -> 840 / 2521,
        rank 9: 54432 variables / 217729 clauses -> 1512 / 4537.

     Across both complete layers the compact block has 221,760 variables and
     665,500 clauses.  It replaces the old shared up-front block of 5,765,760
     variables and 23,063,260 clauses, saving 5,544,000 variables and
     22,397,760 clauses.  `K11_COMPACT_FOUR_SHADOWS.md`, its independent
     audit `K11_COMPACT_FOUR_SHADOWS_AUDIT.md`,
     `scratch/verify_k11_compact_four.cpp`, and the guarded implementation
     `RECOMBINE_COMPACT_FOUR_SHADOWS=1` in `recombine_paths_sat.cpp` enumerate
     all 6,458,760 target/path incidences and verify the projected truth table.

578. The exact 60-branch fourth-edge portfolio was archived and restarted
     with both compact pair- and four-shadow gates.  No interrupted child had
     a candidate, `UNSAT`, or a normal exit.  Live logs show the exact lazy
     markers `420/840` for rank three and `756/1512` for rank nine.  At a
     comparable early stage the fifteen processes use about 5.8 GiB total,
     versus about 16.3 GiB before the four-shadow gate.  This is operational
     evidence, not a search result.

## 147. Globally unrestricted forest/band solver for `k=11`

579. The necessary monotone-band and two-coloured-forest structure is now an
     implemented exact formula, not merely unused theory.  For each of ranks
     five and six, choose 462 sorted central witness slots.  Every slot has one
     of the ten states

        (alpha,beta), 0<=alpha<=beta<=3,

     with both coordinates nondecreasing.  Conditional clauses set eleven
     slot bits equal to the OR of the corresponding physical interval.
     Cardinality fixes the slot rank, and 462-by-462 target indicators force
     the slot values to permute the whole Boolean layer.  The rank-five state
     `(0,3)` is globally impossible because every physical four-window already
     contains a selected rank-six witness.

580. Shared left endpoints and shared right endpoints materialize the two
     inclusion matchings.  Wrong nesting directions are forbidden and legal
     matches expose `rank-5 subset rank-6` directly.  These clauses are
     redundant consequences of the physical interval ORs, so they improve
     propagation without restricting the original problem.  The remaining
     1,123 noncentral targets retain the complete direct endpoint-threshold
     encoding and the proved safe witness-length bounds.

581. The resulting `k11_forest_sat.cpp` formula is globally sound and
     complete:

        SAT iff a universal nonzero 11-bit array of length 465 exists.

     It has exactly 4,892,622 variables and 15,524,818 clauses, versus
     9,815,220 actual variables and 26,452,166 clauses in the older direct
     unrestricted formula.  It assumes no fixed derivative row, Hamilton
     path, Johnson adjacency, forest component count, or endpoint regime.

582. Two low-priority forest-formula seeds and two independently audited

     by `EXACT_OR_SAT_DIRECT_AUDIT.md`; its live instances have 8,098,440
     primary variables, 9,815,220 variables after endpoint auxiliaries, and

     array must pass both independent OR verifiers; a plain in-process UNSAT

## 148. Positive seams force a cross-line desert

583. Fix a selected family of long directed peak plateaux.  Let `V` be the
     union of their plateau vertices, `Lambda` the union of their complete
     coordinate lines, and

        Delta_a=(|Lambda|-|V|)/a^2.

     For every plateau except the first in word order, take the clipped part
     of its predecessor gap which contributes to the first-dangerous seam.
     If `C` is the union of those disjoint clipped cores, put

        Gamma_a=|C|/a^2,
        Gamma_(0,a)=|C\Lambda|/a^2.

     The exact finite inclusion `C subset (C\Lambda) union (Lambda\V)` gives

        Gamma_a <= Gamma_(0,a)+Delta_a.

     This coupling and its weighted form are unconditional inside the
     inherited three-box geometry: they use neither atomic convergence,
     small seam, nor the selected-order hypothesis `D=o(a^2)`.

584. For an atomic plateau profile `mu_a -> 2 delta_x` with
     `4/3<=x<=3/2`, after one common subsequence there is a single clipped-gap
     density `Gamma` such that, for every fixed positive threshold `0<c<x`,

        H(c)=(x-c)Gamma.

     This multiscale seam linearity also does not use `D=o(a^2)`.  Writing
     `u=x-1`, the independently optimized cross-line envelope is

        M(u)=max{2/3, 2-6u+(13/2)u^2}.

     Since the atom requires `2u<=M(u)`, every atom is impossible when

        u>(8-2 sqrt(3))/13,
        equivalently x>1+(8-2 sqrt(3))/13.

     This cutoff is unconditional with respect to `D` and seam mass, but it
     still assumes the atomic profile and the inherited three-box word
     geometry; it is not a theorem about arbitrary limiting measures.

585. The stronger reservoir conclusions do require `D=o(a^2)`.  Under that
     hypothesis the quadratic reservoir law gives

        Gamma >= ((4-x)/4)(3-2x).

     Combining this with the finite coupling and the cross-line slack bound
     yields, for `1/3<=u<=(8-2 sqrt(3))/13`,

        liminf Gamma_0 >= (-5+25u-24u^2)/4 > 0.

     Thus every atom not already excluded by the unconditional cutoff must
     carry a positive density of clipped predecessor-gap positions outside
     all selected plateau lines.  Dropping `D=o(a^2)` preserves Items 583--584
     but does not presently justify either lower bound in this item.

586. The balanced endpoint remains an exact static survivor of all current
     ledgers:

        mu=2 delta_(4/3),
        nu_x=nu_y=nu_z=1_[-1/3,1/3] du,
        Gamma=Gamma_0=2/9.

     It has zero cross-line slack, satisfies the additive-triple, reservoir,
     seam, and line-capacity inequalities, and has enough outside-line area
     for the required gap cores.  These data do not order the desert points
     between successive plateaux and do not construct a permutation word.
     Consequently further scalar or static level-set optimization alone
     cannot finish the argument; the remaining lemma must control the word
     order of the positive-density cross-line desert (or construct the
     survivor).

587. `POSITIVE_SEAM_CROSSLINE_COUPLING.md` contains the proof, and
     `POSITIVE_SEAM_CROSSLINE_COUPLING_AUDIT.md` independently checks the
     finite accounting, common-subsequence passage, three-direction
     maximization, cutoff, and endpoint ledger.  The audit's scope split is
     authoritative: only Items 583--584 and the atomic cutoff are independent
     of `D=o(a^2)`; Item 585 is not.

     therefore at least 324 of the 330 rank-four targets are crossed by both
     rank-five flags.  Such a crossed rank-four witness has length at most
     two, hence lies among exactly `465+464=929` physical candidates.  Dually,
     at least 324 rank-seven targets are crossed by a proper rank-six prefix
     and suffix.  Two distinct six-subsets of the same seven-set have union
     equal to that target.  Six generic exact witness slots per layer cover
     the at most six exceptions without preselecting which targets they are.

## 152. Audit of Fable's proposed seam-level law

600. Fable's 31-minute attack on the balanced atomic survivor did not produce
     a theorem.  Its attempted 12,028-byte edit failed JSON parsing and only
     a 2,048-byte introductory fragment persisted.  Independent audit of the
     complete reasoning trace finds the first fatal inference where the
     capped average/tail law is upgraded to the pointwise assertion that
     every `4a+2` window contains a regular `4a/3` plateau.  The audited
     spectrum gives only `q_i<=2a` and fixed-delta positive-density lower
     tails; it does not give `q_i<=4a/3` everywhere or concentration near
     `4a/3`.  The earlier `FABLE_RUN_SPECTRUM_AUDIT.md` already supplies
     compatible nonconcentrated spectra.

601. Consequently the claimed peak-free gaps, valley normal form, `o(a)`
     poison seams, and exclusion of `2 delta_(4/3)` do not follow.  The trace
     also lacks a bounded-congestion seam-to-run charging map and changes the
     proposed poison cost from approximately `4a/3`, to `a`, to `o(a)`.
     Static limiting identities are repeatedly exactified beyond their
     asymptotic scope.  No part of this failed exclusion is entered as a
     proved theorem.

602. Two local statements survive.  On a directed plateau of edge length
     `lambda`, a strictly rising integer cross-coordinate ends at least at

        lambda-a;

     therefore a regular `4a/3` plateau creates height at least
     `(1/3-o(1))a`.  Across three directions there are only
     `(1+o(1))a` positive high-level lines capable of hosting such regular
     plateaux, while the balanced atom has `(2+o(1))a` regular plateaux.
     This gives a contradiction conditional on almost every predecessor
     seam forcing high-level absorption.

603. The exact missing target is therefore a quantitative seam alternative:
     every nonabsorbing regular seam must yield a span-bounded internal run
     with a fixed positive cost deficit below `4a/3`, and every run/index may
     receive only `O(1)` charges.  Such a theorem would convert the valid
     local height/capacity mismatch into an atom exclusion.  It is currently
     conjectural.  The authoritative rejection and salvage ledger is
     `fable_general_case/FABLE_SEAM_LEVEL_LAW_AUDIT.md`, SHA-256
     `f8a61370e0c4d00a65eb68e37507369bc285b10d7eecf625fb1841ffc081c6d8`.

## 153. Cross-layer width theory in every odd dimension

604. Let `k=2r+1`, `M=C(k,r)=C(k,r+1)`, and suppose a universal nonzero
     array has length `n=M+d`, with `M>=d>=1`.  Independently select and sort
     one witness for every rank-`r` and rank-`r+1` mask.  If `y_j` and `x_j`
     are the respective width profiles, then upper widths lie in
     `0,...,d`, lower widths lie in `0,...,d-1`, and for every `0<=t<=d`,

        X_t:=sum_(j<=t)x_j <= d+sum_(j<t)y_j=:d+Y_(t-1).

     Summing the cumulative inequalities gives the exact necessary
     separation

        W_x-W_y >= M-d(d-1)-x0.

     These are unrestricted endpoint consequences, not a fixed-row ansatz or
     a sufficient characterization of realizable profiles.

605. Let `O_L,O_R` be the `d` positions omitted by the selected lower left
     and right endpoint sets.  Then

        W_y=sum(O_L)-sum(O_R).

     Every selected upper singleton position belongs to
     `O_L intersection O_R`.  Therefore, in the near-width regime,

        W_y <= (d-x0)(M+x0).

     Fan-capped avoidance sharpens simultaneously: for every lower target
     family `F` of containment-chain height at most `h`,

        |F| <= sum_j min(j,h)y_j+h(d-x0).

     An upper singleton deletes a whole free endpoint fan because no lower
     target witness may end at its rank-`r+1` entry.

606. Put

        L=sum_(s=1)^(r-1) C(2r+1,s),
        q=d-x0.

     Applying the fan inequality to the complete lower ideal and combining
     it with the omitted-endpoint upper bound yields

        L <= q(M+d+r-1-q).

     If `q_*` is the least `q in {0,...,d}` satisfying this inequality, then

        x0<=d-q_*.

     Candidate existence guarantees that the defining set is nonempty.  A
     simpler closed consequence is

        x0<=d-ceil(L/(M+d+r-1)).

607. At the conjectural rank-count lengths `B(k)`, exact arithmetic gives:

        k      7    9    11    13     15      17       19
        M     35  126   462  1716   6435   24310    92378
        d      2    2     3     3      3       3        3
        q_*    1    1     2     2      2       2        2

     Hence `x0<=1` in every odd equality case `7<=k<20`.  This has a genuine
     array-level consequence: at most one distinct rank-`r+1` mask may occur
     literally among the entries.  If two distinct such masks occurred,
     deliberately select those singleton occurrences as their witnesses and
     choose all other witnesses arbitrarily; the universally valid theorem
     would give `x0>=2`, a contradiction.  Repeated occurrences of the same
     mask are not excluded.

608. The same calculation gives the worst-case width separations

        32, 123, 455, 1709, 6428, 24303, 92371

     for `k=7,9,...,19`.  These are exact necessary cuts at the proposed
     lengths, not existence theorems.  The proof, checker, and independent
     audit are `ODD_CROSS_LAYER_WIDTH_THEORY.md`,
     `scratch/verify_odd_cross_layer_widths.cpp`, and
     `ODD_CROSS_LAYER_WIDTH_THEORY_AUDIT.md`; the audit SHA-256 is
     `9b5f2450017fa6f9d5ff26e36019f6df00e550c9f82b87a42cf3a717ddb16288`.

     rank-five width two with rank-six width three.  These bounds hold for
     arbitrary witness choices and project away ranks three and four without
     assuming a fixed row or connected forest.

613. Item 607 is an array-level theorem: a hypothetical optimal `k=11`
     array contains at most one distinct literal rank-six mask.  If two
     distinct six-sets occurred as entries, deliberately choosing both
     singleton occurrences as their selected witnesses would contradict
     `x0<=1`.  Repeated occurrences of the same six-set are not excluded.

614. Coordinate permutations commute with bitwise OR and act transitively on
     the 462 six-sets.  Thus, for an existence search, the possible literal
     rank-six mask may WLOG be fixed to decimal `63`, the low six bits.  If no
     rank-six entry occurs, the restriction is vacuous.  For every physical
     position and every other six-set `S`, one 11-literal mismatch clause
     forbids `A[p]=S`.  The exact guarded family

        K11_FOREST_CANONICAL_RANK6_ENTRY=1

     adds zero variables and

        465*(462-1)=214,365 clauses.

     This is a symmetry-WLOG cut, not a necessary statement for one fixed
     coordinate labelling.  Every other hard clause in the frozen formula is
     coordinate-equivariant; the input seed affects phases only.

615. In every odd dimension with `x0<=1`, count all physical intervals of
     length at most `d`.  The lower ideal through rank `r-1`, all selected

     occupy `L+2M-x_d` distinct slots.  If an upper singleton is selected,
     at least one additional interval of each length `2,...,d` contains it
     and cannot represent any counted target.  Therefore

        x_d >= L+2M-[d(M+d)-C(d,2)]+(d-1)x0.

     For `k=11` this is `x3>=93+2*x0`; for `k=9` it forces the exact observed
     rigidity `x0=0,x2=126`.

## 156. A selected upper singleton is forced to the array boundary

619. In the rank-six monotone chain, the proved `x3>0` makes state `03`
     occur.  Every width-zero state compatible with it is either `00` or
     `33`; joint cuts give at most one width-zero occurrence.  Consequently,
     if `x0=1`, the selected singleton is physically `[0,0]` or `[464,464]`.
     Deleting that boundary entry preserves every rank-at-most-five witness.
     The remaining word has length 464 and still covers all 462 rank-five
     masks, so its rank-five endpoint slack is two.  Every one of the 561
     masks in ranks one through four must then use a singleton or adjacent
     pair.

620. Counting those 561 intervals together with the surviving selected
     rank-five and rank-six short intervals gives the globally necessary cut

        x0+x1+y0+y1 <= 380-13*x0,

     equivalently

        y2 >= x1+82+14*x0.

     The number 13 is a net capacity improvement, not thirteen physically
     deleted slots: the shortened word loses two short slots, twelve more
     lower targets become forced short, and the selected singleton itself is
     removed from the surviving central count.  Scalar and endpoint geometry
     still do not eliminate `x0=1`; the explicit surviving profile

        x=(1,0,366,95), y=(0,366,96)

     prevents such an overclaim.

621. Because any literal rank-six occurrence can deliberately be selected as
     the singleton witness, the same argument proves an array-level fact:
     **every literal rank-six entry of an optimal k=11 array lies at position
     0 or 464.**  The proof and independent audit are
     `K11_FOREST_ENDPOINT_ALIGNMENT_SECOND_ORDER.md` and
     `K11_FOREST_SINGLETON_BOUNDARY_AUDIT.md`, audit SHA-256
     `cc26a3a06c55623ec2d80cf6df484aea4d0e42db11a5fc675bef6b66bf4c4a44`.
     This boundary theorem is not yet encoded in the frozen source of Item
     617.

622. The two boundary positions cannot both have rank six.  If they did,
     every target of rank at most five would be represented in the remaining
     463-position interior word.  That word covers all 462 rank-five masks,
     so its rank-five witness band has slack one; every rank-one-through-four
     target would then need a singleton witness.  There are 561 such masks
     but only 463 positions, a contradiction.  Hence an optimal k=11 array
     has at most one literal rank-six occurrence in total.

623. Word reversal and coordinate permutation now give the exact existence

        either no rank-six entry occurs,
        or A[0]=63 is the sole rank-six entry.

     The complete normal form forbids 461 noncanonical six-sets at position

## 158. Odd-dimensional literal boundary rigidity

626. The k=11 argument generalizes.  Let `k=2r+1`, `n=M+d`, and assume the
     unrestricted width ledger gives `x0<=1` and `x_d>0`.  A width-`d`
     selected upper witness has the unique state `(0,d)`.  A diagonal state
     `(a,a)` is comparable with it only for `a=0` or `a=d`; arbitrary
     reselection of any literal upper-middle occurrence therefore localizes
     that occurrence to a word endpoint.

627. If both endpoints have upper-middle rank, deleting them leaves
     `M+d-2` positions which still cover the entire rank-`r` layer.  Every
     lower target must then use an interval of length at most `d-2`.  Thus two
     endpoint occurrences are impossible whenever

        sum_(s=1)^(r-1) C(2r+1,s)
          > sum_(ell=1)^(d-2) (M+d-2-ell+1).

     The empty sum for `d=2` is zero; `d=1` has an immediate endpoint
     pigeonhole proof.  This is an unrestricted witness-band theorem, not a
     fixed-row statement.

628. At every conjectural odd rank-count length `B(k)` for
     `k=7,9,...,19`, the already-audited values `x0<=1`, `x_d>0`, and the
     displayed strict pool inequality all hold.  Consequently each equality
     candidate has at most one literal rank-`r+1` occurrence in total, it is
     at a word endpoint, and up to reversal and coordinate permutation the
     only possible occurrence is the canonical `(r+1)`-set at position zero.
     The theorem and independent audit are `ODD_LITERAL_BOUNDARY_RIGIDITY.md`
     and `ODD_LITERAL_BOUNDARY_RIGIDITY_AUDIT.md`, audit SHA-256
     `482ba8091fdb015b57472a3a82c3f32becee957c6d2a5b7989d14b6ab8e21ee5`.

## 161. Linear-forest completion improves the finite upper bounds

635. Let a partial word miss lower antichain `F` and upper family `G`.  Make
     one literal vertex for every member of `F`, add optional labelled
     auxiliary vertices, and select edges whose endpoint-label ORs cover
     members of `G`.  If the selected graph is a linear forest, ordering each
     path component and concatenating the components preserves every selected
     edge as an adjacent pair.  Reserved upper targets may be appended
     literally.  This gives a completion of length

        |F| + number of auxiliaries + number of reserved literals.

     A shared three-vertex block `P,X,Q` covers two targets whenever
     `P OR X=U` and `X OR Q=V`.  The proof and constructor are in
     `PARTIAL_COMPLETION_FOREST.md` and `partial_completion_forest.cpp`.

636. The 465-entry `k11_upper549_natural_array.txt` misses twelve rank-seven
     masks and the rank-eight mask 958.  A standalone completion needs thirteen
     positions: equality at twelve forces the twelve rank-seven witnesses to
     be the twelve singleton positions, but only 956 is contained in 958.
     The old/new seam saves one position.  Appending

        243,1216,774,956,941,1468,607,1694,1946,1763,1884,493

     477.  In zero-based indices the omitted rank-seven mask 251 uses the

     positions are optimal for this fixed prefix: none of the twelve missing
     rank-seven masks occurs in the prefix, and the suffix ORs ending at one
     new endpoint form a chain, so they contain at most one rank-seven mask.

        466 <= N(11) <= 478.

     This fixed-prefix append optimality is not a global lower bound on
     `nu(11)` and does not rule out changing or deleting prefix entries.

637. The genuine 3434-entry factor
     `k14_pinnable_factor_missing260.txt` misses 238 rank-nine and 22 rank-ten

         c(T)=#{S in A:S proper-subset T}.

         2(n-M) >= sum_(T in B) max(0,2-c(T)).

## 162. Quantitative seam repair excludes the atomic survivor

640. In the inherited three-box model, let

        mu_a=(1/a) sum_P delta_(lambda(P)/a)

     over directed internal coordinate-peak plateaux.  The repaired
     quantitative seam argument proves the following conditional theorem:
     under the selected-middle-order hypothesis `D=o(a^2)`, no sequence can
     satisfy

        mu_a -> 2 delta_x,   4/3 <= x <= 3/2.

     In particular the formerly surviving balanced static profile
     `2 delta_(4/3)` is impossible.  The proof constructs, at every regular
     seam that is neither absorbed at a high fixed line nor separated by a
     long gap, a span-bounded internal threshold run and an exact disjoint
     interval of first-dangerous starts that can be reassigned to it.  At
     `x=4/3` it yields at least `(2/3-o(1))a` cheap seams, at least
     `(4/3-o(1))a` starts per seam, and at least `(1/3-o(1))a` saving per start,
     for total saving `(8/27-o(1))a^3`, contradicting the inherited capped-run
     lower bound.

641. This is a real narrowing of the general asymptotic obstruction, not a
     proof of the all-profile theorem.  Mixed/non-atomic plateau measures can
     still trade mass between lengths and are not excluded.  The reconstructed
     proof is `FABLE_QUANTITATIVE_SEAM_TRACE_AUDIT.md`, SHA-256
     `75483123b4425561847bd00f607a545545af0a0ae2661ce9f3fb41e322bfbde6`.

## 163. Exact component-defect reductions for unrestricted `k=11`

642. Continue with selected witnesses for all rank-five and rank-six masks in
     a hypothetical nonzero length-465 array.  Let `uL` and `uR` be the
     numbers of unmatched masks in the common-left-endpoint and
     common-right-endpoint matchings, and put `c=uL+uR`.  The union of the two
     matchings is the inherited spanning alternating linear forest, so `c` is
     exactly its number of components and

        0 <= uL,uR <= 3,   1 <= c <= 6.

     If `X_t` counts selected rank-six witnesses of width at most `t` and
     `Y_t` counts selected rank-five witnesses of width at most `t`, then for
     each endpoint colour separately

        X_t-Y_(t-1) <= uL,   X_t-Y_(t-1) <= uR,   0<=t<=2.

     These colour-specific inequalities strictly strengthen the old projected
     `2(X_t-Y_(t-1))<=c` rows once exact endpoint defects are branched on.

643. Endpoint alignment also adapts to the defect.  In each colour `q`, at
     least `327-u_q` rank-four/rank-five/rank-six endpoint chains and at least
     `27-u_q` rank-three/rank-four/rank-five/rank-six endpoint chains occur.
     Intersecting the left and right populations yields at least `192-c`
     full rank-four/rank-five/rank-six diamonds.  Every component of the
     central forest is monotone in both witness orders; two same-rank masks at
     distance two in a component have order indices differing by at most six.

644. The minimal-component branches become exact small combinatorial objects.
     If `e=0,c=1`, the forest is one two-sided rainbow alternating Hamilton
     path: one endpoint colour is a perfect order-preserving matching and the
     other is the unit shift, up to reversal.  The exact endpoint-promotion
     law reduces the surviving joint width profiles from `271663750` to
     `609086`.  If `e=1,c=2`, where `e` is the unique literal rank-six entry,
     that singleton is isolated and the remaining 923 central masks have the
     forced order

        P_0,Q_1,P_1,...,Q_461,P_461,
        Q_(i+1)=P_i union P_(i+1).

     Its two-ended promotion law reduces `260613875` joint profiles to
     `372855`; deleting the boundary singleton also reduces the generic
     rank-three and rank-four exception budgets from six to four.

645. These are necessary structural reductions, not sufficiency theorems.
     An explicit `e=1,c=2` endpoint schedule survives every current scalar,
     endpoint, and central-incidence constraint but is not known to factor as
     an OR array or cover noncentral ranks.  Therefore neither `e=1` nor

## 164. Unrestricted local-density cuts at `k=11,n=465`

646. The rank-six witness band implies that every physical interval of length
     at least four has OR-rank at least six.  This yields two new unrestricted
     density theorems.  For every five-set `Y` and six-set `U`, put

        p_Y=#{i:A_i subseteq Y},   p_U=#{i:A_i subseteq U}.

     Then

        p_Y >= 16,   p_U >= 23.

     For `Y`, the marked positions form runs of length at most three; their
     total number of internal intervals is at most `2p_Y`, while all 31
     nonempty subsets of `Y` need distinct witnesses.  For `U`, its 62
     nonempty proper subsets need short witnesses, giving first `p_U>=22`.
     Equality would force one 22-position block whose 63 windows of lengths
     at most three enumerate all nonempty subsets of `U`.  Coordinate
     zero-run counting then forces every coordinate to occur in exactly six
     entries, for total entry-rank 36, whereas the six required singleton
     entries and sixteen other distinct entries force rank sum at least 38.
     Hence equality is impossible.

647. Double counting gives the valid aggregate pseudo-Boolean cuts

        210 n1+84 n2+28 n3+7 n4+n5 >= 7392,
        252 n1+126 n2+56 n3+21 n4+6 n5+n6 >= 10626,

     where `n_s` is the number of literal entries of rank `s`.  These improve
     the inherited dimension restrictions `p_Y>=12` and `p_U>=21`.  They are
     logically independent of the witness-width band/fan cuts.  They are not
     close to tight on the known fixed-row partial factor: direct enumeration
     gives `min p_Y=72` and `min p_U=109`.  Therefore the recommended first
     solver experiment is only the two cheap shared-rank aggregate cuts; an
     eager encoding of all 924 pointwise counters would require about 8.38
     million DP states.

648. In the fixed Johnson-Hamilton-row ansatz only, coordinate degree
     counting gives 82--84 crossing edges when the omitted rank-five colour
     avoids the coordinate and 84--86 when it contains the coordinate.  This
     is a useful checksum but not an unrestricted theorem.  The numerical
     identity `84=2 Cat_5` does not by itself imply a 42-component
     decomposition.  The complete independent audit is
     `K11_LOCAL_DENSITY_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT.md`, SHA-256
     `3320870c553f3f11ad95fd102baa7c9aa448f035e8580b289c954824825622a4`.

## 165. Mixed-profile quantitative seam functional

649. The atomic seam proof has a fixed-threshold measure-level extension.
     For dangerous predecessor length `p`, successor length `s`, and gap `z`,
     an absorbed seam can use only a positive line level

        p-1 <= t <= 2-s.

     Direction-labelled line capacity is at most `dt` in each of the three
     directions; after forgetting directions this gives the safe aggregate
     relaxation `3 dt`.  A nonabsorbed seam has guaranteed saving density

        phi(p,s,z)=min(p,(4-s-z)_+)*(s-z)_+.

     This incorporates the exact forward-window supply and the cheap-run cost,
     including partial successors, intermediate maxima, shared endpoints, and
     the two word boundaries.  At a threshold atom one must take the total
     limiting dangerous mass `||mu||`; writing `mu((c,2])` is valid only when
     `c` is a continuity threshold.

650. Optimizing the coarse atomic gap cutoff improves the certified saving at
     the balanced endpoint from `8/27` to `4/9`.  More importantly, the proof
     is stable: one absolute neighbourhood of every atomic profile

        2 delta_x,   4/3 <= x <= 3/2,

     is excluded under `D=o(a^2)`, even when the mass inside the neighbourhood
     is arbitrarily non-atomic.  This is a genuine mixed-profile theorem, not
     merely atom-by-atom continuity rhetoric.

651. The same calculation identifies the present method's exact limitation.
     The adversarial fixed-threshold value is concave in the plateau measure,
     so atomic exclusion cannot extend to mixtures by convexity.  The broad
     static measure `2*1_[1,2](x) dx` passes the reduced aggregate seam ledger
     separately at every fixed `1<c<2`.  These thresholdwise couplings and gap
     allocations are not one realizable ordering and omit direction labels,
     cross-line placement, and multiscale compatibility.  Thus this is not a
     counterexample to the OR-array conjecture; it proves that the next general
     theorem must couple thresholds or directions globally rather than optimize
     each threshold independently.

## 168. Large-defect transfer for the three-box seam method

659. The hypothesis `D=o(a^2)` has been removed from the conclusion of the
     atomic seam theorem.  For the one-sided forward assignment, the exact
     endpoint congestion is

        C_alpha <= 4a+3,   C_beta=0.

     At cap `h=3a-1`, retaining the endpoint slack gives the finite lower
     cost

        Q >= 4a^3-(15/2)a^2-(1/2)a+1-(7a+2)D.

     More generally, if a structural class admits a forward span-`4a+3`
     run assignment of total cost `(U+o(1))a^3`, then

        liminf D/a^2 >= sup_(2<y<=3) (F(y)-U)_+/(4+y),

     where

        F(y)=y^3/6-(3/2)y^2+(9/2)y-1/2.

     This is a transfer theorem: a strict cost saving forces a quadratic
     excess in local word length instead of disappearing into an error term.

660. Applying the optimized atomic seam saving shows that every atomic
     profile `2 delta_x`, `4/3<=x<=3/2`, satisfies

        liminf D/a^2 >= (4-3x+S_*(x))/7 >= 8/189,

     with

        S_*(x)=x*(sqrt(x(6x-7))-sqrt(3-2x))^2.

     At the balanced survivor `x=4/3`, this gives `4/63`; optimizing over all
     lower-half caps improves it to `0.0657635...`.  The same transfer makes
     the audited narrow non-atomic neighbourhood theorem a positive
     quadratic-defect theorem.  Thus the atomic branch is no longer merely
     excluded under a small-defect assumption: it quantitatively pays a
     constant fraction of the local middle width.

661. This still does not prove a quadratic lower bound for every three-box
     word.  The broad mixed threshold ledger has scalar adversarial value at
     least four at every fixed threshold, so the transfer produces no
     positive defect for that relaxation.  The exact remaining theorem must
     couple nested thresholds, direction-labelled line resources, and gap
     placement in one realizable order; further independent scalar
     optimization cannot close it.

     `34287b12488dd4e639b00f02af3d56336e37114ea96a5d03b635cb7434a811b9`.
     An independent derivation verified the coefficient `7a+2`, all-cap

## 169. Containment multiplicity and exact upper-rank witness caps

663. Let an array have length `n=binomial(k,r)+d`, and choose one witness
     interval for every rank-`r` mask.  If a physical interval `J` has length
     `ell` and OR-rank `s`, then

        ell <= d                         when s<r,
        ell <= d+binomial(s,r)           when s>=r.

     Indeed, after sorting the selected rank-`r` intervals, the `i`-th lies
     inside `[i,i+d]`.  If `J=[u,v]` and `ell>d`, it contains all selected
     witnesses with indices `u,...,v-d`, exactly `ell-d` distinct rank-`r`
     subsets of `OR(J)`.  There are at most `binomial(s,r)` such subsets.
     The endpoint-index check is valid because `v<=binomial(k,r)+d` implies
     `v-d<=binomial(k,r)`.

664. Applying this simultaneously over every eligible `r` gives the exact
     universal cap

        c_s(n)=min( n,
                    min_(r>s) (n-binomial(k,r)),
                    min_(r<=s) (n-binomial(k,r)+binomial(s,r)) ),

     where ranks with `binomial(k,r)>n` are omitted.  Consequently, for
     `1<=t<=n`,

        sum_(s:c_s(n)<=t) binomial(k,s) <=
        sum_(ell=1)^t (n-ell+1).

     The restriction `t<=n` is necessary; the submitted wording “every
     t>=1” with the untruncated quadratic expression is false for `t>n`.
     These nested counts imply the old rank-slack inequalities but do not
     contradict `n=B(k)` in the checked range.

665. At `k=11,n=465`, the caps for ranks one through eleven are exactly

        3,3,3,3,3,4,10,31,87,213,465.

     In particular the old solver bounds for ranks 7,8,9,10 drop from
     `136,301,411,455` to `10,31,87,213`.  This is a large exact pruning of
     the upper-rank interval domains, even though it supplies no new numerical
     lower bound by itself.

666. `k11_forest_sat.cpp` implements these caps behind the optional switch
     `K11_FOREST_CONTAINMENT_CAPS=1`.  In the fully enabled adjacent-shadow
     formula they add no variables and exactly 107368 binary clauses:

        41580 for 330 crossed rank-seven targets,
          756 for six rank-seven exceptions,
        44550 for rank eight,
        17820 for rank nine,
         2662 for rank ten.

     The resulting clause counts without the density PB module are
     `14839748` in generic branch zero, `14879404` in `e0c1`, and `14919126`
     in `e1c2`.  With both theorem modules enabled, the live
     minimal-component inventories are

        e0c1: 2983733 variables, 15159630 clauses;
        e1c2: 2983974 variables, 15199352 clauses.

## 170. MTF--SCD parity lift and the monotone-radius barrier

670. The submitted `k=5` MTF--SCD tour is valid.  Reverse initialization and
     its nine updates give the universal length-14 word

        8,16,1,2,4,8,16,1,2,8,18,20,5,9.

     This is longer than the optimum 12 and the state path does not close in
     one move.  Exact machine-checkable certificates are now also recorded
     for a cyclic `k=3` tour and a `k=4` path.  No explicit `k=6` certificate
     exists in the workspace, so the prose assertion that one was found is
     not certified; the bounded search also fixes the maximal chain first and
     is not an exhaustive nonexistence test.

671. There is an exact one-coordinate state lift.  For an ordered partition
     `Pi=(B1,...,Bs)` and new coordinate `z`, put

        L_z(Pi)=(B1,...,Bs,{z}),
        U_z(Pi)=(B1 union {z},B2,...,Bs),
        V_z(Pi)=({z},B1,...,Bs).

     Then

        L_z(M_X Pi)=M_X(L_z Pi),
        U_z(M_X Pi)=M_(X union {z})(U_z Pi).

     A closed MTF walk of `ell` states splices its lower and upper lifts into
     one path of `2ell` states via the two exact seams

        L_z(Pi_last) --{z}--> V_z(Pi_last)
          --(X_close union {z})--> U_z(Pi_first).

672. Closing ordinary paths by their exact ordered-partition resets before
     splicing gives the recurrence

        L'=2(L+R-p),   R'=R+p,   q'<=2q,

     where `p` is the path count, `R` the sum of first-state block counts,
     and `q` the uncovered-mask defect.  Consequently a path-cover theorem
     with `L=W+o(W)`, `R=o(W)`, and `q=o(W)` in one parity propagates to the
     other parity without losing the leading constant.  It does not create
     such a family from a fixed finite base.

673. A sharp obstruction rules out one tempting induction.  In a direct
     SCD transversal whose assigned-chain arcs all move in the one globally
     fixed direction `d -> d-1`, the reset excess is at least

        (4/sqrt(e)+o(1)) W(2m).

     With the globally reversed orientation it is still

        (4/sqrt(e)-2+o(1)) W(2m).

     Thus an optimized last-pair/collision resolution with one fixed
     monotone orientation cannot prove constant one.  The theorem does not
     exclude mixed orientations, same-radius arcs, skipped radii, or reset
     states that also serve assigned chains.  Those are now the relevant MTF
     possibilities.

674. The corrected source is `MTF_SCD_INDUCTION_NEXT.md`, SHA-256

     The checker `mtf_scd_small_verify.cpp` has SHA-256
     `42a32e6cb0288c56d9528c4d52c03c6862760d4c62e190c9c1a426f92bda0343`.

## 171. Nested local-density inequalities from simultaneous caps

675. The simultaneous containment caps bound every physical interval of a
     given OR-rank, not merely one selected witness.  Fix an `s`-set `U`,
     mark positions `i` with `A_i subseteq U`, and put `p_U` equal to their
     number.  If `C_s=max_(r<=s)c_r`, every marked run has length at most
     `C_s`.  A run of length `ell` contains

        F_t(ell)=sum_(j=1)^min(t,ell) (ell-j+1)

     intervals of length at most `t`.  For `p=qC+r`, convexity shows that the
     maximum over all run decompositions with run cap `C` is

        G_(C,t)(p)=q F_t(C)+F_t(r).

     Therefore, for every `t>=1`,

        sum_(1<=r<=s, c_r<=t) binomial(s,r) <= G_(C_s,t)(p_U).

     This is unrestricted: it assumes no derivative row, Johnson path, or
     grading.

676. At `k=11,n=465`, the cap table

        3,3,3,3,3,4,10,31,87,213,465

     gives, for `s=1,...,10`,

        p_U >= 1,2,4,8,16,28,45,76,129,214.

     The rank-six improvement is particularly simple.  Inside a fixed
     six-set, all 62 nonempty proper subsets need distinct marked intervals
     of length at most three, while every marked run has length at most four.
     Runs of sizes `1,2,3,4` contain `1,3,6,9` such intervals.  Twenty-seven
     marked positions give at most `6*9+6=60`; hence `p_U>=28`.  Raw interval
     cardinality alone does not imply 29.

677. Double counting `(i,U)` gives

        sum_(r=1)^s binomial(11-r,s-r)n_r
          >= p_s binomial(11,s).

     In particular the old six-set PB cut is strictly strengthened to

        252n1+126n2+56n3+21n4+6n5+n6 >= 12936.

     This changes no SAT variable, arithmetic gate, or clause count: only the
     exact comparator constant changes.  The stronger source SHA-256 is
     `c9b27476bfe62c1b0c75cda5f0dd713470a66db10fb2d697fd6cf6698b407049`.
     Its exact `e0c1` and `e1c2` inventories with containment caps remain
     `2983733/15159630` and `2983974/15199352` variables/clauses.  After
     build-only verification, remote seeds 101 and 102 replaced only the
     weaker density-only seeds 81 and 82 on cores 44 and 47; the older
     combined seeds 91 and 92 remain an independent comparison.

678. The theorem is `K11_NESTED_LOCAL_DENSITY_NEXT.md`, SHA-256
     `39b0e6519bfaba6ab4985f26e7547c245de926e9775eb7fc7052b38a224f0a26`.
     The independent mathematical and source audit reports PASS in
     `CONTAINMENT_CAPS_SOLVERS_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT.md`, SHA-256
     `e86622b80bf35b92092fa79df22c26d0e0c9ed00e25d4619143504563b2b5017`.
     The aggregate cuts remain arithmetically feasible at 465 entries, so
