## 172. Multiscale contraction and the remaining broad-profile gate

679. Dangerous-threshold predecessor ledgers are contractions of one ordered
     plateau list.  If a plateau survives thresholds `h1<h2`, its predecessor
     at `h2` is obtained by iterating its predecessor at `h1` until a survivor
     is reached; its attached physical gap cannot decrease.  Deleting an
     intervening plateau merges its length and its adjacent gap additively.
     Equivalently, every physical predecessor edge has one contiguous
     threshold lifetime.  This exact law disproves the particular broad
     static threshold-by-threshold ledger previously used: it assigns a
     positive gap at a lower threshold and zero at a higher threshold to the
     same positive-mass band of surviving plateaux.

680. Threshold nesting alone is nevertheless insufficient.  An explicit
     alternating complement-pair order realizes the broad scalar measure

        2 * 1_[1,2](s) ds,

     obeys additive contraction at every fixed threshold, admits fixed
     direction labels with the separate line capacities, and retains scalar
     value greater than four throughout `1<c<2`.  Thus the old static witness
     is invalid as one word, but a repaired nested scalar obstruction exists.

681. Actual three-line geometry rules out full lifetime saturation.  In the
     explicit lift, line uniqueness forces cross-direction intersection
     density at least `1/4`, while the cross-line inequality would require
     zero.  More generally every actual broad-profile plateau family has at
     least

        (5-2 sqrt(6))a-o(a)

     plateaux on nonpositive fixed-coordinate lines, and its integrated
     absorption mass is at most

        1/2-(5-2 sqrt(6))^2/8+o(1).

     This positive deficit does not yet convert a partially absorbed broad
     profile into one common-threshold seam assignment below four.  Partially
     absorbed broad profiles therefore remain open; no unrestricted three-box
     lower bound or all-`k` OR theorem follows.

682. The proved source is `MULTISCALE_DIRECTION_COUPLING_NEXT.md`, SHA-256
     `b13b7bd5ced0626fb1bf559764f4539ada905c363732a73b56b039620b8e1336`.
     The independent audit reports PASS with endpoint-convention,
     weak-limit-cutoff, duplicate-pair, and submeasure presentation repairs
     in `MULTISCALE_DIRECTION_COUPLING_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT.md`, SHA-256
     `481aa1710c0c88c806cbeaef300a82a02053195a50969c6e3ad072aa5c124dff`.

## 173. Banded double chains forced by equality

683. Let `r` attain `B(k)`, put `M=binomial(k,r)`, `n=M+d=B(k)`,
     `L=sum_(s<r)binomial(k,s)`, and

        sigma=dM+binomial(d+1,2)-L.

     If `nu(k)=B(k)`, then every lower mask has a witness of length at most
     `d`.  Choosing one such witness for each lower mask partitions the
     punctured lower ideal in two ways: by left endpoint into chains `C_i`,
     and by right endpoint into chains `D_j`.  Some indexed chains may be
     empty, every chain has at most `d` members, and

        |C_i intersect D_j|<=1,   i<=j<=i+d-1.

     The occupied incidence cells are exactly `L` distinct cells of the
     one-sided `d`-band, whose size is `L+sigma`; equivalently the lower
     witness placement is the complete band with exactly `sigma` holes.
     Labels strictly increase along a row and strictly increase when a column
     is read in reverse left-endpoint order.

684. For the chosen lower intervals define

        Z_b=[n] minus union_(S:b notin S) I_S.

     Their labels are simultaneously realizable exactly when
     `I_S intersect Z_b` is nonempty for every `b in S`.  Nonempty physical
     entries additionally require `union_b Z_b=[n]`.  This pin theorem covers
     only the selected lower intervals; central and upper witnesses impose
     further constraints and may shrink the legal pin sets.

685. The almost-full band also forces, for every `1<=q<=d`,

        q [n-d+1-sigma]_+
          <= sum_(s=1)^(r-d+q-1) binomial(k,s).

     Count the full band rows' cells of lengths at most `q`.  A hole spoils at
     most `q` of them.  Every surviving cell has all right extensions through
     length `d` occupied; their strict chain forces its label rank to be at
     most `r-d+q-1`.  The symmetric left-extension argument gives the same
     scalar inequality.  The positive part is the clean form because
     `sigma<=M` is not automatic for every attaining-rank choice; e.g.
     `k=3,r=3` has `(M,d,sigma)=(1,3,3)`, while the alternate maximizer `r=2`
     is favorable.

686. This is a valid necessary global reduction, not the missing converse.
     One must still construct the ordered band labeling, preserve all pins
     after central labels are added, and cover all upper ranks.  The corrected
     independent audit is `BANDED_DOUBLE_CHAIN_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT.md`, SHA-256
     `7d820348e42f2461809189027cd48d94c86a872e4c9115eee5d0bd9ee62fedb7`.

## 174. Audit of the single-switch portal proposal

687. The arithmetic defect interpretation is correct.  If

        sigma=dM+binomial(d+1,2)-L

     satisfies `0<=sigma<=M`, the selected central schedule

        [i,i+d-1] for i<=sigma,
        [i,i+d]   for i>sigma

     is a valid nonnested monotone-band schedule with one right-offset switch.
     A shortened central witness makes its containing length-`d+1` cell
     available for other work, but does not force that cell to be a strict
     superset or a new value.  Even small valid single-switch words have
     duplicate portal ORs.  Thus “portal” denotes an available physical cell,
     not one freely selectable upper mask.  The condition `sigma<=M` also
     needs a favorable maximizing rank; it is not automatic for every tied
     maximizer.

688. The advertised `k=11` row counts are arithmetically exact, but their
     proposed `330` rank-seven edges plus `38` internal rank-eight bridges are
     impossible.  Under that grading, no singleton can have rank five: an
     adjacent pair containing it would have rank at most five and duplicate
     it.  Hence all 368 rank-five values in rows one and two are pair windows.
     Every pair `R_2(t)`, `370<=t<=464`, lies in one of the 94 distinct
     rank-five tail triples, so it cannot itself have rank five without
     duplicating that triple.  All 368 rank-five pair values must therefore
     occupy 368 of the first 369 pair slots.

689. For consecutive shortened rank-six triples `P_i,P_(i+1)`, the shared
     pair satisfies

        R_2(i+1) subseteq P_i intersect P_(i+1).

     If their portal union has rank eight, their intersection has rank four,
     forcing this shared pair to have rank at most four.  Since at most one of
     the first 369 pair slots is lower than rank five, at most one of the 368
     internal portals can have rank eight, not 38.  More generally, if two
     rank-`r` shortened windows overlap in a short cell of rank `u`, their
     union portal has rank at most `2r-u`.  Portal height is coupled to the
     lower overlap row; scalar slack alone cannot allocate it.

690. This refutes the specific `369+93` forest blueprint and the assertion
     that 38 missing rank-five pair values can be moved into the Q-region.
     It does not refute the broad single-switch conjecture: under its first
     four clauses at least 93 of the 94 residual triples are rank five, so
     almost all internal P-transitions are Johnson transitions and rank-eight
     masks would have to come mainly from longer windows.  The weaker idea of
     repairing the known twelve rank-seven and one rank-eight omissions with
     a small number of switches remains numerically compatible, but still
     lacks a factorability, lower-reassignment, and pin-survival theorem.

691. The Pascal width identities and the `369=3*126-9`, `93=84+9` counts are
     correct algebra.  They do not provide an operation on factors or pin
     sets.  Portal Absorption and Pascal Fusion therefore remain conjectures.
     The complete audit is `SINGLE_SWITCH_PORTAL_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT.md`,
     SHA-256
     `255f90b2d84b85901d2817986daefdce6a0fe5b4a66852d9580bad13cb887993`.

692. The short-band clauses actually force an exact one-defect dichotomy.
     Among the 369 early pair cells and 94 late triple cells, exactly 462
     have rank five and exactly one has rank at most four.  Either the early
     pairs have 368 rank-five values and one defect while all 94 late triples
     have rank five, or all 369 early pairs have rank five while the late
     triples have 93 rank-five values and one defect.  This follows because
     the 465 singleton cells and 95 late pairs already occupy 560 of the 561
     distinct masks of ranks at most four.

693. Consequently at least 367 of the 368 internal portals have rank exactly
     seven.  Every ordinary shared rank-five pair is the exact intersection

     defect pair can have larger rank; if the defect rank is `b=2,3,4`, its
     portal rank is at most `12-b`.  The seam portal has rank between six and
     nine.  Hence at most two of all 369 portals can have rank at least eight.

     fixed-delay checkpoint: twelve rank-seven masks and the single rank-eight

## 178. Exact atomic seam envelope

706. The one-parameter gap-cutoff bound in the three-box atomic branch is
     not sharp.  In the inherited aggregate, unlabelled, fixed-threshold
     seam relaxation, put

        n=6x-7, Z=3-2x, z_t=sqrt(2x(2-x)),  4/3<=x<=3/2.

     The exact minimum guaranteed saving is

        S_ex(x)=n x^2-(4-2 z_t)Z.

     The proof takes the greatest convex minorant of the exact saving
     integrand `phi_x(z)`.  It is the tangent from `(0,x^2)` to the quadratic
     branch at `z_t`, followed by that quadratic and then its zero tail.
     Jensen reduces every feasible nonabsorbed gap measure to
     `N env_x(Z/N)`, which is minimized at the smallest allowed mass `N=n`.

707. The sharpness claim survives the joint-feasibility audit.  At an atom,
     the projected feasible set is exactly

        n<=N<=2,   integral z dnu <= Z.

     Maximum absorption has mass `3Z` at gap zero.  The remaining mass `n`
     uses the two-point conditional gap law at `0` and `z_t`, with mean
     `Z/n`.  Its absorption demand can be spread at aggregate density three
     on `[x-1,2-x]`.  Thus absorption and gap budget are not double-counted.
     This is attainment inside the aggregate relaxation; no realizing word,
     direction-labelled ledger, or multiscale-compatible ledger is claimed.

708. At the balanced atom,

        S_ex(4/3)=4/3,

     three times the previous optimized-cutoff value `4/9`.  If
     `g(x)=4-3x+S_ex(x)`, direct differentiation shows that `g` is strictly
     increasing from `4/3` to `4`.  The independently audited large-defect
     transfer therefore gives, for every universal three-box word with
     atomic profile `2 delta_x`,

        liminf D_a/a^2 >= g(x)/7 >= 4/21.

     Optimizing over every proportional cap strengthens the uniform bound to

        liminf D_a/a^2 >= t_*^2/2
                          =0.202774508983752...,

     where `t_*` is the root in `(0,1)` of
     `2t^3-21t^2+8=0`.

709. A uniform `H_c->0` estimate completes the limit of the adversarial
     functional, and compact continuity completes the finite-band stability
     argument.  The source has one harmless endpoint typo: at `x=4/3`,
     `n=6x-7=1`, not `1/3`; its stated mean gap, mixture weights, and saving
     use the correct value.  “Tripled constants” is literal only for the
     balanced saving, not for every displayed defect constant.

710. This result seals the atomic optimization only.  It does not exclude
     arbitrary mixed profiles and does not prove the three-box theorem or the
     contiguous-OR conjecture.  Its strategic consequence is negative but
     useful: further progress cannot come from a sharper one-threshold scalar
     cutoff on atoms.  It must add multiscale threshold compatibility,
     direction-labelled absorption, or cross-line gap transport.  The source
     is `EXACT_ATOMIC_SEAM_ENVELOPE.md`, SHA-256
     `eb4f4eca7756a8909dbe803ac909833cb6569f7b8b7680ff4f7f51caaea4fb6d`.
     The independent audit is
     `EXACT_ATOMIC_SEAM_ENVELOPE_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT.md`, SHA-256
     `ee569f12b8a9ad053887091941587287c489295ba09ff34ec34d94c7c4b794aa`.

## 179. Exact maximal shadows and the single-switch boundary reservoir

711. Let `I_i=[i,rho_i]` with strictly increasing right endpoints, and let
     `C_i` be a factorable prescribed central row.  For the coordinatewise
     maximal factor `A^max`, every nonempty common core has the exact identity

        OR_(j=q..rho_p) A^max_j = intersection_(i=p..q) C_i.

     More strongly, for every factor `A` realizing the same central row,

        OR_(j=p..rho_q) A_j = union_(i=p..q) C_i.

     Thus feasible consecutive meets are literal lower OR witnesses in the
     maximal factor, and every central-preserving sparse repair automatically
     preserves all consecutive upper joins.  This holds for arbitrary
     left-anchored increasing-right schedules, not only fixed delay.

712. For the canonical one-switch schedule at rank-count length,

        I_i=[i,i+d-1] for i<=sigma,
        I_i=[i,i+d]   for i>sigma,
        sigma=dM+binomial(d+1,2)-L,

     assuming `sigma<=M-d`, all physical intervals of length at most `d`
     split exactly into

        sigma shortened central cells,
        L-d(d+1) nontrivial meet cores,
        d(d+1) boundary-reservoir cells.

     The reservoir consists of the short cells ending at
     `1,...,d-1,sigma+d` and all intervals contained in the terminal positions
     `[M+1,M+d]`; each side has `binomial(d+1,2)` cells.

713. The maximal factor collapses the whole reservoir to at most `3d-1`
     distinct values: at most `d-1` on the nested left triangle, `d` in the
     switch column, and `d` on the nested terminal triangle.  Consequently it
     realizes at most

        L-(d-1)^2

     distinct lower masks.  Hence for every `d>=2` the canonical maximal
     factor is necessarily nonuniversal.  This is a boundary no-go theorem,
     not an obstruction to arbitrary factors or arbitrary monotone schedules;
     sparse pinning is mathematically necessary.

714. The remaining pin problem is nevertheless local.  Assign the remaining
     `d(d+1)` lower masks to the reservoir.  For each coordinate, impose the
     reservoir's negative labels on the central legal set and retest only the
     positive central, meet-core, and reservoir intervals.  All changed legal
     positions lie in

        Omega=[1,d-1] union [sigma+1,sigma+d] union [M+1,M+d],

     of size at most `3d-1`.  Only `O(d)` central intervals and `O(d^2)` meet
     cores can be affected, giving `O(k d^2)` residual pin conditions after a
     reservoir assignment is selected, independent of the exponential middle
     layer size `M`.  This is a localization theorem, not an existence proof
     for the reservoir assignment.

715. Numerically, at `k=11` the 1,392 short cells split as

        369 central + 1,011 meet cores + 12 reservoir.

     The maximal factor has at most 1,019 of the 1,023 lower masks and must
     miss at least four.  The modification zone has eight positions.  At
     `k=14`,

        6,867 = 392 central + 6,469 meet cores + 6 reservoir,

     and the maximal factor must miss at least one of the 6,475 lower masks;
     the modification zone has five positions.

716. Under the stronger saturated-short-band hypotheses, every rank-`r-1`
     value is localized to `M+1` candidate cells.  With

        delta=M+1-binomial(k,r-1),

     at most `delta` early/late internal portals can rise above rank `r+1`,
     and pairwise-distinct immediate upper portals require

        sigma<=binomial(k,r+1)+delta+1.

     In odd dimension at the upper middle rank, `delta=1`; deleting the one
     lower defect leaves a two- or three-component spanning middle-level
     forest.  This generalizes the k=11 one-defect rigidity and refutes the
     slogan that every slack unit can become a distinct immediate portal.

717. The audited theorem is
     `SINGLE_SWITCH_MAXIMAL_SHADOW_THEOREM.md`, SHA-256
     `fa6ee6c12bcb8c0967579ca9f4fa99a57c1877d1c66735e84ebe614e26e86608`.
     Its independent audit passes, SHA-256
     `127d3307113de8cebdc9a1b07962b762c040b31ccd116c8494a3d41759791edc`.
     The remaining all-dimensional existence problem is now: construct one
     mixed-run central permutation with complete bulk meets and upper joins,
     then solve the bounded reservoir assignment and its local pin test.

## 181. Endpoint saturation and infinite-subsequence rigidity

721. Fix a rank `r`, put

        M=binomial(k,r),
        L=sum_{s=1}^{r-1} binomial(k,s),
        n=M+d,
        sigma=d*M+binomial(d+1,2)-L,

     and suppose a universal nonzero word of length `n` exists.  Select one
     witness for every rank-`r` mask.  Their right endpoints are distinct.
     For a selected endpoint `b`, let `j_b` be the number of nonempty
     last-occurrence blocks needed to form its selected rank-`r` suffix, and
     put `c_b=min(d,b)`.  Then

        sum_{b selected} (c_b-(j_b-1)) <= sigma.                 (181.1)

     Every summand is a nonnegative integer.  Equality zero at an endpoint is
     possible exactly when

        b>=d+1,  j_b=d+1,  and the witness is [b-d,b].           (181.2)

     Proof: choose one length-at-most-`d` witness for every lower mask and let
     `q_b` count those ending at `b`.  At a selected rank-`r` endpoint, every
     lower witness is a proper suffix of the central witness, so
     `q_b<=j_b-1`; elsewhere `q_b<=c_b`.  Sum these inequalities and use
     `sum_b c_b=L+sigma`.  The physical-length bound gives
     `j_b-1<=c_b` and characterizes zero defect.

722. Consequently at least `max(0,M-sigma)` selected rank-`r` witnesses have
     full physical length `d+1` and full recency depth `d+1`.  In the monotone
     band normal form

        I_i=[i+alpha_i,i+beta_i],

     a full-length witness is exactly state `(alpha_i,beta_i)=(0,d)`.  Since
     `alpha` and `beta` are nondecreasing, all such witnesses form one
     contiguous fixed-delay core.  Each core endpoint exposes a strict chain
     of `d` proper lower suffix unions.  This is an unconditional necessary
     condition for an equality-length word, not a construction.

723. The same endpoint chains give the audited rank-deficit inequality

        sum_{s=1}^{r-1} (r-s) binomial(k,s)
          >= (M+1) binomial(d+1,2) + binomial(d+1,3) - d*sigma.  (181.3)

     Indeed, `q_b` distinct lower masks ending at `b` form a strict chain and
     have total rank deficit at least `binomial(q_b+1,2)`.  Writing
     `e_b=c_b-q_b`, the triangular contribution lost from capacity `c_b<=d`
     is at most `d e_b`; summing uses `sum e_b=sigma` and the exact baseline

        sum_b binomial(c_b+1,2)
          =(M+1)binomial(d+1,2)+binomial(d+1,3).

724. For `k=11,r=6,d=3,sigma=369`, this theorem forces only a contiguous core
     of at least `462-369=93` full-depth four-term witnesses.  Thus the q369
     schedule is the extremal minimum-core specialization, not an arbitrary
     split.  For `k=14,r=7,d=2,sigma=392`, it forces at least
     `3432-392=3040` full-depth triple witnesses.  This recovers the earlier
     unrestricted 3040-core theorem and strengthens it by forcing all three
     recency blocks at those endpoints.

     In the *canonical* q369 schedule the endpoint budget is in fact exactly
     saturated.  Its 369 three-term rank-six witnesses each have right defect
     at least one, already exhausting `sigma=369`; hence every one has exactly
     three last-occurrence blocks, while all 93 four-term witnesses have four.
     The symmetric left-endpoint inequality gives the same conclusion for
     first-occurrence blocks.  Thus all 462 prescribed central witnesses are
     nonredundant from both directions.  Moreover the lower-witness endpoint
     counts are forced to equality: at a short central endpoint there are two
     lower proper suffixes, at a long one there are three, and at the three
     omitted central endpoints all available short suffixes are lower.  This
     recovers the exact q369 short-band saturation theorem in Section 184 and
     can be added as redundant SAT propagation; it is not an additional
     restriction on the q369 branch and does not address its Hall/pin or upper
     shadow obstructions.

725. There are infinitely many even dimensions `k=2m` for which the central
     arithmetic residual satisfies

        sigma/W(k)=O(k^(-1/2)).                                 (181.4)

     The proof uses

        rho_m=L_m/W_m
          =(sqrt(pi)/2)sqrt(m)-1/2+sqrt(pi)/(16sqrt(m))+O(m^-3/2),

     eventual monotonicity, and the last `m` before `rho_m` crosses an
     integer.  At that `m`, the required integer delay is the crossing integer
     (the triangular correction divided by `W_m` is exponentially small).
     A uniform `tau=O(2^m)` bound for noncentral ranks, versus the adjacent
     binomial loss `W_m/(m+1)`, shows that the middle rank uniquely maximizes
     `B(2m)` eventually.  Hence any equality word along this subsequence has a
     contiguous full-depth core of

        (1-O(k^-1/2)) W(k)

     middle masks and only `O(W(k)/sqrt(k))` exceptional endpoints/short-band
     cells.  This is conditional rigidity.  It neither proves equality nor
     supplies a new upper bound.

726. The next genuinely stronger target is two-sided saturation: repeat
     (181.1) at left endpoints using first-occurrence blocks, then intersect
     the two exceptional sets.  Along the subsequence in (181.4), almost every
     central window would have full novelty depth from both directions.  A
     useful disproof route would show that such doubly saturated overlapping
     windows necessarily create more than `sigma` collisions or pin defects;
     no such collision theorem is yet proved.

727. The symmetric theorem is now proved.  If `f_a` is the first-occurrence
     depth at a selected left endpoint and `c_a=min(d,n-a+1)`, then

        sum_{a selected} (c_a-(f_a-1)) <= sigma.                 (181.5)

     Thus at least `max(0,M-2*sigma)` selected central witnesses have both
     full first-occurrence and full last-occurrence depth.  This forces 2,648
     doubly saturated triple witnesses at `k=14`, but is vacuous at `k=11`.
     Full depth on both sides does not force Johnson adjacency: already for
     `d=1`, three disjoint nonempty entry blocks give two doubly saturated
     consecutive windows with arbitrarily large exchange distance.

728. For an occupied lower-band cell `x`, let `h_R(x)` count occupied cells
     in its column containing it and `h_L(x)` count occupied cells in its row
     containing it.  Its label has rank deficit at least
     `max(h_L(x),h_R(x))`, so the exact two-sided necessary inequality is

        D(k,r) >= sum_{x occupied} max(h_L(x),h_R(x)).           (181.6)

     The complete-band scalar value is

        F=M*binomial(d+1,2)+sum_{u=1}^d u^2,

     and deleting one cell reduces it by at most `3d-2`; hence

        D(k,r) >= F-(3d-2)*sigma.                               (181.7)

     This coarse consequence is not stronger at `k=11`, `k=14`, or on the
     guaranteed infinite subsequence.  Useful progress now requires the
     actual geometry of the `sigma` holes or coordinate pin constraints, not
     another scalar moment bound.  The independent audit is
     `ENDPOINT_SATURATION_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT.md`, SHA-256
     `a5d1498c2bb2a867682cf409f169fed9ca8c472c372e2639220580d4a24a76f7`.

## 182. Rainbow pair--triple obstruction and failure of local reservoir repair

729. There is a general obstruction to making the first two consecutive-
     intersection rows globally rainbow.  Let `C_1,...,C_M` be distinct
     rank-`r` masks, put

        P_i=C_i intersect C_(i+1),
        T_i=C_i intersect C_(i+1) intersect C_(i+2),
        H=binomial(k,r-1), G=binomial(k,r-2),

     and suppose every `P_i,T_i` is nonzero and all are pairwise distinct,
     including across depths.  If `h` rank-`r-1` masks are absent from the
     pair row, then

        h >= ceil((2H-M-G)/2).                                  (182.1)

     Indeed `M-1-H+h` pair cores have lower rank, so at least
     `2H-M-2h` triples are flanked by two distinct rank-`r-1` facets of the
     common rank-`r` middle set.  Each such triple has rank `r-2`, and there
     are only `G` possible values.

730. At the middle layers this becomes

        k=2m+1: h >= ceil(M/(m+2)),
        k=2m:   h >= ceil(M(m-1)/((m+1)(m+2))).                  (182.2)

     Thus an all-pair/all-triple rainbow architecture requires an
     `Omega(M/k)` deficit, exponentially larger than a polynomial boundary
     reservoir.  This is an obstruction to that architecture, not a lower
     bound on `nu(k)`.

731. For the canonical `k=11` q369 row, Gate R2 asked all 461 pair, 460
     triple, and 90 quadruple cores to be nonzero and globally distinct,
     leaving only 12 lower masks.  Equation (182.2) requires at least 66.
     Equivalently, at least 450 pair cores would have rank five, so at most
     11 low pairs could spoil triples; at least

        460-2*11=438

     distinct triples would then have rank four, versus only 330 available
     rank-four masks.  Hence the q369 rainbow-core/reservoir branch is
     mathematically UNSAT before runs, upper shadows, pins, or SAT.  The bare
     `02|03` witness schedule and unrestricted equality remain open.

732. A collision-tolerant strengthening applies to the coordinatewise
     maximal factor on this same schedule.  Let `q` be the number of lower
     masks missing among its 1,011 core cells and 12 reservoir cells, let
     `ell` be the number of 461 pair cells below rank five, and let `delta_5`
     count repeated rank-five pair occurrences.  The three collapsed
     reservoir zones contribute at most three new rank-five values, giving

        q >= ell+delta_5-2.                                     (182.3)

     At least `460-2ell-delta_5` triples are intersections of distinct
     rank-five facets and hence rank four.  Their excess and the disjoint
     rank-five repeats give

        q >= delta_5+max(0,130-2ell-delta_5).                   (182.4)

     Minimizing the maximum of (182.3)--(182.4) gives

        q >= 42.                                                 (182.5)

     This strengthens the earlier boundary-collapse lower bound `q>=4`.

733. The proposed local repair zone

        Omega={1,2,370,371,372,463,464,465}

     meets exactly 11 nontrivial core intervals and all 12 reservoir cells.
     The 369 other short cells are fixed rank-six central triples.  Therefore
     an Omega-supported central-preserving edit can introduce at most 23 new
     lower values.  Starting from (182.5), at least `42-23=19` lower masks
     remain missing.  The entire boundary-only reservoir repair is therefore
     impossible.  A viable q369 factor must use nonlocal sparse pin changes,
     or a different central row/schedule.

734. The formal proof and scope audit are in
     `RAINBOW_PAIR_TRIPLE_OBSTRUCTION.md`, SHA-256
     `9ccd7b18f6e1b44d5fa56f8a1af42b61fdef6cb84af6343904b24785105499b3`.
     The failed compressed-search design remains useful as a verifier, but
     its heavy search mode is disabled so that this proved-impossible branch
     is not given more compute.

735. The collision-tolerant argument extends to every factorable
     single-switch maximal factor at rank-count equality when `d>=3`.  With

        H=binomial(k,r-1), G=binomial(k,r-2),

     and `q` the number of lower masks missed by its `L` candidate lower
     cells,

        q >= max(0,ceil((2H-M-G-6)/3)).                         (182.6)

     The three maximal-factor boundary zones contribute at most three new
     rank-`r-1` values.  Eliminating the counts of low adjacent pairs and
     repeated high-pair values between the rank-`r-1` coverage inequality and
     the rank-`r-2` triple-collision inequality proves (182.6).  At the middle
     layers this is

        k=2m+1: q>=ceil(2M/(3(m+2))-2),
        k=2m:   q>=ceil(2M(m-1)/(3(m+1)(m+2))-2).

     Hence `q=Omega(M/k)`: even allowing arbitrary bulk collisions, a
     coordinatewise maximal factor cannot be repaired by an `O(d)` boundary
     support changing only `O(d^2)` short cells.  This rules out exact local
     reservoir repair asymptotically.  The loss is still `o(M)`, so it does
     not by itself refute an asymptotic `1+o(1)` construction that appends or
     globally repairs the missing masks.

736. Every factor `A` realizing the same central schedule satisfies
     `A_j subseteq A_j^max`.  If the maximal factor misses `q` lower masks,
     each such mask must acquire a short witness whose OR changes.  One
     changed physical position belongs to at most

        1+2+...+d=binomial(d+1,2)

     intervals of length at most `d`.  Hence

        |{j:A_j != A_j^max}| >= ceil(2q/(d(d+1))).              (182.7)

     Together with (182.6) and `d^2=Theta(k)` at the middle rank, a successful
     factor must differ from the maximal factor at

        Omega(M/k^2)=Omega(2^k/k^(5/2))

     positions.  This is a support-cardinality result, not uniform spatial
     distribution.  At `k=11` it gives at least seven changed positions; the
     sharper incidence calculation in paragraph 733 still proves that the
     particular eight-position boundary zone is insufficient.

740. In the `q369_schedule` branch the first 369 selected rank-six witnesses

        465+464+463=1392

     of physical intervals of lengths at most three.  Hence every short cell
     is used exactly once: the fixed triples carry 369 rank-six values and

741. The maximal residual short cells are exactly the 369 pairs

        [s,s+1], 0<=s<=368,

     Every rank-five cell must be maximal, since a strict residual supercell
     would have a distinct rank-at-most-five OR properly containing it.
     Therefore the 462 selected rank-five witnesses occupy all but one of
     these 463 cells.  In the solver's monotone `(alpha,beta)` convention the
     exact schedule is

        rows   0..367: 01 or 12,
        row       368: 01 or 13,
        rows 369..461: 02 or 13.

751. The compact fixed-row analysis was extended from singleton candidate

753. For a perfect matching `m`, let `D_b(m)` be the union of intervals
     assigned to targets omitting bit `b`, and let `Z_b(m)` be the central
     envelope positions for `b` outside `D_b(m)`.  The matching is an exact
     factor certificate if and only if every position has a surviving bit,
     every positive central `(C_i,b)` meets `Z_b(m)`, and every positive
     matched target/bit pair meets `Z_b(m)`.  When these conditions hold,
     putting every surviving bit at every legal position constructs the
     factor.  Thus zero fixed-matching pin failures is a sufficient, directly
     decodable target, whereas a positive heuristic minimum proves nothing
     about other matchings.

## 187. No-go theorem for the connected 93/369 single-cut braid

758. Reversing the q369 orientation suggests 93 long rank-six witnesses
     followed by 369 short ones.  The proposed connected schedule used

        J_i=[i,i+2], I_i=[i,i+3]       (i<=93),
        J_i=[i+1,i+2], I_i=[i+1,i+3]   (i>=94).

     Although `I_i` is the hull of `J_i,J_(i+1)`, the schedule is impossible.
     Its rank-five pair `J_94=[95,96]` is contained in the residual triple
     `[94,96]`.  The latter was claimed as one of the 561 cells bijecting to
     ranks one through four, but its OR contains the rank-five value of
     `J_94`.  Since the 369 short rank-six values and 1,023 lower values
     saturate all 1,392 short cells, neither a duplicate nor an additional
     rank-five value is possible.

759. The correct maximal residual rank-five pool in this orientation is the
     94 triples starting `1,...,94` together with the 369 pairs starting
     `96,...,464`.  All but one of these 463 cells carry the rank-five layer.
     The proposed schedule instead selected triples `1,...,93` and pairs
     `95,...,463`, using a nonmaximal cell and omitting the wrong boundary
     cells.

760. More invariantly, the rank-six left/right endpoint sets and the correct
     rank-five maximal pool allow at most 922 same-endpoint edges on the 924
     middle vertices after one omission.  The endpoint graph is a spanning
     linear forest, so it has at least two components.  A connected
     alternating Hamilton path across this width switch is impossible for
     every omission choice.  This proves that the two-path correction in
     paragraph 755 is structurally necessary, not just a search convenience.

761. Full proof and the independent audit are
     `SINGLE_CUT_CONNECTED_BRAID_NO_GO.md` and
     `SINGLE_CUT_CONNECTED_BRAID_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT.md`.  The result does not
     refute `nu(11)=465`: `93+369` is only the extremal maximum-short branch,
     while an unrestricted equality word may use more than 93 full witnesses
     or additional monotone-band regimes.

## 188. Exact hole spectrum and weighted boundary moments

762. Fix a rank `r`, put `M=binomial(k,r)`, `n=M+d` with `d>=1`, and select
     one length-at-most-`d` witness for every nonempty mask below rank `r`.
     Let `H` be the other cells in the short interval band.  Then

        |H|=sigma=d*M+binomial(d+1,2)-sum_{s=1}^{r-1}binomial(k,s).

     For every coordinate set `Q`, if `F_Q` counts all short cells whose OR
     avoids `Q`, and `h_Q` counts the holes whose OR avoids `Q`, then exactly

        F_Q=sum_{s=1}^{r-1}binomial(k-|Q|,s)+h_Q.              (188.1)

     If `c_T` counts holes with OR exactly `T`, then

        h_Q=sum_{T subseteq [k] minus Q} c_T.                 (188.2)

     Hence the complete avoidance-error family is one Boolean zeta transform
     of a nonnegative integer vector of total mass `sigma`; Möbius inversion
     recovers that vector.  This part is exact bookkeeping, but it prevents
     the `2^k` avoidance errors from being chosen independently.

763. Projecting every array entry to a `q`-set `Q` and deleting empty
     projections leaves a universal word on `Q`.  If `z_Q` is the number of
     deleted positions, then `z_Q<=n-nu(q)`, and averaging gives

        Z_q:=sum_i binomial(k-|A_i|,q)
             <=binomial(k,q)(n-nu(q)).                        (188.3)

     For the zero runs of the indicator `A_i intersect Q = empty`, let
     `Lambda_Q` be the sum of their lengths truncated at `d-1`.  Exact run
     geometry gives

        F_Q+(d/2)Lambda_Q <= d z_Q.                            (188.4)

764. The cover graph of the short band has

        E_(n,d)=(d-1)(2n-d)

     edges and maximum degree four.  After deleting the `sigma` holes, at
     least `max(E_(n,d)-4sigma,0)` selected-selected cover edges remain.  For
     an oriented selected edge `I proper-subset J`, define its `q`-gradient

        binomial(k-|U(I)|,q)-binomial(k-|U(J)|,q).

     It counts the `q`-sets avoiding the smaller label but meeting the larger.
     A zero run supplies at most two truncated boundary families, so if `G_q`
     is the total selected-edge gradient, then

        G_q<=2 sum_{|Q|=q}Lambda_Q.

     Combining this with (188.1), (188.3), and (188.4) yields the audited
     weighted theorem

        d Z_q >= R_q+H_q+(d/4)G_q,                            (188.5)

     where

        R_q=binomial(k,q) sum_{s=1}^{r-1}binomial(k-q,s),
        H_q=sum_{I in H}binomial(k-|U(I)|,q).

765. Every selected cover edge joins two distinct lower masks, so its lower
     label has rank at most `r-2` and its upper label rank at most `r-1`.
     Therefore

        G_q >= max(E_(n,d)-4sigma,0) binomial(k-r+1,q-1).      (188.6)

     Substituting (188.3), using `nu(q)>=B(q)`, and discarding `H_q>=0`
     produces a completely numerical necessary inequality for `n=B(k)`.
     `check_hole_boundary_moments.cpp` evaluated it at every maximizing rank
     through `k=19`; `HOLE_BOUNDARY_NUMERICAL_CHECK_K19.txt` records zero
     violations.  Thus the coarse averaged form proves no new exact value,
     although the exact Möbius/run system is strictly richer.

766. The independent audit passes all inequality directions, the `d/4`
     coefficient, the gradient minimum, and the projection substitution.
     It also notes that no positive lower bound on `H_1` is available without
     extra structure, since a hole may have full OR.  The report is
     `HOLE_SPECTRUM_BOUNDARY_MOMENT_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT.md`.  This hierarchy is
     a valid unrestricted lower-bound framework, not a proof or disproof of
     `nu(k)=B(k)`.

767. The strongest consequence that uses one common hole-rank spectrum is the
     finite moment LP

        c_s>=0,  sum_s c_s=sigma,
        sum_s c_s*binomial(k-s,q)<=U_q                 (1<=q<=k),

     where `c_s` counts holes whose OR has rank `s` and `U_q` is the remaining
     budget in (188.5) after the projection and gradient terms.  This is exact
     for the rank-averaged hierarchy.  Its dual says that for nonnegative
     multipliers `lambda_q` and allowed hole ranks `S`,

        sum_q lambda_q U_q
          >= sigma min_(s in S) sum_q lambda_q binomial(k-s,q).

     With no rank restriction this gives no unconditional improvement:
     putting all mass at `c_k=sigma` makes every positive moment `H_q` zero.
     Thus common Möbius nonnegativity by itself is exhausted by this LP.

768. If at least `a_j` holes have rank at most `t_j`, with increasing
     thresholds and cumulative counts, the simultaneously sharp forced
     moment is

        H_q >= sum_j (a_j-a_(j-1))*binomial(k-t_j,q).

     In the q369 branch all 369 holes are precisely shortened rank-six
     masks, so `H_q=369*binomial(5,q)`.  Substitution using the exact known
     values of `nu(q)` through ten and the coarse cover-gradient lower bound
     still leaves a minimum margin of 6176.5 (at `q=1`).  Hence even the exact
     hole-rank spectrum cannot refute `n=465` through the present averaged
     theorem.  New leverage must couple hole *locations* to cover edges/run
     boundaries, or retain the unsummed `Q`-indexed system.

## 189. Upward high-hole cones and the exact edge/moment tradeoff

769. Split the `sigma` holes of Section 188 into `h` low holes, whose OR rank
     is below `r`, and `sigma-h` high holes.  High holes form an upset in the
     short-interval containment band: every short superinterval of a high
     interval also has OR rank at least `r` and therefore cannot be a selected
     lower witness.

770. This upset property improves the cover-edge deletion count.  Every edge
     incident with the high upset has its upper endpoint high, and each upper
     interval has at most two immediate subintervals.  Those edges number at
     most `2(sigma-h)`.  All remaining hole-incident edges touch a low hole,
     costing at most `4h`.  Hence at least

        e_sel(h)=max(E_(n,d)-2sigma-2h,0)                      (189.1)

     cover edges have two selected endpoints.  The old degree-only estimate
     is the endpoint `h=sigma`; the all-high endpoint improves `E-4sigma` to
     `E-2sigma`.

771. Low holes compensate for their larger edge cost.  For every `q>=1`,

        H_q >= h binomial(k-r+1,q),

     while each selected-selected edge has gradient at least
     `binomial(k-r+1,q-1)`.  Inserting both facts into (188.5) proves

        d Z_q >= R_q
          + h binomial(k-r+1,q)
          + (d/4)e_sel(h)binomial(k-r+1,q-1).                 (189.2)

     Minimizing the last two terms over the unknown integer
     `0<=h<=sigma` and using the projection bound gives a new completely
     numerical necessary inequality.  It dominates the scalar corollary of
     Section 188 for every `q`.

772. At `k=11,r=6,n=465,d=3,sigma=369`, `E=1854`.  For `q=1`, (189.2) is

        3 Z_1 >= 7007+6h+(3/4)(1116-2h)
              = 7844+(9/2)h.

     Thus the worst spectrum has every hole high (`h=0`).  Projection gives
     `3Z_1<=15312`, leaving slack 7468; the stronger theorem still does not
     refute length 465.  In the q369 branch the exact hole moment
     `H_q=369 binomial(5,q)` and the improved 1116-edge bound leave q=1 slack
     5623.

773. Anti-Monge rhombus geometry adds a conditional local fact.  If an outer
     interval is a minimal high hole and its two lower covers are nonhigh,
     then its OR rank is at most `2r-2` at length two and at most `2r-3` at
     length at least three.  The inner interval is nonempty in the latter
     case and contributes at least one to the anti-Monge inequality.  This
     forces avoidance weight for minimal nonsingleton high holes when those
     rank ceilings are below `k`.  It is not unconditional because a high
     upset may have singleton minimal elements.

774. `check_hole_upset_moments.cpp` evaluates the integer-multiplied form of
     (189.2).  `HOLE_UPSET_NUMERICAL_CHECK_K19.txt` records every maximizing
     rank below 20 and zero violations.  Full proofs and the exact limitation
     of the rhombus refinement are in `HOLE_UPSET_BOUNDARY_TRADEOFF.md`.
     This is a strict unrestricted lower-bound improvement, but it changes no
     exact-value ledger.

775. The rhombus observation admits an unconditional cone-isoperimetric
     refinement.  Let `x` count high singleton holes and `m` count minimal
     nonsingleton high holes.  A singleton cone has at most
     `C1=binomial(d+1,2)` cells and a nonsingleton cone at most
     `C2=binomial(d,2)`, so

        x+m <= sigma-h,
        C1*x+C2*m >= sigma-h.                                (189.3)

     High singleton cells have no downward cover edges, improving (189.1) to

        e_sel >= max(E-2sigma-2h+2x,0).                      (189.4)

     A minimal nonsingleton high hole has rank at most `2r-2`; hence, with
     `c=max(k-2r+2,0)`,

        H_q >= h binomial(k-r+1,q)+m binomial(c,q).           (189.5)

     Minimizing the corresponding boundary-moment expression over integer
     `h,x,m` subject to (189.3) gives a second, stronger numerical necessary
     inequality coupling hole ranks and locations.

776. At `k=11,q=1`, its minimizer is

        h=0, x=61, m=1, selected-edge lower bound=1238.

     The added moment/gradient term is 929.5, so

        3Z_1 >= 7936.5,

     leaving projection slack 7375.5.  The new escape configuration is
     explicit: many high holes can lie in cones above well-separated high
     singleton entries.  Eliminating it requires coupling singleton-cone
     locations to zero runs or literal rank moments; cone cardinality and
     anti-Monge ranks alone still do not decide `k=11`.

## 190. Forced second-order shadow coverage in the q369 schedule

777. Assume a universal 465-entry nonzero word uses the canonical q369
     rank-six witness schedule: triples for the first 369 central masks and
     quadruples for the last 93.  The 369 central triples occupy exactly the
     short-band slack.  Hence the other 1,023 short cells are forced to carry
     every mask of ranks one through five bijectively.  No extra saturation
     hypothesis is needed.

778. Among those cells, the only possible rank-five hosts are the 369 early
     pairs and 94 late triples.  Exactly one of these 463 cells is defective.
     Every nondefective internal host equals the intersection of its two
     flanking rank-six targets.  Thus the two bulk ranges are Johnson arcs
     apart from at most one defective internal transition; the width-switch
     seam remains unconstrained.

779. Rank-four hosts in the bulk are the 367 early singletons and 91 late
     pairs.  Whenever such a cell has rank four and its two flanks are
     nondefective, its value is exactly the corresponding consecutive triple
     intersection `D3`.  Only seven rank-four hosts escape this identity:
     `A_1,A_2,B_370,B_371,B_463,B_464`, and the unique defective rank-five
     slot if that slot has rank four.  Therefore every q369 optimum must have

        at least 323 of the 330 rank-four masks

     among the 458 bulk `D3` windows.  This is the certified D3-coverage law.
     It is now a hard cut in `k11_q369_hall_search.cpp`; the best faithful
     two-path rows pass it with 328 distinct bulk D3 values.

780. The stronger statement that all 1,011 maximal meet cores themselves
     carry distinct lower masks is impossible: it forces at least 438
     distinct rank-four triple meets, or 456 after adding the reservoir rank
     caps, exceeding `binomial(11,4)=330`.  Actual factors escape because
     deep cell values may be proper subsets of their set-theoretic meets.

781. `K11_Q369_MEET_RIGIDITY_NEXT.md` contains the derivation.  The
     independent audit `K11_Q369_MEET_RIGIDITY_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT.md` passes
     the saturation, one-defect, exact-D2, and 323/330 theorems, but rejects
     several stronger conclusions in that source: they do not force a
     two-cut middle-levels Hamilton cycle or crosswise endpoint facets; the
     Section 8 cycle is only a sufficient subclass; up to five upper masks
     may be supplied by the exceptional right endpoint rather than central
     row unions; and the claimed general-k one-defect/D3 laws in Section 9
     are not proved.  Only the audited statements above enter this handoff.

777. The entire theorem, including the cone sizes, the `+2x` edge correction,
     the minimal-hole rank moment, all inequality directions, and the `k=11`
     arithmetic, is independently certified PASS in
     `HOLE_UPSET_BOUNDARY_TRADEOFF_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT.md`, SHA-256

        31209784d23e9e6a87e08acb12f1eb5bbfdf18588d7f6ac7a1621934d5708b51.

     Scope conventions are `d>=1`, zero-free entries for the `2r-3` ceiling,
     zero for out-of-range binomial coefficients, and integer minimization
     over the hole counts.  “Strict improvement” is structural; degenerate
     parameter choices can attain equality with the older scalar bound.

## 191. Entry-rank truncation and arbitrary ideal support

782. For every zero-free universal word `A` and every `1<=s<=k`, let

        p_s(A)=#{i: |A_i|<=s},
        b_s(k)=binomial(k,s)+tau(k,s).

     Deleting every entry of rank greater than `s` preserves all witnesses
     for targets of rank at most `s`.  The rank-count proof at rank `s` needs
     no higher targets, and therefore

        p_s(A)>=b_s(k).                                    (191.1)

     If `n=B(k)=b_r(k)`, every entry has rank at most `r`, and

        #{i:|A_i|>s}<=B(k)-b_s(k).                         (191.2)

     In particular, every hypothetical `k=11,n=465` word has all entries of
     rank at most six and at most one entry of rank six.  These exact cuts are
     now implemented generically in `exact_or_sat.cpp`; SAT/decode regressions
     pass at `(k,n)=(3,4),(4,7),(5,12)`.

783. If `F` is a punctured down-set below the selected rank `r`, and the
     positions whose entries lie in `F` have run lengths `g_1,...,g_rho`, then

        |F| <= sum_j f_d(g_j) <= f_d(sum_j g_j),            (191.3)

     where `f_d(g)=sum_(ell=1)^d (g-ell+1)_+`.  The support also has size at
     least the width `w(F)`, and

        |F|<=d|P_F|-(d-1)rho.                              (191.4)

     This is a sound support/run restriction but does not contain the full
     dimension-restriction theorem; the latter can be strictly stronger.

784. The rank-truncation, ideal-support, literal-central-entry, run--zeta, and
     window-moment claims have been audited in
     `RANK_TRUNCATION_IDEAL_SUPPORT_AUDIT.md`.  The exact run--zeta equations
     are essentially Section 188 in physical-support language.  The moment
     concavity/convexity proof needs a separate length-zero boundary check but
     is valid after that repair.  These theorems supply lossless search cuts;
     they do not change the exact-value ledger or prove that no other scalar
     obstruction can exist.

## 192. Conditional self-dual odd-graph braid

785. For a Hamilton cycle `C_i` in `O_6=KG(11,5)`, let `z_i` be the omitted
     coordinate of the edge `C_i C_(i+1)` and put

        R_i=C_(i-1) intersect C_(i+1).

     Then `R_i` has rank four and the two parity lifts

        L_j=C_(2j+p),  U_j=C_(2j+p+1)^c

     obey

        U_(j-1) intersect U_j = L_j,
        U_(j-1) union U_j = R_(2j+p)^c.                    (192.1)

     Hence complete rank-four transition colors would give complete rank-seven
     union colors by the same certificate.  The omitted-label recurrence also
     translates singleton and two-vertex parity runs into the relevant label
     returns at cyclic distances three and five.

786. This is a useful self-dual coordinate system, but no claimed complete
     `O_6` artifact is currently available locally or on either RunPod.  The
     two parity lifts give a `231+231` cycle cover, not automatically the
     `369+93` paths used by the mixed-width search; a color-safe switch and
     compatible cuts remain necessary.  `verify_o6_cycle.cpp` is the strict
     checker for any future 462-mask candidate.

787. The equality lower bound does **not** force every one of the 369 spare
     short cells to have a distinct rank-six OR.  That collision-free
     saturation, and the resulting arithmetic split `369=231+138`, are valid
     stronger construction ansatzes only.  The full audit and the six missing
     certificate gates are in `SELF_DUAL_ODD_BRAID_AUDIT.md`.  No new upper
     bound or exact value is recorded from this route yet.

## 193. Absorbed direction flow and global line coarea

788. The marked three-box relaxation now retains the physical cost of seam
     absorption.  An actually absorbed predecessor--successor seam must change
     fixed-coordinate direction.  At every threshold its direction matrix is
     off-diagonal, has row/column capacities given by the retained direction
     counts, and satisfies

        A(c)<=min(m(c)-1,2(m(c)-max_d n_d(c)))              (193.1)

     for a linear tail.  Every physical absorbed edge has one common threshold
     lifetime `[H(i,j),min(lambda_i,lambda_j))`; the flow cannot be optimized
     independently at different thresholds.

789. Every absorbed successor lies on a strictly positive coordinate line.
     If `T_B` is their level sum and `I_B` their cross-direction intersection
     count, then the finite line master inequality sharpens to

        E<=2am-T_B-I_B+m.                                  (193.2)

     In the normalized limit this gives

        ell(c)<=2f(c)-tau_A(c)-iota_A(c).                  (193.3)

790. For every nonnegative compactly supported weight `w` on `(1,2)` and
     `W(s)=integral_1^s w(c)dc`, the same physical marked-line process obeys

        integral W(s)(s-2+|t|) dkappa
        +sum_(d<e) integral_(|t+u|<=1)
             W(min(s,s')) dkappa_d dkappa_e
        -integral W(min(s_x,s_y,s_z)) dXi <=0.             (193.4)

     Here `Xi` is the actual additive-triple measure, not a product of
     independently selected marginals.  `ABSORBED_FLOW_COAREA.md` contains the
     full finite-to-limit proof and has received an independent unqualified
     PASS after normalization repairs.

791. Equations (193.1)--(193.4) close the prior loophole in which high seam
     absorption was bought from an unlabelled scalar capacity: high absorption
     now pays direction balance, positive levels, and line intersections; low
     absorption leaves more seams in the exact saving functional.  They do not
     yet close the local three-box theorem.  The remaining analytic target is
     one common weighted inequality coupling both payments, or a single
     physically realizable marked counterprocess satisfying them all.

## 194. Sharp positive-line isoperimetry and the paired broad seal

792. Let `nu_1,nu_2,nu_3<=dt` be positive-line level measures on `[0,1]`,
     with total mass `A`, and put

        E(nu)=sum_i integral t dnu_i
              +sum_(i<j) integral_(t+u<=1) dnu_i(t)dnu_j(u).

     Ferrers compression gives the sharp lower envelope

        E(nu)>=F(A),

        F(A)=A^2/2                    (0<=A<=1),
             A-1/2                    (1<=A<=2),
             A^2/2-A+3/2              (2<=A<=3).            (194.1)

     All branches are attained.  The complement identity

        E(dt-nu_1,dt-nu_2,dt-nu_3)=E(nu)+3-2A

     converts the first branch into the third and independently checks the
     constants.

793. Apply (194.1) to the actual absorbed successor levels of the explicit
     nested alternating-pair broad process.  At `c downarrow 1`, its reflected
     seams have the unique allowed level `t=2-s`, its line measures obey
     `nu_i<=dt`, and (193.3) gives `E(nu)<=1`.  Hence

        A<=3/2.                                             (194.2)

     The protected saving density is

        b(t)=(2-t)(1+t)=2+t-t^2.

     Since the total absorbed density is at most `2dt`, the bathtub principle
     and (194.2) give

        B_abs<=2 integral_(1/8)^(7/8) b(t)dt=423/128.       (194.3)

     The all-nonabsorbed saving is `13/3`, while the scalar part tends to
     five and the contracted gap moment tends to zero.  Therefore every
     arbitrary partial actual-line absorption of this process satisfies

        limsup_(c downarrow 1) U(c)
        <=5-(13/3-423/128)
        =1525/384=4-11/384<4.                              (194.4)

     Thus the sole explicit nested broad scalar survivor is not physically
     realizable in the subquadratic-defect regime.  This strengthens the
     earlier lifetime-saturation exclusion to every partial absorption; it
     does not exclude arbitrary mixed profiles.

794. There is also a common-weight dual valid for every coherent marked
     process.  With

        phi(p,s,z)=min(p,(4-s-z)_+)(s-z)_+,
        G_(w,q)(c)=integral min(w(c)phi,q(c)(p-1)) d rho_c,
        R_A(c)=2f(c)-ell(c)-tau_A(c)-iota_A(c)>=0,

     the absorbed/nonabsorbed seam dichotomy and (193.3) give

        w(c)(U(c)-4)
        <=w(c)(3c+2e(c)+H(c)-4)-G_(w,q)(c)
          +q(c)(2f(c)-ell(c))
          -q(c)(iota_A(c)+R_A(c)).                         (194.5)

     Integrating (194.5) preserves the common physical edge lifetimes.  A
     universal all-profile proof would follow from nonnegative common weights
     `w,q` making its integrated right side strictly negative for every
     coherent process.  The unresolved global payment is

        integral q(c)(iota_A(c)+R_A(c))dc;

     scalar absorption capacity alone cannot replace it.  The proof and
     independent PASS are `POSITIVE_LINE_ISOPERIMETRY.md` and
     `POSITIVE_LINE_ISOPERIMETRY_AUDIT.md`.

## 195. Exact boundary of one-threshold absorbed-line control

795. Absorbed lines alone do not prove the all-profile inequality suggested
     by Section 194.  There is an exact stationary zero-gap limiting ledger
     with

        f=11/5, ell=3, A=9/5, W=7/25,

     equal predecessor/successor length marginals, legal absorption intervals,
     off-diagonal absorbed direction flow, and actual absorbed-line energy

        E_A=261/200<2f-3=7/5.                              (195.1)

     Nevertheless

        2A-W=83/25>1+f=80/25,                             (195.2)

     and the exact local seam functional is

        U(1+)=1029/250=4.116.                              (195.3)

     Thus no theorem using only absorbed mass, request width, and the
     one-threshold positive-line penalty can close the mixed-profile case.

796. The construction uses

        nu_x=Lebesgue|_[0,9/10],
        nu_y=Lebesgue|_[1/10,1],
        w(t)=(4/7)min(t,1-t),
        p(t)=1+t-w(t)/2,
        s(t)=2-t-w(t)/2.

     Absorb `y->x` and `x->y` edges at level `t`, and add nonabsorbed mass
     `2/5` at the `z->z` loop `p=s=11/10`.  The identity
     `p(t)=s(1-t)` gives joint direction-length stationarity.  Its complete
     arithmetic and scope are in `LOCAL_ABSORPTION_COUNTEREXAMPLE.md`; its
     independent audit is `LOCAL_ABSORPTION_COUNTEREXAMPLE_AUDIT.md`.

797. This is not a physical counterprocess.  Every placement of the missing
     nonabsorbed `z`-lines adds at least `2/5` to the full `T+I-J` line
     functional, raising `261/200` to at least `341/200>7/5`; hence the full
     all-plateau coarea gate kills the example.  It refutes the absorbed-line
     relaxation, not (193.4).

798. More generally, if `C=2A-W`, support and common marginals give

        C<=min(2A,6-2f+A),

     while sharp positive-line isoperimetry gives `F(A)<=2f-3`.  These imply

        C<=1+f

     for `f<=2` and for `f>=22/9`.  Therefore the only locally dangerous
     count band is

        2<f<22/9,                                          (195.4)

     apart from strictness/equality at its endpoints.

799. With

        R_beta=integral_(rho-alpha)(p-1)(s-1),

     the exact zero-gap identity is

        U(1+)=3-f+(2A-W)-R_beta.                           (195.5)

     The repaired minimal theorem is consequently

        (2A-W)-R_beta<=1+f,                                (195.6)

     now under the **full all-line coarea and common-lifetime process**, plus
     an equality analysis or fixed strict margin at one common continuity
     threshold.  This is the sharp next target; the local counterexample is
     itself evidence that the full-line term is capable of supplying exactly
     the missing payment.

## 196. Full-line wedge-cover seal for the zero-gap branch

800. Suppose the selected dangerous plateau edge mass satisfies

        ell(1+)=3.

     Their disjoint word-edge intervals then contain `(3-o(1))a^2` middle
     points.  Since these points lie on the selected complete coordinate
     lines and `|H_a|=3a^2+O(a)`, those lines miss only `D_a=o(a^2)` points
     of the middle hexagon.

801. Let `P_a,N_a` count selected strictly positive and strictly negative
     coordinate levels.  For every unselected positive level `x` in one
     direction, the wedge points

        (x,-y,-(x-y)),  1<=y<x,

     must, except at uncovered points, meet a selected negative line in one
     of the other directions.  Splitting according to an uncovered-slice
     threshold `h` gives the exact robust bound

        3a-P_a<=2N_a+3h+3+D_a/h.                            (196.1)

     Taking `h` of order `sqrt(D_a)` yields

        P+2N>=3.                                            (196.2)

     Same-line uniqueness gives `P+N=f`, and therefore

        P<=2f-3.                                            (196.3)

802. Every actually absorbed successor uses a distinct strictly positive
     selected line, so its normalized mass satisfies

        A<=P<=2f-3.                                         (196.4)

     If

        C=integral_alpha(p+s-1),

     absorption legality gives `C<=2A`, while the two common marginal moments
     give `C<=A+2(3-f)`.  Consequently

        C-R_beta<=min(4f-6,3)
                 <=1+f-1/4                                 (196.5)

     throughout `3/2<=f<=3`; the scalar envelopes meet at `f=9/4`.

803. Using the exact zero-gap identity

        U(1+)=3-f+C-R_beta,

     equation (196.5) proves the uniform full-line seal

        U(1+)<=15/4.                                       (196.6)

     This completely closes the edge-mass-three, zero-gap mixed-profile
     branch.  It also explains why the local ledger in Section 195 passes the
     absorbed-line test but fails as soon as all plateau lines are restored.

804. Two independent audits found no normalization, sign, zero-level, or
     triple-concurrency defect.  The theorem and audit are
     `FULL_LINE_WEDGE_COVER_SEAL.md` and
     `FULL_LINE_WEDGE_COVER_SEAL_AUDIT.md`.  The remaining analytic problem is
     the quantitative extension to `ell=3-delta`, where (196.1) has a
     `sqrt(delta)` error and the exact positive-gap/common-threshold payments
     must absorb it.

## 197. Quantitative small-deficit full-line seal

805. Put

        ell(1+)=3-delta,

     and retain the exact gap budget `integral z d rho<=delta`.  If `D_a` is
     the number of middle-hexagon points missed by the selected complete
     lines, disjoint plateau edges give

        limsup D_a/a^2<=delta.

     Summing the wedge-slice excesses before applying a cutoff sharpens
     (196.1) to

        P+2N>=3-sqrt(6delta).                               (197.1)

     Hence, with `epsilon=sqrt(6delta)`,

        A<=P<=2f-3+epsilon.                                 (197.2)

806. For `C=integral_alpha(p+s-1)`, absorption legality and the two common
     marginal moments now give

        C<=4f-6+2epsilon,
        C<=3-2delta+epsilon.                                (197.3)

     The exact positive-gap term is controlled pointwise by

        phi(p,s,z)+(4-s)z>=p+s-1.                           (197.4)

     Thus a nonabsorbed seam's gap-plus-lost-saving contribution is at most
     `3z`, while an absorbed seam contributes at most `z`.  The complete gap
     correction is consequently at most `3delta`; the coefficient three is
     pointwise sharp.

807. Optimizing the two affine branches in `f` gives

        U(1+)<=15/4+(5/4)sqrt(6delta)+(3/2)delta.            (197.5)

     Therefore every full-line-realizable profile satisfies `U(1+)<4` when

        0<=delta<delta_0,
        delta_0=((sqrt(29)-5)^2)/24
               =0.0061813303606... .                        (197.6)

     The theorem and two independent audits are
     `SMALL_DEFICIT_WEDGE_SEAL.md` and
     `SMALL_DEFICIT_WEDGE_SEAL_AUDIT.md`.

808. Sections 196--197 close the entire zero-deficit branch and a uniform
     open neighbourhood of it, including positive gaps.  The unresolved
     marked processes now have the explicit bottom-threshold edge deficit

        delta>=delta_0.                                     (197.7)

     Since the pointwise gap coefficient is already sharp, the next progress
     must correlate where missing wedge points, gaps, and plateau lengths

## 198. Scalar-gap survivor, and its exact service closure

809. There is a coherent two-direction middle-order process which survives
     every scalar-gap, complete-line, threshold-contraction, and
     absorbed-lifetime inequality recorded through Section 197.  At every
     `1<c<2` it has

        f(c)=2-c,
        ell(c)=2-c^2/2,
        p=s,
        z=3/2,
        alpha=0,

     and saturates the complete-line coarea identity.  Its scalar seam bound
     has

        inf_(1<c<2) U(c)=U(8/7)=389/84>4.                (198.1)

     The finite realization uses low directed `x/y` fibres, reflected
     cost-`a` high fibres, and `a/2+O(1)` chunks of the negative-negative
     complement triangle.  Directed word fibres may skip geometric lattice
     levels; the earlier proposed reciprocal-Ferrers interval obstruction is
     therefore false and is retracted.  The construction and corrected
     finite audit are `GAP_SERVICE_PROFILE_SURVIVOR.md` and
     `GAP_SERVICE_PROFILE_SURVIVOR_AUDIT.md`.

810. The same finite realization does **not** survive the inherited
     heterogeneous run-cover theorem.  Apart from `O(a)` boundary positions,
     its records have the form

        L_j, S_j, G_j, L_(j+1),                         (198.2)

     where `L_j` is a long internal peak of cost between `a` and `2a`,
     `S_j` is an internal separator peak of cost `a+O(1)`, and
     `|G_j|=a/2+O(1)`.  Assign starts in `L_j` forward to `S_j`, starts in
     `G_j` backward to `S_j`, and starts in `S_j` forward to `L_(j+1)`.
     The three one-sided spans are respectively at most

        3a+O(1), 3a/2+O(1), 7a/2+O(1),                 (198.3)

     and every run receives only `O(a)` starts.

811. The total long-block edge mass is `3a^2/2+O(a)`, the desert mass is
     `a^2/2+O(a)`, and the separators have total vertex mass `a^2+O(a)`.
     Therefore the assignment has

        Q<=(7/2)a^3+O(a^2),                            (198.4)

     contradicting the fan-capped requirement `Q>=(4-o(1))a^3` when
     `D=o(a^2)`.  Finite checks for `a=12,24,40,80,120` approach the
     coefficient `7/2`; the checker is
     `scratch/verify_gap_service_survivor.py`.

812. Thus `389/84` is a genuine counterexample to the **scalar marked
     relaxation**, but not to the three-box theorem.  The previously stated
     missing service-profile lemma is now proved for this extremal template,
     with saving

        389/84-7/2=95/84>53/84.                           (198.5)

     A future arbitrary-order survivor must evade the cyclic three-block
     service operation itself.  The next general target is to prove that any
     coherent full-line packing with linear many long plateaux either admits
     an analogous separator/desert reassignment of cost below `4a^3`, or has
     a quantitatively different transition geometry that pays in the
     complete-line or gap-coarea ledger.

## 199. The three-row rank-strip LP adds no new obstruction

813. A later exploratory LP assigned every short-band cell of lengths one,
     two, and three a rank or a hole and minimized the total hole count.  Its
     reported equality `minimum holes=sigma` for
     `k=11,13,15,17,19,21` is algebraically forced.  If `z_(ell,s)` is the
     normalized mass in physical row `ell` and rank `s`, and `h_ell` is the
     hole mass, then

        sum_s z_(ell,s)+h_ell=(n-ell)/M,
        sum_ell z_(ell,s)=C(k,s)/M.

     Summing the first equations and subtracting the second gives

        sum_ell h_ell=sigma/M                              (199.1)

     at every feasible point.  The exact dual certificate uses multipliers
     `+1` on the row equations, `-1` on the rank equations, and zero on all
     extension inequalities.

814. The LP's one-sided extension cuts are valid rank-profile projections of
     the occupied-band theorem, but exact integer profiles satisfy them in
     all six reported cases.  Therefore the computation proves neither a
     construction nor a stronger lower bound.  Useful leverage requires hole
     locations, both extension directions, the physical join recurrence, or
     pin survival.  The complete audit is
     `RANKSTRIP_LP_TAUTOLOGY_AUDIT.md`.

## 200. Exact two-sided service envelopes and tropical contraction

815. Fix a one-sided span `Lambda`.  An internal threshold run
     `R=[u,v]`, of cost `lambda=v-u`, can serve exactly the left and right
     source intervals

        Omega_R^right=[max(1,v+1-Lambda),u-1],
        Omega_R^left =[v+1,min(M,u-1+Lambda)].              (200.1)

     For a contracted seam `e`, let `kappa_e^right(i)` and
     `kappa_e^left(i)` be the minimum costs of its deleted runs serving `i`
     from the indicated side.  These two functions are the exact service
     state.  When raising a plateau threshold deletes runs `P_j` and merges
     seams `e_j`, the new envelopes are, pointwise,

        kappa_new^epsilon
        =min(kappa_(e_0)^epsilon,...,kappa_(e_s)^epsilon,
             offer_(P_1)^epsilon,...,offer_(P_s)^epsilon). (200.2)

     Thus scalar gaps add ordinarily, while service envelopes compose by
     tropical addition.  Equivalently, the multiplicities of all run offers
     add.  Threshold contraction merely moves a physical run from the
     retained list into a seam; it creates no correction term.

816. Let `q_h(i)` be the minimum of `h` and the cost of every span-`Lambda`
     run serving source `i`.  Choosing a minimizing run, or treating
     `q_h(i)=h` as unassigned, gives

        |S_h|<=sum_i q_h(i)+(2Lambda+h)D.                   (200.3)

     If `C_t` is the union of all source intervals offered by runs of cost at
     most `t`, discrete layer cake gives

        sum_i q_h(i)=hM-sum_(t=0)^(h-1)|C_t|.              (200.4)

     For the three-box middle hexagon, `h=3a-1` and `Lambda=4a+3` yield the
     exact service-volume obstruction

        sum_(t=0)^(3a-2)|C_t|
        <=5a^3+(3/2)a^2-(3/2)a+(11a+5)D.                  (200.5)

     A fractional certificate assigning at most unit mass per source is
     equivalent: its total saving cannot exceed the right side of (200.5).
     These statements were independently cross-audited.  The proof is
     `TWO_SIDED_SERVICE_ENVELOPE.md`.

817. The bookkeeping problem is therefore solved exactly.  What remains is
     geometric: force service volume greater than `(5+epsilon)a^3` in every
     putative subquadratic-defect order, or build a physical order staying at
     or below `5a^3+o(a^3)` while satisfying the complete-line, seam, and
     pinning laws.  This reduction does not assert that the desired strict
     lower bound already holds.

## 201. Consecutive-peak service and the new direction/order bottleneck

818. Let `P_j,P_(j+1)` be consecutive long internal peak runs, with costs
     `lambda_j,lambda_(j+1)` and `g_j` intervening positions.  If their hull
     has one-sided span at most `4a+3`, assign starts in `P_j` to `P_(j+1)`
     and each gap start to the cheaper neighbouring run.  The exact seam cost
     is

        (lambda_j+1)lambda_(j+1)
        +g_j min(lambda_j,lambda_(j+1)).                    (201.1)

     Bad hulls use the universal cost-`2a` assignment.  Shared endpoints and
     word boundaries cost only the explicitly recorded boundary mass.  Span
     alone keeps both endpoint congestions `O(a)`.

819. In a normalized good-seam limit `(p,s,z)` with bad/boundary mass `b`,
     every subquadratic-defect survivor must satisfy

        integral[ps+z min(p,s)]d rho+2b>=4,                (201.2)

     together with

        integral(p+z)d rho+b=3.                            (201.3)

     For a complete fixed-threshold dangerous list, the bad-gap cost can be
     sharpened using the exact deep-gap function rather than the raw `2a`
     fallback.  The theorem and cross-audit are in
     `TWO_SIDED_PEAK_SERVICE.md`.

820. Equations (201.2) and unlabelled complete-line coarea still do not close
     the relaxation.  The diagonal profile

        mu(ds)=2*1_[1,2](s)ds, p=s, z=b=0

     has service moment `14/3` and is statically realized by a family of
     complete parallel lines.  But it is not a physical peak order: two
     consecutive gap-zero blocks on one coordinate cannot both be internal
     peaks.  The next genuinely new theorem must therefore couple **line
     direction to word order**—parallel coarea saturation must create
     valleys/cheap separators or force direction changes.  Another scalar
     moment inequality cannot distinguish this last relaxed survivor.

## 202. Sharp nonabsorbed short-hull service dichotomy

821. Let consecutive dangerous peak plateaux have normalized predecessor
     length `p`, successor length `s`, and strict gap `z`, with

        1<=p,s<=2,  p+s+z<=4.

     If the seam is nonabsorbed, the audited seam-local maximum theorem
     supplies an internal run inside the seam of cost at most `za+O(1)`.
     Assign predecessor-interior starts to the cheaper of this run and the
     successor; assign gap starts to the cheaper neighbouring peak.  The
     leading record cost is

        C_N(p,s,z)=p min(s,z)+z min(p,s).                   (202.1)

     A four-case optimization proves the sharp pointwise inequality

        C_N(p,s,z)<=(4/3)(p+z),                            (202.2)

     with equality only at

        p=s=z=4/3.                                         (202.3)

     All chosen runs have one-sided span at most `4a+3`; shared endpoints
     contribute only `O(a^2)` globally.

822. Split short seams into nonabsorbed and absorbed measures
     `rho_N,rho_A`, and let `b` be normalized bad-hull/boundary mass.  Put

        Delta_N=(4/3)(p+z)-C_N,
        C_A=ps+z min(p,s),
        Delta_A=C_A-(4/3)(p+z).

     The mass identity gives the global assignment bound

        Q/a^3<=4-integral Delta_N d rho_N
                 +integral Delta_A d rho_A+(2/3)b+o(1).    (202.4)

     Absorption requires `p+s<=3`, and exact optimization gives

        Delta_A<=2/3,                                     (202.5)

     uniquely maximized at `(p,s,z)=(1,2,0)`.  Therefore every
     subquadratic-defect survivor must obey

        integral Delta_N d rho_N
        <=(2/3)(||rho_A||+b)+o(1).                         (202.6)

823. At the bottom threshold, if `delta=3-ell`, a bad seam satisfies

        z>(2-p)+(2-s)+o(1).

     Combining line uniqueness near length two with the total gap budget and
     optimizing the split parameter gives

        N_bad/a<=2 sqrt(6delta)+o(1),
        b<=4 sqrt(6delta)+delta+o(1).                       (202.7)

824. Thus all remaining positive excess is localized to exactly three
     sources: absorbed short seams, bad long hulls, or concentration near the
     neutral triple `(4/3,4/3,4/3)`.  The inherited atomic theorem excludes
     mass two at this point, but not every atomic mass.  The exact next theorem
     must jointly charge absorbed positive lines and the bad-hull budget and
     separately resolve the neutral equality case.  The proof and algebra are
     `SHARP_NONABSORBED_SERVICE.md`.

825. The old sharp **scalar** relaxation has a coherent neutral equality
     ledger

        rho=(9/8) delta_(4/3,4/3,4/3), alpha=0, b=0.       (202.8)

     It has edge mass `ell=3/2`, gap mass `3/2`, service cost exactly four,
     and for every `1<c<4/3`

        U(c)=5-3c/4>=4.                                    (202.9)

     Equal direction-line measures on `[-3/16,3/16]` satisfy the unlabelled
     full-line/coarea inequality with slack.  Section 203 below nevertheless
     excludes a physical realization by restoring completeness of the
     dangerous-plateau list.

## 203. Dangerous-list self-closure removes the neutral equality

826. For consecutive `c`-dangerous directed peak plateaux in a nonabsorbed
     seam, the seam-local maximum theorem gives an internal threshold run
     `R` inside the strict seam.  Taking a top-level block of `R` produces an
     internal constant-coordinate peak `Q`.  If `Q` is nondirected, it
     contains a singleton cross-coordinate peak.  If it is directed and has
     cost greater than `ca`, then it is itself a `c`-dangerous plateau lying
     between two allegedly consecutive members of the complete dangerous
     list, a contradiction.  Therefore the seam has an effective run of
     cost

        at most min(g+1,ca).                               (203.1)

     The statement remains valid at shared endpoints, where the seam run is
     already a singleton.

827. The exact physical nonabsorbed saving is consequently

        phi_c^*(p,s,z)
        =min(p,(4-s-z)_+) [s-min(c,z)],                    (203.2)

     rather than the former

        min(p,(4-s-z)_+) (s-z)_+.

     All safe-source, span, congestion, and boundary arguments are unchanged.
     On a short hull the record cost becomes

        C_(N,c)=p min(c,z)+z min(p,s).                     (203.3)

828. At the former neutral triple `(4/3,4/3,4/3)`, any fixed `c<4/3`
     gives a strict additional saving.  The mass-`9/8` ledger has

        Q(c)/a^3<=2+(3/2)c+o(1)<4.                         (203.4)

     Thus it cannot arise from a physical subquadratic-defect middle order;
     it survived only because the scalar relaxation forgot a newly exposed
     dangerous run.  Three independent audits found no maximality,
     shared-endpoint, or list-order defect.  The theorem is
     `DANGEROUS_LIST_SELF_CLOSURE.md`.

829. The remaining broad obstruction is now reduced to absorbed seams and
     bad long-hull mass.  The next optimization must use the strengthened
     `phi_c^*` jointly with direction-labelled positive-line geometry and the
     bad-gap budget at one common threshold.

## 204. Uniform margin removes the entire neutral branch

830. Fix `1<c<4/3`.  On every nonabsorbed short-hull record

        p,s>=c,  z>=0,  p+s+z<=4,

     dangerous-list self-closure gives the cost

        C_c(p,s,z)=p min(c,z)+z min(p,s).

     A complete case optimization, independently audited, proves the sharp
     uniform inequality

        (4/3)(p+z)-C_c(p,s,z)
        >=K(c):=(4/3-c)(2-c)>0.                       (204.1)

     Equality is unique at

        p=s=(4-c)/2,  z=c.                            (204.2)

831. Let `m_N` be nonabsorbed short-seam mass, `rho_A` absorbed short-seam
     mass, and `b` bad-hull/boundary **word mass**.  Put

        E=||rho_A||+b.

     The service lower bound and the absorbed excess `Delta_A<=2/3` imply

        K(c)m_N<=(2/3)E+o(1).                         (204.3)

     Since every short record has `p+z<=4-c`, the word-mass identity also
     gives

        3<=(4-c)(m_N+E)+o(1).                         (204.4)

     Consequently every subquadratic-defect survivor must satisfy

        E>=3K(c)/[(4-c)(K(c)+2/3)]-o(1).              (204.5)

832. At `c=13/12`, (204.5) is the explicit bound

        E>=396/1505-o(1)=0.26312...-o(1).

     As `c` decreases to one, the lower bound tends to `1/3`.  Hence the
     former neutral concentration is not merely excluded pointwise: every
     remaining process must move a positive amount of mass into absorbed
     seams or bad long hulls.

833. This is the current exact frontier.  The remaining theorem must charge
     the mandatory mass in (204.5) against the positive-line/coarea energy
     of absorbed successors and the direction-labelled bad-gap budget at the
     **same threshold**.  The proof is `UNIFORM_SHORT_HULL_MARGIN.md`.

## 205. Independent audit of Fable's full-line-deficit note

834. Fable's `FABLE_FULL_LINE_DEFICIT_RESOLUTION.md` has one valid new
     contribution.  If `gamma_des` is normalized word mass at middle-hexagon
     points outside the selected complete-line union, then

        D_a/a^2=gamma_des+o(1),  gamma_des<=delta,

     and the fixed-bottom wedge calculation sharpens to

        U(1+)<=15/4+(5/4)sqrt(6 gamma_des)
                       +3 gamma_int-(3/2)delta
              <=15/4+(5/4)sqrt(6 gamma_des)+(3/2)delta.    (205.1)

     Hence every profile with

        gamma_des<(1-6delta)^2/150,  delta<1/6             (205.2)

     is excluded.  The gap partition is valid after defining the terminal
     mass to include both linear end gaps.  The level-tension bathtub bounds
     in its Lemma 6.1 are also correct.

835. The note's Theorem 7.1 is not proved.  The baseline change from threshold
     one to `c` is

        3(c-1)+2(e(c)-e(1)),

     not `3c-3+2e(c)`; its derivative `3-2f(c)` may be negative.  Thus
     monotonicity of `delta(c)` and `gamma_des(c)` does not imply
     bottom-threshold optimality, and the claim that no threshold sweep can
     help must be retracted.

836. The proposed scalar extremizer is internally inconsistent.  Under its
     sharp `(2,2,1)` gap interpretation and the crossing equality `C=2A`,
     its total `p+s` moment is at least six, whereas the required moment is
     `6-2delta`.  The two agree only at `delta=0`.  Therefore it does not
     prove sharpness of the six-family relaxation.

837. Fable's Lemma M remains unproved and uses `gamma_cov` inconsistently.
     Its conditional reduction is algebraically valid (with constant `12.5`,
     not `12`, at `delta_1=1/24`), but its claimed uniqueness/minimality is
     obsolete after the stronger self-closed saving (203.2).  The independent
     audit is
     `fable_general_case/FABLE_FULL_LINE_DEFICIT_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT.md`.

## 206. Sharp absorbed/bad bounds and the missing drift coupling

838. If an absorbed seam uses a successor line at normalized positive level
     `t`, then `p<=1+t` and `s<=2-t`.  Exact optimization gives

        g(t):=max Delta_A
        =2/3-t/3-t^2                  (0<=t<=1/3),
         1/3+2t/3-t^2                 (1/3<=t<=1/2),
         4/3-4t/3-t^2                 (1/2<=t<=2/3),
         2/3-t                        (2/3<=t<=1).    (206.1)

     Since the three direction-labelled successor measures are each
     dominated by Lebesgue measure, total absorbed mass `A` satisfies

        integral Delta_A<=3 integral_0^(A/3) g(t)dt
                        <=(2/3)A-A^2/18.              (206.2)
