     multiset and the same lower and upper shadow multisets at every
     certified depth.

979. The smallest two-path relation is a distant-generator commuting
     square.  No Johnson four-cycle gives a decorated depth-one trade.  If
     its four vertices share one lower facet, the two perfect matchings have
     different upper colours; if they share one upper cofacet, the lower
     colours differ; and in the ordinary coordinate rectangle both sides
     differ.  More generally, complete direction matchings inside one fixed
     coordinate cube have disjoint lower families indexed by the unique
     empty free pair and disjoint upper families indexed by the unique full
     free pair.  Equal decorated multisets therefore force identical
     direction multiplicities.

980. The hoped-for adjacent-toggle hexagon does not exist in the two-row
     specialization.  The three boxes containing consecutive labels form a
     poset of width at most two, and the adjacent-swap graph of its linear
     extensions is a path.  Hence every adjacent BK power relation contains
     a fixed move or immediate reversal.  General cactus interval relations
     still supply homotopies between radius-pure paths, but their endpoint
     identities impose no shadow cancellation.

981. Exhaustive inverse-RSK expansion of nested cactus relations through
     `m=6` finds 24,350 distinct spur-reduced path pairs at `m=6` and no
     equal-middle or equal separate lower/upper decoration.  A separate
     search finds no signed cancellation among two or three vertex-disjoint
     BK squares through `m=5`.  These finite statements are not an
     impossibility theorem for larger complexes.  The first viable local
     target is a connected complex of at least three genuinely conjugated
     relation cells whose signed shadow discrepancies cancel at every
     carried depth.  The proof-level negative results and checkers are
     `CACTUS_ABSORBER_AUDIT.md`, `scratch/check_cactus_absorbers.py`, and
     `scratch/search_three_bk_squares.py`.

## 242. Transversal faces: exact packing parameters and an explicit growing range

982. For a perfect matching `P` of `[2m]`, its full transversal cube

        C(P)={X in C([2m],m): |X intersection e|=1 for every e in P}

     has `2^m` vertices.  If `P,Q` are two perfect matchings and `c(P,Q)`
     is the number of alternating-cycle components of the multigraph
     `P union Q`, then exactly

        |C(P) intersection C(Q)|=2^c(P,Q).

     In particular every two full transversal cubes intersect, so their
     packing number is exactly one.  Full matching cubes can cover only
     `2^m/C(2m,m)=o(1)` of the middle layer and cannot be the global mixing
     mechanism.

983. The correct smaller object is an `s`-dimensional matching face: fix
     disjoint selected and excluded `(m-s)`-sets and choose one endpoint
     from each edge of a matching on the remaining `2s` coordinates.  The
     simple hypergraph of all such faces is `2^s`-uniform and has exact
     degree and maximum pair codegree

        D_s=C(m,s)^2 s!,
        Delta_2/D_s=s/m^2.

     For every fixed `s`, the usual almost-perfect matching theorem gives
     a packing covering `W-o(W)`.  These formulas and the full-cube
     obstruction are proved and exhaustively checked through `m=5` in
     `TRANSVERSAL_CUBE_PACKING.md`, its audit, and
     `scratch/check_transversal_cube_packing.py`.

984. The fixed-`s` diagonal can be made explicit.  Fix `0<alpha<1` and put

        s=floor(alpha log_2 log m),       k_s=2^s.

     Corollary 1.5 of Alon--Bollobas--Kim--Vu applies because

        exp(2k_s) Delta_2=o(D_s/log D_s).

     It supplies a matching whose uncovered middle-vertex fraction is

        O(exp(-c_alpha (log m)^(1-alpha)))

     for some `c_alpha>0`.  Indeed `k_s<=(log m)^alpha`,
     `log D_s=Theta(s log m)`, and the logarithm of the ABKV error is
     `-Omega((log m)^(1-alpha))`.  This is a genuine growing-uniformity
     theorem, not an illicit diagonalization of a fixed-uniformity result.

985. The quantitative face packing is still far below the central-band
     target.  Its free dimension is only `Theta(log log m)`, whereas a
     negligible literal tail requires depth `H/sqrt(m)->infinity`.  The
     matching theorem also gives no radius distribution, shadow ledger,
     shifted ordering, or prescribed diversity of coordinate pairings.
     At polynomial `H` its guaranteed error is not `o(W/H)`.  The accepted
     theorem and independent primary-source audit are
     `GROWING_TRANSVERSAL_FACE_PACKING.md` and
     `GROWING_TRANSVERSAL_FACE_PACKING_AUDIT.md`.

## 243. The exact depth-one problem is an orthogonal two-SDR

986. Put `L=C([2m],m-1)`, `M=C([2m],m)`, and
     `U=C([2m],m+1)`.  A depth-one diamond is an interval `(S,U)` with
     `S subset U`; its two middle vertices are the two sets strictly
     between them.  Selecting every lower and upper colour once while
     keeping middle degree at most two is equivalent to finding two maps

        f_0,f_1:L -> M

     such that each `f_i` is an injective extension SDR,
     `f_0(S)!=f_1(S)`, and all unions

        f_0(S) union f_1(S)

     are distinct.  The unions then biject `L` with `U`.  Orienting the
     projected middle edges from `f_0(S)` to `f_1(S)` shows that the desired
     linear forest is exactly the additional condition of no directed
     cycle.  This is the orthogonal two-SDR lemma; it remains open for
     general `m`.

987. If union orthogonality is deleted, the problem is always feasible.
     The rank-`m-1`/rank-`m` incidence graph has maximum degree `m+1`, and
     any two colour classes in a proper Konig edge-colouring give the two
     injective extensions with combined middle capacity two.  Union
     orthogonality turns the second choice into a three-partite matching.
     The natural load matrix is not totally unimodular (a Johnson triangle
     has determinant `-2`), and the maximum-degree-two edge independence
     system is not a matroid.  Thus neither ordinary `b`-matching nor a
     direct matroid-intersection shortcut supplies the missing integrality.

988. Every lower/upper-colour-perfect diamond selection has an exact
     coordinatewise defect law.  If `d(X)` is middle degree, then

        sum_X d(X)=2N,
        sum_(X containing i)d(X)=N,

     where `N=C(2m,m-1)`.  Under `d(X)<=2`, put `delta(X)=2-d(X)` and
     `Cat_m=W/(m+1)`.  Then

        sum_X delta(X)=2 Cat_m,
        sum_(X containing i)delta(X)=Cat_m

     for every coordinate `i`.  Hence the unused endpoint tokens form a
     weighted one-design; an acyclic solution has exactly `Cat_m` path
     components.

989. There is a smallest exact colour-preserving load trade.  Fix a middle
     set `X`, distinct `a,b in X`, and distinct `c,d notin X`.  Replacing

        (X-a, X+c), (X-b, X+d)

     by

        (X-a, X+d), (X-b, X+c)

     preserves both lower and upper colours.  Its secondary middle-load
     change is

        -1_(X-a+c)-1_(X-b+d)+1_(X-a+d)+1_(X-b+c).

     Alternating cycles in the lower/upper incidence graph give the full
     global move language.  The precise missing augmentation theorem is
     that these trades can eliminate every load at least three, and then
     every projected cycle, without creating another obstruction.  See
     `TWO_SIDED_DIAMOND_2FACTOR.md` and
     `scratch/check_two_sided_diamond_ledger.py`.

## 244. The full-conjugate matching-theorem audit

990. The apparent degree `(2m)!` of the ordered-conjugate reservoir is only
     a parallel-occurrence degree.  A length-`2ell` necklace fixes present
     and absent cores of size `m-ell`, so its stabilizer contains
     `S_(m-ell) x S_(m-ell)`.  After equal conjugates are collapsed, the
     ordinary simple degree satisfies, per radius family,

        (m)_ell^2/2 <= D_simple <= 2ell (m)_ell^2,
        log D_simple=(2+o(1))ell log m.

     Therefore, for maximum decorated edge size
     `K=(4+o(1))ell H`, one still has

        K/log D_simple~2H/log m -> infinity.

     Keeping parallel copies creates no matching choices and introduces a
     full-edge codegree that forces the Gould--Kelly parameter to
     `1+o(1)`.

991. Independently, every physical depth-one-certified cycle has exactly
     two nested middle/facet incidences per middle vertex.  Full symmetry
     makes the normalized nested codegree exactly `2/(m+1)` in the ideal
     occurrence system.  Hence the square-root-codegree scale remains
     `sqrt(m/2)`, and on a typed universe of
     `(sqrt(pi)+o(1))W sqrt(m)` vertices the nominal black-box remainder is
     at least `(sqrt(2pi)+o(1))W`.  Larger parallel degree cannot turn this
     into `o(W)`.

992. Two tempting exact-design theorems also do not close the gap.
     For Kuperberg--Lovett--Peled, the natural typed-incidence space has

        dim V >= rank(A)=(1-o(1))W.

     This follows from the trace-rank inequality and the exact middle
     codegrees.  The desired selected size is only `W/R`, whereas KLP
     requires it to dominate `dim(V)^6` even before its integer-basis
     constants.  Keevash's Designs II fixes the template parameters before
     the ambient limit; here the template size is already
     `R=m^(1/2+o(1))`, and its displayed hierarchy plus the unproved robust
     extendability and signed-lattice conditions do not admit this growing
     regime.

993. The theorem audit leaves two honest structural exits: construct
     abundant bounded-overlap multiconjugate packet absorbers, or first
     contract the forced vertical nested chains and match the resulting
     necklace atoms.  No audited general matching/design theorem currently
     supplies either.  The complete calculation is
     `FULL_CONJUGATE_MATCHING_THEOREM_AUDIT.md`.

## 245. The `k=11` cyclic obstruction and the linear low-pair braid

994. Under the saturated short-band ansatz, distinct short-window orbit
     colours make every physical containment strict.  For a cyclic
     42-position quotient with singleton, pair, and triple ranks

        E: 1^1,2^5,3^15,4^21,
        P: 4^9,5^33,

     let `H` be the nine rank-four pair positions.  Every rank-five triple
     lies on an induced positional edge of `H`.  A proper nonempty subset
     of a cycle with `r(H)` runs has only `|H|-r(H)` induced edges, so it
     supplies at most `9-r(H)<9` of the nine rank-five orbit colours still
     needed.  Hence the fully saturated cyclic grading is impossible.  This
     is a real boundary obstruction, conditional on the saturated grading;
     it is not an unrestricted impossibility theorem for every cyclic
     construction.

995. For a linear word of length 465 whose 1,392 short cells are all
     distinct and equal to all ranks one through five plus 369 six-sets,
     let `c` be the number of rank-five triples and

        H={pair positions of rank at most four}.

     Strict containment gives

        |H|=c+2,
        {rank-five triple positions} subseteq E(H).

     If `H` has `r` path components, then `c<=|H|-r`, hence `r<=2`.
     Thus the two boundary units remove exactly the cyclic component
     obstruction.  They permit one or two low-pair runs; exactly two is the
     tight no-jump ansatz, not a forced consequence of equality.

996. A particularly clean saturated row profile is

        singletons: 11 rank1, 55 rank2, 165 rank3, 234 rank4;
        pairs:       96 rank4, 368 rank5;
        triples:     94 rank5, 369 rank6.

     All counts are exact, but this profile is a construction target rather
     than a WLOG normal form.  In its tight two-run realization the 96
     rank-four pair positions give two runs and all 94 internal edges are
     rank-five triples.  Such two runs contain only

        (ell_1-2)+(ell_2-2)=92

     adjacent pairs of rank-five triples, one fewer than the 93 six-sets
     left after the triple row.  Therefore the claim that all 93 remaining
     six-sets receive length-four witnesses has an off-by-one error.  One
     longer witness or a different one-run/no-jump arrangement is required;
     this is not itself an impossibility result.

997. The supplied 42-mask seed is a valid near-certificate only with
     translation voltage `+1` at the quotient seam:

        B_42=tau(B_0), B_43=tau(B_1),

     not literal modulo-42 closure.  Under this convention its 126 orbit
     colours are distinct and its row profile is

        E: 1^1,2^5,3^15,4^21;
        P: 4^9,5^33;
        T: 5^7,6^35.

     It covers every orbit through rank four and 40 of the 42 rank-five
     orbits, missing representatives 157 and 199.  The nine rank-four pair
     positions form runs of lengths five and four, with exactly seven
     induced rank-five triples.  Zero-voltage closure instead creates ranks
     6,7,9 at the seam and misses a third rank-five orbit.

998. Developing the voltage-correct seed through all eleven translations
     gives a valid cyclic 462-term partial object with 1,386 distinct actual
     short OR values, but it misses two entire rank-five orbits, i.e. 22
     masks.  Cutting it and adding three positions is not yet a completion
     theorem.  The proof, qualification audit, and independent verifier are
     `TWO_RUN_BRAID_AUDIT.md` and
     `scratch/verify_two_run_braid.py`.

## 246. Quartet wreath trades give genuine linear pairing freedom

999. Every perfect coordinate matching partitions the middle layer into
     physical cubes by recording its full, empty, and split pairs.  If two
     matchings differ on one quartet by

        ab|cd  <->  ac|bd,

     their cell-overlap components are completely local after fixing the
     common outside full/empty data.  For local selected rank `t=0,4` the
     component is one-versus-one; for `t=1,3` it is `K_(2,2)`; for `t=2`
     it is three-versus-three, with one four-state two-cube and two
     singletons on each side.  The exact outside balance is

        f_0-e_0=2-t.

     Choosing either complete side independently in every component gives
     another exact partition of the middle layer into physical isometric
     cubes.  No middle vertex is lost or repeated.

1000. Partition the coordinates into disjoint quartets, with one leftover
      pair when `m` is odd.  On each local-rank vector one may choose either
      quartet matching independently and take products of the local cells.
      This gives an exact wreath partition whose pairing frame varies
      cellwise over exponentially many rank sectors.  Every hybrid has the
      same vertex-weighted dimension law as a fixed matching:

        E D=m^2/(2m-1),
        Var D=2m^2(m-1)^2/((2m-1)^2(2m-3)).

      Hence all but `o(W)` vertices lie in cells of dimension at least
      `m/2-m^(2/3)`.  A typical middle vertex has `(1/8+o(1))m` quartets on
      which a local resolution switch changes its cell dimension.  This is
      linear matching-frame freedom and lies outside the sparse-pivot
      obstruction, but by itself proves no shadow statement.  See
      `QUARTET_CELL_TRADE.md`, its independent audit, and
      `scratch/check_quartet_cell_trade.py`.

1001. The possible type diffusion is also uniform pointwise after a
      constant catalog of quartet decompositions.  For a random quartet
      partition and fixed `|S|=t`, the number `N_2(S)` of quartets meeting
      `S` twice has exact mean

        floor(m/2) C(t,2)C(2m-t,2)/C(2m,4).

      Uniformly on `||S|-m|<=rho m`, this is at least
      `(3/16)(1-rho^2)^2m-o(m)`.  Permutation bounded differences gives an
      `exp(-Omega_rho(m))` lower tail.  A union bound over all `4^m` subsets
      therefore produces a constant-size catalog, depending only on
      `rho`, such that every target is good in at least one catalog member.
      On any prescribed `o(m)` band one may take the absolute threshold
      `N_2(S)>=m/8` and an absolute catalog size.

1002. Conditional on a good quartet partition, choose independently and
      uniformly among all three perfect matchings on each quartet.  The
      number of full matching pairs in `S` has the exact law

        F(S)=n_3(S)+2n_4(S)+1_(leftover pair subset S)
             + Bin(N_2(S),1/3),

      and variance `2N_2(S)/9=Omega(m)`.  Thus every central target has a
      frame reservoir with the exact `Theta(sqrt(m))` fluctuation scale
      absent from a fixed matching or sparse-pivot cell.  The good catalog
      member and random frame may depend on the target; no simultaneous
      cube partition, source-target coupling, radius ledger, or shadow
      matching follows.  The proof and audit are
      `QUARTET_DIFFUSION_CATALOG.md` and
      `QUARTET_DIFFUSION_CATALOG_AUDIT.md`.

1003. The next viable global theorem is now concrete: couple the exact
      quartet wreath partition with the pointwise diffusion catalog and
      prove one joint frame/cycle selection whose summed two-sided shadow
      omission through `H=sqrt(m)omega(m)` is `o(W)`.  Unlike the old pivot
      program, this target has both exact middle coverage and linear local
      pairing variation; its remaining difficulty is genuinely joint
      integral routing rather than marginal type capacity.

1004. Allowing all three perfect matchings on each quartet strengthens the
      exact wreath statement.  An arbitrary three-choice frame vector may
      be chosen independently on every admissible local-rank sector, and
      the product cells still partition the middle layer.  For a fixed set
      under a uniform sector frame, and dually for a uniform set under one
      deterministic sector frame, the full-pair statistic has the exact
      shifted `Bin(n_2,1/3)` law.  Every deterministic frame function has
      exactly the canonical fixed-matching cell-dimension histogram, not
      merely the same expectation.

1005. There is in fact a deterministic sector-frame choice for which the
      cell containing all but `exp(-Omega(m))W` middle vertices has
      `Omega(m)` free supports that are not edges of one reference matching.
      This is a rigorous integral escape from the sparse-direction premise
      of `PIVOT_SHADOW_CAPACITY.md`; it does not say that a later cyclic
      factor uses those directions in each short window.  The three-choice
      theorem, odd leftover-pair correction, independent audit, and extended
      checker are `QUARTET_WREATH_DIFFUSION.md`,
      `QUARTET_WREATH_DIFFUSION_AUDIT.md`, and
      `scratch/check_quartet_cell_trade.py`.

## 247. Unrestricted rank-depth majorization

1006. Fix rank `r`, put `M=C(k,r)`, `n=M+d`, and choose one short witness
      for every target below rank `r`.  Let

        sigma=dM+C(d+1,2)-sum_(s<r)C(k,s)

      be the exact number of unselected short-band cells.  If `x_j` counts
      selected rank-`r` witnesses of physical width `j`, then for every
      `u>=1`,

        Lambda_(r-u)>=sum_(j>=u)(j-u+1)x_j-sigma.

      Each central witness contributes its proper-suffix chain; distinct
      selected right endpoints make these physical regions disjoint, so a
      hole is charged at most once.  This is a valid unrestricted
      profile-sensitive strengthening of the scalar rank count.

1007. The proposed selected-endpoint elimination is valid but not sharp.
      If `t=min(sigma,d-1,M)`, `v=max(0,t-d+q)`, it gives

        Lambda_(r-d+q-1)>=q(M-t)+C(v+1,2)-sigma.

      Applying the same chain argument to every right endpoint of the short
      band gives the strictly stronger and simpler inequality

        Lambda_(r-d+q-1)>=qM+C(q+1,2)-sigma.

      Thus the selected-endpoint scalar form should not be advertised as a
      new optimal obstruction; the new information is the full width
      profile above.

1008. At least `C=M-sigma` selected central witnesses have maximum width,
      and the monotone endpoint form puts them in one contiguous core.  If
      `C>=d`, simultaneous localization in the `q` shortest prefix and
      suffix cells gives the genuinely two-sided bound

        Lambda_(r-d+q-1)
          >=q(M-sigma)+qd-C(q,2)-2sigma.

      The prefix/suffix strips overlap in exactly
      `qC-qd+C(q,2)` physical cells.  Because each lower target has one
      fixed selected witness, distinct physical selected cells cannot hide
      an additional label overlap.

1009. When `sigma=0`, every short cell is occupied by a different lower
      target and the selected rank-`r` witnesses are exactly

        [1,d+1],[2,d+2],...,[M,M+d].

      Hence equality is rigidly fixed-delay at the interval level, and

        Lambda_(r-d+q-1)>=q(M+d)-C(q,2).

      This still does not force one pure rank per physical row or any upper
      shadow coverage.

1010. In the odd central case, conditional on `sigma>=d-1`, the weaker
      selected-endpoint formula has exact slack `d^2` at `q=d` and
      `q=d-1`.  This arithmetic identity is correct but does not prove that
      all one-sided counting is exhausted: it concerns one functional and
      two depths, while the full-core theorem is already two-sided.  The
      exceptional zero-residual case `k=9,r=5,d=2` also shows that the
      condition is not universal.  The complete audit and checker are
      `RANK_DEPTH_MAJORISATION_AUDIT.md` and
      `scratch/check_rank_depth_majorisation.py`.

## 248. Exact joint face incidence in quartet wreath partitions

1011. Choose a uniform quartet decomposition of `[2m]` (and one leftover
      pair when `m` is odd), then choose one of the three local perfect
      matchings independently in each quartet at a fixed source sector.  The
      induced global frame is an exactly uniform perfect matching of
      `[2m]`: every prescribed global matching has the same number of
      preimages, obtained by grouping its `m` edges into unordered pairs.

1012. Fix a middle source `X` and a lower target `S subset X`, with
      `|X\S|=q`.  The target is the intersection of a physical `q`-face of
      the wreath cell containing `X` exactly when every demanded coordinate
      in `X\S` is paired outside `X`.  Therefore its exact incidence
      probability, and dually the probability for a prescribed upper face,
      is

          p_m(q)=(m)_q (2m-2q-1)!!/(2m-1)!!
                =prod_(i<q) (m-i)/(2(m-i)-1)
                =(1+o(1))2^(-q),

      uniformly for `q=o(m)`.  The apparent
      `exp(-q^2/(2m))` depletion inside a typical dimension-`m/2` cell is
      real, but incidence size-biases successful sources toward cells of
      conditional mean dimension `m/2+q/2+O(1)`, cancelling that loss in the
      global factorial moment.

1013. Same-source codegrees are also exact.  Two lower demands `D_1,D_2`
      have joint probability `p_m(|D_1 union D_2|)`; disjoint demands are
      asymptotically independent for total depth `o(m)`.  A lower demand of
      size `a` and an upper demand of size `b` instead has positive normalized
      correlation `exp(Theta(ab/m))`, caused by direct matching edges which
      satisfy one demand on each side simultaneously.  Arbitrary two-source
      codegrees have an exact local rank-sector formula and cannot in general
      be reduced to Johnson distance alone.

1014. Every deterministic wreath partition has the same dimension
      histogram and therefore covers exactly a `p_m(q)` fraction of all
      nested source--target pairs at depth `q`.  Any universal catalog must
      consequently contain at least `p_m(q)^(-1)=(1+o(1))2^q` members.
      Conversely, `O(m2^H)` independent members cover every lower and upper
      pair through `H=o(m)` with linear deepest-level multiplicity.  Thus a
      polynomial catalog cannot reach `H>>log m`; the central-band scale
      necessarily carries an `exp(Theta(H))` frame reservoir.

1015. This is a prescribed-source face-availability theorem, not an OR
      construction.  A face does not place its directions in consecutive
      cycle order.  Section 249 sharpens the first interpretation: targetwise
      integral face resolution is automatic, so the true missing resource is
      the consecutive-window trace rather than raw face existence.  The
      theorem, audit,
      and exhaustive checks through `m=5` are
      `QUARTET_JOINT_FACE_INCIDENCE.md`,
      `QUARTET_JOINT_FACE_INCIDENCE_AUDIT.md`, and
      `scratch/check_quartet_joint_face_incidence.py`.

## 249. Exact integral face resolution and the ordered-trace gap

1016. The abstract integral resolver is in fact automatic.  In a quartet
      with any of its three matching frames, every local set of rank `s<=2`
      is the intersection of a `(t-s)`-face at every `s<=t<=2`; dually every
      local set of rank `s>=2` is the union of an `(s-t)`-face at every
      `2<=t<=s`.  The same statement holds around baseline rank one in the
      optional leftover pair.  These local extension laws are completely
      independent of the selected frame.

1017. Consequently every deterministic sector-dependent quartet wreath
      partition contains every rank-`m-q` target as the intersection of a
      physical `q`-face and every rank-`m+q` target as the union of a physical
      `q`-face, for every `0<=q<=m`.  For a lower target with local ranks
      `s_j` and block baselines `b_j in {2,1}`, allocate integers

          0<=r_j<=(b_j-s_j)_+,   sum_j r_j=q,

      and use sector `t_j=s_j+r_j`; the positive deficits have total at
      least `q`, and the frame-independent local lemma applies after the
      sector frame is revealed.  Positive surpluses give the dual upper
      proof.  Thus choosing all cells from any one wreath member is already
      an exact disjoint middle partition with zero abstract face deficit.

1018. This does not reduce the ordered OR problem to a catalog selection.
      A physical `d`-cube has

          C(d,q) 2^(d-q)

      lower `q`-faces and the same number of upper faces, but a cyclic order
      of its `2^d` vertices has only `2^d` starting windows.  Its trace can
      expose at most the fraction

          min(1, 2^q/C(d,q)) <= (2q/d)^q

      of its faces.  At `d=Theta(m), q=Theta(sqrt(m))` this thinning is
      exponentially severe.  A constant-frame wreath explicitly has exact
      all-face coverage while the fixed-type capacity theorem still forces
      `Omega(W)` consecutive-window omissions.  Therefore complete integral
      face resolution does not imply deep-shadow coverage.

1019. Mixing two complete cell partitions is componentwise rigid: on every
      nonempty cell overlap the two selection variables sum to one, so each
      connected overlap component chooses one whole side.  Three or more
      systems leave a genuine exact-cover/absorber problem.  The corrected
      general target is now an **ordered trace resolver**: select one exact
      middle partition, a cycle/path factor and direction order in each cell,
      and globally inject almost all lower and upper targets through growing
      depth, with only `o(W)` seams and repairs.  The exact theorem, audit,
      and exhaustive verification of every frame function through `m=4`
      are `QUARTET_INTEGRAL_FACE_RESOLVER.md`,
      `QUARTET_INTEGRAL_FACE_RESOLVER_AUDIT.md`, and
      `scratch/check_quartet_integral_face_resolver.py`.

## 250. Convex-load traps force dimension-dependent alternating cycles

1020. For a lower/upper-colour-perfect diamond matching, put

          Phi=sum_X C(d(X),2).

      If `z` is the number of degree-zero middle vertices, then the exact
      excess law is

          Phi-(2N-W)=z+sum_(d(X)>=3) C(d(X)-1,2).

      A four-diamond rectangle pivoted at `X` keeps its two incidences at
      `X` and replaces secondary vertices `P,Q` by `R,T`; its exact change is

          Delta Phi=d(R)+d(T)-d(P)-d(Q)+2.

      An incidence `XY` can be removed by a rectangle that lowers `d(X)` if
      and only if `d(Y)>=2`.  Hence an overload all of whose neighbours are
      leaves is pivot-locked against rectangle-only repair.

1021. Rectangle descent is genuinely false already at `m=3`.  An explicit
      colour-perfect matching has load profile `3^1 2^8 1^11`, `Phi=11`,
      and all eleven legal rectangles have positive changes
      `1^4 2^5 3^2`.  One alternating six-cycle changes `Phi:11->10` and
      maximum load `3->2`.  Exhaustive enumeration of all `3,013,854`
      colour-perfect `m=3` matchings finds `99,480` overloaded rectangle
      local minima, including `5,160` strict traps; every one has a
      decreasing alternating six-cycle with nonincreasing maximum load.

1022. A universal four-or-six augmentation theorem is also false.  At
      `m=4` an explicit 56-edge matching has profile `3^1 2^40 1^29` and
      `Phi=43`.  None of its 43 rectangles decreases `Phi`, and none of the
      250 directed exchange triangles does so; their minimum changes are
      both zero.  The directed four-cycle on lower rows `(0,1,35,26)` is an
      alternating eight-cycle that changes `Phi:43->42` and maximum load
      `3->2`.  The full matching vector and set-level reassignment are in
      `RECTANGLE_LOAD_AUGMENTATION.md` and are checked independently by
      `scratch/rectangle_load_checker.py`.

1023. The honest surviving statement is the **bounded-order augmentation
      conjecture**: whenever some middle load is at least three, there is a
      maximum-nonincreasing, `Phi`-decreasing alternating cycle using at most
      `m` selected diamonds.  It is exact for `m<=3`, and order four is
      provably necessary at `m=4`.  A deterministic greedy sampler stopped
      as soon as maximum load reached two and solved `100,000/100,000`
      random `m=4` starts, using 1,623 genuine order-four repairs, and
      `10,000/10,000` random `m=5` starts, using 120 order-five repairs after
      all shorter orders failed.  These `m=4,5` figures are evidence, not a
      theorem.

1024. The corrected proof targets are either a pivot-release path lemma,
      where deleted coordinates force an improving return within `m` rows,
      or a negative-cycle duality theorem which shortens a minimum negative
      exchange cycle to order at most `m` using Boolean containment geometry.
      The first-variation half of the second route is already a theorem.
      Weight a diamond `XY` by `d(X)+d(Y)`.  The current matching has weight
      `sum_X d(X)^2`, whereas the uniform fractional matching has weight
      `lambda sum_X d(X)`, with `lambda=2m/(m+1)`.  Their difference is
      exactly `sum_X(d(X)-lambda)^2>0`; integrality of the bipartite matching
      polytope and alternating-cycle decomposition therefore give a cycle
      with negative linear variation.  For its load change `delta`, however,

          Delta Phi=sum_X d(X)delta(X)+(1/2)sum_X delta(X)^2.

      The positive quadratic term is the precise remaining integrality toll;
      negative first variation alone does not pay it.
      Even success would prove only the depth-one orthogonal two-SDR; cycle
      elimination, longer shadows, and pinning remain separate.  The source
      and independent audit/programs are
      `RECTANGLE_LOAD_AUGMENTATION.md`,
      `RECTANGLE_LOAD_AUGMENTATION_AUDIT.md`,
      `scratch/rectangle_load_checker.py`,
      `scratch/rectangle_load_exhaust_m3.cpp`, and
      `scratch/bounded_cycle_load_sampler.cpp`.

## 251. Negative-cycle duality and the sharp finite repair hierarchy

1025. Contract a colour-perfect lower--upper diamond matching to its matched
      rows.  For an exchange cycle `C`, let `delta_C` be its change in the
      middle-load vector `d`.  The exact convex-potential identity is

          Delta Phi(C)=<d,delta_C>+(1/2)||delta_C||_2^2.

      Thus negative linear variation is necessary but not sufficient for an
      exact improvement.  The positive quadratic term is genuinely nonlocal
      and cannot be encoded by fixed arc costs.

1026. There is nevertheless an exact weighted negative-cycle theorem.  Let
      `mu=2m/(m+1)` be the uniform fractional middle load, and let
      `lambda(X)>=0`.  If

          sum_X lambda(X)(d(X)-mu)>0,

      then the matched-row exchange digraph has a negative directed simple
      cycle.  This follows by comparing the current matching with the uniform
      fractional perfect matching and using integrality of the bipartite
      matching polytope.  Taking `lambda=d` yields the positive variance gap
      `sum_X(d(X)-mu)^2`; taking `lambda=1_X` shows that every vertex of load
      at least two can be relieved by some exchange cycle.  Neither choice
      controls the loads created elsewhere or pays the curvature term.

1027. Boolean containment alone gives no short-chord theorem: the
      rank-`m-1`/rank-`m+1` inclusion graph has induced alternating cycles of
      every order `3,...,m+1`.  Exact certificates sharpen this obstruction.
      There are colour-perfect matchings whose first `Phi`-decreasing,
      maximum-nonincreasing exchange cycle has order exactly

          m=3: order 3,
          m=4: order 4,
          m=5: order 5.

      At `m=5` the profile is `3^1 2^166 1^85`; exhaustive enumeration finds
      `169,1203,10148,103282` cycles of orders two through five, with minimum
      exact changes `0,0,0,-1`.  The repairing row cycle
      `(4,44,154,33,24)` changes the maximum load from three to two.

1028. The surviving **diameter-order augmentation conjecture** asks for a
      `Phi`-decreasing, maximum-nonincreasing exchange cycle of order at most
      `m` whenever some load is at least three.  The order bound would be
      sharp in the three certified dimensions.  A proof must control
      curvature, for example by lifting an overload-to-deficit Johnson path,
      using interacting cycle packets, or a state-expanded residual network.
      Even this would settle only the non-acyclic depth-one two-SDR problem.
      The theorem, certificates, and independent checker are
      `NEGATIVE_CYCLE_DUALITY_AUDIT.md` and
      `scratch/check_negative_cycle_duality.py`.

## 254. Per-chain Shearer--Kleitman lifts have an exact Hall no-go

1038. The 24 union-perfect, almost-orthogonal `Q_6` SCD pairs obtained from
      the good `Q_4` seeds cannot be continued to `Q_8` even when each parent
      chain independently chooses either standard lift mode at both new
      coordinates.  This failure is stronger than SAT: drop `Q_7,Q_8`
      orthogonality, drop consistency of mode choices between different
      targets, and let every rank-three lower target independently choose any
      locally attainable rank-five union.  For every seed the resulting
      relaxed candidate graph still has maximum matching only `55/56`.

1039. Each seed has an explicit three-to-two Hall witness of the uniform
      form

          {ab6,c67,c68} -> {abc67,abc68}.

      For example, one seed has

          Gamma(356)={34567,34568},
          Gamma(467)={34567},
          Gamma(468)={34568}.

      Since every genuine shared-mode assignment is a subcase of this
      independently relaxed graph, these witnesses prove unconditional
      union-UNSAT for the stated lift family.

1040. The local cause is a **lift fork**.  Suppose a lower central set `S`
      has successors `S+a,S+b` in the two decompositions.  For `c in S` put
      `A=(S-c)+a+b` and `V=S+a+b`.  If `A` is a singleton chain in one
      decomposition and lies at depth at least two with successor `V` in the
      other, then after arbitrary lifts by new coordinates `p,q`,

          Gamma(S+p)={V+p},
          Gamma(S+q)={V+q},
          Gamma(A) subset {V+p,V+q}.

      Hall therefore fails.  All 84 good `Q_4` pairs are fork-free, whereas
      all 24 present `Q_6` seeds contain a fork.  Thus

          orthogonal + union-perfect + fork-free

      is a necessary strengthened induction invariant, though it is not
      known to be sufficient.

1041. The exact two-stage formulation has 110 mode variables.  One-stage
      orthogonality is 2-SAT; final orthogonality clauses have width at most
      six, and union-collision clauses width at most eight.  Orthogonality
      alone is SAT for every seed, while union injectivity alone is already
      UNSAT.  The authoritative proof is the independently reconstructed
      Hall certificate, not solver output.  A viable inductive construction
      must therefore start from a different fork-free `Q_6` pair or allow
      nonlocal splices between parent chains.  The theorem, audit, and
      checkers are `PER_CHAIN_OSCD_LIFT_NO_GO.md`,
      `PER_CHAIN_OSCD_LIFT_NO_GO_AUDIT.md`,
      `scratch/per_chain_oscd_lift_q6_q8_sat.py`, and
      `scratch/verify_per_chain_q6_q8_hall.py`.

## 255. A fully vertically complete exact wreath factor on `Q_9`

1042. The first vertically defective published MSW dimension nevertheless
      admits a perfect alternative factor.  Fourteen explicit cyclic orders
      on `[9]` have the property that their `14*9=126` length-four cyclic
      intervals enumerate every four-set exactly once.  Hence they form an
      exact middle wreath factor.  The same orders' intervals of lengths one,
      two, and three cover all `9,36,84` lower targets; complementation gives
      complete ranks five through eight as well.

1043. The rank-three multiplicity histogram is

          1^44 2^38 3^2,

      so its support is all 84 triples, while rank four is `1^126`.  The
      depth defects are therefore exactly

          M_1=M_2=M_3=0.

      This proves that the four first-shadow omissions of the standard MSW
      `m=4` factor are representative-dependent, not an obstruction to exact
      wreath factors.

1044. Linearizing each nine-cycle by emitting its nine singleton masks and
      then its first seven again realizes all cyclic intervals of lengths one
      through eight; the first nine positions realize the full set.  The
      resulting 224-entry word is exhaustively verified to cover all 511
      nonzero nine-bit masks.  This is structurally useful but not length
      competitive with the known optimum `nu(9)=128`.

1045. The factor was found by an exact-cover SAT encoding over the 20,160
      cyclic orders modulo dihedral symmetry.  After fixing one wreath,
      12,741 candidates remain; the full-rank coverage instance has 127,284
      variables and 343,768 clauses.  The explicit fourteen-row certificate,
      rather than solver output, is independently checked.  This supplies a
      positive seed for the lossless multiscale wreath-factor route; the open
      step is a switch or recursion preserving vertical completeness.  See
      `M4_VERTICAL_WREATH_FACTOR.md`, its audit,
      `m4_fully_vertical_wreath_factor.txt`, and
      `scratch/verify_m4_vertical_wreath_factor.py`.

## 256. A concrete secondary potential for neutral load-balancing plateaux

1046. At maximum middle load `D`, call a rectangle a relief rectangle when
      it removes an incidence from a current maximum-load vertex.  Let `r_j`
      count relief rectangles of exact `Phi`-change `j`, and lexicographically
      maximize the finite **relief-readiness word**

          R(P)=(r_(2-2D),...,r_(2+2D))

      on plateaux of fixed `Phi` and fixed maximum load.  On the frozen
      strict one-cycle traps, neutral rectangles change the cheapest relief
      cost by

          m=4: 1 -> 0 -> -1,
          m=5: 0 -> -1,

      after which one rectangle strictly decreases `Phi` and lowers the
      maximum to two.

1047. A precise preparation identity explains the statistic.  If a relief
      rectangle `A` with old secondary vertices `P,Q` and new vertices `R,T`
      remains legal after a neutral trade of load change `eta`, then

          Delta_(new)Phi(A)-Delta_(old)Phi(A)
            =eta(R)+eta(T)-eta(P)-eta(Q).

      Thus neutral moves can prepare a prospective relief rectangle one
      secondary vertex at a time.  Common alternatives fail on the exact
      paths: all separable load moments are invariant, assortativity wants
      opposite orientations at `m=4,5`, and edge gradient, leaf counts, and
      overload-to-leaf distance are non-strict.

1048. Rectangles alone do not support the readiness theorem.  An explicit
      `m=4` rectangle-local profile `3^1 2^40 1^29` has nine neutral
      rectangles, all preserving `r_1=1`, and no decreasing triangle.  A
      neutral directed triangle changes the readiness to `r_0=1` and opens a
      later rectangle descent.  Hence the viable bounded move language must
      include directed triangles even on constant-`Phi` plateaux.

1049. The resulting rectangle--triangle readiness conjecture says that every
      overloaded safe rectangle-local matching has either a max-safe strict
      triangle descent or a max-safe neutral rectangle/triangle which lowers
      the maximum or strictly raises `R`.  Finiteness then gives termination
      at maximum load two.  This alternative is proved for `m=3` by the full
      census and has no counterexample in 7,700 deterministic random
      rectangle-local states at `m=4,5`; the latter is evidence only.  See
      `PLATEAU_READINESS_POTENTIAL.md` and
      `scratch/check_plateau_readiness.py`.

## 257. The finite `Q_6` splice neighborhood also has no OSCD escape

1050. After the lift-fork no-go, the complete neighborhood generated by
      cyclic bounded-rank segment rotations and equal-radius upper-tail
      rotations was enumerated around all 24 current `Q_6` pairs.  Each seed
      has exactly four nontrivial generators, all three-chain tail rotations:
      two in each decomposition.  There are no legal two-chain crossovers and
      no bounded middle-segment rotations in this move class.

1051. The four generators commute.  Their 15 nonempty subsets give the exact
      per-seed depth profile `4,6,4,1`; all 360 noninitial occurrences fail
      almost orthogonality before union perfection or fork-freeness can help.
      Each generator has a private two-mask cross-chain intersection witness
      which persists under every subset of the other three generators.  For
      seed zero the four witnesses are

          {45,345}, {456,3456}, {12,123}, {126,1236}.

1052. Thus independent cyclic splices cannot repair the present seeds, even
      when four are composed.  A viable next move must be atomically coupled
      across the two decompositions so that a new double intersection is
      removed as it is created, or must replace a larger path packet by a
      genuinely non-rotational symmetric cover.  The theorem does not exclude
      arbitrary rechainings or unknown fork-free `Q_6` pairs.  See
      `Q6_SCD_SPLICE_NEIGHBORHOOD_NO_GO.md`, its audit, and
      `scratch/search_q6_scd_splice_escape.py`.

## 258. Balanced wreath switches reach full verticality on `Q_9`

1053. For an exact factor `F` of `KG(2m+1,m)` into minimum odd cycles, the
      depth-one colour at a middle vertex `X` is exactly the intersection of
      its two factor neighbours.  If an alternating cycle switch removes
      neighbour `r_X`, retains `h_X`, and adds `a_X`, its complete local
      colour update is

          c_X^- = h_X intersection r_X,
          c_X^+ = h_X intersection a_X.

      Summing the removal/addition histograms gives the exact global shadow
      multiplicity and missing-colour change; no sign is automatic.

1054. No alternating switch of length four or six can preserve a factor into
      cycles of the minimum odd length `n=2m+1`.  Every touched old wreath
      must be cut at least twice, and a minimum odd cycle is induced.  The
      shortest possible move is therefore an alternating eight-cycle cutting
      two wreaths twice.  If their two path-length profiles are
      `{a,n-a}` and `{b,n-b}`, exactness after reconnection is equivalent to

          {a,n-a}={b,n-b},

      together with the two-component reconnection.  This is the exact
      **balanced two-wreath switch**.

1055. Strict missing-colour descent under balanced switches is false.  The
      `m=4` MSW factor has 14 exact switches with first-shadow changes
      `-2^1 0^7 +1^6`; its unique improving neighbour has defect two and no
      improving switch.  At `m=5`, the initial 45 switches have changes
      `-2^3 -1^2 0^22 +1^18`, while steepest descent stalls at defect 25.
      Hence a plateau potential or bounded temporary increase is essential.

1056. The move class is nevertheless strong enough at the first failing
      dimension.  Six explicitly archived balanced switches follow the
      nonincreasing first-shadow trace

          4 -> 4 -> 4 -> 2 -> 1 -> 1 -> 0

      from the MSW `m=4` factor.  The endpoint is independently verified to
      cover every cyclic-interval target at all depths, while its length-four
      intervals still partition the middle layer exactly.  Thus the MSW
      factor and a fully vertical factor lie in the same natural switch
      component.

1057. A second SAT certificate sharpens the local balance.  Requiring every
      rank-three colour to occur at most twice yields a fully vertical factor
      with the forced optimal histogram

          1^42 2^42.

      It has 356,454 variables and 916,516 clauses after fixing one wreath;
      the explicit factor is checked independently.  This balance is stronger
      than mere coverage and may be the better inductive seed.

1058. The general target is now a plateau-aware balanced-switch/absorber
      theorem: route an exact wreath factor so that the summed excess overlap
      through `H=sqrt(m omega(m))` is `o(W)`.  The raw defect cannot be a
      strict Lyapunov function, but the exact move and finite positive path
      are now known.  See `WREATH_SHADOW_SWITCH_AUDIT.md`,
      `scratch/check_wreath_shadow_switches.py`,
      `m4_switch_fully_vertical_wreath_factor.txt`, and
      `m4_balanced_vertical_wreath_factor.txt`.

## 259. A nested Catalan flag and the exact two-coordinate wreath ledger

1059. The original fully vertical `Q_9` certificate contains a literal
      fully vertical flag

          Q_5 subset Q_7 subset Q_9

      with exactly `Cat_2,Cat_3,Cat_4=2,5,14` wreaths.  Deleting coordinates
      `{2,9}` and retaining rows `2,3,5,6,11` gives the distinguished `Q_7`
      core; deleting `{1,3}` there and retaining its rows `2,3` gives the
      `Q_5` core.  At both steps the retained rows are precisely all rows in
      which the deleted pair has maximum cyclic separation.

1060. Exhausting all `36*C(14,5)=72,072` first projections finds exactly two
      exact `Q_7` subfactors, both fully vertical.  Each contains exactly 35
      projected exact `Q_5` flags.  Thus the `Q_7` recursive core is highly
      constrained inside this certificate, whereas the `Q_5` subcore is
      flexible.

1061. For two marked new coordinates at shorter cyclic distance `h` in a
      row on `2m+1` points, the length-`m` windows containing zero, one, and
      two new coordinates have the exact counts

          (m+1-h, 2h, m-h).

      Hence an exact factor with `r_h` rows of type `h` satisfies

          sum_h r_h=Cat_m,
          sum_h h r_h=((m+1)/2)Cat_m.

1062. If `Cat_(m-1)` inherited rows have maximum type `m` and project to an
      old fully vertical factor, the remaining rows have forced count and
      type moment

          sum_(h<m) r_h=Cat_m-Cat_(m-1)
                         =[3(m-1)/(m+1)]Cat_(m-1),
          sum_(h<m) h r_h=(m-1)Cat_(m-1).

      Their mean type is `(m+1)/3`.  Maximum-separation insertion alone is
      therefore impossible: it covers no middle target containing both new
      coordinates.

1063. For `Q_9 -> Q_11`, the clean one-type lift schedule is forced to be

          14 type-five inherited rows + 28 type-two new rows.

      Their zero/one/two-new-coordinate sector totals are exactly
      `(126,252,84)`.  This gives a finite exact-cover target with 252
      inherited insertion candidates, 362,880 type-two candidates, 462
      exact middle constraints, and 561 lower-coverage constraints.  Its
      satisfiability remains open; other mixed type profiles are also
      arithmetically possible.  See `NESTED_VERTICAL_WREATH_FLAG.md`, its
      audit, and `scratch/check_nested_vertical_wreath_flag.py`.

## 252. Orthogonal chain decompositions reduce, but do not solve, depth one

1029. An orthogonal pair of minimum chain decompositions `D,E` gives two
      injective, pointwise-distinct successor maps from rank `m-1` to rank
      `m`.  Their selected Johnson edges enumerate all lower colours and have
      middle degree at most two.  They need not enumerate the upper colours:
      an explicit almost-orthogonal SCD pair on `Q_4` produces only two of the
      four rank-three unions.  Exhaustive enumeration finds 408 unordered
      almost-orthogonal pairs on `Q_4`, of which 324 fail upper injectivity.

1030. If `H_D,H_E` are the middle singleton-hole families and
      `h_D(z),h_E(z)` count holes containing coordinate `z`, the upper-union
      multiplicity defect has the exact first moment

          Delta_z=Cat_m-h_D(z)-h_E(z).

      Therefore upper injectivity requires `h_D(z)+h_E(z)=Cat_m` for every
      coordinate, and the absolute moment defects give explicit lower bounds
      on the number of missing upper colours.  The condition is not
      sufficient: the standard/complement pair on `Q_6` is moment-balanced
      but still has two repeated and two missing upper masks.

1031. The lower successor matching and the dual upper predecessor matching
      are edge-disjoint perfect matchings on their active middle copies.
      Their union is an exact alternating path/cycle packet decomposition;
      for an SCD pair it consists only of even cycles.  Taking one parity
      gives all lower colours and the other gives all upper colours, so this
      is an augmentation scaffold rather than a solution.

1032. Three pairwise orthogonal minimum chain decompositions give an exact
      sparse reduction.  Each lower set has three distinct middle successors
      and therefore three candidate diamonds, obtained by omitting one
      successor colour.  A choice is feasible exactly when its upper unions
      are all distinct and every middle vertex present in all three successor
      images has at least one of its three incidences omitted.  Candidate
      degrees are exactly three on the lower side, at most six per middle
      vertex, and at most `floor(3(m+1)/2)` per upper mask.

1033. Published existence results supply three orthogonal minimum chain
      decompositions for every even dimension `2m>=4`, so the three-choice
      reduction is genuinely all-dimensional.  However, the canonical even
      construction obtained by duplicating each odd-dimensional chain into
      an untagged and tagged copy has a universal Hall obstruction.  All
      `C(2m-1,m-1)` lower masks avoiding the new coordinate have only
      `C(2m-1,m+1)=C(2m-1,m-2)` possible upper masks avoiding it.  The ratio
      is `(m+1)/(m-1)>1`.  For the explicit duplicated `Q_8` triple the
      maximum matching is `42/56`, with a `35`-versus-`21` Hall witness.
      Thus a successful triple must mix the new-coordinate sectors.

1034. A positive finite seed exists.  Opposite Littlewood--Offord lifts of a
      good `Q_4` pair yield 24 union-perfect `Q_6` orthogonal pairs; all 24
      projected Johnson graphs are acyclic forests, and one explicit pair
      enumerates all fifteen upper colours.  The same uniform global lift
      fails at `Q_8`: among 1,152 orthogonal histories none is union-perfect,
      and the best covers 50 of 56 upper colours.  Per-chain lift choices and
      non-product triples remain open.  The full theorem ledger, Hall proof,
      certificates, and checkers are in `ORTHOGONAL_SCD_TWO_SDR_AUDIT.md`,
      `scratch/enumerate_q4_oscd.py`,
      `scratch/check_oscd_product_successors.py`, and
      `scratch/spink_q8_three_choice.py`.

## 253. Fractional protected packets and neutral-plateau escapes

1035. The negative-cycle duality has a simultaneous fractional form.  Let
      `H={X:d(X)>=2}`.  The uniform fractional matching minus the current
      matching decomposes into directed simple exchange cycles; after
      projecting their load-change vectors to `H`, conic Caratheodory gives
      at most `|H|` cycles with positive coefficients whose aggregate change
      is exactly

          mu-d(X)<0                 (X in H).

      Hence every currently heavy middle coordinate can be protected and
      decreased simultaneously at the fractional level.  The missing theorem
      is now precisely an integral compatible packet with controlled
      cross-curvature, rather than existence of improving directions.

1036. The order-`m` strict one-cycle certificates do not rule out a bounded
      local lexicographic descent.  Exact checked paths escape the `m=4` trap
      by three rectangles with

          Phi: 43,43,43,42,

      and the `m=5` trap by two rectangles with

          Phi: 169,169,168.

      The maximum load remains three on the neutral plateau and falls to two
      at the final step.  Thus orders `3,4,5` are necessary for a single
      strictly decreasing cycle in the displayed traps, but neutral
      rectangles plus a secondary well-founded potential remain a credible
      constant-order route.  The `m=3` strict rectangle trap has no neutral
      rectangle and still needs at least a directed triangle.

1037. The load-balancing fork is therefore sharper than the simple
      diameter-order conjecture: either round the protected fractional packet
      while paying the quadratic curvature, or construct a secondary
      potential that decreases along constant-`Phi` rectangle/triangle moves.
      The updated proofs and frozen plateau paths are in
      `NEGATIVE_CYCLE_DUALITY_AUDIT.md` and
      `scratch/check_negative_cycle_duality.py`.

## 260. Boundary--core rigidity at exact rank-count length

1064. Fix rank `r`, put `M=C(k,r)`, `L=sum_(s<r)C(k,s)`, and let `d` be
      the least slack for which

          L<=dM+C(d+1,2).

      If a segment of length `n=q+t` contains witnesses for `q` distinct
      rank-`r` masks, its selected equal-rank intervals are an antichain and
      hence have increasing left and right endpoints.  Every interval of
      length at least `t+1` contains one of them, so the segment contains at
      most

          F(n,t)=tn-C(t,2)

      distinct lower-rank targets.  The exact superadditivity identity

          F(a+b,u+v)-F(a,u)-F(b,v)=u(b-v)+va>=0

      permits this capacity to be combined across deleted-position
      segments.

1065. Consequently, a word of length `M+d+c` covering all targets through
      rank `r` has at most `c` entries of rank greater than `r`.  At exact
      length `M+d`, all literal rank-`r` entries are distinct and occur in
      two (possibly empty) boundary blocks.  Deleting them leaves one single
      contiguous core, every entry of which has rank below `r`, and that core
      alone covers the complete lower ideal.  The proof first rules out a
      repeated literal rank-`r` mask by obtaining total slack `<d`.  If the
      lower entries occupied `s>1` runs, their positive slacks sum to `d`;
      convexity and the `s-1` separating central entries again fit the lower
      ideal at slack `d-s+1<d`, a contradiction.  No fixed derivative row,
      Johnson adjacency, or connectivity ansatz is used.

1066. If `h` is the total size of the two literal rank-`r` boundary blocks
      and `sigma=dM+C(d+1,2)-L`, then

          h<=min(b_r(k)-max_(s<r)b_s(k), floor(sigma/d)).

      For a hypothetical `k=11,n=465` word this recovers the exact
      alternative already known from Items 619--623: either every entry has
      rank at most five, or one endpoint is the unique rank-six entry.  In
      the latter case, deleting it leaves an exact 464-position rank-five
      equality word with a rank-at-most-four core of length at least 331 and
      rank-five boundary mass at most 133.  The non-singleton six-set
      witnesses have at most three physical components.  For
      `k=14,r=7,n=3434`, the theorem gives at most 196 literal seven-set
      entries, all distinct and confined to the two ends, and forbids every
      literal entry above rank seven.

1067. This is a necessary equality normal form, not a sufficiency theorem.
      It does not force upper-rank targets to be hulls of the selected
      central-witness components: an upper target may use a short hole or
      only part of such a component.  When there is no literal rank-`r`
      entry, the core is the whole word, so the theorem does not by itself
      solve the principal `k=11` branch.  The line-by-line independent audit,
      including the odd-dimensional scope condition, is
      `BOUNDARY_CORE_RIGIDITY_AUDIT.md`.

## 261. Balanced-switch endpoint and failure of literal two-symbol insertion

1068. Starting from the `m=4` MSW wreath factor, six balanced alternating
      eight-switches give a nonincreasing depth-one defect path

          4,4,4,2,1,1,0.

      Two further neutral switches reach the forced-optimal first-shadow
      histogram `1^42 2^42` while preserving exact middle coverage and full
      vertical coverage at every other depth.  Thus one natural switch
      component contains both the MSW seed and an optimally balanced fully
      vertical factor.  The independently checked endpoint is
      `m4_switch_balanced_vertical_wreath_factor.txt`; both
      `scratch/check_wreath_shadow_switches.py --regression` and the
      independent all-rank verifier pass.

1069. The literal `Q_9 -> Q_11` lift that preserves each old cyclic row order
      and merely inserts the two new symbols is impossible already at exact
      rank-five coverage.  Exhausting the 1,260 insertion cycles and an exact
      counting reduction force three candidates above every source row and
      a legal omitted packet of three old cyclic triples.  Base 1 forces
      triple 129 to be omitted at base 4, base 11 forces triple 356 there,
      and none of base 4's ten legal packets omits both.  The direct
      certificate and independent verifier are
      `Q11_WREATH_INSERTION_SEARCH.md`, its audit,
      `q11_wreath_insertion_obstruction_certificate.txt`, and
      `scratch/verify_q11_wreath_insertion_obstruction.py`.  This rejects
      old-order-preserving insertion only; reordered, switched, and general
      Catalan lifts remain open.

## 262. Exact rank-bound constant and a fixed-`sqrt(m)` tail tradeoff

1070. The rank-count bound itself has the full asymptotic expansion

          B(k)=W(k)+sqrt(pi k/8)+O(1),
          W(k)=C(k,floor(k/2)).

      Indeed `tau(k,r)<=ceil(2^((k+1)/2))` uniformly, while the loss from the
      middle binomial layer to the next layer is of order `W/k`; hence the
      maximizing rank is eventually central.  At that rank the triangular
      correction divided by `W` is `o(1)`, so

          tau=L/W+O(1)=sqrt(pi k/8)+O(1).

      In particular `B/W->1`, and a uniform estimate plus the exact
      `k<=11` table gives `B(k)<sqrt(2)W(k)` for every `k>=1`.  The decimal
      coefficient `0.626657...` is `sqrt(pi/8)`, not `sqrt(8/pi)`.

1071. The exact shorter two-tail product word of
      `TRUNCATED_IDEAL_PRODUCT.md` admits a fixed-deviation limit.  In
      dimension `2m`, take `r=m-floor(c sqrt(m))`.  If `L_m(r)` denotes its
      exact length, then

          L_m(r)/W(2m) -> T(c),

      where

          T(c)=4(c^2+1/2)e^(-c^2) erf(c)
               +(4c/sqrt(pi))e^(-2c^2)
               +2sqrt(2) erfc(sqrt(2)c).

      This follows from the local coordinate
      `x=(m-2a)/sqrt(m)`, the exact mesh `2/sqrt(m)`, and Gaussian domination
      of the two chain factors.  Direct exact sums through `m=1000` converge
      to the displayed limit.

1072. The derivative

          T'(c)=4c(1-2c^2)e^(-c^2)erf(c)
                -(8c^2/sqrt(pi))e^(-2c^2)

      is negative for `c>=1/sqrt(2)`.  The unique solution of
      `T(c)=sqrt(2)-1` is

          c_*=1.924707427123100...,

      and

          T(2)=0.3298326130736817....

1073. Let `Gamma(c)` be the limsup coefficient of the shortest word covering
      only the ranks within `floor(c sqrt(m))` of the middle of `Q_(2m)`.
      Concatenation with the tail word gives the rigorous tradeoff

          limsup nu(2m)/W(2m) <= Gamma(c)+T(c).

      Therefore the concrete central-band theorem

          Gamma(2)<1.084380949299413...

      would strictly improve the global `sqrt(2)` upper constant.  A
      near-width band word `Gamma(2)<=1` would give the explicit constant
      `1.329832613073682...`.  This is a new quantitative intermediate
      target, not an achieved upper-bound improvement.  The full audit is
      `RANK_BOUND_CONSTANT_AND_FIXED_TAIL_AUDIT.md`.

## 263. Exact iterated boundary--core recursion and its finite blockers

1074. Put `b_r=C(k,r)+tau(k,r)`, `beta_j=max_(s<=j)b_s`, and call `r` a
      strict record when `b_r=beta_r>beta_(r-1)`.  If a word covers every
      target through rank `j` and has exact length `beta_j`, choose the least
      `r` attaining `beta_j`.  Boundary--core rigidity gives

          W=P_r || C_r || Q_r,

      where the two outer blocks are distinct literal rank-`r` entries and
      the single core has entries below `r` and covers the complete lower
      ideal.  If `h_r=|P_r|+|Q_r|`, `g_r=b_r-beta_(r-1)`, and
      `sigma_r=d_r C(k,r)+C(d_r+1,2)-L_r`, then

          h_r<=H_r:=min(g_r,floor(sigma_r/d_r)).

1075. The equality gate is exact:

          |C_r|=beta_(r-1) iff h_r=g_r.

      Only in this case may boundary--core rigidity be iterated at the least
      rank attaining the lower envelope.  If `e_r=g_r-h_r>0`, the strongest
      automatic continuation is rank-excess stability: inside `C_r` at most
      `e_r` entries have rank above that next active rank.  It gives no
      boundary localization.  Under successive saturated gates the word has
      the nested onion form

          P_(r0)||P_(r1)||...||C||...||Q_(r1)||Q_(r0),

      with exactly `g_ri` literal entries in each rank layer.

1076. Exact arithmetic for every `k<20` shows that complete saturation down
      to singleton entries is possible under these numerical cuts only for
      `k<=5`.  The top-down routes, ending at the first impossible gate, are

          6:3!, 7:4->3!, 8:4->3!, 9:4->3!, 10:5->4!,
          11:6->5->4!, 12:6->5!, 13:7->6->5!, 14:7!,
          15:8->7->6!, 16:8->7->6!, 17:9->8!,
          18:9->8->7!, 19:10->9!.

      Here `!` means `H_r<g_r`, not that an optimal word is impossible.  For
      example, the deepest saturated `k=11` branch has layer masses
      `h_6=1,h_5=133,h_4<=100`; its remaining rank-at-most-three core has
      length at least 231.  Since `100<165=g_4`, it cannot be another exact
      rank-count core.

1077. There is no contradiction to `nu(k)=B(k)`: every equality word may use
      smaller boundary mass, including zero.  The archived exact words for
      `k=8,9,10,12` in fact have zero literal mass at their active record
      ranks, so the saturated onion is not the construction mechanism in the
      known cases.  The proof, full record table, equality-condition audit,
      and exact checker are `ITERATED_BOUNDARY_CORE_RIGIDITY.md`, its audit,
      and `scratch/check_iterated_boundary_core_rigidity.py`; the checker
      exhaustively reconfirms the four certificate coverages and returns
      `PASS`.

## 264. A `1.24714` fixed-frame barrier inside the `2sqrt(m)` band

1078. Fix a perfect matching `P` of the `2m` coordinates and let `F(S)` be
      the number of matching edges contained in `S`.  The exact type counts
      for middle sets and rank-`m-q` targets are

          V_g=m! 2^(m-2g)/(g!^2 (m-2g)!),
          T_(f,q)=m! 2^(m-2f-q)/(f!(f+q)!(m-2f-q)!).

      In one fixed-pair cube cell every vertex has the same full-pair type,
      and the intersection of any family of cell vertices has that same
      type.  Hence a cellwise middle row containing all middle sets once and
      `R` repeats can expose at most

          sum_g min(T_(g,q),V_g)+R+qb

      distinct lower depth-`q` shadows, where `b` is the number of
      contiguous cell blocks.  The `qb` term generously credits every
      boundary-crossing `(q+1)`-window.  Natural fixed-cell and wreath-scale
      traversals have `b=o(W/sqrt(m))`.

1079. At `q=floor(c sqrt(m))`, the complete exact type-overlap sum has the
      limit

          [N_q-sum_g min(T_(g,q),V_g)]/W
             -> delta(c)
              =e^(-c^2)Phi(c/2)-Phi(-3c/2).

      The two type laws have common asymptotic variance `m/16`, their means
      differ by `(c/2)sqrt(m)`, and their local densities cross at target
      coordinate `x=c/8`.  The unique maximizer on `0<=c<=2` is

          c=0.613426084927899...,
          delta_*=0.247141309562647....

      Repeated middle states can remove at most one hole each, and literal
      insertion of the remaining holes pays the balance.  Therefore every
      fixed-frame cell trace plus literal repair has length at least

          (1.247141309562646-o(1))W.

      In particular it cannot establish the target
      `Gamma(2)<1.084380949299413`.  This is scoped to one fixed matching and
      `o(W/sqrt(m))` cell boundaries; positive-density frame changes or
      cross-cell routing remain outside it.

      More quantitatively, if repeats plus literal repair use the entire
      allowed overhead `0.084380949299413W`, the missing capacity must be
      supplied by at least

          (0.341806889960-o(1))W/sqrt(m)

      cell boundaries.  Thus a successful frozen-frame escape would have to
      switch on mesoscopic blocks of average length at most
      `2.92563sqrt(m)`; wreath-scale `Theta(m)` blocks have too few seams.
      In particular, a cyclic pair-flip block geodesic through
      `2sqrt(m)` has length greater than `4sqrt(m)` and is already too long
      to meet this necessary seam density.

1080. The fixed-depth block proof also does not become uniform merely by
      putting `J=2sqrt(m)`.  A proportionally decorated `R`-state block must
      carry

          (sqrt(pi) erf(2)+o(1)) R sqrt(m)

      middle and two-sided shadow vertices.  Since geodesicity needs
      `R>4sqrt(m)`, its uniformity is larger than `7.05m+o(m)`.  A middle
      vertex and one fixed facet have relative block codegree at least
      `2/m`, leaving `r Delta_2/D=Theta(1)` at the projective-plane scale.
      This is a rigorous failure of the existing fixed-uniformity black box,
      not a nonexistence theorem for a special growing matching.

1081. Likewise, abstract quartet face resolution is quantitatively
      insufficient for local ordered routing.  A `d`-cube has
      `C(d,q)2^(d-q)` lower `q`-faces but one cyclic trace has only `2^d`
      starts, so cellwise resolution needs at least `C(d,q)/2^q` traces.
      At typical `d~m/2` and `q~sqrt(m)`, its logarithm is
      `(1/2+o(1))q log m`; no constant or polynomial per-cell catalog closes
      this gap.  Cross-cell target reassignment is not excluded.  The proof,
      scope audit, exact finite type sums, and optimizer are
      `CENTRAL_BAND_1084_ATTACK.md`, its audit, and
      `scratch/check_central_band_1084.py`.

## 265. Boundary--core pin coupling and upper-shadow inheritance

1082. In the exact boundary--core decomposition at active rank `r>=2`, the
      lower core contains a witness for every singleton and therefore has
      total OR `[k]`.  No proper-mask witness can touch both active-rank
      boundary blocks.  At a fixed left boundary endpoint the crossing ORs
      form an inclusion chain, and the analogous statement holds at a fixed
      right endpoint.  If the total boundary mass is `h`, the core therefore
      misses at most `h` masks in each proper rank and at most

          h(k-r)+1

      nonempty masks in total.  When `h=1`, every loss belongs to one nested
      endpoint chain, with at most one loss in each rank.

1083. Pin survival is exact on the peeled boundary:

          Z_b intersect boundary = {i : b in A_i}.

      For a left crossing, the complement of its OR factors as

          D_i intersect E_j,

      where `D_i` is the nested chain of coordinate deficits of boundary
      suffixes and `E_j` is the nested chain of deficits of core prefixes.
      Thus every crossing family has a two-threshold rectangle structure;
      this is a genuinely coordinate-sensitive restriction, not another
      scalar rank count.

1084. In the hypothetical `k=11,n=465` branch with one endpoint six-set,
      deleting that endpoint leaves a 464-entry core covering at least
      `2041/2047` nonzero masks.  Its possible six losses form one nested
      chain, with at most one loss in each of ranks six through eleven.

1085. A surplus version also controls the principal no-six-set branch.
      Delete all literal five-set entries from the 465-word.  The remaining
      rank-at-most-four positions form at most two components.  If there are
      two, the deleted five-set occurrences are all distinct, one component
      has total OR `[11]`, and the component slacks are `{1,2}`.  The
      slack-one component is an exact adjacent-pair rank-five path: all of
      its adjacent pairs are distinct five-sets, and every lower target it
      covers is literal.

1086. These are lossless equality branches, not existence or impossibility
      proofs.  A coordinate-complete component need not itself be universal,
      and a six-mask nested completion of the 464-core remains arithmetically
      possible.  Full proofs, independent audits, and exact-certificate
      regressions are `BOUNDARY_CORE_PIN_COUPLING.md`, its audit, and
      `scratch/check_boundary_core_pin_coupling.py`.

## 266. Amortized subcube density and globally shared long-window credit

1087. Fix a rank `r`, put `M=C(k,r)` and `d=n-M>=1`, and for each `r`-set
      `R` let

          P_R={i:A_i subseteq R},  p_R=|P_R|,

      while `q_R` counts the physical length-`d+1` intervals whose OR is
      exactly `R`.  The already-audited containment-multiplicity lemma says
      that an interval of OR-rank `s` has length at most

          d+C(s,r).

      Hence every `P_R`-run has length at most `d+1`, and its length is
      `d+1` exactly when it is one of the `q_R` intervals.  This containment
      statement is the earlier Section 169 theorem; it is an input, not a
      new result here.

1088. Put

          c_(r,d)=ceil(2(2^r-1)/(d+1)).

      Counting the short intervals inside the `P_R`-runs, with one unit of
      globally accountable credit for each long run, proves the unrestricted
      local and global inequalities

          p_R+q_R >= c_(r,d),
          sum_R q_R <= M,
          sum_R (c_(r,d)-p_R)_+ <= M.

      Thus for every integer `j>=1`, at most `M/j` of the `r`-sets can have
      `p_R<=c_(r,d)-j`.  Double counting `(i,R)` with `A_i subseteq R` also
      gives the general rank-moment cut

          sum_i C(k-|A_i|,r-|A_i|) >= (c_(r,d)-1)C(k,r).

      The novelty is the shared `q_R` credit and the resulting deficiency
      distribution; previous local subcube estimates paid for long windows
      separately.

1089. At the open checkpoint `k=11,n=465,r=6`, one has `d=3` and `c=32`,
      so

          sum_U (32-p_U)_+ <= 462

      and

          252n1+126n2+56n3+21n4+6n5+n6 >= 14322.

      The scalar `14322` improves the earlier standalone density comparator
      `12936`, but it is redundant after the cumulative entry-rank truncation
      cuts are imposed: those already force this moment to be at least
      `18866`, with minimizing rank vector `(11,45,110,165,133,1)`.  The new
      `k=11` information is therefore the individual six-subcube lower-tail
      law, not the aggregate comparator alone.

1090. Equality in the general moment cut forces every length-`d+1` window
      to have rank `r` and `p_R+q_R=c` for every `R`; it does not generically
      force those window values to be distinct.  The `k=11,r=6,d=3` branch
      is exceptionally rigid.  A support with `q_U=2` cannot partition its
      remaining 22 positions into the only tight run length three, so the
      global average forces

          q_U=1,  p_U=31

      for every six-set `U`.  Every support then has the unique run multiset
      `{4,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3}`, and the 462 length-four windows enumerate all
      462 six-sets exactly once.  Thus the fixed-delay rank-six row is forced
      on this tight moment branch, but not on every hypothetical 465-word.
      The proof and independent audit are
      `AMORTIZED_SUBCUBE_DENSITY_THEOREM.md` and
      `AMORTIZED_SUBCUBE_DENSITY_AUDIT.md`.  The optional scalar SAT
      comparator has been raised from `12936` to `14322` without changing its
      59,036-variable/280,226-clause inventory; the deterministic build-only
      regression is `K11_FOREST_AMORTIZED_DENSITY_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.  The
      stronger distributional inequality is not yet encoded.

## 267. Parent-packet obstruction to literal Catalan wreath lifts

1091. Consider a parent-preserving lift of an arbitrary exact middle wreath
      factor from `Q_(2m-1)` to `Q_(2m+1)`: every new cyclic row is obtained
      by inserting the two new coordinates into one old row.  Unique ownership
      of the zero-new and one-new target sectors forces each old parent to
      have exactly

          q_m=2(2m-1)/(m+1)=4-6/(m+1)

      children.  Therefore such a lift is possible only for

          m in {1,2,5}.

      This is independent of which old exact factor is chosen, how its rows
      are ordered, or which balanced-switch representative is used before
      lifting.  A parent-preserving two-coordinate insertion cannot be an
      all-dimensional induction.

1092. More precisely, children over each parent must form a saturated packet:
      their zero-new windows enumerate that parent's old length-`m` intervals,
      and each tagged one-new sector enumerates its length-`m-1` intervals.
      The global lift is exact if and only if the two-new exports of all
      saturated packets partition the old `(m-2)`-sets.  This packet-gluing
      equivalence identifies the exact freedom that cross-parent splicing or
      genuinely new rows must replace.

1093. The first open Boolean transition `Q_9 -> Q_11` is the exceptional
      integral case `m=5`, with exactly three children per parent.  Exhaustive
      local enumeration leaves precisely six saturated packets; their three
      omission phases are

          036, 147, 258,

      each with two insertion realizations.  Thus the fully flexible
      parent-preserving question is equivalent to finding any exact 14-row
      `Q_9` factor and one phase per row such that the six retained cyclic
      triples per row partition all 84 triples.

1094. The exact exceptional-case CNF has 362,697 variables and 991,125
      clauses.  Current exact and balanced-switch searches reached neither
      SAT nor UNSAT, so no `Q_11` certificate follows.  The general theorem
      does not obstruct cross-parent switches after lifting or new rows; it
      proves those freedoms are necessary outside `m=1,2,5`.  The proof,
      independent audit, search, and exhaustive local checker are
      `FLEXIBLE_CATALAN_WREATH_LIFT.md`, its audit,
      `scratch/search_flexible_q9_q11_lift.py`,
      `scratch/search_q9_switch_liftable.py`, and
      `scratch/verify_flexible_catalan_wreath_lift.py`.

## 268. Rank-filtration stability and the Rayleigh onion law

1095. For a word of length `beta_r(k)+c` covering every target through rank
      `r`, let `h_r` count entries above rank `r` and let `delta_r` count
      duplicate literal rank-`r` occurrences after one copy of each distinct
      value is retained.  Deleting all high entries and those duplicate
      copies preserves the complete truncated ideal.  If `s_r` is the number
      of nonempty rank-below-`r` components in that canonical reduction, the
      sharp unrestricted stability inequality is

          h_r+delta_r+s_r-1 <= c.

      Restoring the deleted positions gives the original-word component law

          kappa_r(A) <= n-beta_r(k)+1.

      The proof assigns all nonliteral rank-`r` witnesses to the low
      components, applies the exact segment capacity
      `F(q,t)=tq+C(t+1,2)`, and uses convexity plus the `s_r-1` necessary
      separators.  It assumes no prescribed witness row or grading.

1096. At exact rank-specific equality (`c=0`), no entry is above rank `r`,
      all literal rank-`r` entries are distinct, and they form two boundary
      blocks around one lower-ideal core.  If their total mass is `z`, then

          z <= min(beta_r-max_(s<r)beta_s, floor(sigma_r/d_r)).

      This forces one exact peel only.  A recursive exact onion requires
      `z` to equal the complete next-record gap, as in Section 263; with
      smaller boundary mass the core has positive excess and only the new
      stability/component budget is available.

1097. Rank truncation and coordinate restriction admit the joint transform

          sum_(s=1)^r a_s C(k-s,ell-s)
              >= C(k,ell) nu_(<=r)(ell)
              >= C(k,ell) beta_r(ell)

      for every `1<=r<=ell<=k`.  It follows by retaining, for each `ell`-set
      `Y`, exactly the entries of rank at most `r` contained in `Y`, and then
      summing over `Y`.

1098. In even dimension `k=2m`, any near-width word
      `n=(1+o(1))C(2m,m)` has the Rayleigh-type lower tail

          P((m-|A_I|)_+ >= x sqrt(m)) >= exp(-x^2)-o(1)

      for every fixed `x>=0`; the correct finite rounding is
      `q=ceil(x sqrt(m))`.  Hence the mean positive deficit is at least
      `(sqrt(pi)/2+o(1))sqrt(m)`.  Simultaneous stability also gives

          kappa_(m-q)=O((epsilon_m+(q+1)^2/m)W)

      for `q=o(sqrt(m))`.  The Rayleigh law is an interpretation of the
      cumulative rank cuts; the component hierarchy is the additional
      ordered information.  “Onion” means nested level sets with controlled
      component budgets, not literal boundary shells at every rank.

      Two full-scale corollaries are

          liminf E[(D_m/sqrt(m))^p] >= Gamma(1+p/2)       (p>0),
          limsup kappa_(m-ceil(x sqrt(m)))/W <= 1-exp(-x^2).

      These are respectively a moment lower bound and a component-profile
      upper bound; neither asserts convergence to a Rayleigh distribution.

1099. At the hypothetical `k=11,n=465` equality there are exactly two WLOG
      architectures.  Either one literal six-set occurs at an endpoint and
      deleting it leaves an exact 464-position rank-five boundary/core word,
      with at most 133 literal five-set boundary entries; or there is no
      literal six-set, every entry has rank at most five, the total duplicate
      excess `delta5` among literal five-sets and the physical rank-at-most-
      four component count `kappa5` satisfy `delta5+kappa5<=2` (at least 331
      positions, hence at most 134 rank-five entries).  Thus a duplicate
      forces one physical low component.  The corrected theorem and
      independent audit are `RANK_FILTRATION_STABILITY.md` and
      `RANK_FILTRATION_STABILITY_AUDIT.md`.

## 269. Exact subcube run-credit envelope

1100. The linear amortized support theorem can be sharpened without any new
      structural hypothesis.  For an `r`-set support of size `p` with exactly
      `q` runs of maximum length `d+1`, let `F_d(p,q)` be the maximum number
      of internal intervals of length at most `d`.  Writing

          p-q(d+1)=ad+b,  0<=b<d,

      convexity gives the exact closed form

          F_d(p,q)=q d(d+3)/2+a d(d+1)/2+b(b+1)/2.

      If `gamma_(r,d)(p)` is the least `q` for which this capacity covers all
      `2^r-2` proper targets and, when `q=0`, the target itself, then every
      universal word satisfies

          q_R>=gamma_(r,d)(p_R),
          sum_R gamma_(r,d)(p_R)<=C(k,r).

1101. There is a second independent residual budget.  If `sigma` is the
      number of unused cells after one witness for every lower target is
      selected in the width-`d` band, exact multiplicity accounting gives
