          sum_R (gamma_(r,d)(p_R)-1)_+ <= sigma.

      Indeed, if `z` rank-`r` values are missing from the length-`d+1` row,
      `H` row windows have higher rank, and `D` is the number of duplicate
      rank-`r` row occurrences, then `D=z-H<=z<=sigma`.

1102. At `k=11,n=465,r=6`, the exact charge table is

          p:       28 29 30 31 >=32
          gamma:    7  5  3  1   0.

      Therefore

          7a28+5a29+3a30+a31 <= 462,
          6a28+4a29+2a30     <= 369.

      In particular at most 61 six-subcubes have support 28, at most 92 have
      support at most 29, and at most 154 have support at most 30.  Inside
      the exact boundary/core split the proper-target version has the same
      active table and gives right side `462-h_6`, namely 462 in the no-six
      branch and 461 in the endpoint-six branch, with no support-31 interface
      exception.

1103. The unrestricted solver now has an exact optional guard
      `K11_FOREST_SUBCUBE_DEFICIENCY=1`.  It defines all 462 by 465 support
      indicators, exact Wallace population counts, charge bits, and both
      global comparisons.  It adds 646,781 variables and 4,309,410 clauses;
      the circuit and guard-off stream identity pass independent checks.
      The proof, audit, implementation note, and checkers are
      `EXACT_SUBCUBE_RUN_CREDIT.md`, its audit,
      `K11_FOREST_SUBCUBE_DEFICIENCY_IMPLEMENTATION.md`,
      `scratch/check_exact_subcube_run_credit.py`, and
      `scratch/verify_k11_subcube_run_credit_encoding.py`.

## 270. Simultaneous multirank amortization

1104. All subcube supports at all ranks are one Boolean zeta transform:

          p_R=sum_(nonempty S subseteq R) x_S,

      where `x_S` is the entry multiplicity.  Credit families whose binomial
      layers have the same size use the same physical window row, so their
      total credit is bounded jointly by that row length.  The simultaneous
      containment cap also makes a nominal credit rank dead whenever its
      prescribed row length exceeds the best cap for that rank; then the
      support lower bound is pointwise with no long-window credit.

1105. Summing a rank-`r` support/credit law inside an `s`-set `T` gives the
      local incidence inequality

          C(s,r)c_r <=
              sum_(i:A_i subseteq T) C(s-|A_i|,r-|A_i|)
              +W_(ell_r)(T),

      where the last term counts length-`ell_r` windows contained in the
      physical support of `T` and vanishes for a dead row.  Its one-number
      projection is valid but is dominated, for every `k<20`, by the existing
      nested cap-and-run bounds.

1106. Exact rational checks of the common-zeta, shared-row, containment,
      cumulative rank-filtration, and coarse row-rank constraints reject no
      proposed `B(k)` for `k<20`; symmetric fractional certificates also pass
      at `k=20,25,50,100,200`.  From `k=5` through 200 only the upper-central
      and full-set credit rows remain live.  The zero-boundary profiles used
      by the checker are voluntary feasible certificates: rank-filtration
      stability permits distinct active-rank boundary literals and does not
      force their mass to zero.

1107. The sole raw scalar strengthening checkpoint is `k=6`: residual zero
      forces the 21 entries to be exactly the six singleton and fifteen pair
      masks, and all twenty adjacent ORs enumerate the third layer.  In open
      dimensions the symmetric multirank relaxation remains feasible, so the
      next obstruction must use non-symmetric inclusion correlations,
      physical ordering, or coordinate pins.  The theorem, corrected audit,
      and exact checker are `MULTIRANK_AMORTIZATION.md`, its audit, and
      `scratch/check_multirank_amortization.py`.

## 272. Laminar pin-capacity coupling

1112. Rank-filtration component capacity and coordinate pin eligibility obey
      one joint Hall inequality.  At rank `r`, let `C` range over the physical
      components of entries below rank `r`; let `K_C` be the exact
      side-capacity obtained after assigning nonliteral rank-`r` witnesses to
      `C`; and let `D_C` be the set of coordinates absent from every entry of
      `C`.  Then for every lower-target family `F`,

          |F| <= sum_C min(K_C,
                    |{S in F : S intersect D_C is empty}|).

      This is strictly stronger than imposing total interval capacity and
      total coordinate coverage separately, because both resources must be
      supplied by the same components.  Fixed-pin families and averaging give
      an explicit hierarchy of coordinate-load and moment inequalities.

1113. The component systems at successive ranks form one exact laminar pin
      forest.  If `P` is a component below rank `r+1`, its rank-`r` children
      are `C`, and `E_r(P)` is the set of literal rank-`r` positions in `P`,
      then

          D_P=(intersection_C D_C)
              intersection (intersection_(i in E_r(P)) ([k] minus A_i)).

      The coordinates newly supplied at these merges have total cardinality
      at most `r a_r`, where `a_r` is the number of literal rank-`r` entries.
      Thus per-rank component profiles cannot choose their coordinate deficits
      independently.

1114. Combining the Hall law with rank-filtration stability gives two useful
      structural consequences.  If the canonical reduced component count is
      below `r`, one component is coordinate-complete.  Its convex hull in the
      original word has OR `[k]`, is a separator for proper witnesses, and
      misses at most one mask per outside endpoint in every proper rank.  A
      component with interval slack one is completely rigid: all adjacent
      pairs are distinct rank-`r` witnesses and every lower value represented
      there is literal.

1115. An independent checker reconstructs all exact stored certificates for
      `2<=k<=10` and `k=12` and passes every component capacity, fixed-pin,
      merge, and erosion identity.  The theorem changes no numerical bound by
      itself.  The next exact task is to optimize these Hall minima jointly
      with the entry-rank and merge-erosion budgets and extract a small
      nonredundant `k=11` circuit.  The proof, audit, and checker are
      `LAMINAR_PIN_CAPACITY_THEOREM.md`, its audit, and
      `scratch/check_laminar_pin_capacity.py`.

## 273. All-radius selective triangular portal braid

1116. The triangular arm--peak problem admits an unconditional selective
      two-level recursion.  Peak occurrences are typed zero or one; a
      type-zero peak supplies the zero pin after folding, while a type-one
      peak selectively lifts to the height-one member of its fold fibre.  A
      diagonal prefix, a decreasing outer-row/peak scaffold, the letterwise
      lift of the radius-`R-2` word, and one type-one supplement for each even
      peak form a braidable word at radius `R`.

1117. The four exact witness classes are `x=0`, `r=R`, `u=0`, and the
      shifted interior class.  They prove spanning, every target, and
      preservation of the typed invariant.  The exact length recurrence is

          n_R=n_(R-2)+3R+1+floor(R/2),

      with solutions

          n_(2t)=(7t^2+9t+2)/2,
          n_(2t+1)=(7t^2+15t+4)/2.

      Hence

          g_triangle(R)<=7R^2/8+O(R),
          rho(R)<=3R^2/8+O(R).

      The independent verifier checks the alphabet, exact lengths, all
      targets, and typed-compatible witnesses for every `0<=R<=50`.

1118. In the balanced four-box tail-provider ledger, a quadratic triangular
      coefficient `rho(R)<=cR^2+O(R)` produces ratio `1+2c`.  The new braid
      therefore gives `7/4`, not a new global bound because `7/4>sqrt(2)`.
      Terminal deletion of the outermost diagonal and supplements improves
      only lower-order terms.  Central-square compatibility, reflected-meet
      factorization, a linked interval band, coordinate pins, and uniform
      thick unequal boxes remain unproved.

1119. Literal reuse of the copied diagonal is blocked inside the current
      witness-preserving recursion: inserting the next outer scaffold at its
      crossing cut contaminates inherited `u=0` witnesses.  Removing that
      `R` term requires a distributed portal invariant, witness reselection,
      or multilevel fusion.  Recolouring lifted peaks can reduce supplements
      experimentally, but has no all-radius theorem.  The construction,
      audit, impact ledger, and checkers are
      `ALL_RADIUS_TRIANGULAR_PORTAL_BRAID.md`, its audit,
      `ALL_RADIUS_SELECTIVE_BRAID_FOUR_BOX_IMPACT.md`, and the two scripts in
      `scratch/` named there.

## 274. Complete endpoint-blocker barrier

1120. Let nonnegative target weights have total at most one on every
      inclusion chain.  If `Theta` is their total weight and a physical
      interval has OR `T`, endpoint-fibre chain capacity gives the exact
      fractional containment cap

          |J|<=n-Theta+sum_(S subseteq T)x_S.

      For a fixed target `T`, Dilworth shows that the strongest such excluded
      weight is the width of

          P_T={nonempty S:S not subseteq T}.

1121. If `|T|=s`, product normality and the central-rank comparison give

          width(P_T)=W-C(s,r),
          r=ceil(k/2), W=C(k,r).

      Thus the exact optimal cap is

          lambda_n(k,s)=n-W+C(s,r)   (s<k),
          lambda_n(k,k)=n.

      This includes arbitrary non-level antichains and all fractional
      chain-feasible blockers.

1122. Aggregating every optimal targetwise cap through every nested Hall row
      still gives exactly

          H(k)=B(k)=C(k,ceil(k/2))+tau(k,ceil(k/2)).

      In particular, the upper central rank always maximizes the rank-count
      lower bound.  The arbitrary-antichain barrier follows for every `k`,
      more strongly than the initial range-specific LYM proof.  Exact checks
      verify actual Dilworth widths through `k=7` and the Hall collapse through
      `k=200`.

1123. Therefore every scalar strategy of the form “one endpoint-chain
      blocker -> targetwise length cap -> nested short-interval Hall count”
      is closed at `B(k)`, even with bounded-height families, fractional
      weights, or a separately optimized blocker for every target.  Any
      stronger lower bound must remember named-cell competition, both endpoint
      orders, nonnested precedence, or coordinate pins.  The corrected proof,
      independent audit, and checker are
      `BLOCKER_BARRIER_AND_CONTAINMENT_SPECTRUM.md`, its audit, and

## 275. Controlled search benchmark at solved dimensions

1124. A common unrestricted exact encoding was benchmarked at the known
      equality lengths for `k=7,8,9`.  Rank/containment theory reduces raw
      clause counts by factors approximately `4.5`, `6.0`, and `11.1` and
      substantially raises propagation/search throughput, but no equality
      instance terminated within 120 seconds, even after exact `k=8` or `k=9`
      onion rigidity was added.  A fixed-factor `k=9` ansatz solves in 0.05
      seconds, illustrating the value—and danger—of much stronger prescribed
      structure.

1125. At the impossible lengths `B(k)-1`, the raw exact encodings remained
      unknown after 30--46 seconds, while the rank-count modules returned

      `k=7,8,9`.  The theory therefore solves the lower-bound side and

      geometry to find known optima in the unrestricted selector encoding.

      `THEORY_SEARCH_BENCHMARK_K7_K9_20260723.md`.

## 276. Named-cell Hall localization in the `k=11` onion branches

1126. Let a physical component have length `q+t` and contain selected
      witnesses for `q` distinct rank-`r` targets.  Ordering those
      incomparable witnesses by left endpoint also orders their right
      endpoints, and the `i`th witness lies in `[i,i+t]`.  Consequently every
      component interval of length at least `t+1` contains a selected
      rank-`r` witness.  Every lower-rank target assigned to this named
      component must therefore use one of its actual cells of length at most
      `t`.

1127. This yields the non-scalar component Hall law

          Lambda_u(k) <= sum_C
             |{I subseteq C : 1<=|I|<=t_C, |OR(I)|<=u}|,

      and, more strongly, inclusion of the complete rank-at-most-`u` target
      family in the union of those actual OR-value families.  Unlike the
      endpoint-blocker hierarchy, this remembers the owning component, both
      physical endpoints, and the actual OR rank of every candidate cell.

1128. At `k=11,n=465`, Type I has one rank-at-most-four core of slack two.
      If `z` is its number of literal rank-five boundary values and `E_4`
      counts internal adjacent pairs of OR-rank at most four, then

          E_4>=97+z,
          y_2>=96+z,

      where `y_2` is the selected rank-five triple-witness count.  In the
      two-component Type-II branch the corresponding slack-two component
      obeys

          E_4>=96+z,  |C^(2)|>=97+z,  y_2>=95+z.

      The one-component duplicate branch gives `y_2>=96+z`; the remaining
      one-component duplicate-free branch permits triples and obeys the full
      singleton/pair/triple family inclusion.  The old joint scalar rows gave
      only `91+z` and `87+z` in the first two cases.

1129. The result is the first direct theorem obtained after the blocker
      barrier by using named-cell competition.  An exhaustive checker tests
      5,223 endpoint systems and every branch coefficient.  The theorem,
      independent audit, and checker are `K11_ONION_NAMED_CELL_HALL.md`, its
      audit, and `scratch/check_k11_onion_named_cell_hall.py`.

## 279. Two-antichain endpoint-forest hierarchy

1135. For disjoint antichains `F,G`, let `C(F,G)` be their cross-comparability
      graph and let `lambda(F,G)` be the maximum edge count of a linear-forest
      subgraph.  Shared selected-witness left endpoints give a matching `L`
      of size at least `|F|+|G|-n`; shared right endpoints give a disjoint
      matching `R` of the same minimum size.  Their union is acyclic.  On an
      alternating cycle, writing

          G_i=[ell_i,r_i], F_i=[ell_i,r_(i-1)]

      makes the cyclic shift preserve the strict endpoint order induced by
      both antichains, which is impossible.  Therefore

          n>=|F|+|G|-floor(lambda(F,G)/2).

      This is a valid genuinely joint left/right endpoint bound outside the
      scalar blocker barrier.

1136. Exact optimization does not presently improve `B(k)`.  Exhausting all
      arbitrary disjoint antichain pairs gives

          B_forest(1..5)=1,2,4,6,11,

      versus `B(1..5)=1,2,4,7,12`.  The `k=5` computation exhausts all 7,580
      punctured-cube antichains and 704,639 relevant large pairs.  For every
      pair of complete rank layers, the exact linear-forest number is

          lambda=min(2 min(f,g),f+g-1).

      Consequently full-layer pairs give Boolean width in every even
      dimension and width plus one in every odd dimension (`k>=3`).  Through
      `k=12` the values are

          1,2,4,6,11,20,36,70,127,252,463,924,

      namely Boolean width in even dimensions and width plus one in odd
      dimensions.  At `k=11` this is only `463<B(11)=465`.

1137. The pair theorem is sound, but the data show that interaction-level
      validity is not enough: a useful next lower hierarchy must couple at
      least three witness families, multiple endpoint forests competing for
      named cells, or coordinate pins.  The theorem, independent audit, and
      checker are `TWO_ANTICHAIN_ENDPOINT_FOREST.md`, its audit, and
      `scratch/check_two_antichain_endpoint_forest.py`.

## 280. Three-antichain endpoint packing

1138. For three pairwise disjoint antichains, common left and right endpoints
      form two collections of vertex-disjoint rainbow chain blocks of sizes
      two or three.  Every bichromatic projection is a linear forest, but the
      full three-colour graph need not be acyclic: a six-position OR word
      realizes an alternating trichromatic `C_6`.  Thus the pair theorem does
      not extend by declaring the global shared-endpoint graph a forest.

1139. Let `V` be the total family size, `w` the width of their union, and
      `P=lambda_12+lambda_13+lambda_23`.  If `S` is total endpoint saving,
      then pairwise forests give `S<=P`, the two chain partitions give
      `S<=2(V-w)`, and the exact three-way incidence identity

          D=3S-p<=2V,  p<=P

      gives `S<=floor((2V+P)/3)`.  Hence every universal word obeys

          n>=V-floor(Lambda_hat_3/2),
          Lambda_hat_3=min(P,2(V-w),floor((2V+P)/3)).

      This specializes exactly to the pair theorem and can be stronger than
      every constituent pair bound, but the central `k=11` ranks `5,6,7`
      still yield only `463`.  The exact simultaneous packing number may be
      smaller; the displayed relaxation does not improve `B(11)=465`.  See
      `THREE_ANTICHAIN_ENDPOINT_PACKING.md`, its audit, and
      `scratch/check_three_antichain_endpoint_packing.py`.

## 282. Exact saturation of the central three-antichain packing

1142. The three-family endpoint relaxation is exactly saturated by the full
      `k=11` ranks five, six, and seven.  A frozen 462-vertex rank-six path
      has 461 distinct consecutive rank-five intersections, omitting only
      `535`, and its consecutive unions cover all 330 rank-seven masks.
      Prepending `535` to the intersection row and appending the terminal
      singleton `4` produces a 463-entry word in which

          all rank-five masks are singleton ORs,
          all rank-six masks are adjacent-pair ORs,
          all rank-seven masks are triple ORs.

1143. Selecting those witnesses uses 462 left endpoints and 463 right
      endpoints, hence has endpoint saving

          (1254-462)+(1254-463)=1583.

      The general three-way incidence cap gives the matching upper bound:
      the three projected forests have at most `923,660,660` edges and
      `D=3S-p<=2*1254`, so `S<=1583`.  Therefore

          Lambda_3(C([11],5),C([11],6),C([11],7))=1583.

      Exact simultaneous endpoint order, chain orientation, and even an

          a_s(C1)>=C(11,s)-C(11-|D2|,s),  1<=s<=4.

## 286. Type-I boundary-facet pin-load theorem and deployment

1153. In the Type-I equality branch, delete the unique literal rank-six

          p_R^C = #{i in C4 : A_i subseteq R}.

          p_R^C >= 20.

      one run can have length three.  The thirty nonempty proper subsets of
      `R` require distinct singleton/pair cells within those runs, whereas
      nineteen support positions provide at most twenty-nine.  This is a
      genuine coordinate-facet statement, not a consequence of the existing
      averaged six-subcube moment.

## 287. Audit of the proposed global-sharing typed atom matching

1155. The proposed fractional long-run-atom calculation is correct but is
      not a new integral rounding theorem.  With

          h=ceil(sqrt(m log m)),
          H=floor(m-3 log_2 m)-h,
          c_d=N_d-N_(d+1) (d<h), c_h=N_h,

      the full coordinate orbit of one radius-`d` atom, assigned total mass
      `c_d/H`, gives unit load at every supported band mask.  The total atom
      mass is `W/H`, and the weighted reset excess is at most

          (2h+1)W/H=o(W).

      This is the fractional tiling already proved in
      `GLOBAL_LONG_RUN_MTF_ATOMS.md`.  The floor, tail, literal-repair, and
      odd-lift calculations in the new formulation all pass.

1156. There is one local scope error.  Two-sided radius-`d` buffering alone
      does not imply the displayed Pascal incidence equivalence

          A_t^u subseteq A_s^v iff 0<=s-t<=v-u.

      A repeated-direction four-cycle in `Q_2` is a counterexample.  The law
      becomes valid after imposing the stronger long-run block nonrepetition
      condition.  The actual Gray-code atoms used later satisfy that stronger
      condition, so this error does not invalidate their MTF factorization or
      the fractional ledger.  See
      `GLOBAL_FRACTIONAL_SHARING_PREREQUISITE_AUDIT.md` and
      `scratch/check_long_residence_pascal_scope.py`.

1157. The conditional integral implication is valid only after making the
      quota error explicit.  If `a_d` atoms of type `d` are selected and

          sum_d |a_d-floor(c_d/H)| = o(W/(Hh)),

      their center sets are disjoint, and no two selected atoms share a
      designated noncentral strip mask, then the total band defect and reset
      cost are `o(W)`, whence literal completion gives

          nu(2m)<=(1+o(1))W(2m).

      Atoms must formally be treated as a labelled multihypergraph because
      equal center sets may expose different strips.

1158. No such matching has been proved.  The estimate

          Delta_2/D=(2+o(1))/m^2

      does not yield a near-perfect matching when the uniformity
      `H=(1-o(1))m` grows; all audited black-box matching theorems lose the
      required error, and even the corresponding one-row matching remains
      open.  Moreover, center matching plus the stated pair conflicts is
      exactly full Pascal-strip atom disjointness in another representation,
      with stricter type quotas.  It is stronger than the OR-faithful target,
      which permits overlaps and asks only for `o(W)` total rank defect.

      Therefore the salvageable result is a sufficient conditional theorem
      within the long-run-atom route, not a constant-one construction, a new
      smaller rounding gate, or the unique remaining obstruction.  The full
      audits are `GLOBAL_SHARING_TYPED_MATCHING_AUDIT.md` and
      `FRACTIONAL_FACTORABLE_BRAID_PACKING_AUDIT.md`.

## 288. Central-square shell braid: exact shadow theorem and remaining factor gate

1159. In the equal four-chain box, the middle points admit two exact square
      sector parameterizations

          Q_c(a,b)=(c+a,m-c-b,b,m-a),
          0<=a,b<=R=m-c,

      related by interchange of the two coordinate pairs.  The sectors meet
      exactly in the `c=0` square and satisfy

          |M_m|=(m+1)^2+2 sum_(R=0)^(m-1)(R+1)^2
               =(2m^3+6m^2+7m+3)/3.

      An interval of square points with bounding rectangle
      `[u,r]x[0,x]` has join `(c+r,m-c,x,m-u)`.

1160. Partition a radius-`R` square by the shells `min(a,b)=u`.  In shell
      `u`, traverse the row `b=u` from `a=R` down to `u`, insert the repeated
      portal `(u,0)`, and then traverse the column `a=u` from `b=u+1` up to
      `R`.  The resulting word has exact length

          (R+1)^2+R

      and represents every bottom-anchored rectangle with `x>=u`.  Only the
      `R` bottom portals are repeated.  The separate bottom chain handles
      `x=0`, while the displayed `Delta_u` row-one/column grids correctly
      represent every remaining `1<=x<u<r`; their simultaneous superposition
      is still open.

      Using both square-sector orientations without attempting to share their
      common `c=0` order gives an exact upper-shadow word of length

          |M_m|+(m+1)(2m+1)=|M_m|+O(m^2)

      for the complete `x>=u` branch.  Exhaustive checks pass through
      `m=10` and `R=12`.  See `CENTRAL_SQUARE_SHELL_BRAID_AUDIT.md` and
      `scratch/verify_central_square_shell_braid.py`.

1161. The standard linked-band formulas remain exact: linked monotone
      central intervals transfer consecutive joins, and their common core is
      `[q+alpha_q,p+beta_p]`.  The stated meet-pin criterion needs one
      quantifier repair.  `J cap Z_b` nonempty guarantees the meet for the
      maximal factor `A_j={b:j in Z_b}`.  For an arbitrary already-realizing
      factor with chosen pin sets `H_b`, the required condition is instead

          J cap H_b nonempty.

      A central realization alone need not put a legal occurrence inside the
      core.  The exact counterexample and corrected statement are in
      `CENTRAL_SQUARE_LINKED_MEET_AUDIT.md`.

1162. The conditional exponent arithmetic is correct.  For
      `0<epsilon<=1`, a newly defined full-square excess satisfying

          e(R)<=e(R-2)+O(R^(1-epsilon))

      would be `O(R^(2-epsilon))`; summing the fixed-`c` sectors would give
      `O(m^(3-epsilon))`.  If this were extended uniformly to every unequal
      and degenerate four-box as an actual factor word, the subcritical
      aggregation theorem would yield global excess

          O(W(k) k^(-epsilon/2)).

      No such recurrence, factor realization, or uniform extension is
      proved.  The row-one `Delta_u` grid and its quadratic monotone-fork
      superposition obstruction were already isolated in
      `NONCANONICAL_TRIANGULAR_BRAID.md` and
      `PORTAL_GRID_MASTER_SUPERPOSITION.md`.  Moreover the shell order itself
      still lacks a controlled linked interval band, nonempty reflected meet
      cores, and verified coordinate pins.  Thus the shell braid is a genuine
      new upper-shadow sharing lemma, but the claim that only the strict
      simplex remains is too strong and no global coefficient changes.

## 289. Sparse twofold boundary braid: exact shadow reduction, false pin shortcut

1163. The proposed two-step section

          Sigma_R(P_a)=P_(a+2),
          Sigma_R(E_(a,b))=E_(a+2,b+2)  (b>=1)

      is exact.  It maps every witness of `(u,r,x)` with `x>=1` to a
      witness of `(u+2,r+2,x+2)`.  Its omitted alphabet is precisely

          {P_0,P_1} union {E_(s,1):2<=s<=R}
                    union {E_(s,2):3<=s<=R},

      of size `2R-1=|T_R|-|T_(R-2)|`.  This is the twofold composition of
      the previously proved one-step sparse section, so it is useful but
      does not newly remove an unresolved fibre-expansion tax.

1164. The three displayed words `F_R,K_R,J_R` do cover exactly the missing
      shadow regime `u<2 or x<3`.  Direct enumeration passes through
      `R=30`.  Together they contain every omitted cell; relative to one
      copy of each new cell, only five constant duplicates are new-alphabet
      repeats.  The remaining repeated letters are old-image peak or
      diagonal spine cells.  Consequently, **at the abstract triangular-word
      level**, a superposition preserving all old and boundary intervals with
      only `q_R` unidentified old-spine occurrences would give

          rho(R)<=rho(R-2)+q_R+O(1).

1165. The cross-threshold formulas

          E(c,r,x) join E(c-y,u,y)=Q(c,u,r,x)

      and the alternating `L/U` linked-band calculation are algebraically
      correct upper-join identities.  They are not lower meet cores of a
      physical central-interval factor.  A linked interval in a word of
      middle labels does not by itself provide monotone physical witness
      intervals, their common cores, or pins.  Some internal `U_s` labels
      also leave the fixed triangular sector, so their cost must be charged
      through the full square-sector sharing problem.

1166. The claimed implication

          forest-like band junctions => coordinate pin survival

      is false.  On three positions take

          I_X=[1,2], X={a};  I_Y=[2,3], Y={c};
          I_S=[1,3], S={a,b,c}.

      For coordinate `b`, the two negative intervals form a one-edge tree
      but cover `[1,3]`, so `Z_b` is empty on the positive interval `I_S`.
      A valid negative merge forest additionally requires every linked
      negative hull to lie in an actually assigned sign-correct negative
      parent interval, clean root separators, and global containment
      monotonicity.  The proposed braid supplies none of these automatically.

      Therefore the spine-recycling lemma remains a legitimate open
      **upper-shadow** sharing target, not a factor theorem.  Its sublinear
      recurrence would affect the global coefficient only after a uniform
      unequal-box factor realization with explicit pins.  See
      `SPARSE_BOUNDARY_SPINE_RECYCLING_AUDIT.md` and
      `scratch/verify_sparse_boundary_spine_claims.py`.

## 293. Exact rank-antichain cap for fixed-prefix append repair

1176. Let a fixed prefix miss `m_r` targets of rank `r`, and append `q`
      positions.  Every missing target needs a witness ending at a new
      position.  At one right endpoint the suffix ORs form an inclusion
      chain, so they contain at most one member of the fixed-rank antichain.
      Therefore

          m_r<=q  for every rank r.

      If `m_r=q`, every new endpoint is used exactly once by that layer.  A
      stronger exact propagation form materializes the selected endpoint of
      every missing target and imposes at most one equal-rank target per
      endpoint.  This theorem is valid for every zero-free `1<=k<20` append
      instance and is now implemented generically in
      `append_completion_sat.cpp`.

1177. Applied to the attempted deletion of prefix position zero, the
      shortened prefix misses thirteen rank-seven masks but only twelve new
      endpoints are available.  Thus that entire proposed length-476 repair
      branch is rigorously structurally UNSAT; its earlier solver timeouts
      carried no information.  Exhaustive profiling of all 465 single-prefix
      deletions leaves 82 branches after the rank cap: 79 have exactly twelve
      missing rank-seven masks, while only deletions 7, 89, and 196 have
      eleven.  The other 383 are structurally impossible.

1178. The strengthened append source also repairs a real proof-hook bug:
      CaDiCaL proof tracing is now started immediately after solver
      initialization, before every option, declaration, and clause.  The
      proof-open failure path exits before any formula operation.  The
      original no-deletion 12-entry append remains SAT and decodes to the
      known 477-entry word, passing both independent OR verifiers.  The
      frozen append source SHA-256 is

          c5c75460b861bc96a20ffe42daab241d401769ccd4dd771bae0d09e2254136cd.

      A skip-102 UNSAT run emitted a 25 MiB binary DRAT proof, independently
      verified by `drat-trim` against the exact `1494/90762` CNF.  This is a
      branch certificate, not a global lower bound.  At this stage the three
      rank-11-slack deletions 7, 89, and 196 remained the principal exact
      476-repair searches; Section 295 supersedes that provisional shortlist
      using the full missing-poset width theorem.  See
      `APPEND_RANK_ANTICHAIN_CAP_AUDIT.md`, its independent checker, and
      `K11_APPEND_SKIP102_UNSAT_CERTIFICATE.md`.

## 294. Audit of the role-recycling complete-bipartite proposal

1179. The pivot blocks

          B_j=(P_0,...,P_(j-1),E_(j,j-1),...,E_(j,0),P_(j+1),...,P_R)

      do give an exact triangular assignment at

          j=max(u,x+1).

      Their total length is `(3R^2+R)/2`; every positive-height cell occurs
      once, and the entire excess is the common peak chain repeated across
      blocks.  The central-square identities `A vee B vee H=Q`, the raw
      identity `H(c,u,x)=A(c-x,x,x+u+1)`, and the displayed linked upper
      bands are also correct on their stated domains.  Every relevant raw
      middle point has the unique edge parametrization

          e_(v,u)^(d)=E(d-v,u+v+1,v),

      giving the disjoint label family `K_(d+1,m-d)` and total edge count
      `C(m+2,3)`.

1180. This label sharing does not remove physical ordering multiplicity.
      In one `K_(a,b)`, the prescribed left stars demand `a(b-1)` directed
      adjacencies and the prescribed right stars demand `b(a-1)`, with the
      two sets disjoint.  If `p` edge occurrences are repeated and `c`
      required star adjacencies are cut, directed-grid chain covering gives
      the sharp bound

          p+c >= ab-max(a,b).

      It is attained by retaining all stars on the smaller side and cutting
      the transverse stars.  Summing over `a=d+1,b=m-d` gives

          h(h-1)(4h+1)/3       (m=2h),
          h(h+1)(4h-1)/3       (m=2h+1),

      which is `m^3/6+O(m^2)`.  Even the elementary transition-capacity
      bound sums to `C(m,3)`.  Therefore the proposed simultaneous
      complete-star linearization with `o(m^3)` cuts or repeated edges is
      impossible as stated.

1181. Several later recycling assertions also ignore active path domains.
      A raw equality of `E` labels need not place the destination occurrence
      in a band that is actually present.  For example

          H(4,1,3)=A(1,3,5)

      is a valid point identity, but the destination diagonal arm violates
      `3<=1+1`.  More generally

          D_(c;u,t)=A_(c-u+1;t,u+t-1)

      is an active destination diagonal arm only if `t<=c-u+2`, whereas the
      source allows `t` up to `m-c`.  The low-threshold `E(0,u,t)` identities
      have the same defect.  Thus the raw provider maps are injective, but
      not every nonprimary role is a primary arm occurrence elsewhere in
      the stated `L/C/W` atlas.

1182. The local lower-triangle, diagonal-provider, and low-threshold words
      remain valid upper-join witnesses, with the minor repair `v<=r` needed
      to include `x=r-1`.  They do not construct physical common cores or
      coordinate pins.  Forest junctions imply pin survival only after an
      actually assigned sign-correct negative parent is supplied for every
      linked negative hull, with clean root separators and global
      containment compatibility.  Acyclicity alone fails by the existing
      three-position counterexample.

1183. Consequently the complete-bipartite normal form is a useful
      obstruction theorem rather than the missing coefficient-one
      construction.  A viable replacement must discard most transverse
      full-star adjacency demands, reassign targets to a sparse segment
      system, or provide a different factor with explicit pins.  No new
      unconditional asymptotic upper bound follows.  The complete audit is
      `ROLE_RECYCLING_BIPARTITE_AUDIT.md`.

## 295. Complete single-deletion screen in the fixed-prefix 476 neighborhood

1184. The rank-layer endpoint cap is a special case of an exact missing-poset
      theorem.  If a fixed prefix is completed by `q` appended entries, every
      target absent from the prefix chooses one of the `q` new right
      endpoints.  The suffix ORs at one endpoint form an inclusion chain.
      Hence the complete missing-mask poset is covered by `q` chains and

          width(missing masks under inclusion) <= q.

      This includes all seam-crossing witnesses and assumes no fixed witness
      lengths.  Exact width is `|M|-mu`, where `mu` is a maximum matching in
      the bipartite strict-inclusion graph of the missing family.

1185. Across all 465 branches obtained by deleting one entry of the known
      465-entry prefix and appending twelve entries, the exact width
      distribution is

          width 12:   1 branch,
          width 13:  24 branches,
          width 14: 115 branches,
          width 15: 185 branches,
          width 16: 138 branches,
          width 17:   2 branches.

      Thus 464 branches are structurally impossible.  The former hard
      deletions 7, 89, and 196 have widths 13, 14, and 15.  Their redundant
      live searches were checked for terminal output and candidates, then
      stopped with logs preserved.

1186. The sole width-feasible branch is deletion 102, with 17 missing masks
      and width twelve.  Its exact CNF and binary DRAT proof were already
      independently verified (`25,858,633` resolution steps).  Therefore
      the complete fixed-prefix delete-one-plus-append-twelve neighborhood
      is now rigorously UNSAT: 464 branches by theorem and one by checked
      proof.  This does not rule out an arbitrary 476-entry word.

1187. The production append solver now performs the exact width test for
      missing families of at most 4,096 masks.  It additionally exposes the
      complete endpoint-chain law: endpoint flags of incomparable targets
      receive at-most-one clauses across ranks, and when the width equals
      `q`, every endpoint is required to carry one member of a recovered
      maximum antichain.  These clauses are theorem-redundant and exact.  The
      independently inspected source SHA-256 is

          7e49ea13cd92b42a9a7c2bc7c3116e3b9dd6ca80719111b62d9163fef60368e3.

      A separately written augmenting-path checker recovers and verifies a

      `K11_LENGTH476_SINGLE_DELETION_SCREEN_20260723.md`, and

## 297. Cross-diagonal central lines: exact chamber and scope

1191. In the balanced box `[0,m]^4`, put

          G_(a,x)(s)=(a+s,m-a-x,x,m-s).

      If `x<=c`, `a=c-x`, and

          Y(c;u,r,x)=(c+r,m-c,x,m-u),

      then the segment `s=u,...,r+x` has coordinatewise maximum exactly
      `Y`.  All endpoints are legal because `r<=m-c`.  The lines are
      pairwise disjoint and bijectively partition

          C_23={z in L_(2m):z_2+z_3<=m}

      by the inverse `a=m-z_2-z_3`, `x=z_3`, `s=z_1-a`.  Hence

          |C_23|=sum_(j=0)^m(j+1)^2.

      Concatenating the lines uses every chamber point once and represents
      every advertised `x<=c` upper target internally.  This is a valid
      literal partial max/OR word with no portal repeats.

1192. For the more general pair-{1,4} line

          (t,m-c,x,m+c-x-t),

      the forced segment is `t=c+u-x,...,c+r`; cube feasibility is exactly

          x<=c+u,  r+x<=m.

      Writing the target excess as `d=r+x-u`, this is equivalent to
      `Y_1,Y_4>=d`.  Across all six coordinate-pair orientations, the
      uncovered labels are exactly those having at most one coordinate at
      least `d`.  Six such line foliations are six different physical
      orders; no near-once simultaneous ordering follows.

1193. The no-pair-line family is not the family requiring three central
      providers.  Already at `m=2`,

          Y(0;0,2,1)=(2,2,1,2), d=3

      has every coordinate below `d`, so no coordinate-pair line applies,
      but

          (0,1,1,2) vee (2,2,0,0)=(2,2,1,2)

      uses two central providers.  More generally every upper point of a
      four-chain box is the join of two central points: partition the four
      coordinates into two pairs each with capacity at least the excess and
      subtract the excess on disjoint supports.  This is the existing hull
      lemma in `FOUR_BOX_INTERLEAVING_AUDIT.md`.

1194. Therefore the cross-diagonal theorem is a useful zero-repeat partial
      upper word, but it does not identify the established jointly-thick
      sector, cover lower ranks, merge the six line orders, or improve the
      global asymptotic constant.  Literal local witnesses need no pins;
      the derivative/factor and global pin bridges remain separate.

## 298. Exact simplex-perimeter braid and its dual boundary

1195. For the truncated simplex

          D(P,N)={(d,a)>=0:d<=P,d+a<=N},

      there is an exact-once recursive perimeter word representing every
      feasible triple

          (min d,min a,max(d+a))=(ell,u,h).

      Translate the strict interior by `(-1,-1)`, recurse in
      `D(min(P-2,N-3),N-3)`, then traverse the top, right, bottom, and left
      perimeter.  The induction and four boundary cases are exact.  One must
      explicitly stop when the strict interior is empty and treat `P=0` as
      one vertical side; otherwise the literal right/left lists duplicate
      noncorner points.  With this repair exhaustive enumeration passes for
      every `0<=P<=N<=12`.

1196. Under

          Phi_x(d,a)=(d+a,m-d-x,x,m-a),

      the slice words bijectively use every central point with
      `z_2+z_3<=m` once and cover every upper target `U_(c,u,r,x)` with
      `c>=x`.  The sector size is

          sum_(j=0)^m(j+1)^2=(m+1)(m+2)(2m+3)/6
                            =|M_m|/2+(m+1)^2/2.

      This four-box consequence is equivalent to the simpler cross-diagonal
      fixed-`d` row word from Section 297.  In fact the equivalence is already
      abstract: every feasible `(ell,u,h)` is represented by the fixed-row
      segment

          (ell,u),(ell,u+1),...,(ell,h-ell).

      Conversely every interval triple is feasible.  Thus the recursive
      perimeter word is an alternative exact-once ordering, not a stronger
      target theorem.

      The independent exhaustive checker
      `scratch/audit_simplex_perimeter_braid.py` passes every
      `0<=P<=N<=12` and every four-box instance through `m=10`; its SHA-256
      is `e81f40093298d9a72b68370ab0a8b731ebbf426e1c03b5ee7e222b3e15467624`.

1197. The complementary map

          Psi_c(d,a)=(a,m-c,c+d,m-d-a)

      correctly reduces every remaining `c<x` target to the dual extrema

          max d=x-c, max a=c+r, min(d+a)=u.

      No exact-once or subquadratic-excess dual word is proved.  Even full
      upper sharing would still need linked physical bands, nonempty lower
      cores, and pins.  Therefore both the dual upper-ordering gate and the
      lower factor/pin gate remain.  Exact-once duality is impossible already
      for `D(1,1)`: its three feasible two-point dual targets require all
      three pairs to be adjacent in a three-letter linear permutation.  Thus
      repetitions are intrinsically necessary, although `O(N)` excess per
      slice remains open.  No asymptotic constant changes.  See
      `SIMPLEX_PERIMETER_BRAID_AUDIT.md`.

## 299. Exact domain of the complementary dual trapezoid

1198. For

          D(P,N)={(d,a)>=0:d<=P,d+a<=N},

      a complete dual-extrema target is

          (max d,max a,min(d+a))=(D,A,U).

      It is geometrically feasible exactly when

          0<=D<=P, 0<=A<=N, 0<=U<=min(N,D+A).

      Three explicit providers prove sufficiency.  The complementary
      four-box application is a strict subfamily.  With `c=N-P`, eliminating
      its original parameters gives exactly

          1<=D<=2P-N-1,
          2(N-P)+D+1<=A<=N,
          0<=U<=A-(N-P)-1.

      Thus unrestricted dual obstructions cannot automatically be imported
      into the four-box route.

1199. Two infinite positive families are exact.  `P=0` has the monotone
      vertical word.  For every `N>=1`, the complete family on `D(1,N)` has
      alphabet size plus one: writing `A_j=(0,j)` and `B_j=(1,j)`, use

          A_0,A_1,...,A_N,B_(N-1),...,B_0,A_0.

      The five elementary witness cases cover every feasible triple.  In the
      relevant four-box subfamily, every thinnest nonempty slice

          2P-N-1=1

      has an exact-once block; all unused letters can be placed outside it.

1200. Exact-once fails for the complete dual family already at `D(1,1)`.
      At `D(2,2)`, exhaustive enumeration of all `720`, `15120`, and

      the square `P=N=7`.  At `P=N=8`, a 48-letter word (three repeats over
      45 points) covers all 168 relevant targets; exact-once there remains
      unresolved.

1201. The obvious all-positive-interior recursion plus a closed perimeter
      fails already at `N=3`, so mixed boundary/interior portals are a real

## 300. Exact one-shell triangular boundary and recurrence gate

1202. The word consisting of the complete outer row followed by descending
      peaks, then the row blocks

          P_(s-1),E_(s,1),...,E_(s,s-1),  s=2,...,R-1,

      spans the triangular alphabet with exactly `R-2` repeated occurrences
      for `R>=2`.  Exhaustive interval analysis and a direct proof show that
      its missing targets are exactly

          4<=r<=R-1, 1<=u<=r-2, 1<=x<=r-3.

      Every other target belongs to one of five explicit internal interval
      families.  The change `(u',r',x')=(u-1,r-2,x-1)` maps the missing set
      bijectively to one radius-`R-3` strict triangle with its top height face
      removed.

1203. A separator `t` has the exact portal word

          L_(a,x),...,L_(t,x),P_t,E_(q,x),...,E_(b,x),
          q=max(t+1,x+1),

      where `L_(u,x)=E_(u,min(x,u-1))` and `L_(0,x)=P_0`.  For every
      `a<=u<=t<r<=b`, `x<r`, the interval from `L_(u,x)` through `E_(r,x)`
      has rectangle `(u,r,x)`.  A balanced interval tree assigns every pair
      to such a separator, but literal concatenation still repeats provider
      chains heavily.

1204. The sparse lift `P_s->P_(s+2)`,
      `E_(s,y)->E_(s+2,y+2)` for `y>=1` omits exactly the `2R-1` new alphabet
      cells: `P_0,P_1`, every height-one cell, and every height-two cell.
      Thus lifting a word of excess `rho(R-2)` and adding the omissions once
      has size exactly `|T_R|+rho(R-2)`.  If `chi_R` denotes the further
      ordering cost needed to preserve the lifted, shell, separator, and
      merge-forest witnesses, then

          rho(R)<=rho(R-2)+chi_R.

      This is an exact reformulation, not a bound: the required
      `chi_R=O(R^(1-epsilon))` remains unproved.  Local max-factor validity
      does not itself supply the global splicing or coordinate pins, so no
      asymptotic constant changes.  For the shell multiset alone there is the
      sharper identity

          S_R=Sigma_R(S_(R-2)) plus all omissions plus {P_1,P_2}.

      Hence inherited shell multiplicities leave only a constant inventory
      deficit.  The low peaks inserted at the outer-fan/shell seam contaminate
      the lifted seam-crossing witnesses, so this identity does not remove the
      global ordering problem.

1205. The proof audit is `TRIANGULAR_ONE_SHELL_AUDIT.md`.  Its independent
      checker verifies exact shell/lift behavior through `R=20` and every
      separator gadget through `R=15`; the checker SHA-256 is

          c64c5a1f4a4cfe7392190d9ef9d595875ca7e97df69b2c58bb0d019c16acf1a0.

## 301. Exact central transfer lines and the corrected thick cone

1206. Let `y in [0,m]^4` have weight `2m+delta`.  A middle-level line that
      fixes the two coordinates outside `{i,j}` at their target values and
      varies only `i,j` has join `y` if and only if

          y_i>=delta and y_j>=delta.

      When these inequalities hold, the adjacent line is

          T_t=y-delta*e_i-t*e_j+t*e_i,  0<=t<=delta.

      Every point has weight `|y|-delta=2m`, the join is `y`, and the meet is
      `y-delta*e_i-delta*e_j`.  The earlier displayed proof sentence with
      `|y|-2delta` was an arithmetic typo; the construction itself subtracts
      only one net `delta`.

1207. This line is an actual delay-`delta` OR factor.  In coordinate-chain
      atoms, every incidence pattern along `T_0,...,T_delta` is full, a
      boundary prefix, a boundary suffix, or empty.  Put a full atom at
      factor position `delta`, a prefix atom supported on windows `0,...,b`
      at position `b`, and a suffix atom supported on `a,...,delta` at
      position `a+delta`.  The length-`delta+1` window unions reproduce the
      line exactly.  Hence the lower meet and all local central pins are
      genuine, not only formal labels.

1208. If `2delta<=m`, every upper target has at least two coordinates at
      least `delta`, so some transfer line applies.  In the triangular chart

          Y(c;u,r,x)=(c+r,m-c,x,m-u),  delta=r+x-u,

      coordinate three is always below `delta`.  Put

          A: x<=c+u,
          B: r+x<=m,
          C: r+x-u<=m-c.

      A two-provider line exists exactly when at least two of `A,B,C` hold,
      using respectively one of the pairs `(1,4)`, `(1,2)`, `(2,4)`.  Thus
      the genuinely thick residual is exactly the family on which at least
      two of these inequalities fail.

1209. The non-line-factorable cone has `H(y)={i:y_i>=delta}` of size at most
      one.  If `H(y)={i}`, then

          a=m-y_i, z_j=delta-y_j (j!=i),
          0<=a<=m-delta, z_j>=1,
          a+sum_(j!=i)z_j=2delta-m.

      If `H(y)` is empty, the exact chart is

          z_i=delta-y_i,
          sum_i z_i=3delta-2m,
          max(1,delta-m)<=z_i<=delta.

      The last coordinate bounds are essential for `delta>m`; positivity
      alone admits points outside `[0,m]^4`.

1210. For one fixed transfer pair the maximal lines partition the middle
      level, but concatenating the different foliations repeats a positive
      fraction of that level.  No subcubic simultaneous superposition or
      thick-cone braid is proved, so the global asymptotic upper constant is
      unchanged.  The proof audit and independent exhaustive checker are
      `CENTRAL_TRANSFER_LINE_FACTORIZATION_AUDIT.md` and
      `scratch/audit_central_transfer_lines.py`; the checker SHA-256 is

          e54e7bd2eaf06eb85842f74c46f3d80fff3a75b2cada605277f1316f855d33f2.

## 302. Left-anchored global sharing and the dual-sector gate

1211. Let central labels `C_1,...,C_L` be prescribed on

          I_i=[i,rho_i],
          rho_1<...<rho_L, i<=rho_i<=i+D.

      Then consecutive unions and intersections are exactly

          union_(i=p)^q I_i=[p,rho_q],
          intersection_(i=p)^q I_i=[q,rho_p].

      Put `Z_b=[L+D]` minus the union of all `I_i` whose label omits atom
      `b`, and take the maximal factor

          A_j=max = meet_{i:j in I_i} C_i.

      Individual central pin survival `I_i intersect Z_b != empty` for every
      `b in C_i` realizes every central label.

1212. In this ordered schedule, the same individual pin condition also
      forces pins in every nonempty consecutive common core.  If
      `J=[q,rho_p]` for labels all containing `b` were covered by negative
      intervals, one connected negative component would cover `J`.  Earlier
      negative indices alone cannot reach `rho_p`, and later ones alone
      cannot cover `q`; a component joining both sides contains every whole
      `I_i`, `p<=i<=q`, contradicting an individual central pin.  Hence

          join_(j=q)^rho_p A_j=max = meet_(i=p)^q C_i.

      Combined with the linked-union identity, upper completeness and lower
      consecutive-meet completeness give a universal range-maximum word of
      actual length `rho_L<=L+D`.  The submitted expression
      `L+rho_L-L` should simply be written `rho_L` (or bounded by `L+D`).

1213. The exact-once primal simplex sector covers the four-box targets with
      `c>=x`.  The complementary required sector is the relevant subfamily
      of the dual extrema problem `(max d,max a,min(d+a))`.  A uniform
      alphabet-plus-`O(N^(2-epsilon))` dual word is not known, and an
      upper-only word would still need the increasing-right schedule and the
      lower/pin conditions above.  Finite exact-once evidence applies to the
      required four-box subfamily, not the complete dual family; the latter
      already fails exact-once at `D(1,1)`.

1214. Canonical fixed-height descending peak spines cannot provide the
      missing subquadratic braid.  Arms assigned to one pass form a chain in

          (u,x) <= (v,y) iff u<=v and x>=y.

      The diagonal arms `(2,1),...,(R-1,R-2)` are an antichain.  Distinct
      passes are therefore required, and even shortened passes cost at least

          sum_(u=2)^(R-1)(R-u)=Omega(R^2)

      peak starts.  A successful construction must recycle provider roles in
      a genuinely noncanonical way.

1215. This is a correct sufficient reduction, not a construction.  No
      factorable dual-sector schedule with subcubic total excess is proved,
      so no asymptotic constant changes.  The proof audit and exhaustive
      binary-coordinate checker are `LEFT_ANCHORED_GLOBAL_SHARING_AUDIT.md`
      and `scratch/audit_left_anchored_global_sharing.py`; the checker hash is

          d4fd09b162d0cfd26ada672469beb88561a3b6f89e98e9eb0ebf6655b23fc764.

## 303. Linear-excess triangular endpoint geometry and maximal pin failure

1216. The complete triangular target family has an ordered orthogonal pair
      with only linear excess.  For each rank `r`, use left chains fixed by
      `(r,u)` and right chains fixed by `(r,x)`.  Create

          A_r=(a_(r,0),...,a_(r,r-1))

      and positions `b_r`, ordered

          A_R,A_(R-1),b_R,A_(R-2),b_(R-1),...,A_1,b_2,b_1.

      Assign target `(u,r,x)` the interval beginning at `a_(r,u)` and ending
      at `a_(r-1,x)` for `x<r-1`, or at `b_r` for `x=r-1`.  Both endpoint
      fibres have the correct inclusion order, their chain partitions are
      orthogonal, and every interval is forward.

1217. The construction uses

          sum_(r=1)^R r+R=N_R+R=|T_R|+R-1

      positions.  Every witness crosses at most a suffix of `A_r`, one
      intervening `b` position, a prefix of `A_(r-1)`, and possibly `b_r`;
      hence its physical length is at most `2R+1`.  Thus abstract endpoint
      ordering, triangular placement, orthogonality, and locality do not
      force quadratic excess.

1218. This near-once endpoint system is maximally nonfactorable for `R>=2`.
      For each `r>=2`, the union of all height-zero intervals `(u,r,0)` runs
      from the start of `A_r` through `a_(r-1,0)`.  These unions overlap down
      the complete block order, and the rank-one interval reaches `b_1`.
      Therefore the negative intervals for the first positive height atom
      cover every physical position:

          Z_(h_1)=empty.

      Radius one has no positive-height target, so this obstruction is
      vacuous there.

1219. The result isolates the remaining triangular cost at the coordinate
      pin layer **within the unrestricted Boolean endpoint/pinning normal
      form** for this assignment.  It does not assign physical letters from
      the constrained triangular alphabet or enforce spanning of that
      alphabet; central-point inventory and global superposition remain
      separate requirements in the four-box route.  Thus quadratic excess is
      not forced by endpoint geometry alone, but the stronger slogan
      `quadratic portal cost = pin cost` is not yet a theorem for the
      constrained triangular construction.  The proposed protected-peak
      superposition, which would preserve a lifted factorable backbone while
      adding only `O(R^(1-epsilon))` cut positions, remains unproved.  No
      recurrence or asymptotic constant changes.  Moreover, insertion-only
      padding cannot repair this particular schedule: the height-zero
      intervals remain a connected cover of the complete old endpoint hull,
      so they also cover every newly inserted internal position, while an
      external position lies in no unchanged positive witness.  A successful
      protected construction must reroute or duplicate endpoint chains, not
      merely add separators.  The audit and checker are
      `TRIANGULAR_ENDPOINT_BRAID_AUDIT.md` and
      `scratch/audit_triangular_endpoint_braid.py`; the checker hash is

          f659203fe5eb28870bd2ba5249bb8c3561a89a1c94128f82bd63112c51ce254e.

## 305. Catalan global sharing is affordable, but the switch system is missing

1226. If `ell(w)` is the final-descent length of a Dyck word of semilength
      `m`, then

          #{w:ell(w)=j}=j/(2m-j) binom(2m-j,m).

      Consequently every fixed moment is Catalan-bounded.  In particular,

          sum_w ell(w)       = Cat_m * 3m/(m+2),
          sum_w ell(w)^2     = Cat_m * m(13m-1)/((m+2)(m+3)),
          sum_w (1+ell(w))^2 < 20 Cat_m.

      Thus the submitted constant `52` for the unshifted quadratic moment is
      valid but loose.  Since

          W(2m+1)=(2m+1)Cat_m,

      `O(H(1+ell(w))^2)` local repair work per parent totals
      `O(H Cat_m)=o(W(2m+1))` whenever `H=o(m)`.

1227. The choice `H=ceil(sqrt(m log m))` also makes both literal binomial
      tails `o(W)`.  Hoeffding gives the sufficient estimate

          tail=O(2^(2m+1)/m)=o(W(2m+1)).

      The stronger displayed estimate `O(2^(2m+1)/m^2)` requires a larger
      fixed coefficient, for example `H=ceil(2sqrt(m log m))`; this does not
      affect the asymptotic reduction.

1228. Abstract endpoint neutralization is correct conditionally.  In a
      connected graph on `r` strand labels, a tree-path conjugation realizes
      any transposition with fewer than `2r` edge transpositions, and any
      permutation is a product of at most `r-1` transpositions.  Hence a
      genuinely available connected transposition system corrects arbitrary
      endpoint ownership in fewer than `2r^2` moves.

1229. The hidden word **available** is the entire remaining construction.
      Static connectivity of a graph of desired moves is insufficient.  The
      edge moves must remain flippable after every preceding overlapping
      switch and must preserve the targetwise one-tag colour bijection,
      selected lower merge-forest roots, factor provenance, and coordinate
      pins in the current state.  The `O(H)` cut-halo theorem applies to an
      actual `O(H)` neighbourhood of a literal cut in an already factorable
      word; it is not automatic for an abstract middle-row portal switch.

1230. The known atomic square and ordinary three-strand alpha switches do not
      supply this neutral alphabet.  They satisfy the parity lock

          sign(endpoint monodromy)=(-1)^(signed tag transfer).

      Therefore every ledger-neutral word in those moves has even endpoint
      monodromy and cannot realize a pure transposition.  In addition, all
      these circuit moves preserve the physical endpoint set.  A dynamically
      closed construction needs an off-diagonal move, such as a state-stable
      four-boundary/atomic composite, plus a proof that its support survives
      composition and preserves colours, roots, and pins.

1231. The rigorous conclusion is therefore a no-counting-obstruction theorem:
      quadratic local portal work is asymptotically affordable, but the
      compatible switches have not been constructed.  If the state-stable
      connected neutral-switch lemma is proved, the Catalan accounting gives
      `nu(2m+1)<=W(2m+1)+o(W)`, and the trimmed lift gives the even case.
      Until then the unconditional upper coefficient does not change.  The
      complete audit is `CATALAN_GLOBAL_SHARING_THEOREM_AUDIT.md`.

1232. The constrained triangular optimization has now been encoded directly:
      positions are coherent cells `(s,y)`, every alphabet cell must occur,
      and each target `(u,r,x)` selects a real interval whose extrema are

          (min s,max s,min y,max y)=(u,r,0,x).

      This is the canonical finite model of the factorability/pin obstruction,
      not merely an abstract endpoint schedule.

1233. Independently checked DRAT certificates exclude lengths 17, 18, and 19
      at radius five, while the known length-20 word passes exhaustive interval
      verification.  Since `|T_5|=16`, this proves

          rho(5)=4.

      Together with the previously exact small cases,

          rho(1),...,rho(5)=0,0,1,2,4.

1234. At radius six, `|T_6|=22`; independently checked DRAT certificates now
      exclude lengths 23, 24, and 25.  Hence

          4<=rho(6)<=5,

      with the upper bound supplied by the verified length-27 word.  These
      values neither prove quadratic growth nor a subquadratic recurrence,
      but they give a proof-grade benchmark for proposed protected-backbone
      recursions.  Full formulas, hashes, verifier logs, and the exact encoding

## 307. Monotone-radius rotor atoms and the corrected integral gate

1235. Fix an injective queue `z_(-h),...,z_(H+m-1)` on `2m` coordinates and
      middle windows

          S_t={z_t,...,z_(t+m-1)}.

      For radius `d`, the ordered last-occurrence state beginning with

          L_t(d)={z_(t+d),...,z_(t+m-1)},
          {z_(t+d-1)},...,{z_(t-d)}

      exposes the complete symmetric chain of radius `d` around `S_t`.

1236. If `e<=d`, appending

          X=L_(t+1)(e)={z_(t+e+1),...,z_(t+m)}

      makes the first `1+2e` last-occurrence blocks exactly those needed for
      the radius-`e` chain at `S_(t+1)`.  The resulting complete state is not
      generally the canonical partition: stale singleton blocks remain split
      off after the useful prefix.  The correct invariant for a nonincreasing
      profile `d_0>=...>=d_(H-1)` is

          PiHat_t=(L_t(d_t),{z_(t+d_t-1)},...,{z_(-d_0)},RHat_t).

      All stale blocks occur after the chain prefix and remain harmless under
      every later decrease.  Exhaustive state and suffix-OR checks through
      `m=12` validate this invariant.

1237. Reversing the initial state blocks costs `2d_0+2` nonzero entries, and
      the `H-1` updates cost one each.  Hence one atom has literal word length

          H+2d_0+1.

      Its `H` exposed chains are pairwise disjoint.  Every exposed mask is a
      genuine suffix OR at the corresponding endpoint, so factorability and
      coordinate pins are automatic rather than separately imposed.

1238. Put `W=binom(2m,m)`, `N_q=binom(2m,m-q)`, and `rho_q=N_q/W`.  For one
      atom, let `a_q` be the number of starts whose radius reaches depth `q`.
      The monotone real profile `H rho_q` has an explicit integral random
      representation

          a_q=floor(H rho_q+U),  U uniform in [0,1).

      Coordinate symmetry gives load `H/W` to each mask in each rank
      `m+-q`.  Giving all queue/profile atoms total fractional weight `W/H`
      therefore covers the central band exactly once.  The total fractional
      center mass is `W`, and reset mass is at most

          (2h+1)W/H=o(W)

      when `h=o(H)`.

      A fixed radius-`h` atom already shares all shallower depths in the same
      updates.  The new content of the monotone profile is selective
      truncation to the exact SCD quota law, not a lower reset cost for the
      weaker missing-only OR formulation.

1239. For the invoked width-order two-tail word, a safe proved choice is

          omega=log m, h=ceil(sqrt(m log m)), H=m-h.

      More generally the recorded moderate-deviation theorem covers
      `omega->infinity` with `omega=o(m^(1/3))`.  The submitted broader
      condition `omega=o(m)` is not justified by that theorem.  This is not
      literal tail enumeration: the shared tail word has no
      `sqrt(m/omega)` multiplicity factor.

1240. The integral gate must retain row quotas as well as a collision bound.
      With sign `sigma in {-,+}`, total incidence `T_q^sigma`, duplicate
      excess `D_q^sigma`, and missing count `M_q^sigma`, the exact identity is

          M_q^sigma=N_q+D_q^sigma-T_q^sigma.

      Thus a sufficient packing lemma asks for `W/H+o(W/H)` atoms satisfying

          T_q^sigma=N_q+O(W/H)  for every q and sign,
          D_0+sum_(q=1)^h(D_q^-+D_q^+)=o(W).

      Atom count and small duplicate mass alone do not prevent an entire row
      from being undersupplied.  Under these corrected quotas the conclusion
      `nu(2m)<=W+o(W)` is valid after literal central repairs and the shared
      two-tail word.  This is a sufficient route, not a logical equivalence
      with the constant-one conjecture.

1241. The first nontrivial integral instance is positive.  For

          m=3, h=1, H=2,

      ten explicit atoms partition all 50 masks in ranks 2, 3, and 4 exactly,
      so every duplicate and missing count is zero.  The certificate and
      direct verifier are `ROTOR_PACKING_SMALL_EXACT.md` and
      `scratch/verify_rotor_packing_m3.py`.  The all-`m` quota-respecting
      near-disjoint packing remains unproved.  The theorem audit and exhaustive
      local checker are `MONOTONE_RADIUS_ROTOR_BRAIDS_AUDIT.md` and
      `scratch/audit_monotone_radius_rotor_suffix.py`.

      The next benchmark `m=4,h=1,H=3` is encoded exactly after coordinate
      symmetry reduction (864,951 variables and 2,404,043 clauses), but the
      first bounded solve returned UNKNOWN.  See
      `ROTOR_M4_H1_INTEGRAL_GATE_BENCHMARK_20260724.md`; no SAT or UNSAT claim
      is made.

## 308. Exact rotor codegrees and the random-packing barrier

1242. For one fixed rank row of a queue atom, let the exposed masks have size
      `k=m+-q`, let `a_q` starts be active, and let two masks have Johnson
      distance `r`.  Under a uniform coordinate queue, their exact normalized
      codegree is

          2(a_q-r)/(a_q binom(k,r) binom(2m-k,r))

      for `1<=r<a_q`, and zero otherwise.  The maximum same-row ratio is
      `(2+o(1))/m^2`.

1243. Cross-depth pairs are necessarily more correlated.  For nested lower
      masks at depths `q<r`, put `b=r-q`, `A=a_q`, and `B=a_r`.  The exact
      compatible-position numerator is

          P^-_(q,r)=sum_(j=0)^b min(B,(A-j)_+),

      and the normalized codegree is

          P^-_(q,r)/(A binom(m-q,b)).

      The upper-row analogue has numerator `sum_(j=0)^b(B-j)_+`.
      Adjacent depths therefore have ratio `(2+o(1))/m`.  A typical full
      atom exposes

          K=(sqrt(pi)+o(1))m^(3/2)

      band masks, so `K Delta_2/Delta_1=Omega(sqrt(m))`.  The excellent
      middle-only codegree does not transfer to the one-stage decorated
      full-band hypergraph.

1244. Independent rounding fails sharply.  With `A=floor(W/H)` independent
      atom samples, every fixed band mask has asymptotic Poisson load one and

          E(X-1)_+ -> e^(-1).

      Since the controlled band contains

          (sqrt(pi)+o(1))W sqrt(m)

      masks, the expected summed duplicate excess is

          (sqrt(pi)/e+o(1))W sqrt(m).

      Already the middle row has `(e^(-1)+o(1))W` expected duplicates, and a
      bounded-difference estimate makes `D_0=o(W)` exponentially unlikely.
      Independent queues followed by collision deletion are therefore not a
      route to the corrected packing lemma.

1245. This does not disprove a correlated packing.  It proves that the
      missing theorem must correlate atoms simultaneously across depths and
      achieve an `o(W)` leftover among `Theta(W sqrt(m))` band masks.  A
      routine fixed-uniformity nibble or an `o(1)` relative leftover is not
      enough.  Exact derivations are in `MONOTONE_QUEUE_PACKING_CODEGREES.md`.

## 309. The first neutral-odd switch candidate also collapses

1246. The formal four-boundary endpoint-safe transfer followed by an inverse
      atomic square has an exact local normal form.  When the right canonical
      rhombus is dynamically available, all right-hand changes cancel and the
      composite reduces to the one-tag Johnson-square switch

          {u-a,w-c} -> {u-c,w-a}.

      It is ledger-neutral and swaps the two terminal owners.

1247. Such a square preserves its individual upper-colour multiset if and
      only if the four lower vertices lie in one common `(k+1)`-set.  Then all
      four edge colours are equal, so the switch consumes two occurrences of
      one old colour.  It is impossible in a colour-simple/perfect one-tag
      factor unless a duplicate-colour reservoir is first created.  Thus the
      formal parity-breaking composite is not the missing state-closed neutral
      generator.  The classification and exhaustive checks through all
      `J(n,k)`, `n<=10`, are in `NEUTRAL_ODD_COMPOSITE_COLLAPSE.md`.

## 310. Exact two-sided wreath-shadow transfer

1248. Let `n=2m+1`, `W=binom(n,m)`, and `B=W/n=Cat_m`.  The
      Muetze--Standke--Wiechert `C_n`-factor of the odd graph partitions the
      middle layer into `B` minimum odd cycles.  Every minimum odd cycle is a
      cyclic-interval wreath: if consecutive vertices are `A_i` and `z_i` is
      the unique coordinate outside `A_i union A_(i+1)`, then

          A_(i+2)=A_i union {z_i} minus {z_(i+1)},

      and one circuit shows that the `z_i` are all distinct and the `A_i`
      are the length-`m` intervals in the step-two cyclic order.

1249. For an exact wreath factor `F`, let `M_q(F)` be the number of
      rank-`m-q` masks absent from all cyclic intervals of length `m-q`.
      Complementation gives the same defect at rank `m+1+q`.  For every
      `1<=H<m`, emit from each wreath the `n` entries

          E_j=I_pi(j,m-H)

      followed by `E_0,...,E_(2H)`.  The union of `t<=2H+2` consecutive
      entries is literally `I_pi(j,m-H+t-1)`.  Appending the missing band
      masks and both literal tails proves the exact inequality

          nu(2m+1) <= W + ((2H+1)/n)W
                         +2 sum_(q=1)^H M_q(F)
                         +2 sum_(r=0)^(m-H-1) binom(n,r)-1.

      This is already a genuine OR word, so no later linked-band,
      lower-meet, factor-labeling, contamination, or pin-survival theorem is
      required.

1250. With

          H=ceil((1/2+epsilon)sqrt(n log n)),

      the seam term and the two binomial tails are `o(W)`.  Therefore the
      sole sufficient gate is still

          sum_(q=1)^H M_q(F)=o(W).

      A stronger exact resolution would choose nested active-start sets
      `Omega=A_0 superset ... superset A_m` whose lower and complementary
      upper interval maps are both bijective at every depth.  This exact SCD
      resolution is not necessary: growing-depth near-surjectivity of the
      full shadow maps suffices.  No available wreath, rotor, signed-design,
      or fixed-depth theorem proves it.  The detailed audit is
      `GLOBAL_WREATH_SHADOW_TRANSFER_AUDIT_20260724.md`, and the Pro prompt
      has been updated in `PRO_CONSTANT_ONE_MASTER_PROMPT_20260724.md`.
