1360. The proposed MWB overload reformulation needs three corrections.  First,
      exact central `(2m+1,m)` wreath factors are already unconditional:
      Mütze--Standke--Wiechert Theorem 4 gives a `C_(2m+1)`-factor of the odd
      graph, and every such shortest odd cycle is a wreath.  MWB is open only
      because multidepth balancing is missing.  Second, collision excess does
      dominate overload, but an arbitrary gap-two transfer need not lower
      overload; the exact proof writes

          P-P_min=(1/2) sum d(d-1) >= D^-+D^+ >= O.

      Third, the nonzero core-plus-bonus clone equivalence fails when a target
      has load above `c_q+1`.  Adding unpenalized spill slots makes it exact:
      the minimum of uncovered cores plus `(r-covered bonuses)_+` over
      decorations of a fixed factor equals `O_q`.

      The orbit relabeling argument removes only rankwise aggregate row-sum
      divisibility, not point margins, cross-depth compatibility, support, or
      trade-lattice constraints.  Finally MWB is stronger than the existing
      coefficient-one gate: it asks for collision excess divided by `c_q`,
      while the factorial hole theorem divides by `binom(c_q+1,2)` and may
      take the rankwise hybrid minimum with overload.  Full audit:
      `MWB_BALANCED_OVERLOAD_REDUCTION_AUDIT_20260724.md`.

1361. Simultaneous floor/ceiling-balanced nested deletion flags exist
      integrally through every depth by one lower-bounded layered flow, and
      the labelled histogram coupling gives `O_q(F)<=e_q(F,P)`.  Hence the
      remaining MWB lane is a joint cyclic synchronization theorem, not a
      marginal integrality problem.  The proposed infinite-Gaussian owner
      criterion is formally sufficient but vacuous at
      `H=sqrt(m) log log m`: it charges a positive tail even when an owner
      agrees through all `H` depths.  The exact nonvacuous condition is

          sum_X Psi_(m,H)(a(X))=o(W),
          Psi_(m,H)(a)=sum_(q=a+1)^H 1/c_q,

      and a convenient sufficient bound is

          sum_X (H-a(X)) exp(-a(X)^2/m)=o(W).

      The displayed `m=3` deletion vector obstructs only that particular
      balanced resolution; the explicit `Q_7` wreath factor itself induces
      a perfectly synchronized balanced resolution.  Audit and stand-alone
      corrected model prompt:
      `NESTED_BALANCED_SYNCHRONIZATION_AUDIT_20260724.md` and
      `EXACT_REMAINING_SYNC_THEOREM_BRIEF_20260724.md`.

1362. Twenty-six additional complete arbitrary-two-replacement

1363. The balanced-wreath absorption reduction is valid but its proposed
      leave bound is stronger than needed.  Exact middle wreath factors are
      unconditional by the MSW `C_(2m+1)`-factor, the automatic MWB tail from
      `Q=sqrt(m log m)` to `H=2 sqrt(m log m)` is `o(W)`, and an extendible
      quota-safe submatching with `R` completion wreaths satisfies
      `O_q<=nR`.  However

          sum_(q<Q) 1/c_q = Theta(sqrt(m)),

      so the cardinality-only condition can be weakened to

          R=o(W/(n sqrt(m))),

      gaining `sqrt(log m)`.  More generally, with quota slack
      `s_q=b_q-mu_q^M` and completion `C=F\M`, it is enough that

          sum_(q<Q) c_q^(-1)
            sum_S (mu_q^C(S)-s_q(S))_+ = o(W),

      which may allow a larger completion that fills slack.  The missing
      feature is extendibility into the same exact factor; an ordinary
      conflict-free almost-perfect matching does not provide it.  Audit:
      `BALANCED_WREATH_ABSORPTION_AUDIT_20260724.md`.

1364. MWB is equivalent by diagonalization to solving every fixed Gaussian
      window `q<=A sqrt(m)`.  On such a window the exact integer floor energy

          Q_q=sum_S (mu_q(S)-c_q)(mu_q(S)-c_q-1)

      satisfies `2O_q<=Q_q` and

          Q_q=||mu_q-(W/N_q)1||_2^2-beta_q,

      where `beta_q` is the unavoidable floor.  Overlaying an exact factor
      with a coordinate transposition and choosing complete sides of every
      ownership component is an exact integral heat bath.  It obeys

          E[Q_q(F_next)|F]
            <=(1-2/n)Q_q(F)+gamma_q(F),

      with

          gamma_q=E_tau[1/4 sum_K ||Delta_(K,q)||_2^2]-(2/n)beta_q.

      More sharply this is an equality after subtracting the nonnegative
      higher-harmonic surplus

          s_q=(1/4)E_tau||f_q-tau f_q||_2^2-(2/n)||f_q||_2^2.

      Thus the exact drift obstruction is `gamma_q-s_q`.
      Its discounted sum is identically

          E mathcalQ_A(F_T)-rho^T mathcalQ_A(F_0),

      so a small discounted corrected-noise hypothesis is essentially the
      desired terminal bound itself, not an independent simplification.

      Iteration for `n^2` steps kills the initial energy.  Thus a discounted
      `o(W)` bound on the positive weighted component variance is sufficient
      for fixed-window MWB and hence, after diagonalization, full MWB.  The
      bound itself is unproved and is the old integral component-noise gate
      in multistep form; fair iteration is not automatically energy-biased.
      A connected ownership overlay has one component, so covariance cancels
      all mean smoothing and the child energy is unchanged.
      The scale-correct local replacement for the too-strong constant-gap
      lemma is

          Gamma_A-S_A
            <=((2-eta_A)/n) mathcalQ_A
              +(C_A/n) H_A Cat_m.

      This would contract at rate `eta_A/n` and reach
      `O_A(H_A Cat_m)`.  It remains unproved; the universal bound
      `R_q<=Q_q+beta_q+lambda_q W` is far too large.

      For a fixed transposition there is an additional exact local parity
      floor.  Every ownership component has sides `K,tau K` (each wreath
      owns a `tau`-fixed middle interval), so each component preserves every
      pair sum `mu(S)+mu(tau S)`.  If

          b_q=(1/2) #{ {S,tau S}: pair sum is odd },
          G_q=(1/4)||f_q-tau f_q||^2-b_q,
          C_q=(1/4)sum_K||Delta_(K,q)||^2-b_q,

      then `G_q,C_q>=0` and the exact fixed-transposition drift is

          E[Q_q(F')|F,tau]=Q_q(F)-G_q+C_q.

      Thus the clean missing component theorem compares ideal integral
      pair gain `G` against component-bundling excess `C`; connected overlays
      have `G=C`.  Full audit:
      `MULTISTEP_COMPONENT_HEAT_FLOW_AUDIT_20260724.md`.

1365. Two fixed-window statements must be distinguished.  The unlabelled
      overload minimum on every `q<=A sqrt(m)` window is equivalent by
      diagonalization to MWB.  The labelled theorem aligning one exact factor
      with one common balanced nested resolution is strictly stronger and is
      only a sufficient route; no overload-to-labelled stability theorem is
      known.

      For the labelled route, orienting a wreath factor gives each owner a
      forced deletion permutation.  Any competing full nested flag is a
      second permutation of those deletions, and its synchronization loss is
      exactly the weighted area of the depths where the two prefix sets
      differ.  On a fixed Gaussian window the weights `1/c_q` are bounded
      above and below, so labelled alignment requires only `o(W)` total bad
      owner-depth incidences and therefore leaves all but `o(W)` owners
      completely unchanged through the window.

      One-step shift defects and bounded local containment do not control
      return time: a cyclic shift has zero shift defects and one maximal
      excursion, while a bandwidth-two Hamilton cycle of deletion positions
      stays in a fixed corridor yet has no proper common prefix.  Exact
      corridor Hall cuts were derived.  In the radius-one corridor, every
      owner permutation is a product of disjoint adjacent transpositions;
      the problem becomes simultaneous orientations of sparse sibling
      multigraphs with balanced indegrees, subject only to the conflict that
      one owner cannot toggle adjacent depths.  This is an exact integral
      common-flow formulation, still unproved.  Proof and independent audit:
      `CYCLIC_SHIFT_MARKED_RUN_REDUCTION_20260724.md` and
      `CYCLIC_SHIFT_MARKED_RUN_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT_20260724.md`.

1366. The four-block SCD product route reduces coefficient one to a compact
      balanced four-box theorem: uniformly for `delta R<=ell_i<=C R`, it is
      enough that the local contiguous-maximum length exceed the box width
      by `o(R^3)`.  Exact width additivity, the
      `Theta(W/R^3)` product-box count, Gaussian chain-height tails, and the

      A reset-free complementary portal was constructed that covers a
      quadratic two-directional target rectangle across all depths.  Its
      direct seam identity (the two baselines differ) is

          OR[X_u,...,X_0,Y_0,...,Y_z]
            =(m-A,B+u,m-B,A+z),

      and the equal-box portal core has exact length
      `|L_(2m-1)|+4q(q-1)`.  The safe high-coordinate bound is `m-2q+1`.

      An architecture-specific lower bound shows that separate fixed-line
      rank-`r-t` core epochs plus disjoint linear reset epochs pay critical
      `Theta(R^3)` cost.  This is not an unrestricted lower bound: every core
      epoch must lie on one fixed coordinate line, and the reset conclusion
      uses disjoint linear reset cost at productive seams.  The remaining
      positive lemma is a genuinely reset-free surface braid, or directly
      the compact four-box `width+o(R^3)` theorem.  The lead report and an
      independent audit accepted these claims after the stated corrections.
      **Later status:** item 1414 proves that the proposed uniform compact
      four-box local theorem is false on a closed dominance/boundary sector.
      Only equal/polygon-interior boxes and genuinely global cross-parent
      fusion remain live in this lane.
      A one-cube Jensen bound shows a linear expected first-shadow defect
      unless almost every first-shadow target is already robust inside one
      interaction component.  Audit:
      `MWB_FIXED_WINDOW_HEAT_BATH_AUDIT_20260724.md`.

1367. The compact three-box lane was independently audited.  The primitive

          w(R,R,r_1)+w(R,R,r_2)-w(R,R,R)

1368. The signed-subcube entropy lane and its dynamic deletion-swap
      construction were independently audited.  The Fenchel dual and the
      rank-uniform lower bounds are correct after treating the zero-free
      cube separately.  The Walsh formula must exclude `P=N=empty` (or count
      the coincident opposite faces with multiplicity), and the statement
      `ker A^T=0` concerns only the full column dictionary including the
      zero-free columns; it says nothing about `ker A` or economical
      subdictionaries.  Fixed-window repair must use the restricted
      functional `Psi_(<=K)`, not a global hole family containing deeper
      ranks.

      More importantly, swapping deletion positions `q,q+1` is an exact
      rank-isolated labelled operation: stage `q` changes only the depth-`q`
      owner target, and the number of toggled owners is exactly the labelled
      mismatch `e_q`.  Its orientation criterion is the exact Hakimi/Hall
      cut condition.  However the one-pass diamond sweep is a sufficient
      subclass, not an exact parametrization of all nested resolutions; it
      reaches only products `tau_1^e1 ... tau_K^eK`.  The optimization must
      therefore be global over one adaptive sequence of orientations,
      because each choice determines the next graph.  The remaining theorem
      in this lane is an adaptive Hall-plus-short-transport lemma for that
      sequential policy.  Report and audit:
      `MATH_ATTACK_I_ENTROPY_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md`.

1369. The wreath-trade/Markov-basis lane was independently audited and its

      `ker_Z U_r`, including in characteristics dividing `r` (although its

      The exact Hilbert/Max-Cut identity is

          Psi(F_I)-Psi(F)=-(1/2)<d_I,d_(I^c)>_H,

      with fair resampling drift `-(A_tau-V_tau)/8`.  Hence the smallest
      qualitative theorem for this move class is a local-minimum statement:
      every exact factor having no positive component-correlation cut for
      any transposition must already have fixed-window energy
      `O_A(H_A Cat_m)`.  This remains unproved.  The signed lattice by itself
      cannot provide positivity, support feasibility, or a common owner
      flow.

      Corrections incorporated into the report include: the bounded MSW

      theorem remains motivational until its accumulated-cut estimate is

      `MATH_ATTACK_B_TRADE_MARKOV_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md`.

1370. A factorial family of genuine profile-3 alternating-C8 absorbers
      exists. Every normalized rooted four-label window has exactly
      `(m-1)!(m-2)!` unoriented partners, and toggling the universal
      alternating cycle replaces two old wreaths by two new wreaths. The

          r_1=8,        r_q=4q+6  (2<=q<=m-1),

      but these are removal/addition masses, not necessarily the number of
      nonzero histogram cells or half-L1 distance; the depth-m effect is
      zero. Pointed-owner counts 9 and 4q+6 are upper bounds.

      Consequently one fixed-A trade changes the weighted overload or
      labelled objective by O_A(m). Since the factor has
      Cat_m=W/(2m+1) wreaths, any o(Cat_m) family of such local switches
      changes either objective by only o(W). Thus a conventional sparse
      absorber cannot repair a linear fixed-window defect. Factorial
      ambient abundance does not furnish a disjoint positive-density
      reservoir or a short bundled Hall correction.

      The support condition that a completion shadow lie in at least q+1
      uncovered middle roots is necessary and coarse, not sufficient for
      cyclic completion. The residual clone-Hall theorem exactly extends
      already fixed roots into nested flags but does not cyclically package
      those roots. Finally, EABS_A is merely an equivalent rewriting of
      fixed-window overload MWB (take the safe partial factor empty), not a
      new absorber theorem. Corrected report:
      `MATH_ATTACK_A_ABSORPTION_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md`.

1371. Adjacent swaps of deletion positions q,q+1 give an exact
      rank-isolated labelled operation, provided K+1<=m. In one ascending
      pass, the stage-q toggle indicator is exactly the final depth-q owner
      mismatch; later stages preserve that prefix set. The two choices per
      owner form a sparse multigraph G_q on rank-m-q targets. Prescribed
      indegrees b are feasible exactly when

          e_G(U) <= b(U) <= e_G(U)+|delta_G(U)|

      for every vertex family U. Allowing loads in {c_q,c_q+1} gives the
      corresponding lower/upper capacity cuts.

      If tau_q(b) is the minimum number of toggles supported by the directed
      owner edges, then the correct ledger is

          O_q(F) <= (1/2)||b-mu_q||_1
                 <= tau_q(b) <= T_q=e_q(F,P).

      Equality with tau_q requires that the chosen adaptive orientation be
      minimum-cost for that same b; nonminimal circulations can preserve the
      histogram while changing later owner states. The graphs are
      endogenous: each earlier ownerwise choice changes the carried letter
      and therefore the next graph. Independent rankwise Hall or min-cost
      solutions are invalid.

      The exact remaining labelled theorem is an adaptive sequential policy
      satisfying every Hall cut and total fixed-window toggle cost o(W). It
      is sufficient and strictly stronger than overload MWB. A directed
      even-cycle example proves that Hall feasibility plus overload one can
      require linear supported transport in an abstract sparse graph, but no
      exact-wreath realization of that obstruction is known. Corrected
      reports: `MATH_ATTACK_D_DISCREPANCY_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md` and
      `MATH_ATTACK_E_CYCLIC_SYNC_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md`.

1372. The floor-corrected exact-factor heat lane has an exact Max-Cut form.
      For the full energy

          Q_q=sum_S (mu_q(S)-c_q)(mu_q(S)-c_q-1),

      one has Q_q>=2(D_q+E_q)>=2O_q. Overlaying F with tau F and choosing
      complete ownership-component sides gives genuine exact factors. For
      component effects Delta_K, define

          A_tau=||sum_K Delta_K||_A^2,
          R_tau(epsilon)=||sum_K epsilon_K Delta_K||_A^2,
          beta_tau=min_epsilon R_tau(epsilon).

      The antipodal identity is

          Q_A(F_epsilon)+Q_A(F_-epsilon)
            =2Q_A(F)+(R_tau(epsilon)-A_tau)/2.

      Hence the better antipode gains at least
      (A_tau-beta_tau)/4. The qualitative route-specific missing theorem is
      that every transposition-cut local minimum already has energy
      O_A(H_A Cat_m). Finite strict descent would then prove fixed-window
      overload MWB. This is sufficient, not a necessary characterization of
      the OR conjecture.

      Continuous Johnson/Specht smoothing alone cannot prove it: component
      variance is an independent support-feasible correlation term. The
      occurrence-pair formula for fair heat is exactly

          A-V=4(P_S^sep+P_(tau S)^sep-C_(S,tau S)^sep),

      so same-target duplicates separated across components help, while
      opposite-target cross-component mixing hurts. Abstract pair patterns
      do not constitute exact-factor counterexamples.

      A fixed transposition word of O(n) steps gives only constant coherent
      contraction. From a worst factor, a one-step rate 1-eta/n needs
      O(n log W)=O(n^2) steps to reach the Catalan floor; alternatively, a
      local-minimum theorem avoids iteration. Multistep noise identities
      require the transposition word to be fixed before component signs and
      an explicit integer-floor restitution term. The positive-cut LM_A and
      excess-noise FEN_A statements are sufficient and not known necessary
      or mutually comparable with arbitrary-permutation heat lemmas.

      The signed octahedral selector map is integrally onto, but only in the
      unrestricted signed lattice. It supplies no positivity, packing,
      quota, or nesting theorem. Corrected reports:
      `MATH_ATTACK_C_HEAT_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md` and
      `MATH_ATTACK_J_ALGEBRAIC_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md`.

1373. The rotor/SCD chronology problem has been solved conditionally on one
      full-SCD path-forest statistic. For a fixed full SCD D clipped at
      H<=m-1, let

          Phi_min(D)=min_(spanning directed rotor path forests)
                       sum_(d<=H) (2d+1)p_d.

      The exact coordinate-orbit circulation can be recolored and Eulerized
      so that every color is a genuine full SCD and the total weighted run
      starts are at most Q Phi_min(D), with every physical circuit reset
      charged. The d=0 transition is the ordinary bottom/top swap rather
      than the positive-radius rotor formula. Hence a sequence of full SCDs
      with Phi_min=o(W) for every fixed A would give a literal central-band
      word of length W+o(W), then coefficient one after the audited tails.

      The original converse for an arbitrarily preselected forest was
      false: one SCD may admit both bad and better path forests. The optimized
      Phi_min formulation is the correct statistic. The canonical BTK/GK
      SCD has no positive-radius directed rotor edges below the clipping
      class, yielding a Theta(W sqrt(m)) toll in every fixed window.
      Independent admissible recoloring is also essentially maximally
      switched only when chronology is fixed before colors are sampled;
      adaptive post-color routing is not covered by that probability
      argument. The deterministic pair-capacity obstruction is
      routing-independent. Corrected report:
      `MATH_ATTACK_G_ROTOR_SCD_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md`.

1374. The audited first-wave implication diagram, unconditional theorem
      inventory, redundancies, and five genuinely distinct remaining lemmas
      are consolidated in `MATH_ATTACK_FIRST_WAVE_SYNTHESIS_20260724.md`.
      Of these, the positive-cut/local-minimum lemma is shortest only in
      logical implication distance; no lane yet has quantitative evidence
      selecting a probable winner.

1375. The exact finite objective has been re-audited without running any
      search. For nonzero masks, exact values are proved for K=1,...,10 and
      K=12:

          1,2,4,7,12,21,37,72,128,254,   and   nu(12)=926.

      The unresolved set is exactly

          {11,13,14,15,16,17,18,19},

      with current certified intervals

          nu(11) in [465,477],
          nu(13) in [1719,1852],
          nu(14) in [3434,3676],
          nu(15) in [6438,7352],
          nu(16) in [12873,14704],
          nu(17) in [24313,29408],
          nu(18) in [48623,58816],
          nu(19) in [92381,117632].

      For the literal problem including mask zero, add one to every value or
      endpoint. Upper witnesses through K=14 are directly verified where
      stated; the later uppers are deterministic trimmed lifts. Failed or
      unterminated searches and local DRAT edit-neighborhood closures do not
      improve the global lower endpoints. K=11 remains the only credible
      global equality-model enumeration target. K=13 onward is increasingly
      lemma-first; one-entry improvements of the K=14 base propagate far too
      weakly to close the later gaps. The strongest finite common target is a
      nonsaturated rank-count equality/stability theorem, not another
      saturated-onion local search. Audit:
      `EXACT_K_LT20_STATUS_AUDIT_20260724.md` and
      `FINITE_K_STATUS_20260724.md`.

1376. Standard discrete convexity does not remove the positive-fibre gate.
      On the binary exact-factor fibre, no nontrivial one-wreath exchange is
      feasible: equality of two middle-incidence columns recovers the same
      unoriented cyclic order. Consequently the genuine factor domain is
      neither M-convex, M-natural-convex, nor L-natural-convex. The same
      M/M-natural obstruction holds for every nonsingleton joint rank-load
      image because a one-coordinate load exchange violates the exact point
      margins.

      On an ownership-component cube, for weighted component effects v_K,
      the half floor-energy has exact mixed curvature

          Delta_K Delta_L Psi_H = <v_K,v_L>_H.

      Thus L-natural convexity has the wrong sign for the positive-cut lane:
      nonpositive off-diagonal Gram entries make the current corner minimal,
      whereas a positive Gram cut is precisely legal descent. At actual rank
      two, the MSW factor supplies more than twice the ambient dimension in
      genuine switchable effects for every m>=9, so no reorientation makes
      that full-depth component cube L-natural-convex. This rank-two example
      does not lie in a fixed shallow Gaussian window.

      The correct exact local-to-global statement uses the augmented matrix

          Ahat_H = [[A_m,0],[B_H,-I]]

      together with the genuine box 0<=x<=1, 0<=u<=W. A feasible factor is
      globally floor-energy-minimal iff it has no feasible improving
      augmented-Graver move. Connected ownership components are squarefree
      augmented Graver moves between factor vertices, but cancellation-
      minimal disconnected packets can also occur. The explicit two-component
      packet is currently proved only when H>=m-2. If every individual
      component toward a comparator is nonimproving, the exact near-global
      ledger is

          Psi_H(F)-Psi_H(G)
            <= (1/2)(sum_K ||v_K||_H^2-||sum_K v_K||_H^2)
            <= (1/2)sum_K ||v_K||_H^2.

      No o(W) estimate for this component-variance residue is known. Hence
      the positive-cut/local-minimum lemma LM_A remains the surviving gate;
      standard M/L convexity neither proves nor disproves it. Reports:
      `MATH_ATTACK_Z_DISCRETE_CONVEXITY_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md` and
      `MATH_ATTACK_Z_DISCRETE_CONVEXITY_AUDIT_20260724.md`.

1377. The depth-one wreath problem has an exact colored-cycle normal form,
      but it does not bootstrap rank by rank. Reindexing each odd-graph
      C_(2m+1) by step two gives a Johnson cycle. Its lower edge colors are
      the angle colors, whereas its upper edge colors are automatically all
      rank-(m+1) sets exactly once. For m>=3,

          O_1 = M_1 + (r_1-t_1)_+,
          r_1=2W/(m+2),

      so O_1=o(W) iff the angle-color defect M_1=o(W).

      Cutting every wreath at one fixed coordinate z gives a family of
      complement-ended Johnson geodesics on the remaining 2m coordinates.
      This correspondence is bijective only modulo independent reversal of
      each path (or after adding independent orientations). The path vertices
      partition the middle layer and their edge unions partition the next
      layer. Exact formulas split the angle colors into internal intersections,
      two caps per path, and turn complements. The two near-rainbow deficits
      in this exact normal form are asymptotically equivalent to M_1=o(W).

      A perfect inclusion matching whose associated Johnson graph is a
      spanning complement-ended linear forest is a stronger exact sufficient
      formulation, not equivalent to the o(W)-defect completion lemma absent
      a near-perfect-to-perfect repair theorem. Positive-density four- and
      five-coordinate gadgets prove that generic lower/upper/turn rainbowness
      neither enforces complementary geodesicity nor controls depth two; they
      do not obstruct completion of the particular near-spanning rainbow
      forest or prove an asymptotic O_1-to-O_2 failure.

      More generally, for one oriented wreath define

          V^q_(pi,j)=I_pi(j,m-q).

      In the valid boundary range,

          V^q_j intersect V^q_(j+1)=V^(q+1)_(j+1),
          V^q_j union     V^q_(j+1)=V^(q-1)_j.

      Hence the level-q vertex, lower-edge-color, and upper-edge-color loads
      are respectively mu_q, mu_(q+1), and mu_(q-1). This is one coupled
      occurrence-level cycle tower. The exact 2q fringe count after a fixed
      coordinate cut gives a Theta_A(W) loss for the naive discard or labelled
      seam ledger, not an intrinsic lower bound on unlabelled overload. Thus
      no depth-one-to-Gaussian bootstrap follows from the current forest,
      one-cut, or local-rainbow hypotheses; the unlabelled fixed-window MWB
      theorem remains open. Reports:
      `MATH_ATTACK_Q_COUPLED_CYCLE_TOWER_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md` and
      `MATH_ATTACK_Q_COUPLED_CYCLE_TOWER_AUDIT_20260724.md`.

1378. Signed-face repair admits an exact entropy--geometry characterization.
      For a nonempty fixed-window lower-hole family H, restrict to proper
      opposite signed faces C(P,N) with free set U and use the canonical
      two-copy block cost

          gamma_C=2 nu(|U|)+1_(P nonempty)+1_(N nonempty),

      with nu(0)=0. This is the exact length of the canonical block, not a
      proved optimum over arbitrary words covering that face. For a
      probability distribution pi on H, define

          delta(pi)=max{ ||pi||_infty/2, max_C pi(C)/gamma_C }.

      The Poisson repair functional has the exact dual form

          Psi = max_pi
                  [1+Ent(pi)+log(2 delta(pi))]/delta(pi).

      Its fractional and deterministic face-cover costs satisfy

          D_frac=max_pi 1/delta(pi)=1/min_pi delta(pi),
          D_frac <= D_det <= Psi
                 <= D_frac[1+log(2|H|/D_frac)].

      For the empty hole family all three objectives are separately zero.
      The empty-anchor full-cube column is excluded: its formal two-copy cost
      is 2nu(n), whereas one economical copy costs nu(n). Exclusion preserves
      o(W) feasibility because either cost is at least W, but not the exact
      finite optimum.

      For every nonempty residual G subset H put

          rho(G)=max{1/2, max_C |G intersect C|/gamma_C}.

      Uniform dual witnesses give

          D_frac >= |G|/rho(G),
          Psi >= |G|[1+log(2rho(G))]/rho(G).

      Conversely, if every residual larger than u has rho at least R, greedy
      dense-face peeling gives the actual constructions

          D_det <= 2u+|H|/R,
          Psi <= 2u+|H|[1+log(2R)]/R.

      Hence when |H|=O(W), o(W) fractional repair, deterministic repair,
      Poisson repair, and hereditary unbounded density in every linear-sized
      residual are equivalent. A density-R face must meet at least ceil(R)
      depths and have free dimension at least R^2/2-1. For every nonempty
      depth subset Q, with L_Q=min{|Q|,sqrt(2n)},

          D_frac >= M_Q/L_Q,
          Psi >= [1+log(2L_Q)]M_Q/L_Q.

      An abstract family consisting of the relevant central slices of one
      high-dimensional proper signed face has Theta(W) aggregate holes,
      o(W) holes per rank, deterministic repair O(W/sqrt(n)), and Poisson
      repair Theta(W log(n)/sqrt(n)). Thus summable defect is not necessary
      for this repair architecture. This family is not known to arise from
      an exact wreath factor.

      The remaining route-specific theorem FG_A asks for exact factors whose
      every sufficiently large residual hole family contains an increasingly
      economical proper opposite face. It would directly prove coefficient
      one by peeling, but is neither proved nor necessary for MWB or arbitrary
      OR words. Reports:
      `MATH_ATTACK_V_ENTROPY_GEOMETRY_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md` and
      `MATH_ATTACK_V_ENTROPY_GEOMETRY_AUDIT_20260724.md`.

1379. Permanent prefix freezing has an exact Boolean-flow theorem and an
      exact irreversible-release obstruction. For a nested owner system with
      stopping depths, split the residual Boolean inclusion network at every
      node and impose balanced lower/upper capacities on layers 1,...,K. The
      terminal must have exact demand R_K, equivalently a fixed return arc of
      value R_K; layer zero has only released supplies and no residual-capacity
      arc. Hoffman's theorem gives two complete staircase families (U) and
      (L); their K=1 specializations are the two ordinary Hall inequalities.
      Integral capacities and the unprojected node-arc matrix give an integral
      suffix-path completion whenever these cuts hold.

      If R_q owners have been permanently released before depth q, every
      balanced completion respecting all frozen prefixes satisfies

          O_q(L) <= e_q(L,Q) <= R_q.

      Consequently, with M_q=max_(s<=q) O_s(L), every such prefix scheme has

          prefix cost = sum_q R_q/c_q
                      >= sum_q M_q/c_q.

      The upper inequality requires that Q respect the frozen prefixes; it is
      false for an arbitrary balanced resolution.

      There is an exact rank-one Boolean-owner counterexample. Starting from
      a balanced nested resolution, swap the first two deletion letters for
      R=floor(N_1/sqrt(m)) owners chosen from a large independent set of low
      targets. Then

          O_1=R,        O_q=0 (q>=2),

      the minimum labelled mismatch is R, every residual Hoffman cut is
      feasible, but the exact minimum permanent-prefix cost is

          R sum_(q<=K) 1/c_q = Theta_A(W)

      for K=ceil(A sqrt(m)). Thus feasibility, integrality, o(W) overload,
      and o(W) labelled mismatch do not by themselves overcome irreversible
      release.

      This is a separation only in the class of arbitrary integral nested
      Boolean owner systems. The example need not satisfy exact-wreath point
      margins or cyclic packaging, so it does not refute exact-factor prefix
      freezing, labelled synchronization, MWB, or resynchronizing schemes.
      Reports: `MATH_ATTACK_O_PREFIX_FREEZING_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md` and
      `MATH_ATTACK_O_PREFIX_FREEZING_AUDIT_20260724.md`.

1380. The canonical Catalan component hierarchy has a positive-density but
      shallow-inert tail, and noncommuting preparations create many seams
      without proving component dispersion. For the MSW transposition
      hierarchy, a component of suffix depth r and local index j has

          ||Delta_(j,R)||_1,
          |supp Delta_(j,R)|
             <= (4j+10)(Cat_j+Cat_(j+1)).

      The r=0 case must be proved separately by retaining all n slots. Summing
      over suffix depths r>=L gives O(W/sqrt(L)). Yet when L and m-L grow,
      those components contain (3/8+o(1)) of all wreaths. Thus one can replace
      3/8 of all owners while changing only o(W) first-shadow coordinates.
      This proves inertness only for the exhibited deep-suffix tail subcube,
      not for the entire fixed Catalan cube or an exceptional assignment of
      the remaining shallow components.

      A concrete noncommuting preparation creates (1/8+o(1))Cat_m crossing
      seams. A Johnson-spectral argument also gives a balanced preparation
      with beta Cat_m-o(Cat_m) seams, where

          q=25(2-sqrt(3))/64,
          gamma=1-q=(14+25sqrt(3))/64,
          beta=(1287-700sqrt(3))/512.

      The exact commutator table is sigma, tau sigma tau, tau sigma, sigma tau
      according to the two old/new component signs. Mixed signs certify
      noncommuting target seams, but not that those seams lie in distinct
      components after the overlay is recomputed.

      Three audited barriers remain. Disjoint local two-for-two charts can
      fill at most two holes per chart, so repairing Theta(W) holes needs
      Omega(n) adaptive rounds. Random component signs with both conditional
      probabilities uniformly bounded away from zero retain a linear expected
      defect under a finite-energy hypothesis; this is only an expectation or
      high-probability obstruction and does not exclude a rare deterministic
      assignment. Recomputed moves preserve total load on every orbit of the
      generated coordinate group, giving an exact profile-deficit lower bound.

      A precise conditional NAE lemma does survive: if ell hole--duplicate
      two-point orbits have duplicates split across at least two recomputed
      components and the total fair expected new-hole risk over all initially
      covered orbits is at most theta ell with theta<1/2, then conditional
      expectation yields one legal cube vertex improving holes by at least
      (1/2-theta)ell. Producing such pairs injectively, dispersing them among
      components, controlling risk, and renewing the gain for O(n) rounds are
      all unproved. Reports:
      `MATH_ATTACK_K_CATALAN_REBUNDLING_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md` and
      `MATH_ATTACK_K_CATALAN_REBUNDLING_AUDIT_20260724.md`.

1381. PBBS rebundling by alternating C8s has a lossless local balance
      classification, but no positive-density supply theorem. Deleting the
      four old edges of a simple alternating C8 gives four residual paths.
      Their old/new component-incidence multigraph is connected, so if r and
      s are the old and new component counts then r+s<=5 and the new balance
      equations have rank exactly s-1 modulo the old ones. With centered path
      vectors zeta_i, the exact new-shape conditions are:

          4: automatic;
          31: the singleton vector is zero;
          22: one designated pair is opposite;
          211: both singleton vectors are zero;
          1111: all four vectors are zero.

      A generic zero or opposite pair is sufficient only if it matches the
      actual new cut topology.

      For a path P of L vertices, omitted-label counts t and endpoint counts
      e satisfy

          2 zeta(P)=n(e-t)+(L-n)1.

      Sewing paths of total length kn gives a point-regular component iff the
      internal-plus-seam omitted-label count is k for every coordinate. At
      k=1 the sewn component is literally a wreath.

      For the initial canonical PBBS factor, every alternating C8 is
      equivalent to a clean directed C4 in a loopless outdegree-two digraph
      attached to a unique (m-1)-core. Every such directed cycle lies in at
      most six residual PBBS labels. Hence there are at most

          12 binom(n,m-1) < 12W

      supported alternating C8s; a factor edge lies in at most 8m and a
      middle vertex in at most 16m. These restrictions are not preserved
      automatically after switching away from the initial PBBS factor.

      If component levels are ell_j, the exact component potential obeys

          E=Cat_m-c=sum_j(ell_j-1),
          nE <= L <= 2nE,

      and one alternating C8 improves E by at most three. Thus, conditional
      on a Theta(Cat_m) initial excess, o(Cat_m) local operations cannot
      finish. Neither that initial PBBS excess nor a positive-density family
      of clean, cancellation-compatible, jointly applicable connectors is
      proved. Infinite centered-segment and label-token examples give only
      abstract local obstructions; the latter is not a PBBS or catalytic
      lower bound once other components may import tokens.

      The exact remaining PBBS lane is therefore to prove clean-cycle density,
      topology-compatible cancellation density, a dynamic balanced route, and
      a relative cleanup that preserves shadow progress. Nothing here proves
      MWB or labelled synchronization. Reports:
      `MATH_ATTACK_R_PBBS_REBUNDLING_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md` and
      `MATH_ATTACK_R_PBBS_REBUNDLING_AUDIT_20260724.md`.

1382. The positive-cut lane has an exact parity-floor restitution identity.
      For one transposition and each unordered nonfixed target pair p, let
      z_K be the old-side load imbalance contributed by ownership component
      K, let z=sum_K z_K, let ell be the preserved pair load, and put
      pi=ell mod 2. For a common component signing epsilon define
      u_p=sum_K epsilon_K z_K. Then, for the full weighted floor energy,

          Q_A(F_epsilon)-Q_A(F)
            = Rfrak_tau(epsilon)-Gfrak_tau,

          Gfrak_tau=(1/2)sum_(q,p)(z_p^2-pi_p)/c_q,
          Rfrak_tau=(1/2)sum_(q,p)(u_p^2-pi_p)/c_q.

      Each unweighted numerator is a nonnegative integer, but the weighted
      functionals need not be integer-valued. In Hilbert normalization this
      is exactly

          Q_A(F_epsilon)-Q_A(F)=(R_tau(epsilon)-A_tau)/4.

      Thus F is cut-local for tau iff its all-old signing already minimizes
      the parity restitution over the whole common-signing cube. This is an
      aggregate fixed-window assertion, not a separate pairwise optimum.

      With w_KL=<d_K,d_L>_A, exact cut-locality is

          sum_(KL crossing I) w_KL <= 0  for every component subset I.

      The resulting signed Gram graph satisfies an L1 cut-cone inequality and
      routes every individual positive demand through negative capacity, but
      gives no simultaneous bounded-congestion or squared-Euclidean estimate.
      The previously proposed O_A(W)-per-rank quadratic-locking bound is not
      proved: the available cyclic geometry controls expected L1 displacement,
      while balanced component effects can have quadratic restitution of
      order t^2 with only linear occurrence mass.

      Connected ownership overlays for every transposition would make all
      these component moves energy-neutral and hence give one explicit route
      to a high-energy counterexample to LM_A. Such connectedness is
      sufficient, not necessary: a disconnected overlay with every signed
      cut nonpositive would also refute LM_A. The canonical MSW factor is not
      connected for the audited transposition when m>=3, and its known
      Cat_(m-4) first-shadow holes form only a certified subfamily, not an
      upper bound on all its holes.

      Therefore LM_A remains exactly open: high energy must force a positive
      ownership-component cut for some transposition. Proving it would give
      fixed-window overload by finite strict descent; refuting it would only
      refute this route, not MWB or the OR conjecture. Reports:
      `MATH_ATTACK_L_POSITIVE_CUT_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md` and
      `MATH_ATTACK_L_POSITIVE_CUT_AUDIT_20260724.md`.

1383. Dimension lifts have exact endpoint compression but a strong
      multi-run rank-slack obstruction. If a universal k-word of length n
      ends in a strict descending inclusion tail of length t, its one-bit
      lift has length 2n-t+1. With an ascending prefix of length s and a
      descending suffix of length t, the two-ended lift has length

          n+2+max(0,n-s-t),

      which is 2n-s-t+2 in the disjoint regime. Every lost transformed
      witness is recovered by an exact seam interval. After deleting adjacent
      equal entries, endpoint-chain lengths are at most k, so the maximum
      one- and two-ended savings are k-1 and 2k-2.

      More generally, tag the lifted word by absence/presence of the new bit.
      For old target rank r, let M=binom(k,r) and suppose the high tag has q
      runs. Interval-antichain and product-chain arguments give the sharp
      rank-sensitive inequalities

          zero positions >= M,
          high positions >= M-r[binom(q,2)+3q],
          total length >= 2M-r[binom(q,2)+3q].

      For one transition the stronger special bound is

          total length >= 2M-r,

      so an intact base of length M+d can save at most d+r. The coefficient
      is r, not the ambient dimension k; the original report's k-bound is
      valid but nonsharp.

      Conditional only on the printed certified length endpoints, exact
      even-to-odd central-rank lifts from old dimensions 12,14,16,18 require
      at least

          q = 5, 9, 17, 31

      high runs respectively. At those minimum q values, large high mass is
      forced. For much larger q the same inequalities allow singleton high
      runs, so the theorem is a run-count/high-mass tradeoff rather than a
      simultaneous long-run theorem. Endpoint and bounded-seam lifts cannot
      close the hard finite steps; a genuine multi-transition double interval
      cover is required. No certificate data or search was used. Reports:
      `FINITE_LIFT_SLACK_THEOREMS_20260724.md` and
      `FINITE_LIFT_SLACK_THEOREMS_AUDIT_20260724.md`.

1384. Ownership-overlay expansion has exact leakage and fragmentation
      identities, but no sign theorem for fair heat. For a transposition tau,
      define a_CD as the number of middle windows owned by C and by tau D.
      The symmetric owner-orbit graph has one edge per tau-orbit of
      off-diagonal bipartite ownership edges; the literal raw quotient would
      have multiplicity 2a_CD. If d_C is the shorter cyclic distance between
      the transposed coordinates, then

          a_CC=n-2d_C+2*1_(d_C=m),
          deg(C)=2 min(d_C,m-1).

      For m>=2 every component is nontrivial, Eulerian, and contains a cycle;
      m=1 is the isolated boundary case. The graph has large average degree
      and cycle rank, but these orientation-blind expansion statistics do not
      determine heat descent.

      For a depth-q target S and component K, let x_K(S) be its cyclic
      occurrences and e_K(S) its nongenuine containment leakage. Exact middle
      ownership gives

          (q+1)x_K(S)+e_K(S)
            =(q+1)x_K(tau S)+e_K(tau S),

          sum_S e_K(S)=n|K|[binom(m,q)-(q+1)].

      Hence every component imbalance is a signed leakage gradient. If
      d_K=x_K(S)-x_K(tau S), z=sum_K d_K, and

          D_p=sum_(K<J)d_K d_J,

      then the exact residual identity is

          D_p=B_p-M_p-R_p,

      where B is coherent pair imbalance, M is opposite-sign mixing, and R
      is within-component multiplicity residue. Equality at z=0 requires all
      d_K=0; the sign-of-z characterization applies only for z nonzero.

      Summed over the fixed window,

          A_tau-V_tau=4 D_A(F,tau),
          E Q_A(child)=Q_A(F)-D_A(F,tau).

      Thus separated same-target duplicates help fair heat, while separated
      opposite-target occurrences hurt it. Component fragmentation, degree,
      or cycle rank alone cannot force the sign. Direct arbitrary-permutation
      overlays retain the corresponding parity floor and Max-Cut formulas.
      Layering a fixed permutation word only joins/coarsens endpoint overlay
      components; if an adjacent overlay is connected, the layered overlay is
      connected and produces no new fragmentation. A viable short-word route
      must therefore switch sequentially and recompute components.

      The fixed-word signed obstruction is valid for actual ranks
      2<=r<=n-2 and lives only in signed tangent space. Section 13 refutes a
      universal fixed-middle-edge proof of direct equivariance, not direct
      equivariance itself. Neither RF_A nor LM_A, MWB, or a labelled theorem
      follows. Reports:
      `MATH_ATTACK_AB_OVERLAY_EXPANSION_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md` and
      `MATH_ATTACK_AB_OVERLAY_EXPANSION_AUDIT_20260724.md`.

1385. The SDP/Max-Cut lane separates three exact floors but leaves both
      amplitude locking and global component compatibility uncontrolled. For
      one transposition orbit p and component coefficients z_(pK), define

          A_tau=sum_p alpha_p(sum_K z_(pK))^2,
          Pi_tau=sum_p alpha_p(ell_p mod 2),
          B_tau=sum_p alpha_p min_signs(sum_K sign_K z_(pK))^2,
          beta_tau=min_common_signs sum_p alpha_p(sum_K sign_K z_(pK))^2.

      Then

          Pi_tau <= B_tau <= beta_tau <= A_tau,

      and the exact best component cut is

          C_tau^*=(A_tau-beta_tau)/4.

      Thus ideal parity gain A-Pi loses first to rowwise amplitude locking
      B-Pi and then to the global common-sign/holonomy loss beta-B. These two
      losses cannot be collapsed into one purely global obstruction.

      Averaging the ideal gain at rank r over all transpositions gives

          E_tau G_(tau,q)
            = 2/[binom(n,2)c_q]
              sum_(ST in J(n,r)) floor((mu(S)-mu(T))^2/4).

      Its kernel is exactly the set (not cone) of integer 1-Lipschitz loads
      on the Johnson graph. There are point-regular, correctly totalled,
      depth-one 1-Lipschitz load vectors with

          Q_1/W -> 1/64,     O_1/W -> 1/128,

      so ideal transposition gain alone need not see high floor energy. A
      signed exact-middle selector realizes simultaneous such histograms, but
      not a nonnegative exact factor or a local minimum of the unrestricted
      signed lattice.

      For the genuine component Gram graph w_KL=<d_K,d_L>_H (unordered
      pairs), exact bounds include

          C_tau^* >= (A_tau-V_tau)/4 + M_tau/2,

      where M_tau is the maximum |w|-matching, and

          C_tau^* >= (A_tau-V_tau)/4
                     +(1/36)(sum_(K<L)w_KL^2)^(1/2).

      Matrix-Frobenius notation introduces an extra sqrt(2). At a cut-local
      factor, negative coherence must dominate both the maximum matching and
      the off-diagonal quadratic mass. The forest incidence case admits a
      simultaneous rowwise minimizer; feedback rows isolate the exact place
      where holonomy enters.

      A three-vector parity example obstructs only the basic elliptope/vector
      residual relaxation: metric triangle inequalities remove it, so it is
      not an obstruction to all SDPs. Large positive coherence in the MSW
      local components is favorable for Bernoulli cuts unless larger
      components cancel it; it refutes a sparse-overlap proof, not Bernoulli
      thinning itself. Any final implication must control ideal gain and
      bundling loss for the same transposition, uniformly along descent.
      LM_A and MWB remain open. Reports:
      `MATH_ATTACK_AA_SDP_MAXCUT_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md` and
      `MATH_ATTACK_AA_SDP_MAXCUT_AUDIT_20260724.md`.

1386. The rotor/SCD lane has two exact new reductions and a fixed-frame
      Gaussian obstruction. Any saturated symmetric-chain decomposition of
      the central band extends integrally to a full SCD by one doubly
      stochastic comparison/identity matching at each outer rank; each band
      chain remains a contiguous subchain.

      For a finite directed rotor graph D, the minimum number of components
      in a spanning directed path forest is exactly

          pc(D)=min_orders max_(S subset V_L)
                   (|S|-|Gamma_order(S)|),

      where Gamma is taken in the split-copy bipartite graph of forward arcs.
      It is not the external neighborhood in the original digraph. Thus, for
      one fixed SCD, the exact optimized toll is the sum over radius classes
      of (2d+1) times this ordered Hall deficiency; the SCD must be common to
      every depth.

      Cutting an exact odd wreath factor at one coordinate supplies genuine
      complementary Johnson paths and a physical rotor skeleton whose bare
      run toll can be o(W). The missing binary radius labeling must satisfy
      all lower and upper nested-shadow bijections simultaneously and include
      the boundary condition x_(v,H+1)=0. Bare nested feasibility or a
      separately chosen low-toll labeling does not suffice.

      If every selected rotor arc uses one fixed global coordinate matching,
      rank-m-q targets split into full/empty/split-pair types. With P_q path
      components through radius at least q and type-capacity deficit D_(m,q),

          q P_q >= D_(m,q).

      For q=x sqrt(m),

          D_(m,q)/W -> e^(-x^2) Delta(x),
          Delta(x)=Phi_G(x/2)-e^(x^2)Phi_G(-3x/2)>0.

      Hence every fixed window has a positive toll lower bound

          liminf Phi/W >=
            2 integral_0^A e^(-x^2)Delta(x)/x dx > 0.

      This rules out native fixed-pair/Bender--Knuth frames. If exceptional
      mixed-frame arcs are allowed, the exact repair inequality forces only
      Omega_A(W/sqrt(m)) exceptional arcs, equivalently Omega_A(W) affected
      q-window starts; an Omega(W)-arc claim was too strong. Mixed or
      phase-dependent coordinate frames remain open.

      The general sufficient theorem is one full integral SCD with optimized
      fixed-window rotor toll o(W). The cut-odd-wreath nested-label theorem is
      a stronger structured sublane, not equivalent to every rotor/SCD
      solution. Neither is proved. Reports:
      `MATH_ATTACK_S_RSCD_ROTOR_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md` and
      `MATH_ATTACK_S_RSCD_ROTOR_AUDIT_20260724.md`.

1387. The reset-free four-box portal covers a strictly larger spill family
      at no additional word cost, but remains far from CB4. In each legal
      high/low orientation, existing neighboring portal blocks give literal
      witnesses for two spill families. A selected injective X-spill family
      has exact count

          C_X(2t)=t(t-1)(5t^2-2t-1)/6,
          C_X(2t+1)=t^2(5t^2+3t-2)/6,

      hence C_X(q)=5q^4/96+O(q^3). Together with the previously hard family
      across four orientations, the selected certified family has exact
      leading size

          4 binom(q+3,4)+4C_X(q)=3q^4/8+O(q^3).

      The symmetric Y-spill witnesses are also literal, but X and Y overlap
      without being identical. Thus the displayed 3/8 count is exact for the
      deliberately selected X-subfamily and only a lower bound on all newly
      covered spill targets.

      The unchanged word has exact length

          |W_(m,q)|=|L_(2m-1)|+4q(q-1)
                   =w_4(m,m,m,m)-(m+1)+4q(q-1).

      Spill witnesses are internal intervals and add no occurrences. For an
      architecture retaining every balanced even/odd literal portal, shared
      rays force an orientation-robust repetition ledger

          D'_q=sum_r (2r+1)(q-2-r)=q^3/6+O(q^2).

      The original D_q overcharged one point per ray by fixing both portal
      directions; reversing one block permits a one-point hairpin. This cubic
      barrier is local to the all-literal-balanced architecture and is not an
      unrestricted coverage lower bound. Inserted-corner contamination and
      triangular unique-provider facts are likewise local; they do not force
      global Omega(R) repetition.

      A sufficient next hybrid-atlas theorem would retain the hard portal
      witnesses, include every base point, cover every remaining line-easy
      target through a fixed linear depth, and keep length |L_R|+o(m^3).
      That would finish only the displayed equal-box upper band, not CB4,
      lower ranks, arbitrary aspect ratios, or coefficient one. Reports:
      `MATH_ATTACK_U_FOURBOX_SPILL_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md` and
      `MATH_ATTACK_U_FOURBOX_SPILL_AUDIT_20260724.md`.

1388. The exact component heat chain is a finite reversible projection
      system, but stationary-class selection remains open. For m>=2 and any
      transposition tau, F and tau F are disjoint. Their ownership overlay
      splits into intrinsic tau-cells: independently selecting one complete
      side of every component gives exactly 2^k distinct exact factors, and
      the same cell is obtained from any of its vertices. The fair kernel is
      the orthogonal projection onto cell-constant functions,

          K_tau^2=K_tau=K_tau^*,
          ker(I-K)=intersection_tau Ran(K_tau).

      Every communicating class is a union of complete cells, is S_n-stable,
      and has the uniform stationary law. It need not be one S_n orbit.

      For a fixed target load Z_q in a class,

          E Z_q=lambda_q=c_q+theta_q,
          E Q_q=N_q[Var Z_q-theta_q(1-theta_q)].

      Thus the exact stationary objective is variance above the minimum
      integer floor. On one tau-cell, each moved target pair has invariant
      sum ell and component imbalances d_i. The floor energy decomposes as

          Q_q=J_(q,tau)+G_(q,tau),

      where J is the pairwise balanced floor and G is the common-sign
      residual. Fair averaging replaces G by the cell-invariant component
      noise C, so stationarity gives E G=E C. These are two nonnegative class
      parameters, not bounds on them.

      The minimum stationary-class mean has the exact finite-state dual

          Theta_A=inf_(pi K=pi) E_pi Q_A
                 =sup_h min_F [Q_A(F)+(I-K)h(F)].

      Hence a low class mean implies one low exact factor. This stationary
      condition and the positive-cut/local-minimum lemma LM_A are presently
      incomparable sufficient routes; neither implication is proved for
      exact factors. Component count or entropy alone does not determine the
      harmonic placement of covariance, but enriched entropy arguments are
      not ruled out.

      Linear signed-lattice invariants do not distinguish exact factors.
      An explicit m=4 component flips cyclic-order parity, so that parity is
      not a heat-class invariant. Congruence restrictions give sharp variance
      lower bounds within a class, but one high class does not obstruct the
      existence of another low class. If every transposition overlay of F is
      connected, its S_n orbit is one rigid communicating class with constant
      energy; existence of a high-energy all-transpositions-connected family
      is unproved and would not rule out other low classes.

      The route-specific remaining theorem SCOV_A asks for some communicating
      class with mean O_A(H_A Cat_m). It would imply fixed-window overload but
      is not known necessary for MWB or OR. Reports:
      `MATH_ATTACK_Y_STATIONARY_HEAT_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md` and
      `MATH_ATTACK_Y_STATIONARY_HEAT_AUDIT_20260724.md`.

1389. The global product-box route reduces further to one strongly
      anisotropic three-box ray theorem. Define DRAY as follows: for every
      fixed primitive triple 0<a<b and c>2b,

          g_3(at,bt,ct)=(at+1)(bt+1)+o_(a,b,c)(t^2).

      The width is exactly (at+1)(bt+1), since c>=a+b gives a full plateau.
      Face extension, gcd reduction, and the limit order scale-first,
      mesh-second extend DRAY uniformly to the positive closed dominant cone

          0<a<=b,      c>=2b.

      Zero-coordinate children are not in this projective closure, but the
      elementary slice word gives their required o(R^2) error directly.

      The exact outer-hook identity

          P_r P_s = P_(r+s)+u P_(r-1)P_(s-1)

      partitions a four-chain box into one three-chain child and a translated
      residual four-box. Recursively sort the actual chain segments and pair
      the two largest heights. At each step emit

          (x_j,y_j,z_j)=(h_1,h_2,h_3+h_4),

      which always satisfies z_j>=2 max(x_j,y_j); decrement h_3,h_4 and
      repeat. The child bottoms are forced to rise by j. The exact polynomial
      identity is

          product_i P_(ell_i)(u)
            =sum_j u^j P_(x_j)P_(y_j)P_(z_j),

      and taking the parent central coefficient gives the integral width
      telescoping

          w_4(ell)=sum_j w_3(x_j,y_j,z_j).

      Local child words concatenate with only one anchor for every shifted
      noninitial child. A finite-mesh argument makes pointwise fixed-ray DRAY
      uniform over all moving dominant children; short-side children are
      handled by the slice word. Thus uniformly for 0<=ell_i<=CR,

          (g_4(ell)-w_4(ell))_+ = o_C(R^3).

      Long Boolean-chain parents are negligible only after using truncated
      zeroth and third height moments, not merely a pointwise Gaussian tail.
      Four-block SCD aggregation then gives

          DRAY ==> nu(k)=(1+o(1))W(k).

      This is a strict new sufficient gate: only fixed strongly dominant
      scalene rays need be solved, rather than all compact balanced boxes.
      Boundary rays follow from the mesh proof. The claim that the factor-two
      loss is sharp is proved only for the prescribed recursion that always
      pairs the two largest heights, not every conceivable adaptive hook
      decomposition. DRAY itself remains unproved. Reports:
      `MATH_ATTACK_X_HYBRID_DOMINANT_RAY_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md` and
      `MATH_ATTACK_X_HYBRID_DOMINANT_RAY_AUDIT_20260724.md`.

1390. The adaptive move-to-front lane gives an exact literal band theorem
      for arbitrary finite Johnson walks and reduces its remaining loss from
      quadratic to linear in the number of short coordinate runs. For a
      Johnson walk T_0,...,T_K with successive departures p_i and arrivals
      q_i, an H-saturated one-step MTF lift exists exactly when every internal
      positive run of a coordinate has length at least H+1. Zero-runs are
      unrestricted. The initialization must consist of exactly H singleton
      blocks followed by one nonempty residual block. With

          L_i=T_i\{p_i,...,p_(i+H-1)},
          Theta_(i+1)=({p_i},Theta_i\{q_i}),

      the ordered state is

          Pi_i=(L_i,{p_(i+H-1)},...,{p_i},Theta_i),

      and appending L_(i+1) performs the exact MTF update. A component with K
      edges therefore costs K+2H+1 entries. Its exposed lower flags are the
      successive deletion sets; the advertised intersection identity holds
      only before the right boundary. The first lower and upper Johnson
      colours remain literal consequences of the construction.

      Cutting at every edge ending a positive coordinate run of length at
      most H produces exactly c+rho_H components, where c is the original
      forest component count and rho_H is the number of such short runs.
      Boundary dummies and the H initialization singletons recover the
      deleted first-band colours. For an oriented spanning Johnson forest
      with e edges, the resulting exact canonical-support word satisfies

          L_band <= W+(2H+1)(c+rho_H)+2(N_1-e)
                    +sum_(q=2)^H (Mtilde_q^-+Mtilde_q^+).

      The deeper defects depend jointly on orientation, cut locations,
      boundary dummy choices, and the residual orders Theta; incidental
      intervals can only improve this upper bound. Unconstrained endpoint
      splicing alone gives c<=W/m and hence Hc=o(W), but can create short
      runs or destroy deep-support coverage.

      The exact remaining sufficient theorem AD_A is: for every fixed A,
      with H=ceil(A sqrt(m)), choose one oriented spanning Johnson forest and
      compatible cuts/dummies/residual orders such that

          N_1-e=o(W),
          H(c+rho_H)+sum_(q=2)^H(Mtilde_q^-+Mtilde_q^+)=o(W).

      AD_A directly implies a literal coefficient-one construction after
      the known tails and does not require wreath balancing or MWB. The key
      strict gain is that the short-run toll is (2H+1)rho_H rather than
      O(H^2 rho_H). The future-deletion core is forced only for this
      canonical lift, not for every possible saturated lift; a purported
      unrestricted uniqueness statement is false. Endpoint throughput also
      gives the exact necessary inequality

          sum_j (min(H,d_j)-1)_+
            >= sum_(q=2)^H binom(2m,m-q),

      whose normalized fixed-window limit is at least
      integral_0^A exp(-t^2)dt. This rules out a sparse private refinement
      but not shared adaptive support. Reports:
      `MATH_ATTACK_AD_ADAPTIVE_MTF_FUSION_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md` and
      `MATH_ATTACK_AD_ADAPTIVE_MTF_FUSION_AUDIT_20260724.md`.

1391. The mesoscopic-packet lane now has an audited transition-capacity
      theorem, not a balancing theorem. For an oriented wreath, the usual
      depth-q interval is the intersection of q+1 parity-class successors;
      determining it uses exactly 2q directed successor arcs. Consequently
      a transition supported on L owners and t changed undirected/directed
      seams obeys, respectively,

          D_q^hist <= min(L,2qt_und),
          D_q^point <= min(L,2qt_dir).

      Pointed locality additionally requires the successor orientations to
      agree outside the declared support. Every exact-factor histogram has
      the exact point margins

          sum_(S contains x) mu_q(S)=(m-q)Cat_m;

      in particular the singleton-depth histogram is factor-independent.

      For fixed A and K_A=ceil(A sqrt(m)), the universal capacity envelope

          C_A(L,t)=sum_(q<=K_A) min(L,2qt)/c_q

      has the uniform asymptotic

          C_A(L,t)=2tm F_A(L/(2t sqrt(m)))
                   +O_A(min(L,t sqrt(m))),

      with the corresponding exact constants kappa_A and J_A for the zeroth
      and first weighted moments. This evaluates an upper envelope; it does
      not produce a packet attaining it, give productive signs, or control
      cancellations. Any actual depth-q movement D_q necessarily has owner
      volume at least D_q and seam count at least D_q/(2q). In a specified
      positive-density owner-disjoint O(1)-wreath architecture, a linear
      depth-one improvement therefore requires Theta(m) seams per packet on
      average. This is a transition lower bound and says nothing about
      choosing a good factor ab initio.

      The audited profile-3 switch has coupling masses 8 at depth one and
      4q+6 at depth q>=2. For two disjoint wreaths the odd-graph cross edges
      form a matching, there are no three consecutive cross-incident
      vertices, and the exact replacement ceilings are
      2 floor(n/3) per side and 4 floor(n/3) in total. Reversal gives large
      pointed motion with no unlabelled histogram motion. Frozen adjacent
      Hall slack changes by at most r_(q-1)+r_q, but this gives neither a
      favourable sign nor simultaneous Hall feasibility.

      The remaining unproved content is a positive-density legal packet
      family with correctly signed mesoscopic histogram transport and
      simultaneous fixed-window cancellation control. The capacity theorem
      proves neither MWB nor labelled synchronization and does not constrain
      direct literal constructions. Reports:
      `MATH_ATTACK_P_MESOSCOPIC_CAPACITY_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md` and
      `MATH_ATTACK_P_MESOSCOPIC_CAPACITY_AUDIT_20260724.md`.

1392. The necklace-rounding lane supplies an exact higher-depth two-block
      switch and a separate conditional coefficient-one route. With radius
      law P(D>=q)=rho_q=N_q/W and block length R=2ell,

          V_h=W+2 sum_(q=1)^h N_q
              =(sqrt(pi)+o(1))W sqrt(m),

      while independent Bernoulli rounding has concentrated collision
      excess

          E=(sqrt(pi)/e+o_P(1))W sqrt(m).

      Hence independent rounding fails sharply. Rounded type counts already
      balance every slot class to o(W), and the exact ledger is

          holes U=V_h-T+E.

      One-block replacement has the exact gain formula

          Delta E=|(old-only) intersect {load=1}|
                  -|(new-only) intersect {load=0}|.

      Its transitive average gives only the additive inequality
      n_1>=n_0-o(W), not a general multiplicative conclusion.

      For ell>=3, two aligned blocks with common type, core, exterior,
      outside direction trace, and phase admit an exact coupled adjacent-
      direction switch. It preserves the complete middle multiplicity
      vector and both depth-one vectors. At every deeper certified rank its
      effect is a sum of two signed 2-by-2 rectangles, preserving every
      coordinate point margin. Its old-only mass is

          8 max(0,min(d,ell-2)-1),

      versus 2+8 min(d,ell-2) for one block. A fully occupied rectangle is
      nonimproving, not necessarily neutral; neutrality requires the
      decremented cells to be overloaded. The switch therefore cannot repair
      depth one and is constrained by exact point margins.

      If the unproved Packet-Gain hypothesis supplies, whenever E>eta_m W,
      a physical type-neutral replacement with incidence difference in
      {-1,0,1} and strictly more new holes filled than unique old values
      removed, integer descent reaches E=o(W). Together with cyclic
      linearization and the audited product-SCD tails, this gives a literal
      word of length W+o(W). The sublinear packet-size clause in the raw
      proposal is unused and strictly stronger than needed. Packet-Gain is
      only one sufficient route, not an equivalent remaining theorem; its
      legality, depth-one capability, and simultaneous multidepth signs are
      all open. Reports:
      `MATH_ATTACK_W_NECKLACE_ROUNDING_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md` and
      `MATH_ATTACK_W_NECKLACE_ROUNDING_AUDIT_20260724.md`.

1393. The multitransposition lane separates coherent harmonic contraction
      from integral wall noise exactly. For one exact factor and fixed
      Gaussian window A, a greedily chosen frozen transposition word of
      length O(n) satisfies

          ||P_T...P_1 f||_A^2 <= (1-2/n)^T ||f||_A^2;

      T=ceil(n log 2) gives quarter contraction. An optional universal
      O(n)-length systematic scan follows from a numerical expander gap plus
      the imported symmetric-exclusion theorem; that input is not needed by
      the adaptive greedy version.

      For a frozen word and predictable ownership components, exact fair
      component switches give the martingale identity

          E||f_T-Mf_0||_A^2=N_T/4,
          E Psi_A(F_T)=d+N_T/8.

      The aggregate, rankwise, and coordinate integer-floor restitution
      remainders are all nonnegative and obey

          R_agg >= R_rk >= R_coord >=0.

      The propagated wall-crossing identity has the exact coordinate excess
      variance R_coord/4. The proposed annealed RFEN and the original
      same-word FEN are different sufficient hypotheses because their word
      quantifiers do not match; neither implies the other as stated.

      Correct annealed RFEN, with expectation over an iid frozen word, yields

          E Psi_A(F_T) <= (3/4)Psi_A(F)
                         +(C_A/8)H_A Cat_m.

      Selecting one integral leaf and repeating O(n) macrosteps gives an
      exact factor with Psi_A=O_A(H_A Cat_m)=o(W), hence fixed-window
      overload and, after diagonalization, MWB. The unproved equivalent
      route-specific wall statement controls propagated integer-wall
      crossings together with rank/coordinate floor cancellation. It is not
      a consequence of fragmentation alone and is not necessary for MWB.

      If every transposition overlay of a factor were connected, all heat
      leaves would be relabelings and the floor remainder would be at least
      6 Psi_A for every quarter-contracting word. This is only a conditional
      method obstruction; no high-energy rigid family is known. Thus the
      remaining theorem in this lane is the positive exact-factor RFEN/wall
      inequality, not harmonic contraction or normalization. Reports:
      `MATH_ATTACK_M_MULTITRANSPOSITION_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md` and
      `MATH_ATTACK_M_MULTITRANSPOSITION_AUDIT_20260724.md`.

1394. Near-equality endpoint throughput has an audited finite stability
      theorem that changes no current numerical endpoint. If a word in odd
      dimension k=2m+1 has length M+d, where
      M=binom(k,m), then fixed witnesses for the two middle ranks have at
      least M-3d common two-sided endpoint positions. Under the recorded
      rank cap, all but at most 4d-h low positions are double-fork junctions;
      these form a directed linear forest on the selected rank-m masks.

      The same fixed witness selection gives pointwise coordinate-restricted
      lower-filtration bounds and acyclic upper-incidence bounds. Nearby
      fork windows cannot mix physical widths two and three. Maximal
      homogeneous width-three runs are rainbow Johnson path segments, with
      exact short-band residual sigma and the audited -2 path-boundary term.

      At k=11 this forces at least 319+h double forks, at least 44+h with
      entry rank at most two and 154+h with entry rank at most three. For
      each prescribed coordinate at least 199+h relevant fork bases omit
      it. At k=17 and k=19 the corresponding rainbow-run ledger forces at
      least 2285+3h and 26955+3h Johnson edges. In even dimension k=14, the
      two-sided rank-5/6/7 flag theorem gives 1136 double-diamond bases and
      at least 421 bases omitting each coordinate. In odd dimensions
      k=15,17,19 it forces respectively 125, 2634, and 16778 full four-rank
      flags.

      All displayed constants and inequalities survive audit. The
      coordinate statements concern one fixed witness forest; the 421 claim
      concerns base masks, not every label in the diamond. Summed moment
      inequalities are consequences of, not equivalents to, the pointwise
      subcube inequalities. These conditions have not yet been shown
      infeasible and hence do not improve the exact K<20 intervals. Reports:
      `NONSATURATED_ENDPOINT_FORK_STABILITY.md` and
      `NONSATURATED_ENDPOINT_FORK_STABILITY_AUDIT.md`.

1395. The positive-Graver lane removes false local minima and lattice
      excuses, but not positivity. For the lifted matrix

          M_H=[A 0; B_H -I],

      any exact-factor difference admits a conformal Graver decomposition.
      Convex superadditivity of the floor energy implies that if x* is
      better than x by gap G, some applicable lifted Graver move improves x
      by at least

          G/|supp(x)\supp(x*)| >= G/Cat_m.

      Along a fixed zero-energy target this reaches it in at most Cat_m
      strict moves. Squarefreeness and ownership-component structure apply
      only to moves applicable at an exact-factor vertex; no sub-factor
      support bound follows for arbitrary lifted Graver elements.

      An auxiliary integral formulation with mobile high-quota variables
      gives the exact unlabelled overload objective

          Jbar(F)=sum_(q<=H) O_q(F)/c_q.

      After reoptimizing those variables, the same Graver argument contracts
      the gap to the global optimum by at least a 1/Cat_m fraction per move.
      It does not bound that optimum. The mobile-quota system has the exact
      cone/lattice/semigroup interpretation; signed saturation removes the
      lattice obstruction but not the nonnegative endpoint.

      Every fractional exact factor obeys containment cuts. In prime odd
      dimensions there is an explicit cyclic-invariant, point-regular,
      balanced prescribed quota outside that fractional cone. Any signed
      lift of this target has negative mass Omega(W/n^3). This is a
      prescribed-quota obstruction only: MWB jointly chooses the factor and
      quota, so it gives no lower bound on the mobile optimum. A connected
      squarefree selector-cell composite needs at least ceil((m+1)/2) cells
      under the shared-order connectivity and unoriented-wreath conventions;
      this does not cover arbitrary nonlocal Graver moves.

      Hence exact Graver augmentation proves comparison-based descent to
      Jbar*, not Jbar*=o(W). The missing statement remains a positive exact
      factor with small mobile overload; neither lattice saturation nor
      absence of local minima supplies it. Reports:
      `MATH_ATTACK_AC_POSITIVE_GRAVER_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md` and
      `MATH_ATTACK_AC_POSITIVE_GRAVER_AUDIT_20260724.md`.

1396. The adaptive-Hall lane has an exact one-pass state calculus and two
      rigorous abstract recourse obstructions, but no exact-factor
      counterexample. For owner deletion word a_1,...,a_(K+1), the carried
      letter satisfies

          kappa_1=a_1,
          kappa_(q+1)=kappa_q if toggled, else a_(q+1),

      and the chosen depth-q target is

          P_q=L_(q+1) union {kappa_(q+1)}.

      Immediately before stage q the sibling endpoints have intersection
      L_(q+1) and union P_(q-1). The mismatch count is exactly the number
      T_q of stage-q toggles. Consecutive toggled stages s,...,t-1 rotate
      deletion-word positions s,...,t; this repairs an off-by-one ambiguity
      in the raw report. For each fixed A the capacities c_q are bounded, so
      the weighted and unweighted toggle objectives are equivalent for this
      same one-pass method.

      The dynamic graph G_q rewires exactly the T_(q-1) previously toggled
      owner edges of the canonical graph H_q, and every cut changes by at
      most T_(q-1). Its intersection, anchor, and union histograms are
      respectively mu_(q+1), mu_q, and the preceding chosen histogram. The
      latter is balanced only along an admissible balanced history. Every
      one-coordinate point-star cut and its complement is automatically
      Hall-safe; any obstruction is genuinely higher order. A necessary
      static defect therefore satisfies d_1=0 and sum_q d_q=o(W), but this
      gives no toggle-distance bound.

      The natural K=2 configuration matrix contains a determinant-2 minor,
      so that specific formulation is not TU. This does not rule out every
      extended-flow or matroidal formulation. There is an embedded Boolean
      cube Johnson selector with zero first-order point defect, floor
      overload 2, and minimum balanced reorientation cost 2^(d-1). A single
      literally allowed sibling rewire can change repair cost from 1 to
      2^d in an abstract isolated component. These examples refute generic
      implications from Johnson support, point balance, and Hall feasibility
      to short recourse.

      They are not packetized inside one exact wreath factor. Reachable
      dynamic rows retain n labelled edges, canonical anchors/intersections,
      and a matching for ranks r>=2, but after rewiring their actual
      difference labels need not form the canonical Hamilton coordinate
      cycle and their unions need not be cyclic windows. The exact pair-
      distance ledger applies only to the latent canonical cycles. One cube
      has o(Cat_m) edges, so a global obstruction would require a protected
      positive-density packetization plus exact completion. Neither that nor
      the positive simultaneous Hall/short-transport theorem is known.
      Consequently SDH_A/AO_A remains neither proved nor disproved. Reports:
      `MATH_ATTACK_N_ADAPTIVE_HALL_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md` and
      `MATH_ATTACK_N_ADAPTIVE_HALL_AUDIT_20260724.md`.

1397. The three-box shell lane gives a new literal factor-two braid and
      three architecture-local quadratic obstructions. In the cube
      [0,R]^3, concatenate the triangular boundary cycles C_t for
      t=1,...,R, replacing C_1 by (B_1,C_1,A_1). Every nonzero target has
      an explicit one-shell or one-seam interval witness, including the
      modified t=1 edge case. The exact length is

          |W_R|=3R(R+1)/2+R-1
               =2w(R,R,R)-floor(R/2)-3.

      Thus this is a reset-free literal surface braid, but still has leading
      factor two.

      For selected middle witnesses ordered in complete contiguous radius
      rings of [0,2a]^3, arbitrary ring cuts, orientations, and permutations
      of the complete ring blocks still force quadratic excess. An explicit
      one-surviving-run charge gives

          sum_i d_i <= 2a^3+3a^2+a+(12a+1)D,

      and hence

          D >= (2/15+o(1))a^2.

      This strengthens the raw general constant 2/21. The raw term
      "canonical cut" was undefined, but a new explicit outward six-block
      enumeration has now been proved and independently cross-audited. Its
      half-open-side assignment has alpha congestion at most max(4,a+1) and
      beta congestion at most 4a-2, giving

          sum_i d_i <= 2a^3+2a^2+2+(5a+1)D

      and the stronger exact asymptotic obstruction

          D >= (1/4+o(1))a^2.

      This certifies that precise outward enumeration, not every possible
      meaning of "canonical." For a fixed-coordinate raster with contiguous
      monotone rows, endpoint threshold components have size at most three.
      Direct interpolation within each row improves the raw audited bound to

          D >= [V_a-2(2a+1)^2]/(19a+7)
            =(4/19+o(1))a^2.

      The same argument gives Omega_(delta,C)(R^2) on compact balanced
      unequal boxes within this raster architecture.

      Finally, if every virtual occurrence of W_R is represented by an
      interval whose left and right endpoints are both nondecreasing in the
      shell-word order, then all right endpoints are strictly increasing;
      no such ordered factor can shorten W_R. This does not rule out crossing
      interval endpoints, a new middle order, rebundling occurrences, or any
      unrestricted braid. The heuristic claims that every successful word
      must interleave a positive fraction of radii or use long corridors are
      not proved. The cubic primitive-ray theorem remains open. Reports:
      `MATH_ATTACK_T_THREEBOX_SHELL_REPORT_RAW_20260724.md`,
      `MATH_ATTACK_T_THREEBOX_SHELL_AUDIT_O_AGENT_20260724.md`, and
      `MATH_ATTACK_T_STRONGER_CONSTANTS_CROSS_AUDIT_20260724.md`, with a
      second independent check in
      `MATH_ATTACK_T_STRONGER_CONSTANTS_SECOND_AUDIT_20260724.md`.

1398. Hard-quota exceptional completion gives a clean conditional MWB
      reduction, but the star-side codegree improvement does not solve its
      antecedent. For odd exact factors,

          sum_(q=1)^(m-1) 1/c_q = (I+o(1))sqrt(m),
          I=integral_0^infinity dx/floor(exp(x^2)),

      and in particular the sum is at most sqrt(2 pi m). If one exact factor
      splits as F=G disjoint-union B and, at every controlled depth, a
      balanced full-mass quota b_q dominates the same core histogram
      mu_q^G coordinatewise, then

          O_q(F)<=n|B|,
          sum_(q<=H)O_q(F)/c_q<=n|B|sqrt(2 pi m).

      Consequently |B|=o(Cat_m/sqrt(m)) suffices for MWB; the convenient
      stronger bound |B|=O(Cat_m/m) gives O(W/sqrt(m)). The residual middle
      vertices must actually decompose into the exceptional wreaths; leave
      cardinality alone is not completion.

      This implication to MWB has the common-object quantifier: one uses the
      same split F=G disjoint-union B and the same core G below balanced
      full-mass quotas at every depth in each fixed Gaussian window (or in
      one admissible growing window).  Separately chosen splits or quotas at
      different depths do not suffice.

      Fixing a coordinate v, every wreath contains m middle sets through v
      and m+1 avoiding v. A matching in the full wreath hypergraph that
      saturates the star P_v therefore uses exactly Cat_m edges and is
      automatically a perfect exact factor. In the unoriented support
      hypergraph,

          D_m=m!(m+1)!/2,
          codeg(A,B)/D_m
            =2/[binom(m,d)binom(m+1,d)]
